when-compassion-turns-dangerous.speaker_desc: Kathleen Stock is a British philosopher and author who rose to prominence as a central figure in debates over sex, gender, and truth—resigning from the University of Sussex in 2021 and entering the public discourse. Author and broadcaster, Mary Ann Sieghart is a former Times columnist whose work focuses on gender equality, political analysis, and public policy.
when-compassion-turns-dangerous.subtitle: Should we legalise assisted dying?

the-institutions-that-failed-gaza-norman.speaker_desc: Norman Finkelstein is one of the most high-profile controversial political scientists writing today. He has spent decades as a leading critic of Israeli policy. His 2025 book, Gaza’s Gravediggers, turns his scrutiny on the institutions he accuses of complicity in Gaza’s destruction.
the-institutions-that-failed-gaza-norman.subtitle: Reckoning with descruction

the-dangerous-urge-to-punish.speaker_desc: Andy West is the author of The Life Inside and the Executive Producer of the acclaimed BBC adaptation of that book Waiting for the Out.
the-dangerous-urge-to-punish.subtitle: Waiting For the Out

the-hype-and-limits-of-ai.speaker_desc: Michael Wooldridge is an Oxford computer scientist and one of the world’s foremost authorities on AI. His book The Road to Conscious Machines argues that the hype around AI distracts us from the more immediate risks that the technology poses. Audrey Borowski is a Leverhulme Early Career Fellow at Cambridge specialising in the philosophy of AI. Her research argues that data and algorithmic systems have become a new form of ideology, undermining democratic politics. Tipped by The Times as "the next Einstein," Sabrina Pasterski is a theoretical physicist specializing in celestial holography. Based at the Perimeter Institute, she founded and leads the Celestial Holography Initiative, aimed at uniting our understanding of spacetime with quantum theory. Hilary Lawson is a philosopher best known for his theory of Closure, which puts forward a non-realist account of the relationship between language and the world. He extends the same principles to artificial intelligence, with radical implications for what machines can and cannot do.
the-hype-and-limits-of-ai.subtitle: Is the latest technology our friend or foe?

the-edge-of-the-world.speaker_desc: Joanna Kavenna is an award-winning novelist and one of Granta's Best Young British Novelists. Erling Kagge is a Norwegian explorer, philosopher, and writer. He is the first person in history to reach the North Pole, South Pole, and the summit of Mount Everest on foot. Steven Mithen is an archaeologist whose work explores the evolution of human intelligence, creativity, and social behaviour. Maria Balaska is a philosopher whose work explores subjectivity, ethics, and the limits of experience. HOST: Sophie Scott-Brown
the-edge-of-the-world.subtitle: Are we witnessing the end of the unknown?

why-we-should-embrace-cybersex-with-trud.speaker_desc: Dr. Trudy Barber is a fine artist, sexual futurologist, and pioneer of cybersex research who created one of the first virtual reality sex environments in the early 1990s. Her work focuses on the intersection of human desire and technology, spanning virtual reality, AI, sex robotics, and the posthuman future of intimacy.
why-we-should-embrace-cybersex-with-trud.subtitle: The future of sex robots

carlo-rovelli-on-the-impossibility-of-a-.speaker_desc: Theoretical physicist Carlo Rovelli is a pioneer of theories like Loop Quantum Gravity, White Holes, and the relational interpretation of quantum mechanics. His books include Seven Brief Lessons on Physics, which has been translated into 41 languages and sold over a million copies, as well as the bestselling Reality Is Not What It Seems (2015) and White Holes (2023). He was named one of the 100 most influential thinkers in the world by Foreign Policy magazine, and is Emeritus Professor at the Centre de Physique Théorique of Marseille, as well as holding positions at the Santa Fe Institute and the Perimeter Institute.
carlo-rovelli-on-the-impossibility-of-a-.subtitle: Reality is made of relations

one-giant-conflict-for-mankind.speaker_desc: Adam Frank is an American astrophysicist, writer, and public intellectual who serves as Professor of Physics and Astronomy at the University of Rochester. Kishore Mahbubani is a Singaporean diplomat and scholar, former President of the UN Security Council, and one of Asia's most influential voices on geopolitics and the historic return of Asia to the global centre stage. Laura Grego is an astrophysicist and director of the Global Security Programme at the Union of Concerned Scientists, specialising in space policy and nuclear safety and security. Philip Ball hosts.
one-giant-conflict-for-mankind.subtitle: War and diplomacy on the final frontier

there-can-be-no-ultimate-map-of-the-univ.speaker_desc: A transformative encounter with a German Sufi philosopher in Cairo set Jenann Ismael on her way to becoming the leading philosopher of physics that she is today. Her work confronts the tension between what physics tells us about reality, and how the world actually seems to us in our conscious experience of it. She tries to ground free will in the nature of thermodynamics, and argues that reality is fundamentally unpredictable.
there-can-be-no-ultimate-map-of-the-univ.subtitle: Systems cannot describe themselves consistently

spacetime-and-the-framework-of-the-world.speaker_desc: Avshalom Elitzur is an Israeli physicist and philosopher at the Israeli Institute for Advanced Research whose Elitzur–Vaidman thought experiment reshaped debates on the role of the observer in quantum theory. Jonathan Oppenheim is a Professor of Quantum Theory at UCL, renowned for developing “post-quantum” models in which spacetime remains classical, but interacts consistently with quantum matter. Ivette Fuentes is a Professor of Quantum Physics at the University of Southampton whose work considers fundamental quantum mechanics, quantum optics and their interplay with general relativity. Bjørn Ekeberg hosts.
spacetime-and-the-framework-of-the-world.subtitle: Probing the nature of time

the-rise-and-fall-of-the-educated-elite.speaker_desc: Michael Gove is Editor of The Spectator and served in cabinet across five government departments for more than a decade. Most consequentially as Secretary of State for Education, where he steered through the biggest changes to English schooling in decades. Thangam Debbonaire is a Labour life peer and former MP for Bristol West who served as Shadow Secretary of State for Culture under Keir Starmer. Her work in the Lords spans arts, cultural diplomacy, AI and copyright. Daniel Susskind is a leading economist, Professor of Business at Gresham College, and a member of the UK Government's Expert Panel on AI and the Future of Work. His new book What Should My Children Do explores how AI is changing the future of education. Mary Ann Sieghart is a journalist, author, and public intellectual committed to dismantling the invisible yet powerful bias she calls “the authority gap.”
the-rise-and-fall-of-the-educated-elite.subtitle: Is there any future for traditional education?

desire-and-danger-in-the-age-of-self-lov.speaker_desc: Trudy Barber is an academic exploring the social and cultural implications of emerging technologies. Barber also developed one of the first virtual reality sex environments in 1992. Maureen Dowd is an American journalist and columnist known for her incisive political commentary in The New York Times . Minna Salami is a writer and social critic whose book Sensuous Knowledge draws on African feminist thought to challenge the dominance of Western epistemology and argue for a more embodied approach to understanding the world. Claudia Canavan hosts.
desire-and-danger-in-the-age-of-self-lov.subtitle: Human sexuality and the crisis of liberty

the-media-manufactures-your-ignorance-wi.speaker_desc: Louisa Munch is a critical theorist, PhD researcher, and influencer reaching over 200,000 people on social media, translating complex ideas into clear commentary on politics, culture, and power.
the-media-manufactures-your-ignorance-wi.subtitle: Fighting manufactured ignorance

mysticism-heidegger-and-the-future-of-ph.speaker_desc: Simon Critchley is a leading continental philosopher and Hans Jonas Professor at The New School for Social Research whose more than twenty books span ethics, tragedy, mysticism, and the meaning of life. Host of the Apply-degger podcast, he works to make Heidegger's philosophy more accessible.
mysticism-heidegger-and-the-future-of-ph.subtitle: Phenomenology and the everyday

the-future-of-the-ai-economy.speaker_desc: Sebastian Mallaby is a journalist, author, and economic commentator. He is the Paul A. Volcker Senior Fellow at the Council on Foreign Relations and the author of The Infinity Machine , which tells the inside story of Demis Hassabis and the race to build superintelligence. Martin Wolf is chief economics commentator for the Financial Times , widely recognised as one of the world’s most influential financial journalists. His most recent book T he Crisis of Democratic Capitalism sets out a bold vision to fix the drift between capitalism and democracy.
the-future-of-the-ai-economy.subtitle: Are we building something we can't control?

the-philosophy-and-dangers-of-fame.speaker_desc: Sarah Wilson is a New York Times bestselling author whose most recent book, I Eat the Stars , is a guide to finding meaning in a world that seems to be falling apart. Jordan Stephens is best known as one half of chart-topping hip-hop duo Rizzle Kicks, and as a mental health advocate. His latest book, Avoidance, Drugs, Heartbreak explores the struggles of a young man rising to fame.
the-philosophy-and-dangers-of-fame.subtitle: Fame, the true self and modern masculinity

the-power-of-moral-shaming-with-ken-roth.speaker_desc: Kenneth Roth is an American attorney, human rights activist, and writer, as well as the former Executive Director of Human Rights Watch.
the-power-of-moral-shaming-with-ken-roth.subtitle: Why governments still fear the facts

freedom-democracy-and-the-law.speaker_desc: James Orr is a Cambridge philosopher and theologian. He is admired by JD Vance, who once described him as his "British sherpa." Christopher Steele is a former MI6 officer who ran the Russia desk from 2006 to 2009 and later compiled the "Steele dossier"—intelligence reports alleging ties between Donald Trump and Russia. Marlène Laruelle is a historian, sociologist and political scientist at The George Washington University, where she is directs the Illiberalism Studies Programme. Philippe Sands is a writer and lawyer at University College London whose work in international law has taken him from the trial of Pinochet to the prosecution of Nazi war criminals.
freedom-democracy-and-the-law.subtitle: The rise of lawfare in political life

liberalisms-fight-for-survival.speaker_desc: Michael Ignatieff is a Canadian author, academic and former politician who served as leader of the Liberal Party and leader of the Opposition from 2008 until 2011. Known for his work as a historian, Ignatieff has held senior academic posts at the universities of Cambridge, Oxford, Harvard, and Toronto.
liberalisms-fight-for-survival.subtitle: The way forward in an illiberal era

science-and-art-are-not-separate-with-sh.speaker_desc: Sheila Atim MBE is an actress, singer and playwright, best known for her Olivier Award–winning stage work and roles in The Woman King and Bruised.
science-and-art-are-not-separate-with-sh.subtitle: Creativity under the microscope

language-and-the-illusion-of-reality.speaker_desc: Nick Enfield is Professor of Linguistics at the University of Sydney and Director of the Sydney Centre for Language Research. A major theme in Enfield’s work is how language operates not just as a system of signs but as a form of social action embedded in time. Hilary Lawson is a philosopher known for his theory of 'Closure', he is an outspoken critic of philosophical realism, and is Editorial Director of the IAI.
language-and-the-illusion-of-reality.subtitle: Can words ever capture the truth?

gutenberg-vs-zuckerberg2.speaker_desc: Jimmy Wales is the founder of Wikipedia, the world’s largest collaborative encyclopedia, which is run by the non-profit Wikimedia Foundation. Cory Doctorow is a Canadian-British author and digital rights activist who has served as European Director of the Electronic Frontier Foundation. He is the author of several books including Enshiffication. Mary Harrington is an author and contributor editor for UnHerd and runs her own weekly Substack, Reactionary Feminist, a term she coined.
gutenberg-vs-zuckerberg2.subtitle: Literacy, attention, and the digital revolution

you-are-not-your-brain.speaker_desc: Martine Nida-Rümelin is a German philosopher and professor of philosophy at the University of Fribourg in Switzerland. Her work develops and defends what she calls subject-body dualism.
you-are-not-your-brain.subtitle: The unique nature of conscious beings

curtis-yarvin-challenged-on-his-argument.speaker_desc: Curtis Yarvin, described as "The Philosopher Behind J.D. Vance," argues that democracy is a failed experiment and should be replaced by monarchy.
curtis-yarvin-challenged-on-his-argument.subtitle: Are all functional systems monarchies?

consciousness-is-biologys-biggest-blunde.speaker_desc: Denis Noble is Professor Emeritus of Cardiovascular Physiology at Oxford University who developed the first mathematical model of the working heart and has since become one of the world's leading critics of neo-Darwinian orthodoxy in biology.
consciousness-is-biologys-biggest-blunde.subtitle: The central dogma of biology is incorrect

reason-and-revolution.speaker_desc: Cornel West is an American philosopher and public intellectual whose landmark work Race Matters established him as one of America's most prominent voices on race, democracy, and political philosophy. He ran for president in 2024. Rowan Williams is the 104th Archbishop of Canterbury and one of the world's leading theologians, whose work spans theology, spirituality, and philosophy. Susan Neiman is a philosopher pressing for a renewed commitment to Enlightenment morality and politics. She is Director of the Einstein Forum in Potsdam and author of Left Is Not Woke.
reason-and-revolution.subtitle: Is reason a double-edged sword?

the-not-so-blind-watchmaker.speaker_desc: Denis Noble is Professor Emeritus of Cardiovascular Physiology at Oxford University. He developed the first mathematical model of the working heart and has since become one of the world's leading critics of neo-Darwinian orthodoxy in biology. Eva Jablonka is an evolutionary theorist and geneticist whose work pushes biology beyond a strictly gene-centred view of life. Her book Evolution in Four Dimensions helped pioneer the extended evolutionary synthesis. Samir Okasha is Professor of Philosophy of Science at the University of Bristol and winner of the Lakatos Prize for outstanding contributions to the philosophy of science. Philip Ball hosts.
the-not-so-blind-watchmaker.subtitle: Does evolution have a purpose?

the-hostile-takeover-of-philosophy-with-.speaker_desc: Christoph Schuringa is a British philosopher and Associate Professor of Philosophy at Northeastern University London, whose research focuses on German philosophy and the history of ideas.
the-hostile-takeover-of-philosophy-with-.subtitle: How the Cold War reshaped philosophy

the-crisis-of-attention-is-a-crisis-of-m.speaker_desc: Gloria Mark is a Professor of Informatics at the University of California, Irvine, where she studies how digital technology impacts attention, productivity, and well‑being. Trained in psychology and computer science, her research combines empirical data with human‑centred insights to understand how people manage focus in an always‑on environment.
the-crisis-of-attention-is-a-crisis-of-m.subtitle: Boredom, multitasking, and the fragility of focus

gender-equality-and-the-freedom-trap.speaker_desc: Minna Salami is a writer and social critic whose book Sensuous Knowledge draws on African feminist thought to challenge the dominance of Western epistemology. Mary Harrington is an author and contributing editor for UnHerd and runs a weekly Substack, Reactionary Feminist, a term she coined. Kathleen Stock is a British philosopher and author, best known for her work on sex and gender, who resigned from the University of Sussex in 2021 to become a prominent public voice in the debate. Lucy Jones is a writer and journalist whose book Matrescence draws on neuroscience, evolutionary biology, and cultural history to argue that the transition into motherhood is one of the most profound biological transformations in human life. Chine McDonald hosts.
gender-equality-and-the-freedom-trap.subtitle: The future of gender roles and motherhood

activists-dont-need-to-win-in-order-to-a.speaker_desc: Sophie Scott-Brown is a historian of anarchism, Honorary Research Fellow at the University of St Andrews, and the author of The Radical Fifties: Activist Politics in Cold War Britain .
activists-dont-need-to-win-in-order-to-a.subtitle: Learning from the radical 1950s

the-metamodernist-turn.speaker_desc: Hilary Lawson is a philosopher and renowned critic of objective truth. Best known for his theory of Closure, which goes beyond postmodernism to provide a new account of the relationship between language and reality. Linda Martín Alcoff is an award-winning philosopher whose work interrogates who gets to define what’s real, and whose knowledge counts as knowledge. Professor of Philosophy at City University, New York, in 2021 she was ranked the third-most influential philosopher in the world. Jason Ānanda Josephson Storm is a leading proponent of metamodernism. His work puts forward a philosophical programme, and a guide to what a world beyond postmodernism might look like. He is Chair of Science & Technology Studies and Professor of Religion at Williams College. Güneş Taylor hosts.
the-metamodernist-turn.subtitle: The meaning and functionality of truth

memories-are-not-stored-in-the-brain-vic.speaker_desc: Victoria Trumbull is a philosopher, researcher, and writer who challenges the dominance of reductive materialism in contemporary thought. Working across philosophical psychology, metaphysics, and the history of ideas, she seeks to recover a deeper, more expansive understanding of the human soul.
memories-are-not-stored-in-the-brain-vic.subtitle: We are made of time

the-future-of-the-left-faiza-shaheen-jer.speaker_desc: Faiza Shaheen is an economist, author, and activist whose work exposes the structural forces that uphold inequality. She is Executive Director of Tax Justice UK, a Visiting Senior Fellow at the London School of Economics' International Inequalities Institute, and the author of Know Your Place. Jeremy Corbyn is a British politician and current independent MP who served as the Labour party's leader from 2015 to 2020 and later co-founded Your Party.
the-future-of-the-left-faiza-shaheen-jer.subtitle: Backed into a corner or turning a new one?

patriotism-populism-and-the-fate-of-nati.speaker_desc: James Orr is a Cambridge philosopher and theologian and former Head of Policy for Reform UK. He is admired by JD Vance, who once described him as his "British sherpa." Michael Ignatieff is a writer, historian, and former leader of Canada's Liberal Party whose books on nationalism and human rights established him as a central voice in post–Cold War political thought. One of the few few leading economists who predicted the 2008 financial crisis, Gillian Tett is a columnist for the Financial Times and author of several books including Fool's Gold. Rana Mitter hosts.
patriotism-populism-and-the-fate-of-nati.subtitle: What we don't understand about nationalism

the-thoughts-computers-cant-think.speaker_desc: One of Britain’s most influential psychologists, Simon Baron-Cohen is renowned for his pioneering research on autism, empathy, and the cognitive differences between individuals. Maria Balaska is a philosopher whose work brings together continental philosophy, ethics, psychoanalysis, and political thought.
the-thoughts-computers-cant-think.subtitle: What we don't understand about intelligence

pragmatism-and-the-pursuit-of-truth.speaker_desc: David Edmonds is a British philosopher, and a radio feature maker at the BBC World Service. With Nigel Warburton he produces the popular podcast series, Philosophy Bites One of the most influential contemporary pragmatist philosophers, Cheryl Misak is known for reviving and reshaping the American pragmatist tradition for the 21st century.
pragmatism-and-the-pursuit-of-truth.subtitle: Inside the Vienna Circle and its enemies

physics-has-misunderstood-time.speaker_desc: Avshalom Elitzur is an Israeli physicist and philosopher at the Israeli Institute for Advanced Research whose Elitzur–Vaidman thought experiment reshaped debates on the role of the observer in quantum theory.
physics-has-misunderstood-time.subtitle: Rethinking quantum mechanics

the-self-has-no-center-with-julian-baggi.speaker_desc: The author of best-sellers such as The Pig That Wants to Be Eaten and How the World Thinks, Julian Baggini is a leading philosopher and the co-founder of The Philosopher’s Magazine.
the-self-has-no-center-with-julian-baggi.subtitle: The ego trick and the good life

the-age-of-the-illiberal-democracy.speaker_desc: Kishore Mahbubani is a Singaporean diplomat and scholar, former President of the UN Security Council, whose work examines the geopolitics of Asia's return to the global centre stage. Michael Ignatieff is a writer, historian, and former Leader of Canada's Liberal Party whose books on nationalism and human rights established him as a central voice in post–Cold War political thought. Marlene Laruelle is a historian, sociologist and political scientist at George Washington University, where she directs the Illiberalism Studies Programme.
the-age-of-the-illiberal-democracy.subtitle: Is the new authoritarianism here to stay?

in-defense-of-democracy-michael-ignatief.speaker_desc: Michael Ignatieff is a writer, historian, and former Leader of Canada's Liberal Party whose books on nationalism and human rights established him as a central voice in post–Cold War political thought. Oli Dugmore is a political journalist and executive digital editor at the New Statesman .
in-defense-of-democracy-michael-ignatief.subtitle: Michael Ignatieff on modern-day liberalism

the-future-of-the-tech-crisis.speaker_desc: Cory Doctorow is a Canadian-British author and digital rights activist who has served as European Director of the Electronic Frontier Foundation. He is the author of several books including Enshittification.
the-future-of-the-tech-crisis.subtitle: Building the post-American internet

economists-dont-understand-the-nature-of.speaker_desc: Ingrid Harvold Kvangraven is a Senior Lecturer in International Development at King’s College London, founder of the blog Developing Economics and a leading thinker in heterodox economics.
economists-dont-understand-the-nature-of.subtitle: Why economics is fundamentally political

buddhism-and-the-emptiness-of-reality.speaker_desc: Jessica Frazier is a philosopher at the University of Oxford and Founder of the Journal of Hindu Studies whose research translates classical Indian philosophy into terms that engage contemporary debates on metaphysics and ethics.
buddhism-and-the-emptiness-of-reality.subtitle: Buddhism vs Hinduism on the true nature of reality

rethinking-the-global-orthodoxy.speaker_desc: John Ralston Saul is an award-winning essayist, novelist and President Emeritus of PEN International. His 16 works, including Voltaire’s Bastards and The Collapse of Globalism, have been translated into 29 languages in 38 countries.
rethinking-the-global-orthodoxy.subtitle: How the illusion of globalization empowered elites

consciousness-has-evolutionary-roots-wit.speaker_desc: Eva Jablonka is an evolutionary theorist and geneticist whose work pushes biology beyond a strictly gene-centred view of life.
consciousness-has-evolutionary-roots-wit.subtitle: Why AI isn't conscious and likely never will be

why-plato-matters-now-angie-hobbs.speaker_desc: Angie Hobbs is the chair for the Public Understanding of Philosophy at Sheffield, and a frequent contributor to the BBC’s In Our Time, Night Waves and The Forum. She is the author of Plato and the Hero and is currently working on a new edition of Plato’s Symposium.
why-plato-matters-now-angie-hobbs.subtitle: Ancient answers to modern problems

times-great-mystery.speaker_desc: Tim Maudlin is a celebrated philosopher of science, renowned for his work on the foundations of physics and metaphysics. He is also an author and professor at New York University. Wahida Khandker is a philosopher and co-chair of the Society for European Philosophy. Her work is at the cutting-edge of the philosophy of process and the philosophy of biology. Hilary Lawson is a philosopher and renowned critic of philosophical realism. His main work, Closure: A Story of Everything, has been described as ‘the first non-realist metaphysics’. Ivette Fuentes is a physicist at the University of Southampton and Emmy Fellow at the University of Oxford. Her work and previous collaboration with Roger Penrose considers fundamental quantum mechanics, quantum optics and their interplay with general relativity.
times-great-mystery.subtitle: What does the clock really measure?

what-the-left-misses-about-trump-with-ma.speaker_desc: Political theorist, Labour life peer, and a member of the House of Lords, Maurice Glasman founded the Blue Labour movement in 2009.
what-the-left-misses-about-trump-with-ma.subtitle: What comes after MAGA?

quantum-measurement-influences-the-past-.speaker_desc: Avshalom Elitzur is a theoretical physicist and philosopher at the Israeli Institute for Advanced Research, whose Elitzur–Vaidman thought experiment reshaped debates on the role of the observer in quantum theory.
quantum-measurement-influences-the-past-.subtitle: Time and consciousness in quantum physics

free-will-is-real.speaker_desc: George Ellis is a South African cosmologist and philosopher of science renowned for bridging the gap between physics and metaphysics.
free-will-is-real.subtitle: Why science cannot ignore human agency

the-return-of-the-grand-narrative.speaker_desc: Steve Fuller is a Professor of Sociology at the University of Warwick and founder of the research programme of social epistemology, best known for his work on the post-truth condition and the politics of knowledge. Michael Shermer is one of the world's most prominent sceptics and defenders of scientific reason. He's the founding publisher of the widely read Sceptic Magazine, and the executive director of the Sceptics Society. Dr. Shini Somara is an award-winning media broadcaster and a highly accomplaished British mechanical engineer specialising in Computational Fluid Dyanmics. Jack Symes hosts.
the-return-of-the-grand-narrative.subtitle: Does science preach the same story it replaced?

education-has-lost-its-way-guy-standing.speaker_desc: Guy Standing is a trailblazing economist and long-standing advocate for Universal Basic Income. He is a Professorial Research Associate at SOAS University of London and co-founder of the Basic Income Earth Network.
education-has-lost-its-way-guy-standing.subtitle: Reclaiming learning as a public good

beyond-the-sci-fi-myths-of-ai.speaker_desc: Philip Mirowski is the Carl Koch Professor of Economics and the History and Philosophy of Science at the University of Notre Dame. He is a leading historian and philosopher of economic thought, known for his trenchant critiques of neoliberalism, the commercialisation of science, and the epistemology of economics.
beyond-the-sci-fi-myths-of-ai.subtitle: How open science is privatising knowledge

the-end-of-the-great-alliance.speaker_desc: Jeremy Corbyn is a British politician and current independent MP who served as the Labour party's leader from 2015 to 2020. He is co-founder and interim leader of Your Party. Michael Ignatieff is a writer, historian, and former Leader of Canada's Liberal Party whose books on nationalism and human rights have established him as a central voice in post–Cold War political thought. One of the few leading economists who predicted the 2008 financial crisis, Gillian Tett is a columnist for the Financial Times and author of several books including Fool's Gold . Rana Mitter hosts.
the-end-of-the-great-alliance.subtitle: What next for the US and Europe?

disloyalty-is-not-betrayal.speaker_desc: Yasmin Alibhai-Brown writes a weekly opinion column for The i Paper, focusing on British politics, social justice, and cultural issues. She is an award-winning journalist and was named Broadsheet Commentator of the Year at the Media Freedom Awards. Alibhai-Brown was also the founder of the British Muslims for Secular Democracy.
disloyalty-is-not-betrayal.subtitle: When loyalty becomes complicity

the-return-of-malcolm-x.speaker_desc: Kehinde Andrews is the first Black Studies professor in the UK, currently working at Birmingham City University. He is the director of the Centre for Critical Social Research, founder of the Harambee Organisation of Black Unity, and co-chair of the UK Black Studies Association.
the-return-of-malcolm-x.subtitle: Recovering the radical philosophy of civil rights

the-idea-of-progress-is-a-dangerous-lie-.speaker_desc: John Gray, hailed as "Britain's best philosopher," is a leading critic of liberalism and the Enlightenment. He has long challenged the belief in inevitable progress, predicting both the 2008 financial crisis and the rise of populism. Jonny Thomson hosts.
the-idea-of-progress-is-a-dangerous-lie-.subtitle: There is no moral arc of history

the-key-to-the-cosmos.speaker_desc: Sarah Hart is the first female Professor of Geometry at Gresham College and the author of Once Upon a Prime. Her research focuses on the cutting-edge of group theory. Dean Rickles is historian and philosopher of Modern Physics at the University of Sydney, where he is also a director of the Sydney Centre for Time. He investigates the frontiers of quantum gravity, string theory and the philosophy of the mind. Hilary Lawson is a philosopher and renowned critic of philosophical realism. His main work, Closure: A Story of Everything, has been described as ‘the first non-realist metaphysics’. Hosted by Jay Shapiro: an award-winning filmmaker, writer, and podcaster.
the-key-to-the-cosmos.subtitle: Does mathematics describe reality?

the-science-of-creativity.subtitle: Breaking the arts vs science binary

science-and-the-unknowable-universe.speaker_desc: Lera Boroditsky is a cognitive scientist and linguist whose research has transformed our understanding of how language shapes thought. Avshalom Elitzur is an Israeli physicist and philosopher at the Israeli Institute for Advanced Research whose Elitzur–Vaidman thought experiment reshaped debates on the role of the observer in quantum theory. HOST: Philip Ball is a British science writer. For over twenty years he has been an editor of the journal Nature for which he continues to write regularly. He now writes a regular column in Chemistry World.
science-and-the-unknowable-universe.subtitle: How much can science really tell us?

new-rebels-and-a-failed-establishment.speaker_desc: Thangam Debbonaire is a Labour member of the House of Lords, having served for nine years as MP for Bristol West and as a senior figure in Keir Starmer’s Shadow Cabinet. Eric Kaufmann is Professor of Politics at the University of Buckingham and Director of the Centre for Heterodox Social Science. His research focuses on political demography, national identity, immigration, and cultural change. Louisa Munch is a critical theorist, PhD researcher, and influencer reaching over 200,000 people on social media, translating complex ideas into clear commentary on politics, culture, and power.
new-rebels-and-a-failed-establishment.subtitle: Should we heed the voice of youth?

what-50-days-of-silence-can-teach-you-wi.speaker_desc: Erling Kagge is a Norweigian explorer, philosopher, and writer who has spent his life testing the limits of the physical world and human mind. He is the first person in history to reach the North Pole, South Pole and the summit of Mount Everest on foot. He has also sailed across the Atlantic twice, rounded Cape Horn, and sailed to Antarctica and back. After his record-breaking feat, Kagge founded a publishing house which went on to acquire one of Norway's oldest publishing companies. In 2021, Kagge sold his publishing company and in 2025 he left his position as publisher. His writing on exploration and philosophy has appeared in the Financial Times, The New York Times, and the Guardian.
what-50-days-of-silence-can-teach-you-wi.subtitle: The philosophy of making our life harder

pride-and-prognosis.speaker_desc: Charlotte Blease is a philosopher of medicine whose research focuses on the ethical, psychological and social dimensions of healthcare innovation, particularly the use of digital and artificial intelligence technologies in clinical settings.
pride-and-prognosis.subtitle: Why AI could save care

the-mystery-of-the-self-and-the-body.speaker_desc: Slavoj Žižek is a Senior Researcher at the University of Ljubljana and the author of more than fifty books applying Lacanian psychoanalysis and Hegelian philosophy to politics, film, and culture. Monima Chadha is Professor of Indian Philosophy at the University of Oxford. A leading figure in cross-cultural philosophy, her work brings classical Indian traditions into dialogue with contemporary epistemology and the philosophy of mind. Martine Nida-Rümelin is a German philosopher and professor of philosophy at the University of Fribourg in Switzerland. Her work develops and defends what she calls subject-body dualism. Federico Faggin is an Italian-American physicist and engineer who led the design of the world's first commercial microprocessor at Intel in the 1970s, earning him the National Medal of Technology and Innovation.
the-mystery-of-the-self-and-the-body.subtitle: The mind-body problem from East to West

immunity-and-impunity-in-a-lawless-world.speaker_desc: Philippe Sands is a writer and lawyer known for his work in international law and human rights. His books chart the use of international law to hold to account violations of international law from Chile's Pinochet to Nazis who fled to avoid the Nuremberg trials. He has emerged as a leading defender of the rule of law around the world in an age where populism and conflict threaten to send the world into anarchy. He is currently a Professor of Laws and the Director of the Centre on International Courts and Tribunals at University College London. He has appeared as a counsel and advocate at the International Court of Justice, the European Court of Justice, the European Court of Human Rights and the International Criminal Court. His most recent book, 38 Londres Street, charts the trial of Pinochet, the first national leader to be tried under international law, and the efforts to hold Nazi officers responsible for the holocaust to account.
immunity-and-impunity-in-a-lawless-world.subtitle: From Nazis in Patagonia to Pinochet in London

neurodiverse-pattern-seeking-drives-huma.speaker_desc: One of Britain’s most influential psychologists, Simon Baron-Cohen is renowned for his pioneering research on autism, empathy, and the cognitive differences between individuals. Professor of Developmental Psychopathology at the University of Cambridge, Baron-Cohen has challenged conventional views of the human mind with a body of work that spans theories of mind, systemizing-empathizing, and the biological basis of social cognition. He is the author of The Essential Difference , Mindblindness , Zero Degrees of Empathy , and The Pattern Seekers , as well as a frequent contributor to the Guardian , Scientific American , and academic journals worldwide. Baron-Cohen’s rigorous research and thought-provoking theories continue to shape contemporary debates on neurodiversity, education, and the nature of human cognition.
neurodiverse-pattern-seeking-drives-huma.subtitle: Rethinking autism and how we approach it

warfare-in-the-academy.speaker_desc: James Cleverly is a Conservative politician who has served as Foreign Secretary, Home Secretary, and Education Secretary, as well as Party Chairman. He is currently Shadow Secretary of State for Housing, Communities and Local Government. Minna Salami is a writer and social critic whose book Sensuous Knowledge draws on African feminist thought to challenge the dominance of Western epistemology and argue for a more embodied approach to understanding the world. John Ralston Saul is an award-winning essayist, novelist and President Emeritus of PEN International. His 16 works, including Voltaire’s Bastards and The Collapse of Globalism , have been translated into 29 languages in 38 countries.
warfare-in-the-academy.subtitle: What should we be teaching our children?

eva-jablonka-evolution-beyond-genes.speaker_desc: Eva Jablonka, Professor at the Cohn Institute for the History and Philosophy of Science and Ideas at Tel Aviv University, is an evolutionary theorist and geneticist whose work pushes biology beyond a strictly gene-centred view of life.
eva-jablonka-evolution-beyond-genes.subtitle: Teleology, consciousness, and want

philosophy-of-the-senses-our-inner-world.speaker_desc: Barry C. Smith is a professor of philosophy and directs the Institute of Philosophy at the University of London’s School of Advanced Study. As founding director of the Centre for the Study of Senses, he has created a platform for collaborative research between philosophers, psychologists and neuroscientists.
philosophy-of-the-senses-our-inner-world.subtitle: The limits of digitising sensations

cosmology-in-crisis.speaker_desc: George Ellis is a South African cosmologist and philosopher of science renowned for bridging the gap between physics and metaphysics. Claudia de Rham is a Swiss theoretical physicist at Imperial College London whose theory of massive gravity proposes that the graviton carries a nonzero mass—offering an alternative account of the universe's accelerating expansion. Bjørn Ekeberg is a Norwegian philosopher of science, author, entrepreneur, and cultural creator whose work challenges orthodox thinking in cosmology, scientific knowledge, and human understanding. Hosted by Jay Shapiro.
cosmology-in-crisis.subtitle: The smoking gun of the James Webb Telescope

rebalancing-the-global-order.speaker_desc: Kishore Mahbubani is a Singaporean diplomat and scholar. A former President of the UN Security Council, his work examines the geopolitics of Asia's return to the global centre stage.
rebalancing-the-global-order.subtitle: The rise and fall of Western hegemony

language-shapes-thought-not-the-other-wa.speaker_desc: Lera Boroditsky is a cognitive scientist and linguist whose research has transformed our understanding of how language shapes thought.
language-shapes-thought-not-the-other-wa.subtitle: Why linguistic relativity matters

the-hidden-philosophy-of-food.speaker_desc: Julian Baggini is a philosopher and author renowned for translating deep philosophical questions into engaging, practical insights. Co-founder of The Philosopher’s Magazine and author of best-sellers such as The Godless Gospel , How the World Thinks , The Virtues of the Table , and The Ego Trick , Baggini defends Enlightenment values and champions reason, scepticism, and humanism in a complex world.
the-hidden-philosophy-of-food.subtitle: The philosophy behind every meal

everything-we-knew-about-economics-is-wr.speaker_desc: Faiza Shaheen is an economist, author, and activist whose work analyses the structural forces behind inequality. She is Executive Director of Tax Justice UK, and the author of Know Your Place . Llŷr Powell is a member of Reform’s shadow cabinet in the recently elected Senedd, where he is responsible for Business and is also Chief Whip. Maurice Glasman is the founder of Blue Labour and a life peer whose political thought draws on Jewish socialism, Christian democracy, and guild association to make the case for a conservatism rooted in working-class culture. Paul Johnson is an economist currently serving as Provost of Queen's College Cambridge, having spent fourteen years as Director of the Institute for Fiscal Studies analysing tax, spending, and public policy across successive governments.
everything-we-knew-about-economics-is-wr.subtitle: Do we need a new economic theory?

michael-shermer-reality-doesnt-care-what.speaker_desc: Michael Shermer is one of the world's most prominent sceptics and defenders of scientific reason. He's the founding publisher of the widely read Sceptic Magazine, and the executive director of the Sceptics Society.
michael-shermer-reality-doesnt-care-what.subtitle: Can we separate fact from fiction?

why-you-should-ignore-the-economics-nobe.speaker_desc: Cahal Moran is a behavioural economist and Visiting Fellow at the London School of Economics and the creator of the YouTube channel Unlearning Economics.
why-you-should-ignore-the-economics-nobe.subtitle: From equations back to everyday life

memes-minds-and-the-myth-of-control.speaker_desc: Tony D. Sampson is an academic and author whose research connects digital culture, media theory, and political philosophy. Victoria Trumbull is a philosopher and writer working across the philosophy of mind and the philosophy of time, whose recent work argues that memory unfolds in time rather than being stored in the brain. Sylvie Delacroix is a scholar and philosopher reimagining how communities might govern shared digital resources in ways that promote fairness, accountability, and trust in the age of AI. Jonny Thomson hosts.
memes-minds-and-the-myth-of-control.subtitle: Where do our ideas come from?

the-simulation-matrix.speaker_desc: Paulette Clancy is a Johns Hopkins engineering professor and leading computational materials scientist, pioneering atomic-scale modelling and ML-driven materials discovery. John Ioannidis is a Stanford professor and one of the world’s most-cited scientists, known for reshaping debates on evidence, bias and reproducibility. Steve Koonin is a NYU physicist and former US Undersecretary of Science, known for scrutinising political claims about climate change. Adviser to major science and defence agencies, and author of the controversial Unsettled (2021). Bahar Gholipour hosts.
the-simulation-matrix.subtitle: Can a simulation find truth?

the-view-from-somewhere-with-miriam-scho.speaker_desc: Miriam Schoenfield is a leading epistemologist, Associate Professor of Philosophy at the University of Texas at Austin, and award-winning essayist.
the-view-from-somewhere-with-miriam-scho.subtitle: How the tools of rationality fail

the-economics-of-the-new-world-order.speaker_desc: Formerly a lead research economist at the World Bank, Branko Milanović is one of the world’s leading experts on income inequality and globalization. He is a senior scholar at the Stone Center on Socio-economic Inequality at the City University of New York and is best known for the “Elephant Curve,” a visual representation of how different income groups benefit unevenly from globalization, which has shaped debates on economic development and social justice. Milanović has brought rigorous data analysis and historical insight to some of the most pressing questions of our time. His new book, The Great Global Transformation, examines the decline of neoliberalism and the rise of a new economic order shaped by nationalism, trade conflicts, and shifting power. Drawing on original research, Milanović examines how Asia’s economic growth is reshaping income patterns and the uncertainties facing the global order.
the-economics-of-the-new-world-order.subtitle: The great global transformation

memory-is-a-construction.speaker_desc: Charan Ranganath is Professor of Psychology and Neuroscience and Director of Dynamic Memory Lab at the University of California, Davis, where he spent more than 25 years investigating how the brain encodes, stores and retrieves memories. He is the author of Why We Remember: The Science of Memory and How It Shapes Us .
memory-is-a-construction.subtitle: How the brain actively rebuilds memory

the-pathology-of-everyday-life.speaker_desc: Anna Lembke is a groundbreaking psychiatrist and addiction medicine expert, best known for her bestselling book, Dopamine Nation. Joanna Moncrieff is Professor of Critical and Social Psychiatry at UCL and was the lead author of a landmark scientific study into the theory of serotonin and depression. She is also a founding member and co-chairperson of the Critical Psychiatry Network. Sarah Wilson is a multi-New York Times and Amazon bestselling author, social philosopher, and philanthropist. She founded the global ‘I Quit Sugar’ movement.
the-pathology-of-everyday-life.subtitle: The hidden cost of the mental health movement

the-james-webb-telescopes-threat-to-the-.speaker_desc: Bjørn Ekeberg is a Norwegian philosopher of science, author, entrepreneur, and cultural creator whose work challenges orthodox thinking in cosmology, scientific knowledge, and human understanding. He holds a Ph.D. in philosophy of science from the University of Victoria (Canada) and has combined rigorous academic inquiry with creative and practical ventures. Ekeberg’s philosophical writing spans cosmology, metaphysics, and the limits of scientific knowledge, exemplified by his book Metaphysical Experiments: Physics and the Invention of the Universe, which critiques assumptions in modern physics and invites fresh perspectives on how we understand the universe.
the-james-webb-telescopes-threat-to-the-.subtitle: New cracks in our story of the universe

bhaskar-sunkara-on-the-left-after-trump.speaker_desc: Bhaskar Sunkara is the founding editor of Jacobin , the president of the Nation , and the author of The Socialist Manifesto: The Case for Radical Politics in an Era of Extreme Inequality .
bhaskar-sunkara-on-the-left-after-trump.subtitle: Is socialism due a revival?

evidence-in-the-dock.speaker_desc: Nick Enfield is Professor of Linguistics at the University of Sydney and Director of the Sydney Centre for Language Research. He is the author of Language vs Reality. Analytic philosopher and author of Knowledge and Its Limits, Timothy Williamson is a Senior Research Fellow at New College, Oxford and former Wykeham Professor of Logic. Genia Schönbaumsfeld is Professor of Philosophy at the University of Southampton and the author of several books – most recently, Wittgenstein on Religious Belief. In 2023, Genia was awarded a highly prestigious ERC Advanced Grant for her project entitled ‘The Ethics of Doubt – Kierkegaard, Scepticism and Conspiracy Theory’. Jay Shapiro hosts.
evidence-in-the-dock.subtitle: Calling truth to the stand

carissa-veliz-privacy-is-power.speaker_desc: Carissa Véliz is a philosopher and Associate Professor at Oxford Univeristy, specialising in AI ethics, privacy and political philosophy. She explores how data and algorithmic prediction shape power, autonomy and democracy.
carissa-veliz-privacy-is-power.subtitle: Can democracy survive the rise of digital tech?

the-big-bang-miracle.speaker_desc: Phil Halper is a science communicator and Fellow of the Royal Astronomical Society. His recent book, Battle of the Big Bang, explores alternative theories of the universe’s birth, especially those often dismissed for challenging established cosmological ideas. Joseph Silk is a cosmologist and the Savilian Professor of Astronomy Emeritus at the University of Oxford, whose work investigates the early universe, dark matter, and galaxy formation. Priya Natarajan is a Professor of Astrophysics at Yale University and was named as one of Time Magazine's top 100 most influential people in 2024 for her groundbreaking work in the field. Hilary Lawson hosts.
the-big-bang-miracle.subtitle: Will cosmology ever be truly objective?

to-save-democracy-we-need-fewer-election.speaker_desc: Dedicated to reimagining democracy as a system that truly empowers people, Hélène Landemore is a political philosopher and Professor at Yale University. As founder of Yale’s Citizens’ Assemblies research program and a Distinguished Research Fellow at Oxford’s Institute for Ethics in AI, she blends deep theoretical insight with practical innovation. Landemore challenges traditional electoral democracy by arguing for a more inclusive, deliberative model—one that better captures collective intelligence and democratic reason. Her work, including advising OpenAI’s Democratic Inputs to AI program, explores how democratic institutions can become more stable, representative, and capable of addressing today’s complex political and technological challenges.
to-save-democracy-we-need-fewer-election.subtitle: The ancient Athenian idea that may save democracy

the-rise-and-fall-of-the-city.speaker_desc: Luís Bettencourt is a physicist, author, and urban systems researcher, currently Professor at the University of Chicago and External Professor at the Santa Fe Institute. Kiran Sidhu is an evocative and honest writer known for blending personal insight with lyrical storytelling. She regularly writes for Prospect magazine about rural life and the philosophical implications of this change in her life. Joanna Kavenna is a novelist and travel writer whose work explores themes of place, displacement, and the contrasts between urban and rural existence. She's held the Alistair Horne Fellowship at St Antony’s College Oxford and the Harper-Wood at St John’s College Cambridge.
the-rise-and-fall-of-the-city.subtitle: The politics of place

iain-mcgilchrist-on-why-the-mind-is-not-.speaker_desc: Iain McGilchrist is a distinguished British neuroscientist, psychiatrist and philosopher. A former Fellow of All Souls College, Oxford, he has also worked as a consulting psychiatrist, and is known for his influential work on the relationship between the structure of our brains, human cultures and our understanding of the world.
iain-mcgilchrist-on-why-the-mind-is-not-.subtitle: The end of materialism

the-patriarchy-in-question.speaker_desc: Paul Dolan is a behavioural scientist and happiness expert at LSE, widely known for his research on wellbeing, decision-making, and human motivation. Nick Fletcher is a former Tory MP for Don Valley known for his opinions on gender equality, trans issues and immigration. He was chair of the Men and Boys All-Party Parliamentary Group. Catherine Hakim is a social scientist and author specialising in women's employment and women's issues, known for inventing the concept of "erotic capital". Mary Ann Sieghart is an author, broadcaster and former Times columnist whose work focuses on gender equality, political analysis, and public policy. Avantika Chilkoti hosts.
the-patriarchy-in-question.subtitle: Has feminism left men behind?

how-to-sue-your-government-with-jolyon-m.speaker_desc: Jolyon Maugham KC is an activist barrister, founder of the Good Law Project, and thorn in the side of the government. Jolyon has sought to challenge the UK government's approach to Brexit, Covid and transgender rights. He has written for the Telegraph, Guardian and New Statesman on the legal implications of Brexit.
how-to-sue-your-government-with-jolyon-m.subtitle: The fight to democratise justice

imagination-and-the-real.speaker_desc: Nadine Dijkstra is Principal Investigator at UCL’s Queen Square Institute of Neurology, where she leads the Imagine Reality Lab in exploring how the brain constructs our sense of reality. Karl Friston is a world-leading neuroscientist and Professor at UCL, best known as the architect of the influential Free Energy Principle and a Principal Research Fellow with the Wellcome Trust. Maria Balaet is a leading voice in psychedelic research, using advanced neuroimaging at King’s College London to uncover how these substances transform consciousness. Hosted by Claudia Canavan.
imagination-and-the-real.subtitle: Could reality be a controlled hallucination?

love-is-more-than-magic.speaker_desc: Alain de Botton is the bestselling philosopher redefining how we understand love, work, and meaning in the modern world. He first rose to prominence with Essays in Love, a novel-philosophy hybrid that became an international bestseller. He has since authored several bestselling works that blend literary elegance, psychological insight, and philosophical depth.
love-is-more-than-magic.subtitle: Why romantic idealism fails us

ivette-fuentes.speaker_desc: Ivette Fuentes is a Professor of Quantum Physics at the University of Southampton and an Emmy Fellow at Keble College, University of Oxford. She earned her PhD in physics from the University of Nottingham and completed postdoctoral research at the University of Vienna, where she worked extensively on quantum optics and relativistic quantum information theory. Fuentes has since established herself as a leading figure in the study of quantum gravity, focusing on how quantum phenomena behave in curved spacetime — bridging quantum mechanics with general relativity.
ivette-fuentes.subtitle: Could tabletop experiments be the future?

technology-is-always-political-with-shei.speaker_desc: Sheila Sen Jasanoff is an Indian-American academic in the field of Science and Technology Studies. In 2021 she was elected to the American Philosophical Society. Her research has been recognized with many awards, including the 2022 Holberg Prize "for her groundbreaking research in science and technology studies."
technology-is-always-political-with-shei.subtitle: Technocrats and codes of social understanding

navigating-the-unknown.speaker_desc: Graham Priest is Professor of Philosophy at City University of New York. He is well known for his work on non-classical logic and Buddhist Philosophy. Jessica Frazier is an Oxford philosopher who works on Indian Philosophy and the European tradition of phenomenology. She is also a frequent consultant for the BBC and speaker on In Our Time. Hilary Lawson is a philosopher and renowned critic of philosophical realism. His main work, Closure: A Story of Everything , has been described as ‘the first non-realist metaphysics’. Shini Somara hosts.
navigating-the-unknown.subtitle: The weeds within the theory of truth

the-world-after-liberalism-maurice-glass.speaker_desc: Political theorist, Labour life peer, and a member of the House of Lords, Maurice Glasman is the founder of the Blue Labour movement in 2009. Co-founder of Compact magazine and author of Tyranny, Inc., Sohrab Ahmari is a celebrated journalist and cultural critic.
the-world-after-liberalism-maurice-glass.subtitle: Moving beyond the myth of the individual

in-the-name-of-reason.speaker_desc: Dan Sperber is a distinguished anthropologist and philosopher who is the author of several critically-acclaimed books, including The Enigma of Reason. Steve Fuller is a professor of sociology at the University of Warwick. He is the author of dozens of books, including Post-truth: Knowledge as a Power Game. Miriam Schoenfield is a leading epistemologist, Associate Professor of Philosophy at the University of Texas at Austin, and award-winning essayist. Jack Symes is a public philosopher and writer. He is the producer of The Panpsycast Philosophy Podcast and editor of the Bloomsbury series Talking about Philosophy. He is currently Teacher and Researcher at Durham University, UK.
in-the-name-of-reason.subtitle: Is rationality really a social good?

riches-and-rags.speaker_desc: Ingrid Robeyns is a philosopher and economist best known for developing limitarianism, the case for placing ethical limits on personal wealth. She holds the Chair of Ethics in Institutions at Utrecht University. Yaron Brook is an entrepreneur and political commentator, best known as chairman of the Ayn Rand Institute and host of The Yaron Brook Show. He co-authored the bestseller Free Market Revolution. Thangam Debbonaire is a Labour member of the House of Lords, having served for nine years as MP for Bristol West and as a senior figure in Keir Starmer’s Shadow Cabinet. Avantika Chilkoti hosts.
riches-and-rags.subtitle: Are we wrong to worry about wealth inequality?

the-fight-for-the-ai-economy-zoltan-istv.speaker_desc: Transhumanist thinker and former US presidential candidate, Zoltan Istvan is known for promoting life extension and emerging technologies in politics. Aaron Bastani is the co-founder of Novara Media, described as 'the slickest of the guerrilla news and opinion operations that have sprung up in Britain' by the Guardian .
the-fight-for-the-ai-economy-zoltan-istv.subtitle: Visions of an automated future

the-end-of-woke.speaker_desc: Eric Kaufmann is Professor of Politics at the University of Buckingham and Director of the Centre for Heterodox Social Science. His research focuses on political demography, national identity, immigration, and cultural change.
the-end-of-woke.subtitle: A 'vibe shift' in mass media

science-beyond-the-physical.speaker_desc: Lisa Feldman Barrett is among the most cited scientists in the world for her research on the psychology and neuroscience of emotions. Adam Frank is an astrophysicist who explores the origins of stars, civilizations and consciousness, and is a leading figure in astrobiology and the search for alien life. Michael Levin is a synthetic biologist whose pioneering work in regenerative biology involves building biological robots to probe the nature of life, intelligence and evolution. Güneş Taylor hosts.
science-beyond-the-physical.subtitle: Is materialism becoming obsolete?

mental-health-and-the-chemical-imbalance.speaker_desc: Joanna Moncrieff is Professor of Critical and Social Psychiatry at University College London, and a consultant psychiatrist for the NHS. She is also a founding member and co-chairperson of the Critical Psychiatry Network. Her most recent book is Chemically Imbalanced: The Making and Unmaking of the Serotonin Myth.
mental-health-and-the-chemical-imbalance.subtitle: Exposing the shaky science behind antidepressants

the-only-freedom-which-deserves-the-name.speaker_desc: Curtis Yarvin, described as "The Philosopher Behind J.D. Vance," argues that democracy is a failed experiment and should be replaced by monarchy. Expert on the challenges facing liberal democracy in the 21st century, Yascha Mounk is a political scientist and Professor at Johns Hopkins University. Writer, social critic, and thought leader Minna Salami is known for fusing feminism, philosophy, and political thought. She is the author of Can Feminism Be African?.
the-only-freedom-which-deserves-the-name.subtitle: Can liberalism survive the century?

the-only-fans-paradox-with-farha-khalidi.speaker_desc: Farha Khalidi is a feminist cultural commentator, TikToker and OnlyFans model with 1.7 million followers on TikTok.
the-only-fans-paradox-with-farha-khalidi.subtitle: Misogyny, double standards and the sex work debate

mysticism-vs-modernity.speaker_desc: Transhumanist philosopher David Pearce, author of Philosophy of Action Naomi Goulder, and world-renowned biologist Rupert Sheldrake debate mysticism and modernity. Hosted by Jay Shapiro.
mysticism-vs-modernity.subtitle: Spirituality makes a comeback

in-conversation-john-gray-and-hilary-law.speaker_desc: One of Britain’s most provocative thinkers, John Gray is a political philosopher famous for dismantling liberalism and exposing the illusions of human progress. Former Professor of European Thought at the London School of Economics, Gray has challenged orthodoxy across the political spectrum with a body of work that ranges from critiques of Enlightenment rationalism to meditations on the limits of secular humanism. He is the bestselling author of Straw Dogs, The Silence of Animals , and Seven Types of Atheism as well as a frequent contributor to The Guardian , New Statesman, and The Times Literary Supplement . Gray’s sharp insights and contrarian stance continue to shape contemporary debates on ethics, politics, and the future of humanity.
in-conversation-john-gray-and-hilary-law.subtitle: Human nature, truth, and the decline of liberalism

the-mirror.speaker_desc: Dean Rickles is historian and philosopher of Modern Physics at the University of Sydney, where he is also a director of the Sydney Centre for Time. He investigates the frontiers of quantum gravity, string theory and the philosophy of the mind. Winsome Pinnock is a British playwright and dramaturge, known for her pioneering contributions to contemporary theatre. Joanna Kavenna is an award-winning writer. She is the author of six books and has written for The New Yorker, The Guardian and London Review of Books. Hosted by Jessica Frazier.
the-mirror.subtitle: Can art and thought mirror reality?

global-challenge-and-global-action.speaker_desc: James Bacchus is a professor of Global Affairs and Director of the Global Economic and Environmental Opportunity Centre at the University of Central Florida. With a long and storied career in Congress and the World Trade Organisation (WTO), his most recent work argues that we need global democracy in order to have true, sustainable development. Leah Downey is a political theorist, a junior research fellow at St. John’s College, Cambridge and a lecturer at Kings College London. She has published research on the macroeconomics of the green transition and is the author of Our Money: Monetary Policy as if Democracy Matters . Kai Heron is a political organiser, trade unionist, and Lecturer in Political Ecology at Lancaster University. He is the co-editor of the De Gruyter Degrowth Handbook , has published widely on the politics of green energy and is the co-author of Radical Abundance: How to Win a Green Democratic Future . Adrienne Buller hosts.
global-challenge-and-global-action.subtitle: Can liberal democracies face the climate crisis?

our-future-theories-of-the-universe.speaker_desc: Awarded the 2020 Nobel Prize in Physics for his work on black holes, Roger Penrose is a world-renowned mathematician and physicist. In recent years, he has investigated the relationship between physics and the mind, famously arguing that quantum mechanics plays an essential role in solving the mysteries of human consciousness. Penrose has made numerous appearances on media such as BBC, Closer to Truth, and The Joe Rogan Experience. In 1994, he was knighted for his services to science. Famed for his poetic take on the cosmos, physicist and broadcaster Brian Cox has become one of the world’s most recognizable voices in science communication. A former musician turned particle physicist, Cox has played a key role in major experiments at CERN and the Large Hadron Collider, while also captivating millions through BBC series such as Wonders of the Universe, The Planets, and Forces of Nature. Cox has been showered with praise for his contributions, appointed Commander of the Order of the British Empire (CBE), and is the recipient of the Institute of Physics Kelvin Medal and the Michael Faraday Prize. Beyond his work as a Royal Society professor of physics at the University of Manchester, Cox advocates for public scientific literacy and political responsibility in science funding. His style blends rigorous physics with a deep sense of awe — bringing relativity, entropy, and quantum theory into living rooms around the globe. His rare ability to fuse clarity with wonder has earned global acclaim.
our-future-theories-of-the-universe.subtitle: Brian Cox interviews Roger Penrose

democracy-in-the-ruins-of-neoliberalism.speaker_desc: Wendy Brown is one of the most influential political theorists of her generation, known for her penetrating analyses of power, neoliberalism, democracy, and the fate of the public good in contemporary political life. Brown is currently the UPS Foundation Professor in the School of Social Science at the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton and Professor Emerita of Political Science at the University of California, Berkeley. Hosted by Sophie Scott-Brown.
democracy-in-the-ruins-of-neoliberalism.subtitle: Nihilism, populism, and political renewal

the-price-of-populism-with-jason-furman.speaker_desc: Jason Furman is a prominent American economist known for his extensive contributions to public policy, academia, and economic analysis. He currently serves as the Aetna Professor of the Practice of Economic Policy at Harvard University. He served as the Chairman of the Council of Economic Advisers (CEA) under President Barack Obama from August 2013 to January 2017. In this role, he acted as a principal economic advisor to the President.
the-price-of-populism-with-jason-furman.subtitle: The hidden costs of Trump's economic promises

the-wealth-cap.speaker_desc: Ingrid Robeyns is a political philosopher known for her work on economic justice, the capability approach, and limits on extreme wealth.
the-wealth-cap.subtitle: A bold case for limiting extreme wealth

how-to-reclaim-the-body.speaker_desc: Susie Orbach is a psychotherapist, psychoanalyst, and social critic. She came to prominence with the book Fat Is A Feminist Issue, and was therapist to Diana, Princess of Wales.
how-to-reclaim-the-body.subtitle: Moving beyond the beauty industry

ai-and-the-mysteries-of-reality.speaker_desc: Computer scientist Roman Yampolskiy, philosopher Steve Fuller, and co-curator of AI: More than Human Suzanne Livingston debate whether AI can make novel scientific discoveries. Hosted by Güneş Taylor.
ai-and-the-mysteries-of-reality.subtitle: The future of scientific discovery

i-forget-therefore-i-am.speaker_desc: Join Oliver Hardt, Professor of Psychology at McGill University, Catherine Loveday, Author of The Secret World of the Brain, and Iain McGilchrist, famed neuroscientist, philosopher and psychologist at the University of Oxford as they clash over what it means to be human. Hosted by Oxford philosopher Jessica Frazier.
i-forget-therefore-i-am.subtitle: Is memory essential to who we are?

thinking-isnt-only-in-the-brain-with-bar.speaker_desc: Barbara Tversky is an active Emerita Professor of Psychology at Stanford and Professor of Psychology at Columbia Teachers College. Her research has spanned memory, categorization, language, spatial cognition, event perception and cognition, diagrammatic reasoning, sketching, creativity, design, and gesture. The overall goals have been to uncover how people think about the spaces they inhabit and the actions they perform and see and then how people use the world and the things in it. Her 2019 book, Mind in Motion: How Action Shapes Thought, provides an overview of some of that work. She has collaborated widely, with linguists, philosophers, neuroscientists, computer scientists, chemists, biologists, architects, designers, and artists.
thinking-isnt-only-in-the-brain-with-bar.subtitle: How the body shapes the mind

the-iron-fist-vs-the-invisible-hand.speaker_desc: Curtis Yarvin, described as "The Philosopher Behind J.D. Vance," argues that democracy is a failed experiment and should be replaced by monarchy. Aaron Bastani is the co-founder of Novara Media, described by the Guardian as 'the slickest of the guerrilla news and opinion operations that have sprung up in Britain’. Hélène Landemore is a political philosopher and professor at Yale University, and is also a Distinguished Research Fellow at Oxford’s Institute for Ethics in AI.
the-iron-fist-vs-the-invisible-hand.subtitle: The new economic order

peace-passion-and-adventure.speaker_desc: Janne Teller was formerly a UN macroeconomist specialising in developing economies. She has since become a bestselling author of novels, essays, and short stories. Alenka Zupančič is a leading Lacanian philosopher and social theorist. She is a professor at The European Graduate School and at the University of Nova Gorica. Paul Bloom is a Canadian-American psychologist, bestselling author, and celebrated speaker. He is Professor Emeritus at Yale and a professor at the University of Toronto. Bloom’s work explores human nature, morality, and pleasure.
peace-passion-and-adventure.subtitle: The comfort of chaos

there-is-no-fundamental-basis-to-reality.speaker_desc: Susan Schneider is an American philosopher and cognitive scientist, known for her work on the nature of consciousness, artificial intelligence, and the future of mind. She is the founding director of the Center for the Future Mind at Florida Atlantic University and holds the Baruch S. Blumberg NASA/Library of Congress Chair in Astrobiology, Exploration, and Scientific Innovation. Schneider is best known for her exploration of post-biological intelligence and the philosophical implications of machine consciousness. In her widely discussed book Artificial You: AI and the Future of Your Mind, she examines whether machines could ever truly possess consciousness, and whether humans should merge with them. James Ladyman is a pioneering philosopher renowned for combining rigorous natural science with deep metaphysical inquiry. A leader in philosophy of science and physics, he champions ontic structural realism, the view that reality is fundamentally relational, and defends a naturalised metaphysics that aligns with our best scientific understanding, challenging inherited intuitions that mislead us about the nature of the universe. In Everything Must Go: Metaphysics Naturalized, Ladyman argues that many common metaphysical assumptions—about objects, causation, or essence—are relics incompatible with modern science. Ladyman’s fusion of analytic clarity with scientific insight reshapes how we think about reality—revealing a cosmos that is stranger and more beautiful than our unexamined instincts suggest.
there-is-no-fundamental-basis-to-reality.subtitle: Physics, AI and the structure of everything

materialism-and-emergence-cant-explain-c.speaker_desc: Alex O’Connor is a YouTuber, public speaker, writer, and host of the Within Reason Podcast. He first began posting videos to his YouTube channel "CosmicSkeptic" before taking his degree in philosophy and theology at St John's College, Oxford. He has since grown his following to over 1.5 million subscribers with his rigorous yet accessible philosophy videos. O’Connor has appeared on television programmes such as Piers Morgan Uncensored, BBC Sunday Morning Live, and Channel 4 News. He has debated philosophy, religion, free speech, and more with leading thinkers Slavoj Žižek, Richard Dawkins, Neil deGrasse Tyson, and more.
materialism-and-emergence-cant-explain-c.subtitle: From new atheism to panpsychism

dreams-of-the-future.speaker_desc: Daniel Markovits is the Guido Calabresi Professor of Law at Yale Law School and the author of the best-selling book, The Meritocracy Trap . Thangam Debbonaire is a Labour member of the House of Lords, chair of the Labour Women's Network, and a leading voice on cultural policy. Eric Kaufmann is Professor of Politics at The University of Buckingham and Director of the Centre for Heterodox Social Science. Hosted by Jack Symes.
dreams-of-the-future.subtitle: Are visions of progress coming to an end?

the-power-and-politics-of-shame.speaker_desc: Kenneth Roth is an attorney, activist and author best known as the Executive Director of Human Rights Watch for nearly thirty years. He is currently a fellow of the Harvard Kennedy School and a lecturer at Princeton's School of Public and International Affairs.
the-power-and-politics-of-shame.subtitle: The ugly reality behind human rights

the-universe-existed-before-the-big-bang.speaker_desc: Phil Halper is a prominent science communicator whose work probes the limits of cosmology and challenges the dominance of the standard Big Bang narrative.
the-universe-existed-before-the-big-bang.subtitle: The end of the beginning

the-green-technology-paradox.speaker_desc: Erik Swyngedouw is a leading critical geographer at the University of Manchester. He combines political ecology and economics with analyses of contemporary capitalism, showing how urbanisation, water, and governance are entwined with power and democracy. Harvard scholar Sheila Jasanoff is one of the most influential voices in Science and Technology Studies, dismantling the myth that science and technology operate above human choices, cultural assumptions, and political power. Paul Stein is one of the most influential engineers of his generation, shaping aerospace and energy as former CTO of Rolls-Royce and co-founder of Floral Energy. His work links technological innovation to climate action and national strategy.
the-green-technology-paradox.subtitle: Will scientific progress save our planet?

war-power-and-the-future-of-global-order.speaker_desc: Owen Matthews is a British author, historian and journalist. He is author of several books including Stalin's Children , which was shortlisted for the 2008 Guardian First Book Award and the Orwell Prize for political writing. He is one of Britain's leading authorities on Russian history and politics.
war-power-and-the-future-of-global-order.subtitle: Why the West continues to misunderstand Putin

the-grandest-of-grand-narratives.speaker_desc: Steve Fuller is a professor of sociology at the University of Warwick. He is the founder of the research program of social epistemology and the author of dozens of books, including Post-Truth: Knowledge as a Power Game. Barry C. Smith is a professor of philosophy and director of the Institute of Philosophy at the University of London. He is an expert on the senses and consciousness and leads groundbreaking interdisciplinary work on flavour, smell, and perception. Jessica Frazier is a philosopher at the University of Oxford and Fellow of the Oxford Centre for Hindu Studies. She is an expert on Indian Philosophy and the European tradition of phenomenology. Phil Collins hosts.
the-grandest-of-grand-narratives.subtitle: Science, philosophy or religion: which story wins?

the-trouble-with-meritocracy-daniel-mark.speaker_desc: Daniel Markovits is an American legal scholar, best known for his work on law and behavioural economics, contract law, distributive justice, and market regulation. His best-selling book, The Meritocracy Trap: How America's Foundational Myth Feeds Inequality, Dismantles the Middle Class, and Devours the Elite, has sparked a significant discussion about the problems inherent in meritocratic societies.
the-trouble-with-meritocracy-daniel-mark.subtitle: Suffering from success

how-to-hack-the-reality-simulation-with-.speaker_desc: Roman Yampolskiy is a professor and computer scientist at the University of Louisville who specialises in artificial intelligence, AI safety, digital forensics and behavioural biometrics. He is the author of Considerations on the AI Endgame.
how-to-hack-the-reality-simulation-with-.subtitle: Can intelligence escape its own universe?

mental-health-in-an-age-of-over-diagnosi.speaker_desc: Alastair Santhouse is a consultant psychiatrist with over 20 years of experience at Guy's Hospital and the Maudsley Hospital in London. From 2013 to 2017, he served as Vice Chair of the Royal College of Psychiatrists' Faculty of Liaison Psychiatry. Santhouse also served as the President of the Psychiatry Section of the Royal Society of Medicine. His clinical work focuses on the often overlooked intersection of physical and mental health.
mental-health-in-an-age-of-over-diagnosi.subtitle: Pathologising everyday life

overcoming-evolution.speaker_desc: Critic of evolutionary psychology Subrena E. Smith, philosopher of mind Keith Frankish, and clinical psychologist Simon Baron-Cohen debate the significance of evolutionary psychology. Hosted by Güneş Taylor.
overcoming-evolution.subtitle: Going beyond Darwin

the-new-moral-elite-with-catherine-liu.speaker_desc: Catherine Liu is an American cultural theorist, critic, and professor of Film and Media Studies at the University of California, Irvine. A sharp public intellectual, Liu is best known for her incisive critiques of elite liberalism, academic hypocrisy, and the commodification of virtue. She brings together Marxist cultural analysis with polemic flair, offering a compelling—and at times confrontational—challenge to the moral self-image of the contemporary professional class.
the-new-moral-elite-with-catherine-liu.subtitle: From identity politics to class struggle

the-lefts-identity-crisis.speaker_desc: Maurice Glasman is a political theorist, Labour life peer, and founder of the Blue Labour movement in 2009. Pam Cox is the Labour MP for Colchester who was recently elected to Parliament in 2024. Prior to this she was a professor of social history and criminology at the University of Essex and a fellow of the Royal Society of Arts. Bhaskar Sunkara is currently the president of The Nation, the oldest continuously published weekly magazine in the United States. He is a former vice-chair of the Democratic Socialists of America and the author of The Socialist Manifesto. Roger Hearing hosts.
the-lefts-identity-crisis.subtitle: Woke vs work

the-life-and-philosophy-of-jeremy-corbyn.speaker_desc: Jeremy Corbyn is a British politician and current independent MP who served as the Labour Party's leader from 2015 to 2020. Representing the constituency of Islington North since 1983, he was a vocal backbencher with a reputation of voting against his party until he was elected leader with the largest party membership for a generation. He contested the 2017 general election and won 40% of the vote, the largest Labour share since 2001. Since he has been expelled from the Labour Party, Jeremy has gone on to win his Islington seat as an independent and has recently been elected the parliamentary leader of Your Party, a party he founded with fellow MP Zarah Sultana. His views place him firmly on the progressive left where he is staunchly anti-war, anti-austerity, pro-nationalisation and pro-Palestine. In the current Parliament, Jeremy is a key opponent to Keir Starmer, holding the government to account from the left.
the-life-and-philosophy-of-jeremy-corbyn.subtitle: A life on the Left

the-end-of-ideology.speaker_desc: Glenn Greenwald is a Pulitzer-prize winning journalist, known for publishing the Snowden files and uncovering the largest corruption scandal in Brazil's history. One of the most influential political philosophers of her generation, Seyla Benhabib is Senior Research Scholar at Columbia Law School and has shaped global debates on democracy, migration, and human rights. Sam Kiley is a multi-award winning journalist currently working as World Affairs Editor of The Independent and has covered conflict for more than 30 years, reporting from the front lines in Afghanistan, Iraq and Somalia, among other war zones.
the-end-of-ideology.subtitle: Power, geography and the global order

forgiving-the-unforgivable-lucy-allais.speaker_desc: Lucy Allais is Professor of Philosophy at Johns Hopkins University and the University of the Witwatersrand, renowned for her work on Immanuel Kant, forgiveness, punishment, and bioethics. She is the author of Manifest Reality: Kant's Idealism and His Realism.
forgiving-the-unforgivable-lucy-allais.subtitle: The true meaning of forgiveness

all-the-worlds-a-stage.speaker_desc: Claire Blencowe is an associate professor of Sociology and co-chair of the Just Eco-Geo-Political Futures research group at Warwick University. She is a leading scholar of Foucault. Paul Bloom is a psychologist and the author of several bestselling works, including Against Empathy . He is Emeritus Professor of psychology and cognitive science at Yale University and Professor of Psychology at the University of Toronto.
