Michelle Terry is an Olivier Award-winning actor and the Artistic Director of Shakespeare's Globe, where she has gained critical acclaim for her modern interpretations of Shakespeare's plays. Matthew Taylor is a British former political strategist and current Chief Executive of the Royal Society for the Encouragement of Arts, Manufactures and Commerce.
all-the-worlds-a-stage.subtitle: Performance and the search for the true self

glenn-greenwald-trumps-iran-attacks-are-.speaker_desc: After founding a law firm concentrating on First Amendment litigation (protecting free speech and a free press), Glenn Greenwald turned to journalism. He became a vocal critic of the Iraq War and American foreign policy, a position he has maintained. He started contributing to Salon in 2007 and to The Guardian in 2012, and in the latter published a series of reports detailing covert American and British global surveillance programmes based on classified documents provided by Edward Snowden. For this work, his team won a Pulitzer Prize. Glenn Greenwald has written multiple best-selling books, including How Would a Patriot Act and No Place to Hide: Edward Snowden, the NSA, and the U.S. Surveillance State . He now hosts System Update , where he has interviewed academics, political figures, and commentators including Jeffrey Sachs, John Mearsheimer, Edward Snowden, Robert F. Kennedy Jr., and many others.
glenn-greenwald-trumps-iran-attacks-are-.subtitle: A new phase in interventionist foreign policy

the-structure-of-consciousness.speaker_desc: Karl Friston is Professor of Imaging Neuroscience at University College London and Principal Research Fellow for the Wellcome Trust. Jan Westerhoff is Professor of Buddhist Philosophy at Oxford University. He researches the philosophical aspects of the religious traditions of ancient India, and contemporary analytic metaphysics. Susan Schneider is an American philosopher and cognitive scientist, known for her work on the nature of consciousness, artificial intelligence, and the future of mind.
the-structure-of-consciousness.subtitle: Questioning our relation to reality and the self

how-the-right-won-the-culture-war.speaker_desc: Inaya Folarin Iman is a British political commentator, writer, and the founder of the Equiano Project, an initiative promoting free speech, open dialogue, and a more inclusive approach to discussions about race and identity. Recently, she has focused on challenging the dominance of identity politics in public discourse and advocating for policies rooted in shared humanity rather than divisive rhetoric. Her work at the Equiano Project emphasizes the need for critical reflection on how society addresses complex issues like racial inequality and multiculturalism. She argues for open debate on topics often constrained by political correctness, such as integration and cultural identity. She was a regular presenter on GB news and is also a regular writer for Spiked Online , the Telegraph , and the Daily Mail .
how-the-right-won-the-culture-war.subtitle: The contradictions within woke politics

atomic-dreams-and-nuclear-nightmares.speaker_desc: M. V. Ramana, physicist and Simons Chair at the University of British Columbia, is a leading critic of nuclear power. Tim Gregory is a senior nuclear chemist at the UK’s National Nuclear Laboratory and author of Going Nuclear , where he makes a passionate case for atomic power as the backbone of a sustainable future. Harvard scholar, Sheila Jasanoff, is one of the most influential voices in Science and Technology Studies, dismantling the myth that science and technology operate above politics.
atomic-dreams-and-nuclear-nightmares.subtitle: Risk, reactors and the climate

lionel-shriver.speaker_desc: Lionel Shriver is an American author and journalist best known for her 2003 novel We Need to Talk About Kevin , which won the Orange Prize for Fiction. Her work often explores controversial social and political themes with dark wit and psychological insight. A dual US-UK citizen, Shriver is also a frequent commentator on cultural issues in publications like The Spectator and The Guardian.
lionel-shriver.subtitle: The post-rational reign of mania

unelected-elites-and-the-limits-of-democ.speaker_desc: Ken Roth is an attorney, activist and author best known as the Executive Director of Human Rights Watch for nearly thirty years. Political Philosopher and Professor at Yale University, Hélène Landemore is also a Distinguished Research Fellow at Oxford’s Institute for Ethics in AI. James Bacchus is a lobal trade judge and legal scholar renowned for shaping WTO law and championing sustainable international governance. Mary Ann Sieghart hosts.
unelected-elites-and-the-limits-of-democ.subtitle: Who really holds all the power?

the-medicalisation-of-mental-illness-joa.speaker_desc: Joanna Moncrieff is a British psychiatrist and academic. She is Professor of Critical and Social Psychiatry at University College London and a leading figure in the Critical Psychiatry Network.
the-medicalisation-of-mental-illness-joa.subtitle: Why psychiatry should move past chemical imbalance

the-brain-is-not-responsible-for-conscio.speaker_desc: Àlex Gómez-Marín is a theoretical physicist and neuroscientist. He is Associate Professor at the Institute of Neuroscience, Alicante, and Director of the Pari Center in Italy.
the-brain-is-not-responsible-for-conscio.subtitle: Science’s 400-year blind spot

climate-politics-in-the-new-world-order-.speaker_desc: Mike Berners-Lee is a fellow of the Institute for Social Futures at Lancaster University and director and principal consultant of Small World Consulting.
climate-politics-in-the-new-world-order-.subtitle: Will bureaucracy kill the planet?

anxiety-and-the-souls-itch-sarah-wilson.speaker_desc: Sarah Wilson is multi - New York Times bestselling author, social philosopher and philanthropist. She edited Cosmopolitan Australia at 29 and founded the global I Quit Sugar movement.
anxiety-and-the-souls-itch-sarah-wilson.subtitle: How to find meaning in an age of collapse

rethinking-the-fundamentals-of-quantum-p.speaker_desc: Jacob Barandes is a theoretical physicist and philosopher of physics known for his work on the foundations of quantum mechanics and his proposal of “Indivisible Quantum Theory."
rethinking-the-fundamentals-of-quantum-p.subtitle: The hidden assumptions that limit our theories

beyond-truth-and-reality.speaker_desc: Slavoj Žižek is a senior researcher at the University of Ljubljana's Department of Philosophy. Hilary Lawson is a post-post modern philosopher and the author of Closure . Hosted by Güneş Taylor.
beyond-truth-and-reality.subtitle: There is no universal truth

us-and-them.speaker_desc: Thangam Debbonaire is a Labour member of the House of Lords and former MP for Bristol West. Regarded as one of the founders of the cognitive science of religion, Harvey Whitehouse is a statutory Chair in Social Anthropology at the University of Oxford. Sophie Scott-Brown is an intellectual historian with research interests in modern European political thought, Anarchism and the history of education. She is a lecturer in Philosophy at the University of East Anglia and former director at the Europaeum Institute at the University of Oxford. Rana Mitter hosts.
us-and-them.subtitle: Can belonging exist without exclusion?

the-future-of-artificial-minds.speaker_desc: Anders Sandberg is a Swedish researcher, futurist, and transhumanist renowned for his work on human enhancement and future technologies. Former NASA Chair in Astrobiology, Exploration, and Scientific Innovation, Susan Schneider, is a philosopher and cognitive scientist, specialising in consciousness and AI.
the-future-of-artificial-minds.subtitle: Can machines ever be conscious?

the-one-and-the-many.speaker_desc: Sabine Hossenfelder is a theoretical physicist and acclaimed science communicator, known for her sharp critiques of the scientific mainstream. She is also a best-selling author and YouTuber. Ivette Fuentes is a theoretical quantum physicist at the University of Southampton and Emmy Fellow at the University of Oxford. James Ladyman is a philosopher of science at the University of Bristol. He is best known for his book Every Thing Must Go, calling for a metaphysics grounded in physics and complexity science. Hosted by Jack Symes.
the-one-and-the-many.subtitle: Is the universe a seamless unity?

stories-of-unreality.speaker_desc: Martha Fiennes is an award-winning filmmaker and pioneering AI artist, known for Onegin, Chromophobia, and her AI-driven work Yugen, which has been showcased from Venice to the Serpentine Gallery. Josh Cohen established himself as an academic in American literature and critical theory, before deciding to train as a psychoanalyst. Novelist and travel writer Joanna Kavenna won the Orange Award for New Writers for her novel Inglorious . She's held the Alistair Horne Fellowship at St Antony’s College Oxford and the Harper-Wood Award at St John’s College Cambridge. Johnny Thomson hosts.
stories-of-unreality.subtitle: Breaking the realist frame

europes-second-chance-timothy-garton-ash.speaker_desc: Prominent political commentator Timothy Garton Ash is a leading Oxford Professor of European Studies and a Senior Fellow at the Hoover Institute.
europes-second-chance-timothy-garton-ash.subtitle: How the continent can come back from the brink

the-chains-of-freedom.speaker_desc: Daniel Markovits is Professor of Law at Yale Law School and the Founding Director of the Center for the Study of Private Law. He is the author of the bestselling book The Meritocracy Trap Elizabeth Anderson is Professor of Public Philosophy, Politics and Economics at the University of Michigan. She specialises in moral, social and political philosophy, as well as feminist theory and the philosophy of economics and the social sciences. Yaron Brook is an entrepreneur, writer, activist, and political scientist. He is currently chairman of the board of the Ayn Rand Institute and host of the Yaron Brook Show. Isabel Hilton hosts.
the-chains-of-freedom.subtitle: Is freedom a universal good?

sex-society-and-erotic-capital.speaker_desc: Catherine Hakim is a social scientist and author specializing in women’s employment and gender issues, with over 100 papers and numerous books published.
sex-society-and-erotic-capital.subtitle: The social effects of sex appeal

how-to-build-real-relationships-with-jor.speaker_desc: Jordan Stephens is a British musician, writer, performer, and mental health advocate best known as one half of the hip-hop duo Rizzle Kicks, who rose to fame in the early 2010s with hits like “Down with the Trumpets” and “Mama Do the Hump.” Since then, Stephens has emerged as a multi-talented creative voice, using his platform to explore issues of identity, masculinity, race, fame, and mental health through music, television, and activism.
how-to-build-real-relationships-with-jor.subtitle: Leading with love

the-state-of-modern-conservatism-jesse-n.speaker_desc: Jesse Norman is a British politician, author, and academic. Serving as the Member of Parliament for Hereford and South Herefordshire since 2010, he has held various ministerial roles and currently serves as Shadow Leader of the House of Commons. Sir Vernon Bogdanor is a British political scientist and constitutional expert. He is a research professor of Contemporary British History at King's College London.
the-state-of-modern-conservatism-jesse-n.subtitle: Division in the ranks

the-battle-of-the-big-bang-phil-halper.speaker_desc: Phil Halper is a fellow of the Royal Astronomical Society and science popularizer. He is the creator of the popular YouTube series Before the Big Bang.
the-battle-of-the-big-bang-phil-halper.subtitle: Is the Big Bang a creation myth?

neighbours-before-strangers.speaker_desc: Alain de Botton is the best-selling philosopher and founder of The School of Life, an organisation dedicated to developing emotional intelligence through philosophy, psychotherapy, and culture. Seyla Benhabib is one of the most influential political philosophers of her generation and is the author of At the Margins of the Modern State . Tommy Curry is the Personal Chair of Africana Philosophy and Black Male Studies at the University of Edinburgh, renowned for his critical scholarship on the intersection of race, gender, and power. Alex O'Connor hosts.
neighbours-before-strangers.subtitle: Should everyone be treated equally?

the-return-of-sparta.speaker_desc: Sarah Wilson is a multi-New York Times and Amazon bestselling author, social philosopher, international keynote speaker, minimalist, and philanthropist. She edited Cosmopolitan magazine Australia at 29, founded the global ‘I Quit Sugar’ movement and hosted MasterChef Australia – the most-watched TV series in the nation’s history. Anders Sandberg is a Swedish researcher, futurist, and transhumanist renowned for his work on human enhancement and future technologies. He served as a senior research fellow at the Future of Humanity Institute and the Oxford Martin School at the University of Oxford. His research encompasses societal and ethical implications of emerging technologies, cognitive enhancement, and existential risks. David Pearce is a British philosopher best known for his advocacy of the abolitionist project, the ethical vision of using advanced science and technology to eliminate suffering in all sentient life. A co-founder of the World Transhumanist Association (now Humanity+), he authored The Hedonistic Imperative, a manifesto that argues for the use of genetic engineering, nanotechnology, and neuroscience to replace the biological substrates of pain with gradients of intelligent bliss.
the-return-of-sparta.subtitle: Could Ancient Greece guide our future?

how-brains-construct-reality-with-karl-f.speaker_desc: Karl Friston is a neuroscientist and theoretical neurobiologist best known for developing the Free Energy Principle, a unifying framework for understanding brain function, perception, and action. He is Professor of Imaging Neuroscience at University College London and a leading figure in computational psychiatry, cognitive neuroscience, and the philosophy of mind.
how-brains-construct-reality-with-karl-f.subtitle: Uncertainty shapes consciousness

living-without-limits.speaker_desc: Anna Lembke is a groundbreaking psychiatrist and addiction medicine expert at Stanford. She is author of Drug Dealer MD and most recently Dopamine Nation which argues that too much pleasure in the short time leads to pain in the long-term. Federico Campagna is a leading philosopher, metaphysician and expert on Nihilism. His book Technic and Magic: The Reconstruction of Reality argues for a completely different conception of the structure of reality. Barry Schwartz is an American psychologist and the Dorwin Cartwright Emeritus Professor of Social Theory and Social Action at Swarthmore College. He is author of several famous books including Why We Work and The Paradox of Choice. He argues for a moderated and balanced approach to life. Hosted by Güneş Taylor.
living-without-limits.subtitle: Is it a mistake to pursue short-term pleasure?

cracking-the-code-for-thought.speaker_desc: Roger Penrose is a world-renowned mathematician, mathematical physicist, philosopher of science and Nobel Laureate in Physics. He is best known for his work on general relativity and black holes, and for his public appearances popularising physics and philosophy. Max Tegmark is a Swedish‑American MIT physicist and cosmologist, and president and co-founder of the Future of Life Institute. He is known for championing the Mathematical Universe Hypothesis and pioneering the notion of consciousness as a state of matter. Sabrina Gonzalez Pasterski is a theoretical physicist at the Perimeter Institute whose work on space, time, and gravity has been cited by Stephen Hawking. She now leads efforts to encode the universe as a hologram, a bold step toward uniting quantum theory with general relativity.
cracking-the-code-for-thought.subtitle: Could consciousness be computational?

the-strange-search-for-knowledge-in-the-.speaker_desc: Steve Fuller is Professor of Sociology at the University of Warwick, and a founding figure in the field of social epistemology. He has authored dozens of books, including Post-Truth: Knowledge as a Power Game .
the-strange-search-for-knowledge-in-the-.subtitle: Optimism in the post-truth age

alenka-zupancic.speaker_desc: Alenka Zupančič is a Slovenian philosopher whose work focuses on psychoanalysis and continental philosophy. A prominent member of the Ljubljana School of Psychoanalysis, Zupančič is best known for her rigorous and often provocative readings of Freud and Lacan, filtered through the lens of German Idealism and Nietzsche.
alenka-zupancic.subtitle: The truth we ignore

jeremy-corbyn-arrogance-in-office-comes-.speaker_desc: Jeremy Corbyn is a British politician and current independent MP who served as the Labour party's leader from 2015 to 2020.
jeremy-corbyn-arrogance-in-office-comes-.subtitle: How the far right is manipulating the public

making-europe-great-again.speaker_desc: Timothy Garton Ash is a leading British historian, political writer, and one of Europe’s most compelling chroniclers of modern transformation. He is Professor of European Studies at the University of Oxford and a Senior Fellow at the Hoover Institution, Stanford University. Nathalie Tocci is one of Europe’s most influential and thoughtful strategists on international affairs, known for her pivotal role in shaping European foreign policy and advancing a nuanced approach to diplomacy, security, and global cooperation. She currently serves as the director of the Instituto Affari Internazionali. Johnny Mercer is a former Veterans Minister, Conservative MP and British Army Captain who served three tours of duty in Afghanistan. He used his time in Parliament to aid veterans in their access to healthcare, mental health support and housing, as well as fighting the criminal prosecution of soldiers in Iraq and Northern Ireland. Yascha Mounk is a political scientist and public intellectual known for his analysis of the threats to liberal democracy. A Professor at Johns Hopkins and founder of the online magazine Persuasion, he argues that identity-based ideologies can undermine democratic norms and social cohesion. Hosted by Isabel Hilton.
making-europe-great-again.subtitle: Can the continent emerge from America's shadow?

reclaiming-work.speaker_desc: Elizabeth Anderson is Arthur F. Thurnau Professor and John Dewey Distinguished University Professor of Philosophy and Women’s Studies at the University of Michigan and author of Hijacked .
reclaiming-work.subtitle: Designing work for dignity, not control

after-science-has-spoken.speaker_desc: Genia Schönbaumsfeld is Professor of Philosophy at the University of Southampton. Her work ranges across epistemology and the philosophy of religion, with a distinctive focus on the ethical and existential dimensions of thought in Ludwig Wittgenstein and Søren Kierkegaard.
after-science-has-spoken.subtitle: Wittgenstein, God, and the limits of language

nicola-sturgeon-has-a-lot-to-be-frank-ab.speaker_desc: Nicola Sturgeon, is the former First Minister of Scotland and former leader of the Scottish National Party (SNP) and remains a prominent political figure, despite stepping down from her leadership roles in 2023. She has been at the forefront of Scottish politics since 2004 when she first ran to be leader of the SNP.
nicola-sturgeon-has-a-lot-to-be-frank-ab.subtitle: The former First Minister's hopes for Scotland

nuclear-is-not-the-solution-m-v-ramana.speaker_desc: M.V. Ramana is the Simons Chair in Disarmament, Global and Human Security and Professor at the School of Public Policy and Global Affairs, University of British Columbia, Vancouver, Canada.
nuclear-is-not-the-solution-m-v-ramana.subtitle: M.V. Ramana on nuclear’s false promise

freedom-and-fate.speaker_desc: Paul Bloom is a Canadian-American psychologist, bestselling author, and celebrated speaker. He is Professor Emeritus at Yale and a professor at the University of Toronto. Bloom’s work explores human nature, morality, and pleasure. Joining us from California is Robert Sapolsky. Sapolsky is a distinguished neuroscientist, primatologist, and author, best known for his research on stress and its impact on behaviour and health. He is also a professor at Stanford University. Lucy Allais is a philosopher at Johns Hopkins University and the University of the Witwatersrand, renowned for her work on Immanuel Kant. Her writing spans ethics, metaphysics, and political philosophy. Hilary Lawson hosts.
freedom-and-fate.subtitle: Choice, blame, and the brain

the-life-and-philosophy-of-neil-kinnock.speaker_desc: Neil Kinnock is a Welsh politician who was Leader of the Opposition and Leader of the Labour Party from 1983 to 1992. He undertook the monumental task of modernising the party after its crushing electoral defeat, battling internal factionalism, confronting Militant entryism, and laying the groundwork for the eventual rise of New Labour.
the-life-and-philosophy-of-neil-kinnock.subtitle: The making of a socialist

the-undoing-of-biologys-central-dogma-wi.speaker_desc: Philip Ball is a renowned British science writer and former editor of Nature, celebrated for uncovering the poetic wonder within hard science. In over thirty books, including Critical Mass (Royal Society Winton Prize), Beyond Weird (Physics World Book of the Year), and How Life Works, he explores how science is deeply entwined with culture, politics, and imagination.
the-undoing-of-biologys-central-dogma-wi.subtitle: How life actually works

the-great-innovation-race.speaker_desc: Daniel A. Bell is a prominent political theorist known for his work on Chinese political thought and comparative political philosophy. He currently serves as Chair of Political Theory at the University of Hong Kong's faculty of Law. Previously, he served as Dean of the School of Political Science and Public Administration at Shandong University and as a professor at Tsinghua University Anu Bradford is a leading scholar on the EU’s regulatory power and a sought-after commentator on the European Union, global economy, and digital regulation. She is the Henry L. Moses Professor of Law and International Organisation at Columbia University and was previously at Chicago Law School. Jason Furman is a prominent American economist known for his extensive contributions to public policy, academia, and economic analysis. He currently serves as the Aetna Professor of the Practice of Economic Policy at Harvard University. He served as the Chairman of the Council of Economic Advisers (CEA) under President Barack Obama from August 2013 to January 2017. In this role, he acted as a principal economic advisor to the President. Roger Hearing hosts.
the-great-innovation-race.subtitle: Is democracy really necessary?

the-end-of-materialism-with-alex-gomez-m.speaker_desc: Àlex Gómez-Marín is a Theoretical physicist and neuroscientist, Associate Professor at the Instituto de Neurociencias of Alicante in Spain, and director of the Pari Center in Italy.
the-end-of-materialism-with-alex-gomez-m.subtitle: Science beyond dogma

the-search-for-higher-states-of-consciou.speaker_desc: Jessica Frazier is a professor of theology and religion at Trinity College, Oxford, as well as a Fellow of the Oxford Centre for Hindu studies. During her academic career, she has explored key philosophical themes across various cultures cultures, ranging from Indian concepts of Being to 20th century phenomenology. In addition, Frazier is the founding editor of the 'Journal of Hindu Studies' and a frequent contributor to BBC radio.
the-search-for-higher-states-of-consciou.subtitle: How to become more than who you are

we-must-exploit-tribalism-as-a-force-for.speaker_desc: Regarded as one of the founders of the cognitive science of religion, Harvey Whitehouse is a statutory Chair in Social Anthropology at the University of Oxford.
we-must-exploit-tribalism-as-a-force-for.subtitle: Harvey Whitehouse on our evolutionary roots

lies-damned-lies-and-misinformation.speaker_desc: Aaron Maté is an independent journalist, author, and commentator known for his analysis of international relations and U.S. foreign policy. Writer-in-chief at The Draft, Phil Collins has held positions at almost every major newspaper in the country. Inaya Folarin Iman is a British political commentator, writer, and the founder of the Equiano Project. Myriam François is a trailblazing journalist, filmmaker and writer. She is also the founder of MPWR productions. Hosted by Sophie Scott-Brown.
lies-damned-lies-and-misinformation.subtitle: Can democracy still share facts?

erotic-power-and-the-new-sexual-revoluti.speaker_desc: Catherine Hakim is a social scientist and author specialising in women’s employment and gender issues, with over 100 papers and numerous books published. Minna Salami is a writer and thinker who blends feminism, philosophy, and politics, and is the author of Can Feminism Be African? Farha Khalidi is a feminist cultural commentator, TikToker and OnlyFans model with 1.7 million followers on TikTok.
erotic-power-and-the-new-sexual-revoluti.subtitle: Sex, power, and the internet

skeletons-in-the-academys-closet.speaker_desc: Tommy J. Curry is Professor of Philosophy at the University of Edinburgh, holding a Personal Chair in Africana Philosophy and Black Male Studies. He is the author of several influential works, including The Man-Not: Race, Class, Genre, and the Dilemmas of Black Manhood, which won an American Book Award in 2018, and Another White Man’s Burden: Josiah Royce’s Quest for a Philosophy of Racial Empire.
skeletons-in-the-academys-closet.subtitle: The hypocrisy behind universalism

the-self-and-the-world.speaker_desc: Slavoj Žižek is one of the most famous philosophers in the world and is the author of more than 50 books, including most recently at the time of the debate Zero Point . Alenka Zupančič is a leading Lacanian philosopher and social theorist. She is a professor at The European Graduate School and at the University of Nova Gorica. Joining from America, Carlo Rovelli is a leading theoretical physicist, the author of several best-selling books, and a founding figure in the field of quantum gravity. His recent book, Reality Is Not What It Seem s, has ethical implications for the nature of the self and personal identity. Jack Symes hosts.
the-self-and-the-world.subtitle: The relationship between mind and matter

reimagining-the-right-richard-tice.speaker_desc: Richard Tice is a British businessman and politician, best known for his leadership of Reform UK, formerly the Brexit Party prior to Nigel Farage. A prominent advocate for Brexit, Tice played a key role in the campaign for the UK's departure from the European Union and was elected to Parliament in 2024. Since founding the Brexit party in 2018, Tice has been at the heart of a political movement that has upended politics and reached out to many dissatisfied voters.
reimagining-the-right-richard-tice.subtitle: Farage's deputy on the future of Reform UK

zoltan-istvan-on-transhumanism.speaker_desc: Zoltan Istvan is a transhumanist, futurist, entrepreneur, and former US Presidential candidate. With his bestselling book The Transhumanist Wager, and speeches at institutions like the World Bank, World Economic Forum, and the UK Parliament, Zoltan Istvan has spearheaded the effort to transform transhumanism into a thriving worldwide phenomenon.
zoltan-istvan-on-transhumanism.subtitle: How we could soon transcend death

the-worlds-most-dangerous-idea.speaker_desc: Zoltan Istvan is a transhumanist, futurist, entrepreneur, and former US Presidential candidate. He has spearheaded the effort to transform transhumanism into a thriving worldwide phenomenon. Àlex Gómez-Marín is a theoretical physicist, neuroscientist, and director of the Pari Center in Italy. He explores the nature of consciousness, human experience, and the limitations of mainstream science. Susan Schneider is an American philosopher and cognitive scientist, known for her work on the nature of consciousness, artificial intelligence, and the future of mind. She is the founding director of the Center for the Future Mind at Florida Atlantic University. Adam Goldstein is the Co-Founder, Chairman, and Head of Research at Softmax, a company that seeks to engineer AI that scales through coordinated diversity rather than imposed control. Hosted by Jay Shapiro.
the-worlds-most-dangerous-idea.subtitle: Is technology rewriting what it means to be human?

gravity-reveals-the-quantum-world-raphae.speaker_desc: Raphael Bousso is a theoretical physicist at the University of California, Berkeley, who studies how gravity, space, and quantum physics fit together. He is known for discovering powerful limits on how much information the universe can store, using ideas from black holes and cosmology to reveal how reality works at its most fundamental level.
gravity-reveals-the-quantum-world-raphae.subtitle: The conspiracy that ties gravity to the quantum

the-good-the-bad-the-transgressive.speaker_desc: Rowan Williams, the 104th Archbishop of Canterbury, is a highly acclaimed theologian, writer, and pastor. Josh Cohen established himself as an academic in American literature and critical theory, before deciding to train as a psychoanalyst. Catherine Liu is a professor of Film and Media Studies at the University of California, Irvine, renowned for her incisive critiques of contemporary cultural and political dynamics. Hosted by Barry C. Smith.
the-good-the-bad-the-transgressive.subtitle: Is transgression vital to a healthy culture?

aaron-mate-contradictions-of-liberalism.speaker_desc: Aaron Maté is an independent journalist, author, and commentator known for his analysis of international relations, U.S. foreign policy, and media coverage of geopolitics.
aaron-mate-contradictions-of-liberalism.subtitle: Russia, Israel, US hegemony, and more

the-rise-of-technofeudalism.speaker_desc: Yanis Varoufakis is a leading critic of the economic establishment. He was the former Finance Minister of Greece, and is a professor, bestselling author, and current chair of the Democracy in Europe Movement 2025.
the-rise-of-technofeudalism.subtitle: The new feudal lords of tech

in-defence-of-irrationality.speaker_desc: Paul Bloom is Professor Emeritus of Psychology and Cognitive Science at Yale University and Professor of Psychology at the University of Toronto. His research explores the psychology of morality, identity, and pleasure.
in-defence-of-irrationality.subtitle: An interview on moral psychology

the-substance-of-the-world.speaker_desc: Tim Maudlin is a celebrated philosopher of science, renowned for his work on the foundations of physics and metaphysics. He is also an author and professor at New York University. Sabine Hossenfelder is a theoretical physicist and acclaimed science communicator, known for her sharp critiques of the scientific mainstream. She is also a best-selling author and YouTuber. Hilary Lawson is a philosopher and renowned critic of philosophical realism. His main work, Closure: A Story of Everything, has been described as ‘the first non-realist metaphysics’. Sabrina Gonzalez Pasterski is a theoretical physicist at the Perimeter Institute whose work on space, time, and gravity has been cited by Stephen Hawking. She now leads research on uniting quantum theory with general relativity through celestial holography. Güneş Taylor hosts.
the-substance-of-the-world.subtitle: Particles, waves, or something else entirely?

the-philosophy-of-performance-michelle-t.speaker_desc: Michelle Terry is an Olivier-Award-winning actor and writer, and the Artistic Director of Shakespeare’s Globe. Renowned for her innovative interpretations of Shakespeare, she is a leading figure in contemporary British theatre. Dr Myriam François is a journalist, filmmaker and writer. She also founded MPWR productions, an independent documentary production company which seeks to platform minority voices.
the-philosophy-of-performance-michelle-t.subtitle: How performance shapes identity and truth

the-life-and-philosophy-of-nicola-sturge.speaker_desc: Nicola Sturgeon, is the former First Minister of Scotland and former leader of the Scottish National Party (SNP) and remains a prominent political figure, despite stepping down from her leadership roles in 2023. She has been at the forefront of Scottish politics since 2004 when she first ran to be leader of the SNP. Hosted by journalist and author of The Authority Gap Mary Ann Sieghart.
the-life-and-philosophy-of-nicola-sturge.subtitle: The philosophy of the greatest threat to the UK

the-blueprint-for-life.speaker_desc: Stuart Kauffman is a theoretical biologist whose work on self-organisation and complexity reshapes our understanding of life’s origins. He is Emeritus professor at the University of Pennsylvania and a MacArthur Fellow.Joanna Moncrieff is Professor of Critical and Social Psychiatry at UCL and a consultant psychiatrist with the NHS. She is a leading critic of the “chemical imbalance” theory of depression.Denis Noble is a world-renowned biologist and pioneer of Systems Biology, Professor Emeritus, and co-Director of Computational Physiology at Oxford. Hosted by Philip Ball.
the-blueprint-for-life.subtitle: Was the Human Genome Project oversold?

foreign-policy-isnt-guided-by-morality.speaker_desc: Sir Simon Jenkins is a British Author, newspaper columnist and editor. He was an editor of the Evening Standard from 1976 to 1978 and of the Times from 1990 to 1992.
foreign-policy-isnt-guided-by-morality.subtitle: An interview with Simon Jenkins

journalism-in-the-age-of-post-truth.speaker_desc: Cathy Newman is the first female main presenter of Channel 4 News. She spent over a decade in Fleet Street, latterly with the Financial Times. Since joining Channel 4 News in 2006 she has broadcast a string of scoops, including allegations of violent abuse against the British barrister John Smyth, sexual harassment allegations against the Liberal Democrat Peer Lord Rennard, and an investigation into a British sex offender, Simon Harris, which saw him jailed for 17 years. She was also the only broadcast journalist to travel with Angelina Jolie and the foreign secretary William Hague to the Congo as part of a campaign against sexual violence.
journalism-in-the-age-of-post-truth.subtitle: Cathy Newman discusses journalism and truth

the-future-of-european-thought.speaker_desc: Associate Professor of Philosophy at Northeastern University London, Christoph Schuringa is known for his works on German philosophy and is Editor of the Hegel Bulletin.Genia Schönbaumsfeld is Professor of Philosophy at the University of Southampton and the author of several books – most recently, Wittgenstein on Religious Belief. Babette Babich is Professor of Philosophy at Fordham University and the editor of the journal New Nietzsche Studies. Hosted by Danielle Sands.
the-future-of-european-thought.subtitle: Is the analytic-continental divide over?

the-life-and-philosophy-of-john-gray.speaker_desc: John Gray is one of Britain’s leading philosophers and public intellectuals, renowned for his penetrating critiques of liberalism, humanism, and the Enlightenment faith in progress. A former professor at the London School of Economics, Gray is the author of numerous acclaimed works including Straw Dogs, The Silence of Animals, and The New Leviathans . His writing challenges our most cherished assumptions about morality, politics, and what it means to be human. Andy Owen is a writer and former British Army officer whose work explores morality, leadership, and the human experience in conflict.
the-life-and-philosophy-of-john-gray.subtitle: Dismantling the myths of progress

the-end-of-free-trade-and-the-new-world-.speaker_desc: Ingrid Harvold Kvangraven is a Senior Lecturer in International Development at King’s College London and critic of economic orthodoxy. Mark Littlewood is an economist, politician and former director of the Institute of Economic Affairs. He is a regular fixture of UK political media defending free market and laissez-faire approaches to managing the economy. Policy and Analysis correspondent at BBC Verify, Ben Chu was formerly the Economics Editor of Newsnight and is a non-fiction economics author. Greg Hands is a former Conservative Minister who most recently was the Minister of State for Trade Policy under Rishi Sunak. Isabel Woodford hosts.
the-end-of-free-trade-and-the-new-world-.subtitle: Questioning free trade and Trump's tariffs

copying-consciousness-the-future-of-mind.speaker_desc: Anders Sandberg is a senior fellow at the Future of Humanity Institute at Oxford University and is best known for his work on human enhancement and emerging technologies.
copying-consciousness-the-future-of-mind.subtitle: The science behind brain simulation

lost-in-thought.speaker_desc: Steven Pinker is a cognitive psychologist, linguist, and bestselling author known for his work on language and human nature. A Professor of Psychology at Harvard University, his books, including Enlightenment Now and The Better Angels of Our Nature , have made him one of the world’s most influential public thinkers. Hilary Lawson is a philosopher and leading critic of realism. His major work, Closure: A Story of Everything , sets out a radical non-realist metaphysics that challenges traditional views of truth and the world. Barbara Tversky is Emerita Professor of Psychology at Stanford and Professor of Psychology at Columbia Teachers College. A pioneer of embodied cognition, she has written extensively on memory, spatial thinking, and creativity, exploring how our minds shape the world we perceive. Sophie Scott-Brown hosts.
lost-in-thought.subtitle: Unravelling the ties between thought and language

the-west-vs-the-islamic-world-with-ali-a.speaker_desc: Ali Abdul-Amir Allawi was Iraq's Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister. An Iraqi politician and scholar, from May 2020 to August 2022, he ran as Iraq's Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister. He resigned from the post of finance minister on August 16, 2022 due to the deteriorating political situation in Iraq. Interviewed by Alasdair Craig
the-west-vs-the-islamic-world-with-ali-a.subtitle: Former Iraqi finance minister on global capitalism

how-words-warp-reality.speaker_desc: Nick Enfield is Professor of Linguistics at the University of Sydney and Director of the Sydney Centre for Language Research.
how-words-warp-reality.subtitle: How language decieves us

the-age-of-the-universe.speaker_desc: Roger Penrose is a world-renowned mathematician, mathematical physicist, philosopher of science and Nobel Laureate in Physics. Claudia de Rham is a theoretical physicist at Imperial College London, working at the interface between gravity, cosmology and particle physics, and in 2020 won the Blavatnik Award for Young Scientists for her ground-breaking work. Karen Crowther is a Professor at the University of Oslo, specialising in the philosophy of science and physics. Hosted by Güneş Taylor.
the-age-of-the-universe.subtitle: Are we wrong about the beginning?

the-metaphysics-of-quantum-mechanics-aly.speaker_desc: Alyssa Ney is Professor and Chair of Metaphysics in the Faculty of Philosophy, Philosophy of Science, and Religious Studies at LMU Munich.
the-metaphysics-of-quantum-mechanics-aly.subtitle: Insights from the quantum world

girl-power.speaker_desc: Clare Chambers is Professor of Political Philosophy at Jesus College Cambridge, and the author of Intact and Against Marriage: An Egalitarian Defence of the Marriage-Free State. Aaron Bastani is the co-founder of Novara Media, described as 'the slickest of the guerrilla news and opinion operations that have sprung up in Britain' by the Guardian. Susie Orbach is a psychotherapist, psychoanalyst, and social critic, who came to prominence with the book Fat Is a Feminist Issue, and was therapist to Diana, Princess of Wales. Barry Smith hosts.
girl-power.subtitle: What is modern feminism?

the-future-of-the-right.speaker_desc: Sohrab Ahmari is a celebrated journalist and cultural critic and co-founder of Compact magazine and author of Tyranny, Inc. Gawain Towler is a British political strategist, journalist, and long-standing figure in the Eurosceptic movement. Best known for his work in party communications and media strategy, he currently serves on the governing board of Reform UK. Rachel Maclean is a former UK minister, Conservative peer, and is Director of Strategy to the Leader of the Opposition. Mark Littlewood is a libertarian economist and media commentator known for his provocative advocacy on free markets, regulation, and public policy. He’s currently director of the think tank Popular Conservatism. Hosted by Roger Hearing.
the-future-of-the-right.subtitle: Courage, populism, and the new right

lessons-for-the-left.speaker_desc: Diane Abbott is a British politician and a Member of Parliament for Hackney North and Stoke Newington since first being elected in 1987. She served in the Shadow Cabinet of Jeremy Corbyn as Shadow Home Secretary from 2016 to 2020 and is an advisor to the Privy Council. She was the first black woman elected to parliament and is the longest-serving black MP.
lessons-for-the-left.subtitle: The left’s crisis of connection

norman-ohler-on-hitler-and-the-nazis-lit.speaker_desc: Norman Ohler is an author, novelist and screenwriter, best known for his popular history book 'Blitzed: Drugs in the Third Reich'. His most recent book, 'Tripped: Nazi Germany, The CIA and the Dawn of the Psychedelic Age', explores the US government's research into LSD as a mind control drug following their discovery of Nazi experimentation during the Holocaust.
norman-ohler-on-hitler-and-the-nazis-lit.subtitle: How the Nazis started the psychedelic drug war

in-search-of-nothing.speaker_desc: David Deutsch is a pioneering theoretical physicist best known as the founding father of quantum computation and as a key figure and advocate for the many-worlds interpretation of quantum mechanics. Amanda Gefter is a celebrated science writer specialising in fundamental physics, cosmology, cognitive science and philosophy. Lee Smolin is a renowned theoretical physicist known for his work on loop quantum gravity, cosmological natural selection, and, more broadly, in the philosophy of physics. Hosted by Matt O’Dowd.
in-search-of-nothing.subtitle: Is the idea of 'nothing' impossible?

the-biology-of-conflict.speaker_desc: Massimo Pigliucci is an Italian-American philosopher and biologist specialising in evolutionary biology and the philosophy of science. His recent work focuses on Stoicism. John Dupre is Professor of Philosophy and Director of Egenis, The Centre for the Study of Life Sciences, at the University of Exeter. He has wide-ranging interests in the philosophy of biology and naturalistic, empirically grounded metaphysics. Maria Balaet is a leading psychedelics researcher and neuroscientist in the Department of Neuroimaging at King’s College London.
the-biology-of-conflict.subtitle: How evolution shapes our divisions

hilary-lawson-on-god-the-world-and-what-.speaker_desc: Hilary Lawson is a philosopher, renowned critic of philosophical realism, and editorial director of the Institute of Art and Ideas. His main work, 'Closure: A Story of Everything', has been described as "the first non-realist metaphysics". Robert Lawrence Kuhn is the co-creator, executive producer, writer, and host of Closer To Truth, the PBS/public television series on cosmos, life, mind, and meaning that presents leading scientists, philosophers, and creative thinkers discussing the fundamental questions of existence. You can find out more about Closer to Truth HERE .
hilary-lawson-on-god-the-world-and-what-.subtitle: Robert Kuhn interview with Hilary Lawson Part Two

the-holy-grail-of-economics.speaker_desc: Daniela Gabor is a Professor of Economics at SOAS. She has been published in The Guardian, Financial Times and Jacobin. Matthew Lynn is a financial columnist and author. He writes for The Daily Telegraph, The Spectator, and MoneyWeek, and he has worked as a columnist for The Sunday Times and Bloomberg. Cahal Moran is a behavioural economist and Visiting Fellow at the London School of Economics and Political Science and the creator of the YouTube channel Unlearning Economics. Hosted by the BBC's Roger Hearing.
the-holy-grail-of-economics.subtitle: How do we get growth?

why-we-worship-without-knowing-it-with-a.speaker_desc: Alain de Botton is a philosopher, author, and founder of The School of Life. Known for works such as The Consolations of Philosophy, Religion for Atheists, and The Course of Love, his writing explores how ancient wisdom can guide us through the complexities of modern existence. Alex O’Connor, known online as The Cosmic Skeptic, is a philosopher, podcaster, and broadcaster whose work investigates the boundaries between reason, faith, and moral life.
why-we-worship-without-knowing-it-with-a.subtitle: Religion, meaning, and the sacred in a secular age

tim-maudlin-why-imaginary-numbers-are-ce.speaker_desc: One of the world's foremost philosophers of physics, Tim Maudlin is Professor of Philosophy at NYU and Founder and Director of the John Bell Institute for the Foundations of Physics. He is a member of the "Foundational Questions Institute" of the Académie Internationale de Philosophie des Sciences and is the recipient of a Guggenheim Fellowship. Maudlin is the author of 'The Metaphysics Within Physics', 'Truth and Paradox: Solving the Riddles' and 'Quantum Non-Locality and Relativity'.
tim-maudlin-why-imaginary-numbers-are-ce.subtitle: Demystifying the "i" in quantum mechanics

a-world-without-morality.speaker_desc: Famed international relations professor John Mearsheimer, former Executive Director of Human Rights Watch Kenneth Roth, and Chief Foreign Correspondent of The Sunday Times, Christina Lamb, debate a world without morality. Hosted by Mary Ann Sieghart.
a-world-without-morality.subtitle: Can foreign policy be moral?

the-delusions-of-the-digital-age.speaker_desc: Lionel Shriver is an award winning author and provocative voice in contemporary literature, unafraid to tackle contentious subjects with unflinching honesty. Her acclaimed novel, We Need to Talk About Kevin, delves into the complexities of motherhood and moral responsibility, which earned her the Orange Prize for Fiction in 2005.
the-delusions-of-the-digital-age.subtitle: We need to talk about mania

the-philosopher-behind-jd-vance.speaker_desc: Curtis Yarvin, described as "The Philosopher Behind J.D. Vance," argues that democracy is a failed experiment and should be replaced by monarchy. Yarvin has profoundly influenced American politics, counting among his readers Steve Bannon, Peter Thiel, and Vice-President J.D. Vance. Alastair Campbell is one of the most important voices in modern British politics. Best known for his role as chief spokesman and strategist under Tony Blair, Campbell now works predominantly as a writer and broadcaster, remaining a leading thinker on the centre-left. He is also the co-host of multi award winning podcast, The Rest is Politics.
the-philosopher-behind-jd-vance.subtitle: Monarchies, democracy and the price of freedom

dimensions-of-the-unknown.speaker_desc: Karen Crowther is a Professor at the University of Oslo, specialising in the philosophy of science and physics. Raphael Bousso is Professor and The Chancellor's Chair in Physics at UC Berkeley, where he studies quantum information, gravity, black holes, and cosmology. Dean Rickles is Professor of History and Philosophy of Modern Physics at the University of Sydney, Australia, where he is also a director of the Sydney Centre for Time. Hosted by Robert Lawrence Kuhn.
dimensions-of-the-unknown.subtitle: Are dimensions real or just a mathematical tool?

massive-gravity-and-the-dark-energy-enig.speaker_desc: Claudia de Rham is a leading Professor of Theoretical Physics at Imperial College, London. Claudia is recognised for her revitilisation of and research into massive gravity theory, for which she won the Blavatnik Award for Young Scientists.
massive-gravity-and-the-dark-energy-enig.subtitle: The status quo in physics is wrong

technology-and-freedom.speaker_desc: Yanis Varoufakis is a world-renowned economist, academic, and politician. His latest book is Technofedualism: What Killed Capitalism. Timothy Nguyen is a leading AI researcher at Google DeepMind and the host of the podcast The Cartesian Café . Janne Teller is a critically-acclaimed writer of novels, essays, and short stories. Teller’s work includes existential themes on a grand scale, which often spark controversial debate. Hosted by Shini Somara.
technology-and-freedom.subtitle: Should we socialise big tech?

hilary-lawson-on-reality-and-the-illusio.speaker_desc: Hilary Lawson is a philosopher, renowned critic of philosophical realism, and editorial director of the Institute of Art and Ideas. His main work, 'Closure: A Story of Everything', has been described as "the first non-realist metaphysics". Robert Lawrence Kuhn is the co-creator, executive producer, writer, and host of Closer To Truth, the PBS/public television series on cosmos, life, mind, and meaning that presents leading scientists, philosophers, and creative thinkers discussing the fundamental questions of existence. You can find out more about Closer to Truth HERE .
hilary-lawson-on-reality-and-the-illusio.subtitle: Robert Kuhn interview with Hilary Lawson Part One

migrant-forms.speaker_desc: Rowan Williams former Archbishop of Canterbury is a theologian, poet, and author known for his wide-ranging work on Christian theology, ethics, and the relationship between faith and society. Natalya Din-Kariuki is an Associate Professor at the Department of English and Comparative Literary Studies at the University of Warwick. She is also affiliated with the Centre for the Study of the Renaissance and the Global History and Culture. Issam Kourbaj was born in Syria and trained at the Institute of Fine Arts in Damascus. His work has been widely exhibited and collected. His Dark Water, Burning World is in the permanent collection of the Pergamon Museum and the British Museum. Subha Mukherji is Professor of Early Modern Literature and Culture. Since her influential book on Renaissance law and drama she has been working on a project titled Crossroads of Knowledge in Early Modern England.
migrant-forms.subtitle: How art becomes politics

why-youre-probably-getting-poorer.speaker_desc: Cahal Moran is a behavioural economist, host of the YouTube channel "Unlearning Economics", and author of the books, "The Econocracy" and "Why We’re Getting Poorer". Cahal is also a Visiting Fellow at the London School of Economics and Political Science.
why-youre-probably-getting-poorer.subtitle: The rot at the heart of the economy

the-story-of-the-universe.speaker_desc: John Dupré is a celebrated Professor of Philosophy and Director of Egenis, The Centre for the Study of Life Sciences, at the University of Exeter. He has made important contributions to the philosophy of biology, as well as naturalistic, empirically-grounded metaphysics. Alex Rosenberg is a novelist and philosopher, renowned for his work in the philosophy of biology and the philosophy of economics. He is one of the most prominent defenders of physical reductionism, and his radical stances have earned him the moniker, "The Mad Dog Naturalist." Ivette Fuentes is a Professor of Quantum Physics at the University of Southampton and Emmy Fellow at Keble College, University of Oxford. Her work considers fundamental quantum mechanics and she is a close collaborator with Roger Penrose.
the-story-of-the-universe.subtitle: The changing face of fundamental science

slavoj-zizek-on-the-madness-of-reality.speaker_desc: Slavoj Žižek is a world-renowned philosopher, cultural critic and public intellectual. Foreign Policy named Žižek a Top 100 Global Thinker "for giving voice to an era of absurdity”. Interviewed by Charlie Barnett.
slavoj-zizek-on-the-madness-of-reality.subtitle: The philosophy of quantum, sex, AI and happiness

the-importance-of-giving-up.speaker_desc: Adam Phillips is a psychoanalytic psychotherapist and essayist. He has been the general editor of the Penguin Modern Classics translations of Sigmund Freud. Hosted by Claudia Canavan the Head of New Features at the New Scientist. She writes on mind, drugs, hormones, and emotions, with a focus on emerging health trends.
the-importance-of-giving-up.subtitle: Resisting the tyranny of completion

the-language-of-the-unconscious.speaker_desc: Alenka Zupančič is a Lacanian philosopher and social theorist. She is a professor at The European Graduate School and at the University of Nova Gorica.
the-language-of-the-unconscious.subtitle: The unconscious is like a large language model

chatgpt-doesnt-understand-anything-with-.speaker_desc: Michael Wooldridge is the Ashall Professor of the Foundations of Artificial Intelligence in the Department of Computer Science at the University of Oxford, and a Senior Research Fellow at Hertford College.
chatgpt-doesnt-understand-anything-with-.subtitle: The ethics and future of AI

a-world-that-cares.speaker_desc: Catherine Liu is a professor of Film and Media Studies at UC Irvine. Her work critiques cultural politics, political economy, and the professional managerial class. Her books include Virtue Hoarders and The American Idyll. Tim Jackson is an ecological economist and writer. He has been at the forefront of international debates on sustainability and has worked closely with the UK Government, the UN, the European Commission, and numerous NGOs. David Goodhart is the former editor of Prospect and Director of the London based think tank Demos. Author of The British Dream: successes and failures of post-war immigration. Barry C Smith is a professor of philosophy and directs the Institute of Philosophy at the University of London’s School of Advanced Study.
a-world-that-cares.subtitle: Building an economy that values care

beliefism-paul-dolan.speaker_desc: Paul Dolan is a British behavioural scientist and the Professor of Behavioural Science at the London School of Economics. His research and writing focus on how pleasure and purpose weave together in everyday life, arguing that happiness lies in what we do and attend to, not the grand narratives we tell ourselves. Dolan is the author of three widely acclaimed books: 'Happiness by Design', 'Happy Ever After', and 'Beliefism'. He combines rigorous academic analysis with accessible advice grounded in behavioural science.
beliefism-paul-dolan.subtitle: A cure for the age of political extremism

democracy-gender-and-the-future-of-polit.speaker_desc: Catherine Mayer is a writer, activist, and the co-founder and president of the Women's Equality Party. Nicola Sturgeon is the former First Minister of Scotland and leader of the Scottish National Party (SNP), the first woman to hold both titles. John Burn-Murdoch is a columnist and the chief data reporter for the Financial Times, where he writes the weekly 'Data Points' column. David Goodhart is a journalist, author, and policy analyst. He founded Prospect magazine and later directed the think tank Demos. His books, including 'The Road to Somewhere', examine social divisions, work, and identity.
democracy-gender-and-the-future-of-polit.subtitle: Populism, polarisation, and gender

the-collapse-of-the-wave-function.speaker_desc: Jacob Barandes is a Harvard University theoretical physicist and philosopher of science. His research explores the foundations of quantum theory, spacetime, and the nature of scientific explanation. Alyssa Ney is a philosopher at LMU Munich whose work reshapes how we think about reality through the lens of quantum mechanics. Specializing in the metaphysics of physics, she challenges deeply held assumptions about the nature of the universe and our place within it. Roger Penrose is a world-renowned mathematician, mathematical physicist, philosopher of science and Nobel Laureate in Physics.
the-collapse-of-the-wave-function.subtitle: Searching for reality in the quantum world

the-philosophy-of-reform-with-richard-ti.speaker_desc: Richard Tice is a businessman and politician. Since 2024, he has served as member of parliament for Boston and Skegness, as well as deputy leader of Reform UK, having previously been the chairman of the party from 2019 to 2021 and again briefly in 2024. Interviewed by Hilary Lawson. Hilary Lawson is a post-postmodern philosopher and a renowned critic of philosophical realism.
the-philosophy-of-reform-with-richard-ti.subtitle: Can modern populism escape the horrors of the past

the-rise-and-fall-of-identity-politics.speaker_desc: James Schneider is a journalist and political organiser currently serving as Communications Director for Progressive International. He previously served as Spokesperson and Head of Strategic Communications for Jeremy Corbyn. Myriam François is a trailblazing journalist, filmmaker and writer. She is a former columnist at the New Statesman and a familiar face on the BBC, Channel 4, and Al Jazeera. Thangam Debbonaire was Labour MP for Bristol West and a senior member of Keir Starmer’s Shadow Cabinet. She now advises on culture, tech, and global policy, focusing on issues like migration, identity, and democracy. Hosted by Roger Hearing.
the-rise-and-fall-of-identity-politics.subtitle: Identity, billionaires, and the future of the Left

out-of-our-minds.speaker_desc: Maria Balaet is a leading psychedelics researcher and neuroscientist in the Department of Neuroimaging at King’s College London. Joanna Moncrieff is Professor of Critical and Social Psychiatry at University College London, and a consultant psychiatrist for the NHS. Norman Ohler is an award-winning novelist and investigative journalist, best known for Blitzed: Drugs in the Third Reich, an explosive account of the Nazi regime’s covert use of psychedelics and stimulants.
out-of-our-minds.subtitle: Drugs, culture, and the shaping of human thought

organisms-are-processes-not-things-with-.speaker_desc: Wahida Khandker is a senior lecturer in philosophy at Manchester Metropolitan University. Her research focuses on intersections between process and thought, particularly the work of Henri Bergson, and the philosophy of biology. Khandker currently also serves as co-chair of the Society for European Philosophy. Khandker is the author of two monographs, Philosophy, Animality, and the Life Sciences (2014) and Process Metaphysics and Mutative Life (2020).
organisms-are-processes-not-things-with-.subtitle: A revolution in our understanding of nature

draining-the-swamp.speaker_desc: Richard Tice is a British businessman and politician, currently serving as the Deputy Leader of Reform UK and MP for Boston and Skegness. Sherelle Jacobs is Assistant Comment Editor at The Daily Telegraph, known for her bold columns on politics, culture, and identity. A former foreign correspondent, she brings a global lens to Britain’s evolving conservatism. David Goodhart is a British journalist and author, best known as the founder and former editor of Prospect magazine. His book The British Dream argues that high immigration can undermine national solidarity and social cohesion.
draining-the-swamp.subtitle: Does the right want a small state?

the-struggle-for-the-good-life.speaker_desc: Massimo Pigliucci is a renowned philosopher and professor at the City College of New York. He is the author of several books, including, 'How to be a Stoic' and 'Beyond Stoicism'. A former co-host of the Rationally Speaking Podcast and a self-proclaimed sceptic, Pigliucci is a champion of Enlightenment notions of reason and rationality.
the-struggle-for-the-good-life.subtitle: Massimo Pigliucci on a life worth living

why-politics-should-be-the-focus-of-femi.speaker_desc: Catherine Mayer is a writer, activist and the co-founder and President of the Women's Equality Party. She started her career in journalism at The Economist. She then went on to be FOCUS's London-based correspondent. She later joined TIME as a senior editor, becoming the London Bureau Chief, the Europe Editor and, finally, Editor at Large. She was the founding Executive Director of the think tank Datum Future and has also co-founded the Primadonna Festival, which debuted in 2019. She is the author of Attack of the 50ft Women, Amortality: The Pleasures and Perils of Living Agelessly and Charles: The Heart of A King, a political biography of the King Charles that made headlines across the world in 2015. Her upcoming works include TIME/LIFE, her first novel, and Send Them Victorious: Royal Women, Their Battles and Why We Should Care.
why-politics-should-be-the-focus-of-femi.subtitle: How to be an effective modern feminist

einsteins-biggest-blunder-with-claudia-d.speaker_desc: Claudia de Rham is a theoretical physicist based at Imperial College London, who works on cutting-edge research at the interface of gravity, cosmology and particle physics. In 2020 she won the Blavatnik Award for Young Scientists for revitalizing the theory of massive gravity.
einsteins-biggest-blunder-with-claudia-d.subtitle: Why the graviton should be given mass

the-future-of-entanglement.speaker_desc: Jacob Barandes is a Harvard University theoretical physicist and philosopher of science. His research explores the foundations of quantum theory, spacetime, and the nature of scientific explanation. Ivette Fuentes is a physicist at the University of Southampton and Emmy Fellow at the University of Oxford. Her work and previous collaborations with Roger Penrose considers fundamental quantum mechanics, quantum optics and their interplay with general relativity. Tim Maudlin is a celebrated philosopher of science, renowned for his work on the foundations of physics and metaphysics. He is also an author and professor at New York University.
the-future-of-entanglement.subtitle: What is Einstein’s ‘spooky action at a distance'?

the-new-world-order-and-the-fight-for-de.speaker_desc: Malcolm Rifkind is the former UK Foreign Secretary. He was one of only five ministers to serve throughout the whole Prime Ministerships of both Margaret Thatcher and John Major. In 1997, he was knighted in recognition of his public service. Rifkind also served as Chairman of the Standards & Privileges Committee from 2009 to 2010, and as the UK’s representative to the Eminent Persons Group from 2010 to 2011. He also served as chairman of the Intelligence and Security Committee from 2010 to 2015. Roger Hearing hosts.
the-new-world-order-and-the-fight-for-de.subtitle: The state of the world with Malcolm Rifkind

after-postmodernism.speaker_desc: Robin van den Akker is Senior Lecturer in the Philosophy of Culture. He is a leading scholar of Metamodernism and founding editor of Notes on Metamodernism. Abby Innes is an Associate Professor in Political Economy at the LSE. Hilary Lawson is a philosopher best known for his theory 'Closure', a post-analytic return to metaphysics, and an outspoken critic of philosophical realism.
after-postmodernism.subtitle: Escaping certainty and chaos

trouble-with-temptation.speaker_desc: Paul Dolan is Professor of Behavioural Science at the LSE. His main research interests are human behaviour and happiness, and the relationships between them, particularly as they apply to policy. Jordan Stephens is a musician and author. He is one-half of the chart-topping hip-hop duo Rizzle Kicks, and recently released his first novel, 'Avoidance, Drugs, Heartbreak and Dogs'.
trouble-with-temptation.subtitle: Finding meaning in heartbreak

the-unconscious-mind.speaker_desc: Josh Cohen is a distinguished academic in American literature and critical theory, as well as a trained psychoanalyst. Barbara Tversky is an active Emerita Professor of Psychology at Stanford and Professor of Psychology at Columbia Teachers College. Edward Harcourt is a philosopher at the University of Oxford, where he researches ethics, the philosophy of mind, and Wittgenstein.
the-unconscious-mind.subtitle: Was Freud's unconscious a delusion?

stranger-than-fiction.speaker_desc: Mary Ann Sieghart is a distinguished journalist and the author of The Authority Gap: Why Women Are Still Taken Less Seriously Than Men, and What We Can Do About It. Catherine Mayer is a writer, activist and the co-founder and was the President of the Women's Equality Party. She started her career in journalism, writing for The Economist, FOCUS and TIME.
stranger-than-fiction.subtitle: Sci-fi politics and feminism

the-untold-power-of-small-states-with-ar.speaker_desc: Armen Vardani Sarkissian is an Armenian politician, physicist, investor, businessman, and computer scientist who served as the 4th president of Armenia from 2018 to 2022. He also served as Prime Minister of Armenia from 1996 to 1997. He was the first president of post-Soviet Armenia born in former Armenian SSR.
the-untold-power-of-small-states-with-ar.subtitle: The theory of quantum politics from a physicist tu

hacking-our-way-out-of-the-universe.speaker_desc: Roman Vladimirovich Yampolskiy is a Latvian computer scientist at the University of Louisville, known for his work on behavioral biometrics, security of cyberworlds, and artificial intelligence safety. He holds a PhD from the University at Buffalo (2008). He is currently the director of Cyber Security Laboratory in the department of Computer Engineering and Computer Science at the Speed School of Engineering. Yampolskiy is an author of some 100 publications, including numerous books.
hacking-our-way-out-of-the-universe.subtitle: How to hack the simulation

reason-replication-and-reality-with-john.speaker_desc: John Ioannidis is a Greek-American physician, scientist and writer. He is a Professor of Medicine, Epidemiology and Population Health, and Biomedical Data Science at Stanford University. His research focuses on evidence-based medicine, clinical research and the study of scientific research itself. Not only has Ioannidis served on the editorial board of over twenty scientific journals, but his 2005 essay "Why Most Published Research Findings Are False" was the most-viewed article in the history of the Public Library of Science, with over 3 million views.
reason-replication-and-reality-with-john.subtitle: Why Most Published Research Findings Are False

the-politics-of-populism.speaker_desc: Lionel Shriver is a bestselling author and outspoken commentator known for tackling incendiary themes in both fiction and public debate. Her novel We Need to Talk About Kevin won the Orange Prize for Fiction in 2005. Aaron Maté is an independent journalist, author, and commentator known for his incisive analysis of international relations, U.S. foreign policy, and media coverage of geopolitics. Jesse Norman is a distinguished British politician, author, and academic. Serving as the MP for Hereford and South Herefordshire since 2010, he currently is Shadow Leader of the House of Commons. Hosted by Roger Hearing.
the-politics-of-populism.subtitle: Challenging the liberal order or reviving a dark p

the-diagnosis-delusion.speaker_desc: Karsten Juhl Jørgensen is a leading medical researcher and professor at the University of Southern Denmark, known for challenging the idea that more tests mean better care. He’s a bold voice exposing the hidden harms of overdiagnosis and overscreening. Gina Rippon, Emeritus Professor of Cognitive Neuroimaging, is a trailblazing neuroscientist debunking brain-gender myths. Author of The Gendered Brain and The Lost Girls of Autism, she uses cutting-edge science to expose long-ignored truths. Alastair Santhouse is a leading consultant psychiatrist and former President of the Psychiatry Section at the Royal Society. Author of No More Normal, he is a sharp critic of the over-diagnosis trend in mental health today. Hosted by Claudia Canavan.
the-diagnosis-delusion.subtitle: Is there an overdiagnosis epidemic?

the-seduction-of-advertising-barry-c-smi.speaker_desc: Barry C Smith is a professor of philosophy and directs the Institute of Philosophy at the University of London’s School of Advanced Study. Founding director of the Centre for the Study of Senses, Barry C Smith has created a platform for collaborative research between philosophers, psychologists and neuroscientists.
the-seduction-of-advertising-barry-c-smi.subtitle: How companies use philosophy to control your taste

kith-and-kin.speaker_desc: Harvey Whitehouse is a Chair in Social Anthropology at the University of Oxford. He is the author of 'Inheritance: The Evolutionary Origins of the Modern World'. David Goodhart is a journalist, author, and policy analyst. He founded Prospect magazine and later directed the think tank Demos. Sophie Scott-Brown is an intellectual historian with research interests in Anarchism and modern European political thought. She is a Research Fellow at the University of St Andrews. Matthew Taylor hosts.
kith-and-kin.subtitle: How to make more babies

yanis-varoufakis-on-the-end-of-capitalis.speaker_desc: Yanis Varoufakis is a leading critic of the economic establishment. He was the former Finance Minister of Greece, a professor, bestselling author, and current chair of the Democracy in Europe Movement 2025. Interviewed by the host of The Why Curve podcast and BBC presenter Roger Hearing?
yanis-varoufakis-on-the-end-of-capitalis.subtitle: Technofeudalism and the scourge of big tech

a-landscape-of-consciousness.speaker_desc: Robert Lawrence Kuhn is the co-creator, executive producer, writer, and host of Closer To Truth, the PBS/public television series on cosmos, life, mind, and meaning that presents leading scientists, philosophers, and creative thinkers discussing the fundamental questions of existence. Kuhn has published over 30 books and is also a commentator on the BBC, CNN, CCTV, and Bloomberg as a trusted expert on China. Most recently, and what we’re discussing today, Robert released a paper, 'A landscape of consciousness', in which he chronicled over 200 theories of consciousness.
a-landscape-of-consciousness.subtitle: Collecting every theory of consciousness we have

the-taiwan-tripwire.speaker_desc: Malcolm Rifkind is a renowned British politician who served in the cabinets of both Margaret Thatcher and John Major, most famously in the roles of Foreign and Defense Secretary. Isabel Hilton is a renowned international relations expert, journalist and broadcaster. She is the founder of China Dialogue. Bill Hayton is a distinguished former BBC journalist and Chatham House associate fellow. He is the author of four books on Asia. Hosted by Mary Ann Sieghart.
the-taiwan-tripwire.subtitle: Is war over Taiwan inevitable?

the-limits-of-absence.speaker_desc: Join philosopher Peter van Inwagen as he explores the metaphysics of 'nothing' in modern physics.
the-limits-of-absence.subtitle: The metaphysics of "nothing"

indian-philosophy-and-the-search-for-uni.speaker_desc: Jessica Frazier is a professor of theology and religion at Trinity College, Oxford, as well as a Fellow of the Oxford Centre for Hindu studies. During her academic career, she has explored key philosophical themes across various cultures, ranging from Indian concepts of Being to 20th century phenomenology. In addition, Frazier is the founding editor of the 'Journal of Hindu Studies' and a frequent contributor to BBC radio.
indian-philosophy-and-the-search-for-uni.subtitle: Why we are all one

the-hope-you-find-at-rock-bottom.speaker_desc: Slavoj Žižek is a world-renowned philosopher, cultural critic and public intellectual. Foreign Policy named Žižek a Top 100 Global Thinker "for giving voice to an era of absurdity”.
the-hope-you-find-at-rock-bottom.subtitle: Freedom at the edge of collapse

the-worst-prediction-in-the-history-of-s.speaker_desc: Claudia de Rham is a theoretical physicist based at Imperial College London, who works on cutting-edge research at the interface of gravity, cosmology, and particle physics. In 2020, she won the Blavatnik Award for Young Scientists for revitalizing the theory of massive gravity. Raphael Bousso is Professor and The Chancellor's Chair in Physics at UC Berkeley, where he researches theoretical cosmology and quantum gravity. He was elected Fellow of the American Physical Society "for fundamental discoveries in the field of quantum cosmology." Bjørn Ekeberg is a philosopher of science whose work focuses on the limits of scientific knowledge, challenging the standard model of cosmology by probing some of the biggest inconsistencies and mysteries in science today. Jacob Barandes hosts.
the-worst-prediction-in-the-history-of-s.subtitle: A century-old cosmological crisis

how-neoliberalism-broke-economics-with-a.speaker_desc: Abby Innes is Associate Professor of Political Economy at the European Institute, London School of Economics. Her research focuses on state theory, post-communist transitions, and the political economy of the UK. She is the author of Late Soviet Britain: Why Materialist Utopias Fail. Interviewed by Harry Carlisle.
how-neoliberalism-broke-economics-with-a.subtitle: The delusions of late Soviet Britain

psychedelics-nazi-germany-and-the-cia.speaker_desc: Norman Ohler is an award-winning novelist and investigative journalist, best known for 'Blitzed: Drugs in the Third Reich', an explosive account of the Nazi regime’s covert use of psychedelics and stimulants.
psychedelics-nazi-germany-and-the-cia.subtitle: The true story of LSD

unmasking-the-mind.speaker_desc: Nick Brown, a Cambridge-trained engineer, began studying psychology in his 50s and is known for debunking the "positivity ratio." His critiques have appeared in The Guardian, Science, and more. John Ioannidis, a Stanford professor, is known for his work on evidence-based medicine and research integrity. His 2005 essay Why Most Published Research Findings Are False has over 3 million views. David Yeager, a UT Austin psychology professor, studies brief interventions that shape adolescent behavior. Featured in major media, he authored 10 to 25 and teaches the MasterClass The Power of Mindset. Hosted by the editor of the New Humanist, Niki Seth-Smith
unmasking-the-mind.subtitle: Is psychology in a replicability crisis?

after-the-west.speaker_desc: Former Finance Minister of Greece and bestselling author Yanis Varoufakis, political commentator and host of The Young Turks, Cenk Uygur, former Chief Election Commissioner of India S.Y. Quraishi, historian, columnist, and author Zoe Strimpel, and others clash over the future of global power. Hosted by philosopher Hilary Lawson.
after-the-west.subtitle: Who will remake the world?

the-philosophical-failure-of-evolutionar.speaker_desc: Subrena Smith is a Professor of Philosophy at the University of New Hampshire. She works at the intersection of biology and psychology, where she focuses on topics about human behaviour. Interviewed by Nour Khairi.
the-philosophical-failure-of-evolutionar.subtitle: Why we will never understand the human mind

physics-without-numbers.speaker_desc: Tim Maudlin is a celebrated philosopher of science, renowned for his work on the foundations of physics and metaphysics. He is also an author and professor at New York University.
physics-without-numbers.subtitle: Why we should do physics without numbers

human-nature-and-the-possibility-of-utop.speaker_desc: Paul Bloom is a Canadian-American psychologist, bestselling author and celebrated speaker. He is the Brooks and Suzanne Ragen Professor Emeritus of psychology and cognitive science at Yale University and Professor of Psychology at the University of Toronto.
human-nature-and-the-possibility-of-utop.subtitle: True utopia is impossible

crisis-in-the-academy.speaker_desc: Yaron Brook is a political scientist, and chairman of the Ayn Rand Institute. He’s a bestselling author and the host of The Yaron Brook Show. Catherine Liu is a Professor of Film and Media Studies at the University of California, Irvine. She’s the author of Virtue Hoarders: The Case against the Professional Managerial Class Eric Kaufmann is Professor of Politics at the University of Buckingham. He’s the author of Taboo and Whiteshift: Immigration, Populism and the Future of White Majorities. Jay Shapiro hosts.
crisis-in-the-academy.subtitle: The end of the woke university

consciousness-in-the-clouds.speaker_desc: Nadine Dijkstra is a Senior Research Fellow at the Wellcome Centre for Human Neuroimaging at UCL and leads the Imagine Reality Lab. Her research focuses on computational and neural mechanisms of mental imagery. Roman Yampolskiy is a professor and computer scientist at the University of Louisville who specialises in artificial intelligence, AI safety, digital forensics and behavioural biometrics. Anders Sandberg is a Swedish researcher, futurist, and transhumanist renowned for his work on human enhancement and future technologies. Massimo Pigliucci is an Italian-American philosopher and biologist specialising in evolutionary biology and the philosophy of science. His recent work focuses on Stoicism. Hosted by mechanical engineer, media broadcaster, producer and author, Shini Somara.
consciousness-in-the-clouds.subtitle: Can we upload our minds to the cloud?

the-russia-hoax.speaker_desc: Aaron Maté is an independent journalist, author, and commentator known for his analysis of international relations, U.S. foreign policy, and media coverage of geopolitics. He has contributed to various outlets, including The Nation, RealClearPolitics, and Grayzone News, where he serves as a senior writer.
the-russia-hoax.subtitle: Aaron Maté on how Russiagate fueled war in Ukraine

the-case-for-radical-feminism-with-finn-.subtitle: On patriarchy and meaning of gender

the-mind-body-problem-and-animal-conscio.speaker_desc: Peter Godfrey-Smith is a philosopher of science and a leading thinker on the evolution of consciousness and animal minds. He is a professor at the University of Sydney and the author of several acclaimed books, including Other Minds: The Octopus, the Sea, and the Deep Origins of Consciousness and Metazoa: Animal Life and the Birth of the Mind . His work combines philosophy, biology, and firsthand experience with marine animals to explore how subjective experience arises in the natural world. Through his research and writing, Godfrey-Smith offers a compelling naturalistic account of the mind that bridges science and philosophy.
the-mind-body-problem-and-animal-conscio.subtitle: What animal consciousness reveals about the mind

the-us-dollar-and-the-future-of-the-worl.speaker_desc: David McWilliams is a prominent Irish economist, author, broadcaster, and public intellectual. He has worked for the Irish Central Bank and famously predicted the 2008 financial crisis. He is also a columnist, author, festival organiser and podcaster. Janne Teller was formerly a UN macroeconomist specialising in developing economies. She has since become a bestselling author of novels, essays, and short stories. Hosted by Harvard's Rana Mitter.
the-us-dollar-and-the-future-of-the-worl.subtitle: Will the dollar remain the dominant currency?

white-holes-are-a-mathematical-fantasy.speaker_desc: Daniel Sudarsky is a Professor of Theoretical Physics at the National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM) and a Professor at the John Bell Institute for the Foundations of Physics.
white-holes-are-a-mathematical-fantasy.subtitle: Einstein's mythical white hole solutions

the-normal-and-the-abnormal.speaker_desc: Rose Cartwright is a writer for the Netflix hit show 3 Body Problem, she is a mental health advocate and author of a book on mental health, The Maps We Carry.
