Frank Tallis is a multi-award winning clinical psychologist and author, his latest book is The Act of Living: What the Great Psychologists Can Teach Us About Surviving Discontent in an Age of Anxiety. Dinesh Bhugra is the former President of the World Psychiatric Association and Professor of Mental Health and Cultural Diversity at King's College London. Bessel van der Kolk is a psychiatrist and expert in the field of trauma therapy. He is the author of the bestselling book The Body Keeps The Score. Hosted by Barry Smith.
the-normal-and-the-abnormal.subtitle: Who defines what's normal?

the-theory-of-everything-is-a-mirage.speaker_desc: Jo Dunkley is a distinguished astrophysicist and Professor of Physics at Princeton University, working on major international projects including the Atacama Cosmology Telescope and Simons Observatory, which focus on measuring the earliest observable light in the universe. Her contributions have been recognised with numerous accolades, such as the Maxwell Medal and the Rosalind Franklin Award and she has recently been elected a fellow of the Royal Society. Dunkley works on uncovering evidence of "inflation" in our early universe and furthering our understanding of the big "tensions" in cosmology and dark matter.
the-theory-of-everything-is-a-mirage.subtitle: Why we can never know it all

the-new-surveillance-culture.speaker_desc: Judith Donath is a writer, designer and artist whose work focuses on the co-evolution of technology and society. She has published numerous articles about social media, AI, ethics and anonymity, and is the author of The Social Machine: Designs for Living Online (MIT Press). As the former director of the MIT Media Lab's Sociable Media Group, she and her students designed innovative interfaces for on-line communities; their art projects examining the future of identity, privacy and mediated life have been exhibited in museums and galleries worldwide. Currently, she is a faculty fellow at Harvard's Berkman Klein Center and is writing a book about technology, trust and deception.
the-new-surveillance-culture.subtitle: The end of trust

the-rules-of-war.speaker_desc: Jeremy Corbyn is a British politician and current independent MP who served as the Labour party's leader from 2015 to 2020. Bronwen Maddox is the Director and Chief Executive of Chatham House.Yanis Varoufakis is a world-renowned economist, academic, and politician who rose to international prominence in 2015 as Greece's Minister of Finance. Malcolm Rifkind is a renowned British politician who served in the cabinets of both Margaret Thatcher and John Major, most famously in the roles of Foreign and Defence Secretary. Hosted by Mary Ann Sieghart.
the-rules-of-war.subtitle: What's the point of international law?

the-fantasies-of-descartes-antonio-damas.speaker_desc: Antonio Damasio is an award-winning neuroscientist known for his pioneering work on emotions, intuitions and the biological origins of consciousness. He is the author of several books including Descartes' Error and The Strange Order of Things. His most recent book Feeling & Knowing: Making Minds Conscious explores the origin and evolution of consciousness.
the-fantasies-of-descartes-antonio-damas.subtitle: Antonio Damasio's radical theory of consciousness

the-politics-of-beauty.speaker_desc: Jessica DeFino is an award-winning reporter and beauty culture critic. Her work sheds light on the negative impacts of the beauty industry. Simon May is a Visiting Professor of Philosophy at King's College London. May's most recent book, Love: A New Understanding of an Ancient Emotion, proposes a wholly new theory on the nature of love. Janne Teller is a critically-acclaimed writer of novels, essays, and short stories. Teller’s work explores existential themes and ethical questions of life and civilization. Sophie Scott-Brown hosts.
the-politics-of-beauty.subtitle: Are aesthetic choices always tyrannical?

david-deutsch-on-the-foundations-of-real.speaker_desc: David Deutsch is a theoretical physicist best known as the founding father of quantum computation and as a key figure and advocate for the many-worlds interpretation of quantum mechanics. Deutsch is a Visiting Professor of physics at the Centre for Quantum Computation and the Clarendon Laboratory, Oxford University. Interviewed by Charlie Barnett, Senior Producer at the IAI.
david-deutsch-on-the-foundations-of-real.subtitle: The many-worlds interpretation is all there is

the-equality-dream.speaker_desc: John Bercow is one of the most recognisable and iconoclastic figures in British politics. As Speaker of the House of Commons from 2009 to 2019, his distinctive bellow for order spanned the tenure of four Prime Ministers and a decade of political turmoil. Tommy J. Curry holds a Personal Chair in Africana philosophy and Black Male studies at the University of Edinburgh. Vicky Pryce is a British economist and a former Joint Head of the United Kingdom's Government Economic Service. Isabel Hilton hosts
the-equality-dream.subtitle: The hidden costs of the equality revolution

the-two-party-system-is-over-with-carla-.speaker_desc: Carla Denyer is co-leader of the Green Party of England and Wales, selected along with Adrian Ramsay in October 2021. Carla is the MP for Bristol Central.
the-two-party-system-is-over-with-carla-.subtitle: The philosophy of green politics

competition-destroys-collective-intellig.speaker_desc: Liv Boeree is an educator and researcher specializing in the intersection of game theory, technology and risk. She is also one of the UK's most successful poker players, winning multiple championship titles during her professional career. In 2014 she co-founded the charity movement Raising for Effective Giving, and today continues her work in the area as an ambassador for Longview Philanthropy. Liv also hosts the Win-Win Podcast.
competition-destroys-collective-intellig.subtitle: An interview with Liv Boeree

imagining-the-unimaginable.speaker_desc: Film-maker and Director Martha Fiennes, professor of developmental psychopathology Simon Baron-Cohen, and award-winning novelist Joanna Kavenna, debate whether the imagination is limited. Hosted by Myriam François.
imagining-the-unimaginable.subtitle: Is the imagination unlimited?

truth-science-and-reality.speaker_desc: John Ioannidis is a physician, scientist and writer as well as a professor at Stanford University. He is the author of Why Most Published Research Findings Are False. Hilary Lawson is a philosopher and long-standing critic of realism, best known for his theory of closure. Hosted by Imperial College London Material Physicist Jess Wade.
truth-science-and-reality.subtitle: The replication crisis vs truth

the-quantum-unknown.speaker_desc: Sabine Hossenfelder is a ground-breaking physicist, the creator of the YouTube channel "Science without the gobbledygook", and a New York Times best-selling author. Matt O'Dowd is an astrophysicist and the host of PBS Space Time. He is also Professor of Physics and Astronomy at City University of New York.
the-quantum-unknown.subtitle: Sabine Hossenfelder speaks with Matt O’Dowd

journey-in-search-of-a-destination.speaker_desc: Parisian philosopher Sandra Laugier, Nietzschian philosopher Babette Babich, clinical psychologist Frank Tallis, and author of Rethinking Existentialism Jonathan Webber debate the purpose of life. Hosted by Jack Symes.
journey-in-search-of-a-destination.subtitle: Are we mistaken to seek out purpose?

the-making-and-unmaking-of-humanity.speaker_desc: Regarded as one of the founders of the cognitive science of religion, Harvey Whitehouse is a statutory Chair in Social Anthropology at the University of Oxford.
the-making-and-unmaking-of-humanity.subtitle: How evolution might destroy us

what-is-wrong-with-history-and-how-to-ch.speaker_desc: Philippa Gregory CBE is a renowned writer and author of historical fiction. She is best known for The Other Boleyn Girl (2001), which was adapted into two films and in 2002 won the Romantic Novel of the Year Award from the Romantic Novelists' Association.
what-is-wrong-with-history-and-how-to-ch.subtitle: How women have been left out of history

the-future-of-money-with-gary-stevenson.speaker_desc: Gary Stevenson is a British economist, former financial trader, and YouTuber known for his economic analysis and activism against economic inequality. Interviewed by Abby Innes, an Associate Professor of Political Economy in the European Institute at the LSE. She is the author of Czechoslovakia: The Short Goodbye (Yale University Press, 2001) and Late Soviet Britain: Why Materialist Utopias Fail (Cambridge University Press, 2023).
the-future-of-money-with-gary-stevenson.subtitle: Gary Stevenson vs the financial elite

the-forgotten-crimes-of-war-with-christi.speaker_desc: Christina Lamb is Chief Foreign Correspondent for The Times and Sunday Times. She is one of Britain’s leading foreign correspondents and a bestselling author.
the-forgotten-crimes-of-war-with-christi.subtitle: The Times Foreign Correspondent on modern conflict

the-good-the-bad-and-the-beautiful.speaker_desc: Babette Babich is a philosopher of technology and science. She is a Professor of Philosophy at Fordham University, New York City. Ankhi Mukherjee is a Professor of English and World Literatures at Oxford University. She is the author of several books and is currently writing A Very Short Introduction to Postcolonial Literature, forthcoming with Oxford University Press. Paul Ernest is Emeritus professor of the philosophy of mathematics education at the University of Exeter. He is best known for his work on philosophical aspects of mathematics education and his contributions to developing a social constructivist philosophy of mathematics. Sarah Wilson is a multi-New York Times and Amazon bestselling author, social philosopher and philanthropist. She edited Cosmopolitan magazine Australia at 29 and founded the global I Quit Sugar movement. Hosted by British mechanical engineer, media broadcaster, producer, and author, Shini Somara
the-good-the-bad-and-the-beautiful.subtitle: How central should beauty be to our values?

capitalism-and-the-end-of-innovation.speaker_desc: Ali Abdul-Amir Allawi was Iraq's Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister. An Iraqi politician and scholar, he served in those positions from May 2020 to August 2022. He resigned from the post of finance minister on August 16, 2022 due to the deteriorating political situation in Iraq.
capitalism-and-the-end-of-innovation.subtitle: Iraq's Finance Minister on how to develop properly

the-mindful-body-with-ellen-langer.speaker_desc: Ellen Langer is Professor of Psychology at Harvard University and the author of The Mindful Body. Among other honours, she is the recipient of three distinguished scientist awards, a Guggenheim Fellowship, and the Liberty Science Genius Award. She is widely known as the mother of mindfulness.
the-mindful-body-with-ellen-langer.subtitle: Exploring embodied experience

medicine-magic-misunderstanding.speaker_desc: Author of the highly influential paper, 'Why Most Published Research Findings are False', John Ioannidis, award-winning neuroscientist and feminist, Gina Rippon, and psychiatrist and groundbreaking author of 'The Body Keeps The Score', Bessel van der Kolk, debate whether we truly know what health and illness are. Hosted by Claudia Canavan.
medicine-magic-misunderstanding.subtitle: Does modern medicine really understand disease?

the-essential-philosophy-of-fun.speaker_desc: Journalist and filmmaker Myriam François, author of Philosophy in a Meaningless Life James Tartaglia, and the mind behind the Substack GIRLS , Freya India, debate the philosophy of fun. Hosted by Güneş Taylor.
the-essential-philosophy-of-fun.subtitle: Have we lost out on the best part of life?

francis-fukuyama-on-why-he-was-surprised.speaker_desc: Francis Fukuyama is an American political scientist, political economist, and international relations scholar. He is most famous for his work The End of History and the Last Man which argues that liberal democracy and free-market capitalism are the final stages of humanity's political evolution.
francis-fukuyama-on-why-he-was-surprised.subtitle: The new global order

the-misunderstood-side-of-mental-health.speaker_desc: Rose Cartwright is a trailblazing screenwriter, author, and mental health advocate. She is the writer of the Netflix hit show 3 Body Problem, and is also widely known for her 2016 memoir Pure, which detailed her experiences living with obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD). Beyond her writing, Cartwright is an outspoken voice raising awareness about OCD and challenging the stigma surrounding it. She is also the co-founder of the mental health non-profit Made of Millions.
the-misunderstood-side-of-mental-health.subtitle: In conversation with Rose Cartwright

from-baghdad-to-british-parliament.speaker_desc: Nadhim Zahawi is a British politician who served in various ministerial positions under Prime Ministers Theresa May, Boris Johnson, Liz Truss, and Rishi Sunak from 2018 to 2023. He most recently served as Chairman of the Conservative Party and Minister without Portfolio from 25 October 2022 until January 2023. As a member of the Conservative Party, he was Member of Parliament for Stratford-on-Avon from 2010 to 2024.
from-baghdad-to-british-parliament.subtitle: The life and politics of Nadhim Zahawi

rupert-sheldrake-in-conversation-with-hi.speaker_desc: Rupert Sheldrake is an English scientist whose research into parapsychology and evolution led to the theory of morphic resonance, expounded in the book A New Science of Life. The theory posits that "memory is inherent in nature" which makes it possible for "telepathy-type interconnections between organisms." Hilary Lawson is a philosopher best known for his theory 'Closure', a post-analytic return to metaphysics, and an outspoken critic of philosophical realism. He is Editorial Director of the IAI.
rupert-sheldrake-in-conversation-with-hi.subtitle: The unspoken dogmas of science

why-more-is-less.speaker_desc: Barry Schwartz is an American psychologist and the Dorwin Cartwright Emeritus Professor of Social Theory and Social Action at Swarthmore College. He is author of several famous books including Why We Work and The Paradox of Choice. Schwartz is famous for his insight that too much choice paradoxically limits freedom.
why-more-is-less.subtitle: In conversation with Barry Schwartz

white-holes-fact-or-fantasy.speaker_desc: Carlo Rovelli is a leading theoretical physicist and the author of 'White Holes'. Laura Mersini-Houghton is a pre-eminent physicist at the University of North Carolina and the author of 'Before The Big Bang: The origin of the universe and what lies beyond'. Roger Penrose is a world-renowned mathematical physicist and philosopher of science. He was awarded the Nobel Prize in 2020 for his work on black holes. Robert Lawrence Kuhn hosts.
white-holes-fact-or-fantasy.subtitle: Can we go beyond the horizon of the universe?

the-psychology-behind-the-culture-wars.speaker_desc: Andrew Gold is a YouTuber and former BBC Presenter who writes about the culture wars and cultish ideologies. He is the author of The Psychology of Secrets and creator of the Heretics YouTube Channel.
the-psychology-behind-the-culture-wars.subtitle: The origin of wokeness

having-it-all.speaker_desc: Aaron Bastani is the co-founder of Novara Media. He is the author of Fully Automated Luxury Communism and an upcoming book on the aging crisis. Claire Provost is an investigative journalist and co-founder and co-director of the non-profit Institute for Journalism and Social Change. Vicky Pryce is an economist and the Chief Economic Advisor and Board Member at the Centre for Economics and Business Research. She is the former Joint Head of the UK's Government Economic Service. Roger Hearing presents the BBC World Service's Business Matters and World Business Report. He formerly presented Bloomberg Radio and BBC Radio 4's The World Tonight.
having-it-all.subtitle: Can women really have it all?

therapy-psychedlics-and-why-the-body-kee.speaker_desc: Bessel van der Kolk is one of the world’s leading experts on trauma. A pioneering psychiatrist and author of the groundbreaking bestseller The Body Keeps the Score, he has spent over 50 years researching how trauma reshapes both body and brain. His work has revolutionized our understanding of psychological suffering, showing that trauma is not limited to soldiers or those in extreme situations, but is a far more common and deeply human experience.
therapy-psychedlics-and-why-the-body-kee.subtitle: Challenging Descartes' legacy

a-world-without-values.speaker_desc: Dale Turner, Associate Professor in the Department of Political Science and Centre for Indigenous Studies at the University of Toronto, Janne Teller, critically-acclaimed writer of novels, essays and short stories, and Robin van den Akker, Senior Lecturer in the Philosophy of Culture at Erasmus University College Rotterdam, debate the values that govern our lives, and whether they are universal.
a-world-without-values.subtitle: Is there a human moral code?

darwin-vs-consciousness.speaker_desc: Stuart Hameroff is an American anesthesiologist and professor at the University of Arizona. He is known for his controversial and creative theories on the quantum origin of consciousness. Antonella Tramacere is an expert in the philosophy of cognition and neuroscience. She is an assistant professor at the Department of Philosophy, Communication and Performance at Roma Tre in Rome. Denis Noble is Professor Emeritus and co-Director of Computational Physiology at Oxford University. He is known for his ground-breaking work in biology and physiology. Hosted by Güneş Taylor, training fellow at the Francis Crick Institute, the London-based biomedical research centre.
darwin-vs-consciousness.subtitle: The biology of consciousness

the-return-of-empire.speaker_desc: Leading journalist and foreign policy analyst, Robert Kaplan, author of The End of History? Francis Fukuyama, chief foreign affairs commentator of the Financial Times, Gideon Rachman, and Times and Telegraph columnist Juliet Samuel lock horns over the future of Europe and the West.
the-return-of-empire.subtitle: What will the new world order be?

ai-and-the-story-of-the-universe-marika-.speaker_desc: Marika Taylor is Professor of Theoretical Physics and Pro-Vice Chancellor and Head of the College of Engineering and Physical Sciences, University of Birmingham. She completed her doctorate at Cambridge University under the supervision of Stephen Hawking and her research ranges from exploring the frontiers of fundamental physics to using physics led approaches to develop artificial intelligence.
ai-and-the-story-of-the-universe-marika-.subtitle: How AI will help us make scientific discoveries

babette-babich-nietzsche-the-birth-of-tr.speaker_desc: Babette Babich is a leading philosopher of technology and science. Renowned for her exploration of the philosophy, history, and sociology of science as well as studies of ecology and animal philosophy, Babich is a Professor of Philosophy at Fordham University, New York City. Her work crosses the analytic-continental divide, drawing heavily on Nietzsche, Heidegger, Adorno, and Illich. She is the director of The Nietzsche Society. Her latest book, Günther Anders’ Philosophy of Technology, explores the philosophy of isolation.
babette-babich-nietzsche-the-birth-of-tr.subtitle: Why we're addicted to tragedy

faster-than-light.speaker_desc: João Magueijo is a Portugese cosmologist and Professor of theoretical physics at Imperial College, and a pioneer of varying speed of light theory. Claudia de Rham is a prize winning theoretical cosmologist, known for her theory of massive gravity which is seen as an explanation for the acceleration of the universe and an alternative to dark energy. Tim Maudlin is a leading professor of the philosophy of science at New York University who proposes that we should determine our metaphysics from physics. Hosted by post-realist philosopher Hilary Lawson.
faster-than-light.subtitle: Is the speed of light an absolute limit?

lost-in-stories.speaker_desc: Matthew Beaumont, Professor of English literature at University College London and acclaimed author, joins Ruth Padel, award-winning poet, and Theodore Dalrymple, a well-loved English cultural critic, prolific writer and psychiatrist, to discuss the power of the narratives we tell ourselves. Myriam François hosts.
lost-in-stories.subtitle: Can we ever escape our narratives?

ai-and-the-future-of-film-with-martha-fi.speaker_desc: Martha Fiennes is an award-winning film director, writer, producer and digital artist, best known for her films Onegin and Chromophobia. Her directorial debut was lavished with praise, including winning the London Film Critic's Choice Newcomer of the Year and the Tokyo International Film Festival award for Best Director.
ai-and-the-future-of-film-with-martha-fi.subtitle: Film, freedom and expression

peril-and-progress.speaker_desc: Camila Vergara is a critical legal theorist, historian, and journalist writing on the relation between inequality and the law. Nadhim Zahawi is a politician who served in various ministerial positions including as Chancellor, Secretary of State for Education and Chairman of the Conservative Party. Nadhim Zahawi is a politician who served in various ministerial positions including as Chancellor, Secretary of State for Education, and Chairman of the Conservative Party. John Bercow is the former Speaker for the House of Commons, former chancellor of the University of Essex and current professor at Royal Holloway. Guy Standing is a labour economist known for his support for Universal Basic Income. Mary Ann Sieghart hosts.
peril-and-progress.subtitle: A lost ideal or a new beginning?

why-we-are-out-of-our-minds-ruby-wax.speaker_desc: Ruby Wax OBE is a seminal British-American talent, excelling as an actress, writer, TV personality, and mental health advocate. Her impressive career includes captivating performances with the Royal Shakespeare Company and a memorable role in the ITV sitcom Girls on Top.
why-we-are-out-of-our-minds-ruby-wax.subtitle: Entrapped by the human condition

the-dawn-of-machine-consciousness-with-j.speaker_desc: Joscha Bach is a cognitive scientist, AI researcher, and philosopher whose research aims to bridge cognitive science and AI by studying how human intelligence and consciousness can be modeled computationally.
the-dawn-of-machine-consciousness-with-j.subtitle: The limits, risks, and future of AI

something-for-nothing.speaker_desc: Paul Bloom is a Canadian-American psychologist, bestselling author, and celebrated speaker. Bloom has written widely on human nature, and he won the Klaus J. Jacobs Research Prize for his investigations into how children develop a sense of morality. Dan Ariely is a Professor of Psychology and Behavioural Economics at Duke University and best-selling author. Ariely is a scholar of irrationality and decision-making, explaining how we repeatedly and predictably make the wrong decisions in many aspects of our lives. Nancy Sherman is a Professor of Philosophy at Georgetown University who has conducted research in general ethics, moral psychology, and the history of philosophy with focus on the Stoic tradition. A New York Times Notable Author and sought-after speaker, her views on military ethics have been influential. Hosted by Myriam François, trailblazing journalist, filmmaker and writer. Myriam’s writing and work has appeared in the Guardian, TIME, Foreign Policy, the Telegraph, CNN online, Middle East Eye, the BBC, Channel 4, and Al Jazeera.
something-for-nothing.subtitle: The risks of reward

data-deception-and-truth.speaker_desc: John Burn-Murdoch is a columnist and the chief data reporter for the Financial Times where he writes the weekly Data Points column. Abby Innes is an Associate Professor in Political Economy at the LSE focusing on the UK state and empiricism. She is the teaching chair of the European Institute. Kenneth Cukier is deputy executive editor at the Economist and the host of the hugely popular weekly podcast, Babbage. Hosted by The Head of New Formats for the Financial Times, Juliet Riddell.
data-deception-and-truth.subtitle: Can we trust the numbers?

the-axis-of-autocracy-with-anne-applebau.speaker_desc: Anne Applebaum is a Pulitzer Prize winning author and a Staff Writer at The Atlantic. Her condemnation of Russian aggression has seen her personally sanctioned by Putin's government. Her most recent book is Autocracy Inc. She is interviewed by Penny Mordaunt, former Foreign Secretary and Conservative MP.
the-axis-of-autocracy-with-anne-applebau.subtitle: The Axis of Autocracy

adventures-in-space.speaker_desc: Matt O'Dowd is a renowned professor of astrophysics and host and writer of the biggest physics and space show on YouTube, PBS Space Time. Avi Loeb is a leading theoretical astrophysicist and the Frank B. Baird Jr. Professor of Science at Harvard University. Carol Cleland is Director of the Center for the Study of Origins and Professor of Philosophy at the University of Colorado Boulder.
adventures-in-space.subtitle: Humanity and the final frontier

the-ugly-truth-behind-beauty-jessica-de-.speaker_desc: Jessica DeFino is an award-winning beauty reporter and critic, having written for the New York Times, Sunday Times, and Vice. She currently writes the Guardian’s beauty advice column Ask Ugly. DeFino also writes a weekly newsletter, The Review of Beauty, which “basically gives the middle finger to the entire beauty industry” (HuffPost). She is working on her first book.
the-ugly-truth-behind-beauty-jessica-de-.subtitle: Unmasking the beauty industry

language-wars.speaker_desc: Babette Babich is a pioneering philosopher known for her deep exploration of science, technology, and ecological thought. She is a Professor of Philosophy at Fordham University, NYC, and the director of The Nietzsche Society. Graham Priest is the Distinguished Professor of Philosophy at the Graduate Center, City University of New York, renowned for his work in logic, especially non-classical logic. Sandra Laugier is an acclaimed Professor of Philosophy at Université Paris 1 Panthéon Sorbonne, known for her influential work on ordinary language philosophy and the intersection of philosophy and popular culture.
language-wars.subtitle: The weapon of the word

mental-health-is-not-a-medical-condition.speaker_desc: Simon Wessely is a visionary psychiatrist and epidemiologist at the forefront of research in medicine, psychiatry, clinical epidemiology and military health. He currently holds the position of Regius Professor of Psychiatry at King's College London.
mental-health-is-not-a-medical-condition.subtitle: Reflections on the crisis in mental health

the-price-of-everything-value-of-nothing.speaker_desc: Will Hutton is a leading political economist, author and journalist. Throughout his career, he has gone from being an investment banker in the City, to holding the Economics editorship of the Guardian and BBC2 Newsnight and the Principal of Hertford College Oxford. Daniel Susskind is an associate member of the Economics Department at Oxford University specialising in growth and the impact of AI. His most recent book is Growth: A Reckoning . Richard Kibble is a Deloitte Partner and former banking executive. Abby Innes is an Associate Professor in Political Economy at the LSE focusing on how the UK’s economy mirrors the Soviet Union. Her work blends the philosophy of science, economics, and history. Hosted by the BBC's Roger Hearing
the-price-of-everything-value-of-nothing.subtitle: Can economics care about value?

john-ioannidis-on-why-science-is-broken.speaker_desc: John Ioannidis is one of the world’s leading experts on scientific integrity and evidence-based medicine. A professor at Stanford University, his groundbreaking work has exposed systemic flaws in research methodology, publication bias, and the reproducibility crisis. Best known for his landmark paper Why Most Published Research Findings Are False, he continues to challenge the scientific establishment and advocate for more rigorous, transparent, and reliable research practices.
john-ioannidis-on-why-science-is-broken.subtitle: The ongoing crisis in research replication

the-rise-of-the-new-right.speaker_desc: Times columnist David Aaronovitch has won the Orwell prize for journalism, and the What the Papers Say columnist of the year award in 2003. He is the author of Paddling to Jerusalem and Voodoo Histories.
the-rise-of-the-new-right.subtitle: The changing face of conservatism

quantum-and-the-unknowable-universe.speaker_desc: Roger Penrose is a world-renowned mathematician, mathematical physicist, philosopher of science and Nobel Laureate in Physics. He is best known for his work on general relativity and sharing the Wolf Prize for Physics with Stephen Hawking for his work on black holes. He is also the author of The Road to Reality , Cycles of Time and Shadows of the Mind . Fearlessly critical of the scientific mainstream, Sabine Hossenfelder is a groundbreaking theoretical physicist who specialises in the foundations of science. She is a leading science communicator, best-selling author and researcher. Her recent books include Lost in Math , and the bestselling Existential Physics . Slavoj Žižek is a globally renowned philosopher and cultural critic. He is international director of the Birkbeck Institute for the Humanities at the University of London, visiting professor at New York University and a senior researcher at the University of Ljubljana's Department of Philosophy. He is the author of several books, including The Sublime Object of Ideology , The Parallax View , and Heaven in Disorder. Hosted by Güneş Taylor, training fellow at the Francis Crick Institute.
quantum-and-the-unknowable-universe.subtitle: Has quantum physics made the universe unknowable?

the-life-and-philosophy-of-peter-singer.speaker_desc: Peter Singer is the most prominent figure in contemporary ethics. He has made groundbreaking contributions to animal welfare, bioethics, effective altruism and practical ethics more broadly. He is a founder of both Animals Australia and The Life You Can Save, and has been a key figure in the Effective Altruism movement - an initiative that uses evidence and careful analysis to find the very best way for individuals to do good. Singer has received multiple accolades for his work, including a nomination as one of Australia's ten most influential public intellectuals and the $1 million Berggruen Prize in 2021.
the-life-and-philosophy-of-peter-singer.subtitle: Behind the scenes with "The Dangerous Philosopher"

stories-and-poems-from-the-front-lines.speaker_desc: Lindsey Hilsum is the International Editor of Channel 4 News and a regular contributor to The Sunday Times, The Times Literary Supplement, and The Guardian among others. She is also a bestselling author. Sarah Howe, award-winning poet, hosts.
stories-and-poems-from-the-front-lines.subtitle: Truth, trauma and testimony

the-world-at-sea.speaker_desc: Simon Jenkins is an author, newspaper columnist and editor. He is currently a columnist for the Guardian and was formerly editor of the Times and Evening Standard. Duncan Potts is a retired Vice Admiral of the Royal Navy where he was the Director of the Joint Force Development. Before this, he was commander of the EU's counter-piracy operations in the Indian Ocean at the height of Somali Piracy. Isabel Hilton is a renowned international relations expert, journalist and broadcaster. She is the founder of China Dialogue, an organisation dedicated to fostering understanding of China. Hosted by the BBC's Roger Hearing.
the-world-at-sea.subtitle: Will the waves dominate the 21st century?

the-philosophy-of-dehumanisation-with-da.speaker_desc: David Livingstone Smith is a philosopher and author, most recently of Making Monsters: The Uncanny Power of Dehumanization. His research interests include self-deception, dehumanization, human nature, ideology, race and moral psychology. His book Less Than Human: Why We Demean, Enslave, and Exterminate Others, won the Anisfield-Wolf Book Award.
the-philosophy-of-dehumanisation-with-da.subtitle: Animals, monsters and race

the-phantom-of-the-present.speaker_desc: Winner of the Orange First Novel prize, Joanna Kavenna’s works include A Field Guide to Reality, The Ice Museum and Inglorious. Her journalism has appeared in the London Review of Books, The Guardian, and the New York Times. Timothy Morton is the Rita Shea Guffey Chair in English at Rice University. A member of the object-oriented philosophy movement, Morton's work explores the intersection of object-oriented thought and ecological studies. Morton has published numerous books including 'Dark Ecology: For a Logic of Future Coexistence', 'The Ecological Thought' and 'Hyposubjects: On Becoming Humane'. Rupert Sheldrake is a scientist, author, and parapsychology researcher. At Cambridge University, he worked in developmental biology as a Fellow of Clare College. He was Principal Plant Physiologist at the International Crops Research Institute for the Semi-Arid Tropics in Hyderabad, India. Hosted by Curt Jaimungal, renowned filmmaker and presenter. He is founder and host of the legendary Theories of Everything YouTube podcast that explores cutting-edge topics in physics, consciousness, free will and AI with some of the leading experts in the world.
the-phantom-of-the-present.subtitle: On grasping the present

in-conversation-priya-natarajan-hilary-l.speaker_desc: Priya Natarajan is a Professor of theoretical astrophysics at Yale University. Natarajan was included on the TIME100 list of most influential people in the world in 2024 and is the 2025 recipient of the Dannie Heineman Prize in Astrophysics awarded by the American Astronomical Society and the American Institute of Physics. Hilary Lawson is a philosopher best known for his theory 'Closure', a post-analytic return to metaphysics, and an outspoken critic of philosophical realism. He is Editorial Director of the IAI.
in-conversation-priya-natarajan-hilary-l.subtitle: In conversation: Priya Natarajan and Hilary Lawson

the-danger-and-promise-of-the-algorithm.speaker_desc: Aaron Bastani is the co-founder of Novara Media, described as 'the slickest of the guerrilla news and opinion operations that have sprung up in Britain' by the Guardian. Craig Gent is a director at Novara Media, where he has worked for over ten years. He is the author of Cyberboss: The Rise of Algorithmic Management and the New Struggle for Control at Work (2024, Verso Books).
the-danger-and-promise-of-the-algorithm.subtitle: How algorithms control our lives

make-china-great-again-steve-tsang-on-xi.speaker_desc: Steve is the Director of the SOAS China Institute. Before taking on his current position in 2016, he was the Head of the School of Contemporary Chinese Studies at the University of Nottingham, and before that a Professorial Fellow at St Antony’s College, Oxford. He is a frequent commentator for the BBC, including for programmes like Newsnight, BBC News and the World at One.
make-china-great-again-steve-tsang-on-xi.subtitle: Putting the East into the Global South

profit-planet-and-pretence-carla-denyer-.speaker_desc: Carla Denyer is co-leader of the Green Party of England and Wales. Carla is the MP for Bristol Central and was instrumental in getting Bristol Council to declare a climate emergency, the first in Europe. Guy Shrubsole is a researcher, writer and campaigner. He wrote The Lost Rainforests of Britain (The Sunday Times Science book of the Year 2023) and, most recently, The Lie of the Land. Socrates Mokkas is a leading economist operating at the intersection of macroeconomic policy and sustainability. He has close to 20 years of experience across academia, government and industry. Hosted by Isabel Hilton.
profit-planet-and-pretence-carla-denyer-.subtitle: Is green finance just marketing hype?

controlling-the-tech-titans.speaker_desc: Alexander Evans is a former diplomat and visiting Senior Fellow at LSE. His research includes the relationship between geopolitical insecurity, modern technology and online child safety. Kenneth Cukier is deputy executive editor of The Economist, following two decades as a foreign correspondent, technology writer, data editor and commentary editor. He is the coauthor of the NYT bestselling book “Big Data”. Shannon Vallor is the Chair in the Ethics of Data and Artificial Intelligence at the Edinburgh Futures Institute. Her research explores how new technologies especially AI reshape our lives. Joscha Bach is a AI researcher, cognitive scientist and consciousness researcher. He currently works at Liquid AI in Silicon Valley. Roger Hearing hosts.
controlling-the-tech-titans.subtitle: Should we regulate Big Tech?

creating-life-in-a-lab.speaker_desc: Katarzyna (Kate) Adamala is a pioneering synthetic biologist and genetics professor at the University of Minnesota. Her groundbreaking work spans the realms of astrobiology, synthetic cell engineering, and biocomputing.
creating-life-in-a-lab.subtitle: Building biology from scratch

consciousness-is-quantum-mechanical-with.speaker_desc: Stuart Hameroff is a Professor of Psychology and Anesthesiology, and Director of the Center for Consciousness Studies at The University of Arizona, Tucson, Arizona.
consciousness-is-quantum-mechanical-with.subtitle: Why the quantum collapse is consciousness

the-dark-side-of-mental-health-susie-orb.speaker_desc: Dr Susie Orbach is a psychotherapist, psychoanalyst, and social critic. She is a best-selling author, a columnist for The Guardian, and a visiting scholar at the New School for Social Research, in New York, whilst continuing to run her well-known practice, in London.
the-dark-side-of-mental-health-susie-orb.subtitle: The mind and body in dialogue

the-rise-of-the-rest.speaker_desc: Join us as former UK Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind, Yale Jackson School Senior Fellow Elizabeth Knup, former Defence Secretary Penny Mordaunt, and current Ukrainian MP Inna Sovsun debate the rise of a new global world order.
the-rise-of-the-rest.subtitle: Is Western economic dominance finished?

a-world-of-order-and-chaos.speaker_desc: Marcus du Sautoy is a leading British mathematician, and Simonyi Professor for the Public Understanding of Science at the University of Oxford. Marika Taylor is a Professor of Theoretical Physics, Pro-Vice Chancellor, and Head of the College of Engineering and Physical Sciences at the University of Birmingham.She previously studied under Stephen Hawking at Cambridge. Nick Lane is a Professor of Evolutionary Biochemistry at University College London and a bestselling author of five critically-acclaimed books on evolutionary biochemistry. Hosted by Bjørn Ekeberg.
a-world-of-order-and-chaos.subtitle: Challenging the second law of thermodynamics

a-politics-for-the-future.speaker_desc: Will Hutton is a British writer, weekly columnist at the Guardian and the Observer, and currently Principal of Hertford College, Oxford and Chair of the Big Innovation Centre.
a-politics-for-the-future.subtitle: How to fix the economy

the-world-as-one-jessica-frazier.speaker_desc: Jessica Frazier is a professor of theology and religion at Trinity College, Oxford, as well as a Fellow of the Oxford Centre for Hindu studies.
the-world-as-one-jessica-frazier.subtitle: The illusion of separation

lies-damned-lies-and-economics.speaker_desc: Nadhim Zahawi is a politician who served in various ministerial positions under Prime Ministers Theresa May, Boris Johnson, Liz Truss, and Rishi Sunak. Gary Stevenson is a former financial trader who became an activist against inequality and a prominent YouTuber. Abby Innes is an Associate Professor in Political Economy at LSE focusing on how the UK’s economy mirrors the Soviet Union. Hosted by Hilary Lawson.
lies-damned-lies-and-economics.subtitle: Can economics be a hard science?

untangling-language-sandra-laguier.speaker_desc: Sandra Laugier is an award-winning Professor of Philosophy at Université Paris 1 Panthéon Sorbonne. She is the author of the celebrated book, 'Why We Need Ordinary Language Philosophy'. A key liaison between American and European philosophical thought, her work spans moral philosophy, political philosophy, philosophy of language, gender studies, and popular culture.
untangling-language-sandra-laguier.subtitle: The unknown origins of analytic philosophy

physics-next-paradigm-shift-with-matt-od.speaker_desc: Matt O'Dowd is a renowned astrophysicist and science communicator. He researches extragalactic astrophysics (black holes, quasars, gravitational lensing, and more) and is a Professor of Physics and Astronomy at City University of New York, Lehman College. O'Dowd is also the host and writer of the weekly YouTube show PBS Space Time, currently the biggest physics and space show on YouTube with over 3 million subscribers. He is also a regular guest at StarTalk radio, the popular science show with Neil Degrasse Tyson.
physics-next-paradigm-shift-with-matt-od.subtitle: Understanding the cosmos

new-frontiers-in-art.speaker_desc: Jaron Lanier is a computer scientist, visual artist, composer, futurist, and writer. His 2014 book Who Owns the Future? received critical acclaim, winning Harvard’s Goldsmith Book Prize and the Peace Prize of the German Book Trade. He has performed and recorded with a wide range of musicians, including Philip Glass, Yoko Ono, and Ornette Coleman, and his paintings and drawings have been displayed in museums and galleries across the globe. TIME magazine has named him one of the world’s 100 most influential people. Join Lanier as he discusses his recent artistic projects and the role of originality in art.
new-frontiers-in-art.subtitle: Creativity in the digital age

videogames-and-the-meaning-of-life.speaker_desc: James Tartaglia is Professor of Metaphysical Philosophy at Keele University. HIs latest book is Inner Space Philosophy: Why the Next Stage of Human Development Should Be Philosophical, Explained Radically (Suitable for Wolves).
videogames-and-the-meaning-of-life.subtitle: Loading... Existentialism

the-lie-of-meritocracy-with-daniel-marko.speaker_desc: Daniel Markovits is an American legal scholar, best known for his work on law and behavioural economics, contract law, distributive justice, and market regulation. His best-selling book, "The Meritocracy Trap: How America's Foundational Myth Feeds Inequality, Dismantles the Middle Class, and Devours the Elite", has sparked a significant discussion about the problems inherent in meritocratic societies.
the-lie-of-meritocracy-with-daniel-marko.subtitle: Why we must abandon merit

the-values-of-ai-ruth-chang.speaker_desc: Ruth Chang is the Professor and Chair of Jurisprudence at the University of Oxford, a Professorial Fellow of University College, Oxford, and a professor of philosophy. She is known for her pioneering research on the incommensurability of values and making hard choices.

consciousness-ai-and-the-pattern-of-real.speaker_desc: Joscha Bach is an exceptional cognitive scientist who is pushing the limits of what we can achieve with Artificial Intelligence. As an AI researcher for MIT Media Lab and the Harvard Program for Evolutionary Dynamics, he is constantly exploring new frontiers in cognitive architectures, mental representation, emotion, social modelling, and multi-agent systems. Bach's groundbreaking MicroPsi project is creating virtual agents that are revolutionizing our understanding of how emotion, motivation, and cognition interact in situated agents.
consciousness-ai-and-the-pattern-of-real.subtitle: Understanding the algorithms of consciousness

the-divided-self-sam-harris-roger-penros.speaker_desc: Joining us live from the US via Zoom, neuroscientist and philosopher Sam Harris, Nobel Prize winner Roger Penrose and director of the Institute of Cognitive Neuroscience Sophie Scott discuss whether the self is divided.
the-divided-self-sam-harris-roger-penros.subtitle: What is the nature of consciousness?

what-is-meaningful-work.speaker_desc: Isabel Berwick is the host of the Financial Times' Working It podcast, editorial lead for the FT's Women in Business forum, and author. Caleb Althorpe is a Research Fellow in the Department of Philosophy at Trinity College Dublin. He researches contemporary political theory and political philosophy. Dr Nilufar Ahmed is an award-winning professional psychologist with over 20 years of experience working in academia, the third sector, and as a freelance researcher and evaluator. Guy Standing is professor of Development Studies at SOAS and co-founder of the Basic Income Earth Network.
what-is-meaningful-work.subtitle: How to link labour and life

the-lasting-legacy-of-stolen-land.speaker_desc: Dale Turner is an Associate Professor of Political Science at the University of Toronto. He works on Indigenous politics, contemporary Indigenous intellectual culture, contemporary political theory, and the philosophy of Ludwig Wittgenstein. He is currently working on a new book which draws from his community’s experiences over the past few hundred years in dialogue with the venerated Western European philosophical tradition.
the-lasting-legacy-of-stolen-land.subtitle: Reopening the conversation

turtles-all-the-way-down.speaker_desc: Priya Natarajan is a Professor of Astrophysics at Yale University and has been named as one of Time Magazine's top 100 most influential people in 2024 for her groundbreaking work in the field. Donald Hoffman is a renowned anti-reality theorist and Professor of Cognitive Sciences at the University of California, Irvine. Hilary Lawson is a philosopher best known for his theory 'Closure', a post-analytic return to metaphysics, and an outspoken critic of philosophical realism. Hosted by Jack Symes.
turtles-all-the-way-down.subtitle: In search of the foundations of reality

how-liberals-get-education-wrong-katheri.speaker_desc: Enter Katharine Birbalsingh, known as "the world's strictest headmistress" and the leader of one of the U.K.'s most successful schools. Birbalsingh passionately argues that this crisis of meaning begins in childhood. She believes that unless we embrace discipline, endure boredom, and return to more traditional methods of teaching and parenting, we will fail to reverse this troubling trend.
how-liberals-get-education-wrong-katheri.subtitle: Philosophy of education with Katherine Birbalsingh

the-communication-crisis.speaker_desc: Nolen Gertz is an Assistant Professor of applied philosophy at the University of Twente. He is the author of the books Nihilism, and Nihilism and Technology. Julia Hobsbawm OBE is an award-winning writer and broadcaster who captures the zeitgeist about work, life, and technology. Her books include "Fully Connected" and The Nowhere Office which is now a popular podcast. Katie Farrell is the lead of the brand practice at Deloitte Digital, she works with executive teams to develop and build influential ideas for organisations. Shini Somara hosts.
the-communication-crisis.subtitle: Reclaiming communication from tech

nothing-and-everything-graham-priest.speaker_desc: Graham Priest is a philosopher and logician at CUNY. A key defender of dialetheism, the view that there are true contradictions.
nothing-and-everything-graham-priest.subtitle: The paradox of nothing

stories-of-reality-sunetra-gupta.speaker_desc: Sunetra Gupta is a novelist and professor of Theoretical Epidemiology at the University of Oxford, with an interest in infectious disease agents that are responsible for malaria, HIV, influenza and bacterial meningitis. Her fictional works include So Good in Black and A Sin of Colour.
stories-of-reality-sunetra-gupta.subtitle: The risk of false narratives in science

lisa-randall-on-theory-fantasy-and-disco.speaker_desc: One of the most daring theoretical physicists alive today, Lisa Randall is the Frank B. Baird, Jr. Professor of Science at Harvard University. Due to Randall's advances in understanding and testing the Standard Model of particle physics, supersymmetry, and cosmology of extra dimensions, Newsweek called her "one of the most promising theoretical physicists of her generation."
lisa-randall-on-theory-fantasy-and-disco.subtitle: Understanding approaches to scientific discovery

the-freedom-fable.speaker_desc: Faiza Shaheen is a UK politician, former professor of economics, think-tank director, and expert in Inequality. Uriel Abulof is a professor of political science and expert in the politics of nationalism, social movements, and conflict. He is the author of several books, including The Morality and Mortality of Nations. Lisa Cameron is a Scottish Conservative politician who has served as a Member of Parliament. Lisa is also a former clinical psychologist who worked for the NHS. Hosted by Isabel Hilton.
the-freedom-fable.subtitle: The reality and rhetoric of freedom

the-global-population-crisis.speaker_desc: David Aaronovitch is an award-winning journalist and author, Presenter of BBC Radio 4's Briefing Room, and former long-standing columnist for The Times. Janne Teller is a critically acclaimed writer of novels, essays, and short stories. She was educated as a macro-economist and has previously worked for the United Nations on humanitarian assistance and conflict resolution. Peter Godfrey-Smith is a philosopher of science. He is the author of Other Minds: The Octopus, The Sea, and the Deep Origins of Consciousness as well as Metazoa: Animal Life and the Birth of the Mind. Hosted by Harvard's Rana Mitter.
the-global-population-crisis.subtitle: Do we need more people?

the-theory-of-quantum-politics-armen-sar.speaker_desc: Armen Vardani Sarkissian is an Armenian politician, physicist, investor, businessman, and computer scientist who served as the 4th president of Armenia from 2018 to 2022. He also served as Prime Minister of Armenia from 1996 to 1997. He was the first president of post-Soviet Armenia born in former Armenian SSR.
the-theory-of-quantum-politics-armen-sar.subtitle: How small states control the future

creating-the-meaning-of-life-babette-bab.speaker_desc: Babette Babich is a trailblazing philosopher of technology and science. Renowned for her exploration of the philosophy, history, and sociology of science, Babich also works on the philosophy of digital media, poetry and art. Babich is a Professor of Philosophy at Fordham University, New York City.
creating-the-meaning-of-life-babette-bab.subtitle: What Nietzsche teaches us about meaning

the-values-and-prejudices-of-science.speaker_desc: Tim Palmer is a world renowned expert on climate physics at the Royal Society Institute in Oxford. He was appointed as CBE in the 2015 New Year’s Honours list for services to science. Shini Somara is a highly accomplished British mechanical engineer. With a mission to bring science to everyone, she has participated as an engineering expert on Sky, Discovery, and more. Ben Ware is a leading philosopher and an expert on Wittgenstein. He is the co-director of the Centre for Philosophy and the Visual Arts at King’s College London and the author of On Extinction: Beginning Again at The End. Hosted by post-postmodern philosopher Hilary Lawson.
the-values-and-prejudices-of-science.subtitle: The place of values in science

the-real-risks-of-ai-natalie-cargill.speaker_desc: Natalie Cargill is a renowned philanthropic advisor and researcher of AI risk. Cargill is also the founder and President of LongView Philantropy.
the-real-risks-of-ai-natalie-cargill.subtitle: A decade on and a decade to go

a-new-theory-of-ethics-martha-nussbaum.speaker_desc: Martha Nussbaum is Distinguished Professor of Law and Ethics at the University of Chicago. She has made ground-breaking contributions to topics ranging from sex and gender, ethics and politics, to justice. Her latest book is Justice for Animals .
a-new-theory-of-ethics-martha-nussbaum.subtitle: The future of ethics beyond species

the-riddle-of-the-beginning.speaker_desc: Scott Aaronson is a world renowned quantum complexity theorist and Associate Professor at MIT. He currently works at OpenAI, where he researches the theoretical foundations of AI safety. Joscha Bach is a computer scientist and AI researcher for MIT and the Harvard Program for Evolutionary Dynamics. With a mission to build a model of the mind, Bach is at the forefront of the creation of Strong AI. Priya Natarajan is a Professor of Astrophysics at Yale University and has been just named as one of Time Magazine's top 100 most influential people in 2024 for her groundbreaking work in the field. Hosted by British mechanical engineer, media broadcaster, producer, and author, Shini Somara.
the-riddle-of-the-beginning.subtitle: Making sense of the beginning of the universe

morality-and-prejudice.speaker_desc: Tommy J. Curry is a Professor of Philosophy and holds the Personal Chair of Africana Philosophy and Black Male Studies at the University of Edinburgh. He is the author of The Man-Not: Race, Class, Genre, and the Dilemmas of Black Manhood, which won the 2018 American Book Award. Michael Huemer is a professor of philosophy at the University of Colorado. He is the author of more than eighty academic articles in epistemology, ethics, metaethics, metaphysics, and political philosophy, and he has written several books including Ethical Intuitionism. Huemer is also known for his detailed defence of philosophical anarchism. Melis Erdur received her Ph.D. in philosophy from the New York University in 2013. In her philosophical work, she examines central meta-ethical questions concerning moral truth and objectivity and argues that common ways of posing and answering these questions are based on serious moral mistakes.
morality-and-prejudice.subtitle: Is ethics determined by principles or power?

katharine-birbalsingh-future-of-multicul.speaker_desc: Katharine Birbalsingh is a British teacher and education reform advocate who is the founder and head teacher of Michaela Community School, a free school established in 2014 in Wembley Park, London. Katharine read Philosophy & Modern Languages at The University of Oxford and has always taught in inner London. She has made numerous appearances on television, radio, podcasts and has written for several publications. Katharine has also written two books and edited another two about Michaela; Battle Hymn Of The Tiger Teachers and The Power of Culture. Katharine was appointed Honorary Fellow of New College, Oxford in 2021 and Commander of the Order of the British Empire (CBE) in 2020. Follow Katharine on Twitter: @Miss_Snuffy
katharine-birbalsingh-future-of-multicul.subtitle: UK's strictest headmistress on the culture wars

the-crisis-of-the-new.speaker_desc: The author Joanna Kavenna hosts this debate between Martin Puchner, the Byron and Anita Wien Professor of Drama and English and Comparative Literature at Harvard University, Claire Hynes, an Associate Professor in Literature & Creative Writing at the University of East Anglia, and Stanley Fish, a literary critic, legal scholar, and public intellectual who is currently a Distinguished Visiting Professor of Law at Yeshiva University's Benjamin N. Cardozo School of Law in New York City.
the-crisis-of-the-new.subtitle: Is the idea of the new a fantasy?

objects-from-other-worlds-avi-loeb.speaker_desc: Avi Loeb is a theoretical astrophysicist and the Frank B. Baird Jr. Professor of Science at Harvard University.
objects-from-other-worlds-avi-loeb.subtitle: The evidence for alien life in the solar system

recovering-meaning-in-the-information-ag.speaker_desc: Martha Fiennes is an award-winning film director, writer, producer and digital artist, best known for her films Onegin and Chromophobia. Her directorial debut was lavished with praise, including winning the London Film Critic's Choice Newcomer of the Year and the Tokyo International Film Festival award for Best Director. Richard Davey is a Senior Research Fellow at Nottingham Trent University.
recovering-meaning-in-the-information-ag.subtitle: How to reclaim our humanity from tech

the-politics-of-time-guy-standing.speaker_desc: Guy Standing is professor of Development Studies at SOAS and co-founder of the Basic Income Earth Network. He is best known as a long-standing and prominent advocate of Universal Basic Income, but he is also responsible for redefining and revitalizing the term ‘precariat’ which describes a new emerging social class suffering from job insecurity as well as identity insecurity and lack of time control.
the-politics-of-time-guy-standing.subtitle: What to do with our most valuable asset

consciousness-beyond-the-brain.speaker_desc: Rupert Sheldrake is a preeminent biologist and author best known for his hypothesis of morphic resonance. His books include Science and Spiritual Practices, Ways to Go Beyond And Why They Work and The Science Delusion. Furthermore, he was ranked in the top 100 thought leaders for 2013 by the Duttweiler Institute, Switzerland's leading think tank, and has been recognised as one of the 'most spiritually influential living people' by Watkins' Mind Body Spirit Magazine.
consciousness-beyond-the-brain.subtitle: Re-thinking the limits of the mind

humanity-and-the-gods-of-nature-slavoj-z.speaker_desc: Firebrand philosopher Slavoj Žižek, renowned ethicist Peter Singer, and Georgetown professor of philosophy Nancy Sherman, question human centred morality. Hosted by public philosopher Jack Symes.
humanity-and-the-gods-of-nature-slavoj-z.subtitle: Is morality human?

roger-penrose-on-the-blatant-contradicti.speaker_desc: Roger Penrose is a world-renowned mathematician, mathematical physicist, philosopher of science and Nobel Laureate in Physics. He is best known for his work on general relativity and sharing the Wolf Prize for Physics with Stephen Hawking for his work on black holes. Interviewed by renowned filmmaker and presenter, Curt Jaimungal.
roger-penrose-on-the-blatant-contradicti.subtitle: Where our best theories have gone wrong

gary-stevenson-on-hidden-dangers-of-ineq.speaker_desc: Gary Stevenson (born 1986 in Ilford) is a British economist, former financial trader, and YouTuber known for his economic analysis and activism against economic inequality. Interviewed by Alyssa Erspamer.
gary-stevenson-on-hidden-dangers-of-ineq.subtitle: How do we fix society

sartre-vs-baldwin-the-unknown-other.speaker_desc: Jonathan Webber is a professor at Cardiff University specializing in moral philosophy and the philosophy of psychology. Marie-Elsa Roche Bragg is an author, teacher, and priest. Her first novel, Towards Mellbreak is about four generations of a quiet hill farming family on the North Western fells of Cumbria. Joanna Kavenna is an award-winning writer. She was born in the UK but as a seasoned traveller, she was led to her first book, The Ice Museum, which details her experience travelling in the remote North. Hosted by presenter, writer and professor of the History and Politics of Modern China at Oxford, Rana Mitter
sartre-vs-baldwin-the-unknown-other.subtitle: Can we only know ourselves?

tim-palmer-the-global-climate-future.speaker_desc: Tim Palmer is an internationally renowned meteorologist and Professor at the University of Oxford. He works on the tough, crucial problems of uncertainty in our weather and climate, drawing on his background in fundamental physics to do so.
tim-palmer-the-global-climate-future.subtitle: How can we tackle climate emergency

what-religion-and-stoicism-both-misunder.speaker_desc: Rowan Williams, the 104th Archbishop of Canterbury, is a highly acclaimed theologian, writer, and pastor. In addition to his ten-year post as Archbishop, Lord Williams has also enjoyed an esteemed academic career, having been a lecturer at the University of Cambridge as well as having held the Lady Margaret Chair of Divinity at the University of Oxford. Angie Hobbs is the chair for the Public Understanding of Philosophy at Sheffield, and a frequent contributor to the BBC’s In Our Time, Night Waves and The Forum. She is the author of Plato and the Hero and her forthcoming book is Why Plato Matters.
what-religion-and-stoicism-both-misunder.subtitle: Rowan Williams and Angie Hobbs In Conversation

why-most-published-research-findings-are.speaker_desc: John Ioannidis is a physician-scientist, writer and Stanford University professor who has made contributions to evidence-based medicine, epidemiology and clinical research. Ioannidis studies scientific research itself, meta-research primarily in clinical medicine and the social sciences.
why-most-published-research-findings-are.subtitle: The replicability crisis of research

konstantin-kisin-on-wokeness-free-speech.speaker_desc: Konstantin Kisin is a Sunday Times best-selling author, comedian, satirist, social commentator and host of the YouTube show, TRIGGERnometry. Born in the late Soviet Union and raised in Britain, Kisin has appeared on flagship TV shows like BBC Question Time and Real Time with Bill Maher, as well as the Joe Rogan Experience and other popular podcasts.
konstantin-kisin-on-wokeness-free-speech.subtitle: Political polarisation and the future of Britain

the-consciousness-test-yoshua-bengio.speaker_desc: Joining us live from Montreal, Turing Award winner Yoshua Bengio, science YouTuber and theoretical physicist Sabine Hossenfelder, evolutionary biochemist Nick Lane, and post-postmodern philosopher Hilary Lawson lock horns over whether AI is, or can ever be, conscious.
the-consciousness-test-yoshua-bengio.subtitle: Is AI sentient?

the-life-and-philosophy-of-sadiq-khan.speaker_desc: Sadiq Khan is the current Mayor of London, former MP and human rights lawyer. He has had an extensive political career, most recently winning an unprecedented third term as Mayor. Prior to the mayoralty, Sadiq was an MP and member of the Shadow Cabinet under Ed Miliband where he held the posts of Shadow Secretary of State for Justice, Lord Chancellor, and Minister for London. In conversation with Will Hutton a leading political economist, author and journalist. His long and storied career has taken him from the City as an investment banker, the Economics editorship of the Guardian and BBC2 Newsnight , the editorship of the Observer, the chief executive of the Work Foundation and Principal of Hertford College Oxford.
the-life-and-philosophy-of-sadiq-khan.subtitle: The ideas behind the Mayor of London

the-dangerous-misunderstanding-of-diseas.speaker_desc: Sunetra Gupta is an award-winning epidemiologist and novelist. She is currently a Professor of Theoretical Epidemiology at the University of Oxford. Bahar Gholipour is a leading New York-based journalist and neuroscientist writing about cutting-edge issues in technology and science.
the-dangerous-misunderstanding-of-diseas.subtitle: In conversation with Sunetra Gupta

motherhood-vs-the-machine.subtitle: How technology could change motherhood completely

a-precarious-peace.speaker_desc: Tariq Ali is a writer, political activist and filmmaker, and is considered to be a leading figure of the international left. Malcolm Rifkind is a renowned British politician who served in the cabinets of both Margaret Thatcher and John Major. Camila Vergara is a critical legal theorist, historian, and journalist writing on the relation between inequality and the law, and the possible institutional solutions to systemic corruption. William Browder is the CEO and co-founder of Hermitage Capital Management, firebrand financier and anti-Putin activist. Hosted by the BBC's Roger Hearing.
a-precarious-peace.subtitle: Foreign policy in a multipolar world

hilary-greaves-on-the-philosophy-of-long.speaker_desc: Hilary Greaves is a professor of philosophy at the University of Oxford and was the founding director of its Global Priorities Institute.
hilary-greaves-on-the-philosophy-of-long.subtitle: Effective altruism and its discontents

books-and-the-future-of-civilisation.speaker_desc: In a live recording of the podcast in partnership with Theos, Reading our Times, Senior Fellow at Theos Nick Spencer discusses the future of books and reading with Times literary critic Johanna Thomas-Corr, Guardian literary editor David Shariatmadari and editorial director of Oneworld Publications Juliet Mabey.
books-and-the-future-of-civilisation.subtitle: Why the written word continues to endure

the-rise-and-fall-of-the-grand-narrative.speaker_desc: Konstantin Kisin is a Sunday Times best-selling author, comedian, satirist, social commentator and host of the leading YouTube show, TRIGGERnometry. David Aaronovitch is an award-winning journalist, presenter of BBC Radio 4's Briefing Room, and former long-standing columnist for The Times. Jessica Frazier is a philosopher at the University of Oxford and Fellow of the Oxford Centre for Hindu Studies. She is an expert on Indian Philosophy and the European tradition of phenomenology. Hosted by Rana Mitter.
the-rise-and-fall-of-the-grand-narrative.subtitle: Finding meaning in the postmodern age

denis-noble-on-the-symmetry-of-order-and.speaker_desc: One of the founders of the field of systems biology, Denis Noble is an Emeritus professor of cardiovascular physiology at the University of Oxford. He was the first to develop computer models of the heart in 1960.
denis-noble-on-the-symmetry-of-order-and.subtitle: An interview with Denis Noble

the-elections-that-change-everything.speaker_desc: The longest-serving Speaker of the House of Commons since the Second World War (2009-2019), John Bercow was once seen as on the right of the Tory party, later becoming a member of the Tory shadow cabinet. He moved to the left throughout his political career subsequently becoming a thorn in the side of the Conservative Johnson government and leaving the party.
the-elections-that-change-everything.subtitle: The troubling state of our governments

ai-is-a-mirror-on-humanity-shannon-vallo.speaker_desc: Shannon Vallor is the Baillie Gifford Chair in the Ethics of Data and Artificial Intelligence at the Edinburgh Futures Institute, the Director of the Centre for Technomoral Futures, and a former AI ethicist at Google. Her research explores how new technologies -- especially AI, robotics, and data science -- reshape human moral character, habits, and practices. Her work includes advising policymakers and industry on the ethical design and use of AI.
ai-is-a-mirror-on-humanity-shannon-vallo.subtitle: Humanity's non-human reflection

the-democracy-show.speaker_desc: S.Y. Quraishi is an Indian civil servant who rose to be the 17th Chief Election Commissioner of India, the largest democracy in the world. He has served as a UN election observer in South Africa, Kenya, Russia, and Myanmar to name a few. Amy Chua is an author, professor of law at Yale Law School and populariser of the term ‘Tiger Mom’. She is a renowned commentator on everything from American politics, to populism and parenting. Sophie Scott-Brown is the former Director of Gresham College and an Honorary Research Fellow in the History faculty at the University of St. Andrews. Her work specialises in the history of anarchism. Hosted by the BBC's Roger Hearing.
the-democracy-show.subtitle: Can democracy empower us all?

challenging-peter-singers-ethics.speaker_desc: Peter Singer is a prominent philosopher, author and academic. He a professor of Bioethics at Princeton University, and specialises in practical ethics. His is best known for his work on global poverty and animal ethics. His book Animal Liberation was a key to the early environmental movement. Interviewed by Senior Producer at the IAI Charlie Barnett.
challenging-peter-singers-ethics.subtitle: Can morality be objective?

caught-in-time.speaker_desc: Philosopher Timothy Morton, author of Everything to Play For Marijam Didzgalvyte, and Guardian and UnHerd writer Freya India debate our obsession with recording every experience.
caught-in-time.subtitle: Should we stop recording and recounting our lives?

lifting-the-lid-on-the-economic-elite-ta.speaker_desc: Join Matt Kennard, co-founder and head of investigations at Declassified UK and a former fellow and then director at the Centre for Investigative Journalism (CIJ) in London, for an in-depth conversation with Tariq Ali. Ali is a writer, political activist and filmmaker, and is considered to be a leading figure of the international left. He has written numerous books on world history and politics as well as novels and scripts for the stage and screen.
lifting-the-lid-on-the-economic-elite-ta.subtitle: Challenging American empire

metaphysics-vs-consciousness.speaker_desc: Philip Goff is a philosopher of consciousness at Durham University. His research focuses on integrating consciousness into our scientific worldview. Hilary Lawson is a post-postmodern philosopher and a renowned critic of philosophical realism. He is best known for his work on reflexivity and his theory of Closure.
metaphysics-vs-consciousness.subtitle: In conversation: Philip Goff and Hilary Lawson

troubling-echoes-of-the-big-bang.speaker_desc: Martín López Corredoira is an astrophysicist and philosopher at the Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias in Tenerife, Spain. Marika Taylor is a Professor of Theoretical Physics, Pro-Vice Chancellor, and Head of the College of Engineering and Physical Sciences at the University of Birmingham. She previously studied under Stephen Hawking at Cambridge. Matt O'Dowd is a renowned professor of astrophysics and host and writer of the biggest physics and space show on YouTube, PBS Space Time. Hosted by Bjørn Ekeberg.
troubling-echoes-of-the-big-bang.subtitle: The false promise of Cosmic Background Radiation

respect-and-loathing-in-the-us.speaker_desc: Jeff Spinner-Halev is the Keenan Eminent Professor of Political Ethics at the University of North Carolina. He specialises in tensions within political identity and the ways people perceive their political opponents and social situation. Elizabeth Theiss-Morse is a professor of Political Science at the University of Nebraska-Lincon specialising in political psychology and identity. Their most recent book Respect and Loathing in American Democracy seeks to bridge the gaps between divided political tribes.
respect-and-loathing-in-the-us.subtitle: Can we bring back respect

politics-culture-and-mass-deception.speaker_desc: Peter York is a management consultant, author, and broadcaster, who has written columns for GQ and The Independent on Sunday.
politics-culture-and-mass-deception.subtitle: The big money behind culture wars

the-age-of-emergency.speaker_desc: Daron Acemoglu is the 2024 Nobel Prize winner in economics, an Institute Professor at MIT, and is a regular writer on political economy and the state of liberal society. He was named the most cited economist in 2015 and he was awarded with Prospects 2024 thinker of the year. Genevieve Gunther is a climate activist and author of the book The Language of Climate Politics. She is a founding director of the organisation End Climate Silence. Steve Koonin is a theoretical physicist and the former director of the Centr for Urban Science and Progress at NYU. He served as President Obama's Undersecretary of Science in the Department of Energy and has since researched the science behind political claims about climate change. Hosted by Sophie Scott Brown, a political philosopher at NYU.
the-age-of-emergency.subtitle: Can we overcome the polycrisis?

what-einstein-got-wrong-about-time-avsha.speaker_desc: Avshalom Elitzur is Professor in the Centre for Quantum Studies at Chapman University. He is best known for his groundbreaking work on the Elitzur–Vaidman bomb-testing problem in quantum mechanics.
what-einstein-got-wrong-about-time-avsha.subtitle: How physics ignores our experience

the-myth-of-universal-values-tommy-curry.speaker_desc: Tommy Curry is a philosophy professor at Edinburgh University where he holds a Personal Chair in Africana Philosophy and Black Male studies. His research focuses on Africana Philosophy, Critical Race Theory, Anti-Colonialism, Black Male Studies, and Public Health.
the-myth-of-universal-values-tommy-curry.subtitle: Liberal values cannot be universal

thinking-set-free.speaker_desc: Quantum consciousness theorist Stuart Hameroff, evolutionary psychology critic Subrena E. Smith, and best-selling author and psychologist Paul Bloom, explore the nature of thought, philosopher Hilary Lawson hosts.
thinking-set-free.subtitle: Does rationality guide us to truth?

the-economics-of-a-viable-palestinian-st.speaker_desc: Nadia Naser-Najjab is a Senior Lecturer in Palestine Studies at the European Centre for Palestine Studies, University of Exeter. Camila Vergara is a critical theorist, historian, and journalist. She is also a Senior Lecturer at the University of Essex. Guy Standing is a Professorial Research Associate at SOAS University of London. Uriel Abulof is an Associate Professor at Tel-Aviv University’s School of Political Science, Government and International Affairs. Hosted by Rana Mitter, ST Lee Chair in US-Asia Relations at the Harvard Kennedy School.
the-economics-of-a-viable-palestinian-st.subtitle: Creating a prosperous Palestine

russia-china-and-the-future-of-world-pow.speaker_desc: Michael Clarke is former Director of the Centre for Defence Studies and the International Policy Institute. He is now head of the School of Social Science and Public Policy at King's College London.
russia-china-and-the-future-of-world-pow.subtitle: An interview with Michael Clarke

screens-arent-causing-a-mental-health-cr.speaker_desc: Christopher Ferguson is a psychologist and professor at Stetson University Florida. In 2013 he was awarded a Distinguished Early Career Professional Award from the American Psychological Association. Ferguson strongly disputes the link between video games and violent behaviour as well as social media and mental health problems.
screens-arent-causing-a-mental-health-cr.subtitle: Why we're wrong to panic about screen time

marx-deserves-better-critics-ben-burgis.speaker_desc: Ben Burgis is a Jacobin columnist, an adjunct philosophy professor at Rutgers University and the host of the YouTube show and podcast Give Them An Argument. He’s the author of several books, most recently Christopher Hitchens: What He Got Right, How He Went Wrong, and Why He Still Matters.
marx-deserves-better-critics-ben-burgis.subtitle: Understanding Marxism's publicity problem

freedom-of-speech-is-necessary-to-democr.speaker_desc: John Ralston Saul is an award-winning essayist, novelist and a long-time champion of freedom of expression. He was the President of PEN International from 2009 to 2015, and has written a number of best-selling books on culture, politics and philosophy.
freedom-of-speech-is-necessary-to-democr.subtitle: An interview with John Ralston Saul

dark-energy-and-the-universe.speaker_desc: Claudia de Rham is a theoretical physicist working at the interface of gravity, cosmology, and particle physics. She is well known for her ground-breaking research into the theory of massive gravity. Priya Natarajan is a Professor of Astrophysics at Yale University and has been named as one of Time Magazine's top 100 most influential people in 2024 for her groundbreaking work in the field. Chris Lintott is Professor of Astrophysics in the Department of Physics at the University of Oxford. He is also the Gresham Professor of Astronomy at Gresham College, and has worked as a presenter on several popular science projects including with the BBC. Hosted by Jonjoe McFadden.
dark-energy-and-the-universe.subtitle: Physics and the unknown

the-case-for-conscious-ai.speaker_desc: Joscha Bach is an exceptional cognitive scientist who is pushing the limits of what we can achieve with Artificial Intelligence. As an AI researcher, he is constantly exploring new frontiers in cognitive architectures, mental representation, emotion, social modelling, and multi-agent systems.
the-case-for-conscious-ai.subtitle: Software and the self

the-truth-of-true-crime.speaker_desc: Margie Ratliff is a critically acclaimed American film producer. She is currently starting a non-profit organisation, Documentary Participants Empowerment Alliance, which seeks to support participants of documentaries. Camilla Hall is an award-winning documentary film Director and Executive Producer.
the-truth-of-true-crime.subtitle: Fiction and the impact on justice

in-search-of-oneself.speaker_desc: Joanna Kavenna hosts this debate on how our contemporary culture is influenced, shaped and potentially misinformed by our most recent self-help culture. Joining her are Frank Furedi, an emeritus professor of sociology at the University of Kent, John Vervaeke, an award-winning professor of psychology at the University of Toronto, and Isabel Millar, an associate resercher at Newcastle University.
in-search-of-oneself.subtitle: The risk of self reflection

shini-somara-on-stems-diversity-problem.speaker_desc: Dr Shini Somara was awarded a Doctorate in Engineering in 2004. The main objective of Shini's work today as a producer and broadecaster is to translate complex science and technology into engaging, accessible and informative content
shini-somara-on-stems-diversity-problem.subtitle: It's time we discussed it openly

ai-google-and-the-fight-for-culture.speaker_desc: Timothy Nguyen is a AI researcher at DeepMind and host of The Cartesian Cafe podcast. Previously an academic mathematical physicist working in gauge theory and quantum field theory. Interviewed by Darcy Bounsall.
ai-google-and-the-fight-for-culture.subtitle: Mathematics vs Art

philosophy-at-the-end-of-the-world.speaker_desc: Ben Ware is the co-director of the Centre for Philosophy and the Visual Arts at King’s College London. Ben has published widely on modern European philosophy, the philosophy of Wittgenstein, and modernist aesthetics.
philosophy-at-the-end-of-the-world.subtitle: The birth of a new civilisation

happily-ever-after.speaker_desc: Barry C. Smith hosts this debate between Jenny Kleeman, a distinguished journalist and TV presenter, Myriam François, a trailblazing journalist, filmmaker and writer, and Simon May, a Visiting Professor of Philosophy at King's College London.
happily-ever-after.subtitle: Romantic love isn't the only love

remaking-the-left-susan-neiman.speaker_desc: Susan Neiman, author of Evil in Modern Thought and Moral Clarity: A Guide for Grown-Up Idealists, is a moral philosopher and director of the Einstein Forum in Potsdam.
remaking-the-left-susan-neiman.subtitle: The left is not 'woke'

journey-to-other-dimensions-roger-penros.speaker_desc: Nobel prize-winner Roger Penrose, philosopher of quantum mechanics Avshalom Elitzur, and theoretical physicist Claudia de Rham debate the possibility of multiple dimensions. Hosted by Güneş Taylor.
journey-to-other-dimensions-roger-penros.subtitle: The physics of higher worlds

paterson-joseph-on-acting-race-and-ident.speaker_desc: Beginning his career as a Shakespearean actor, Joseph later transitioned to TV with appearances in Casualty and Law and Order, alongside a successful film career. He is the author of The Secret Diaries of Charles Ignatius Sancho, a novel which brilliantly conveys the life and times of the 18th-century composer through fictionalised diaries, letters, and commentary. He is also Chancellor of Oxford Brookes University which has cemented his status as both an actor and public intellectual.
paterson-joseph-on-acting-race-and-ident.subtitle: Making sense of ourselves

ode-to-outsiders.speaker_desc: Best-selling author, former law associate and award-winning academic, Amy Chua is the John M.
