Duff Jr Professor of Law at Yale Law School where she specialises in topics ranging from ethnic conflict, globalisation and international business transactions. Chua has been named one of Atlantic Monthly’s Brave Thinkers, one of Foreign Policy’s Global Thinkers and has been named one of TIME’s 100 most influential people.
ode-to-outsiders.subtitle: How immigrants change the world

beyond-the-reality-illusion-hilary-lawso.speaker_desc: A British philosopher best known for his theory of 'Closure', Hilary Lawson is an outspoken critic of philosophical realism and Editorial Director of the IAI.
beyond-the-reality-illusion-hilary-lawso.subtitle: Science and the end of the real

truth-theory-and-ultimate-reality.speaker_desc: Cutting-edge philosopher of physics Tim Maudlin, leading theoretical physicist Lisa Randall, insightful interdisciplinary thinker Abby Innes, and dark-matter physicist Bernard Carr, lock horns over whether theories are true or just our best guesses.
truth-theory-and-ultimate-reality.subtitle: Can science ever be true?

destiny-are-we-really-in-control.speaker_desc: Nadia Idle is a communications lecturer, intellectual and life-long activist from London and Cairo. She runs consciousness-raising workshops to fight atomisation and build collectivity, Jeremy Gilbert is Professor of Cultural and Political Theory at the University of East London, and the current editor of the journal New Formations. Keir Milburn is a writer, researcher and political activist.
destiny-are-we-really-in-control.subtitle: How society shapes us

how-moral-laws-fail-feminism-carol-gilli.speaker_desc: Carol Gilligan is an ethicist, psychologist and Professor of Humanities and Applied Psychology at New York University. She is a feminist icon, and the mind behind the revolutionary "ethics of care". She is best known for her now classic work In a Different Voice.
how-moral-laws-fail-feminism-carol-gilli.subtitle: An interview with Carol Gilligan

the-truth-about-quantum-computing.speaker_desc: Scott Aaronson is one of the top quantum complexity theorists in the world, renowned for both his research in quantum computing and computational complexity theory. Aaronson is famous for his popular blog Shtetl Optimized, which has kept the scientific community up to date on quantum hype for nearly the past two decades. His research and popular writing have earned him numerous awards, including the United States Presidential Early Career Award for Scientists and Engineers and the Alan T. Waterman Award. Aaronson is an Associate Professor of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science at MIT, but took leave of his academic commitments in 2022 to work at OpenAI.
the-truth-about-quantum-computing.subtitle: Beyond the hype

tyranny-of-the-pen.speaker_desc: Rana Mitter hosts this debate on the future of writing, whether its era has passed or if its cultural influence remains. Joining him for this panel are Ruth Padel, an award-winning poet, novelist and non-fiction writer, John Ralston Saul, an essayist, novelist and the former President of PEN International, and, finally, the acclaimed novelist and writer Jo Kavenna, who in 2013 was named as one of Granta’s Best Young British Novelists.
tyranny-of-the-pen.subtitle: Is the age of the pen over?

how-to-win-against-power-and-privilege-j.speaker_desc: Jolyon Maugham KC is an activist barrister, founder of the Good Law Project, and thorn in the side of the government. Jolyon is most famous for his use of the law to hold the government to account. Through the Good Law Project, Jolyon has sought to challenge the UK government's approach to Brexit, Covid, and transgender rights. From humble origins to a foremost legal force, Jolyon has become a key defence against government overreach.
how-to-win-against-power-and-privilege-j.subtitle: Rethinking our legal system

nancy-sherman-on-stoicism-and-society.speaker_desc: Nancy Sherman is Professor of Philosophy at Georgetown University and a New York Times Notable Author. Her latest book is Stoic Wisdom: Ancient Lessons for Modern Resilience. She is also the author of Afterwar: Healing the Moral Wounds of our Soldiers, among various other book on ethics, drawing especially from the ancients and her experience as the inaugural Distinguished Chair in Ethics at the United States Naval Academy.
nancy-sherman-on-stoicism-and-society.subtitle: Ancient philosophies for modern problems

the-agents-of-life.speaker_desc: Oxford biologist Denis Noble, pioneering researcher and geneticist Frances Ashcroft, and multidisciplinary scientist Johnjoe McFadden, debate life and its environment. Shini Somara hosts.
the-agents-of-life.subtitle: Should we abandon the idea of individual organisms

the-devil-in-all-of-us-paul-bloom.speaker_desc: Paul Bloom is a trailblazing Canadian American psychologist, bestselling author and celebrated speaker. He is the Brooks and Suzanne Ragen Professor Emeritus of psychology and cognitive science at Yale University and Professor of Psychology at the University of Toronto.
the-devil-in-all-of-us-paul-bloom.subtitle: Our human shadow

the-new-overlords.speaker_desc: Armen Sarkissian is the former President of Armenia, a physicist, investor, businessman and computer scientist. He spearheaded Armenia’s response to the 'Velvet Revolution' and border skirmishes with Azerbaijan. Claire Provost is an investigative journalist and co-founder and co-director of the non-profit Institute for Journalism and Social Change specialising in the backroom dealings of the largest corporations. Ali Allawi served as Deputy Prime Minister, Finance Minister and Minister of Defence of Iraq. He has also worked as a Professor at the University of Oxford, and a visiting Fellow at Harvard.
the-new-overlords.subtitle: Can we defeat monopolies?

avshalom-elitzur-on-physics-consciousnes.speaker_desc: Avshalom Elitzur is a Professor in the Centre for Quantum Studies at Chapman University in the United States and is deemed by many to be an intellectual powerhouse in both the fields of physics and philosophy. Having left school at sixteen to work as a lab technician, he presented a paper on quantum mechanics at Temple University, after which he was invited to Tel Aviv University to complete his doctorate on the subject. Elitzur is best known for his work on the Elitzur–Vaidman bomb-testing problem in quantum mechanics.
avshalom-elitzur-on-physics-consciousnes.subtitle: Mind, matter and beyond

rationality-in-the-dock.speaker_desc: Kathleen Stock is a daring and bold philosopher famous for her gender-critical views. She is a founding faculty fellow at the University of Austin. Carol Gilligan is a groundbreaking feminist, ethicist and psychologist based at New York University. Michael Shermer is the founder of The Skeptics Society. He is best known for his searing critiques of pseudoscience and the supernatural. Myriam François hosts.
rationality-in-the-dock.subtitle: Life at the end of reason

the-price-of-life-jenny-kleeman.speaker_desc: Jenny Kleeman is a distinguished British journalist, broadcaster and author. After two decades at the cutting edge of politics and culture, Kleeman boasts an impressive career spanning foreign correspondence, radio hosting, and presenting for the BBC, Channel 4 and HBO.
the-price-of-life-jenny-kleeman.subtitle: Who decides what we're worth?

the-laws-of-physics-are-not-fixed-joao-m.speaker_desc: João Magueijo is a Portuguese cosmologist and professor in theoretical physics at Imperial College London. He is a pioneer of the varying speed of light (VSL) theory.
the-laws-of-physics-are-not-fixed-joao-m.subtitle: A radical new path for physics and reality

amy-chua-on-tribes-and-tribalism.speaker_desc: Amy Chua is the John M. Duff Jr Professor of Law at Yale Law School where she specialises in ethnic conflict, globalisation and international business transactions. Alongside her best-selling parenting memoir, Battle Hymn of the Tiger Mother, Chua has written for major publications on the state of American politics, tribalism, identity politics, polarization and nationalism. Most recently, she was awarded the Lux and Veritas Prize by the Buckley Institute for fostering intellectual diversity in her classroom and beyond.
amy-chua-on-tribes-and-tribalism.subtitle: Understanding a divided world

the-great-rewiring-of-our-lives.speaker_desc: Jonathan Haidt, a renowned psychologist and NYU Stern professor, has made significant contributions to moral psychology. His latest book, The Anxious Generation, attributes teen mental distress to reduced free play and increased smartphone use. Katharine Birbalsingh CBE, 'Britain's strictest headmistress,' founded Michaela Community School in 2014, securing the country's top Progress 8 score. Emily Edlynn, PhD is a clinical psychologist passionate about integrating science and common-sense in parenting guidance to support healthier and more sustainable lives for parents. She is an award-winning author of the book, Autonomy-Supportive Parenting
the-great-rewiring-of-our-lives.subtitle: Have we ruined childhood forever?

better-left-unsaid.speaker_desc: Theodore Dalrymple is the pen-name for Anthony Malcolm Daniels, an English cultural critic, prolific writer, satirist, prison physician and psychiatrist. Vanessa King is a positive psychology expert and a board member at Action for Happiness. Simon Wessely is the Regius Professor of Psychiatry at King's College London and Former president of the Royal College of Psychiatrists. Our host Peter York is a columnist, broadcaster, management consultant, and author of 1982's The Sloane Ranger Handbook.
better-left-unsaid.subtitle: Our unexpressed emotions

conflict-and-its-future-david-petraeus.speaker_desc: General (U.S. Army, Ret.) David H. Petraeus is the Kissinger Fellow at Yale’s Jackson School of Global Affairs, the Chair of the Global Institute of a major investment firm, and a former director of the CIA. Petraeus served over 37 years in the U.S. military, culminating his career with six consecutive commands as a general officer, five of which were in combat, including command of the Surge in Iraq, command of U.S. Central Command, and command of coalition forces in Afghanistan. Following retirement from the military, Petraeus served as Director of the CIA during the global war on terror. He is the author, with Andrew Roberts, of Conflict: A Military History of the Evolution of Warfare from 1945 to Ukraine. Petraeus graduated with honors from the U.S. Military Academy and earned a Ph.D. at Princeton University.
conflict-and-its-future-david-petraeus.subtitle: Strategic leadership in action

the-tech-crisis-john-ralston-saul.speaker_desc: John Ralston Saul is an award-winning essayist, novelist and President Emeritus of PEN International. His 16 works, including Voltaire’s Bastards and The Collapse of Globalism, have been translated into 29 languages in 38 countries. He has been recognised internationally with a host of literary awards, including Chile’s Pablo Neruda Medal, South Korea’s Manhae Grand Prize for Literature, Italy’s Premio Letterario Internazionale and Canada’s Governor General’s Literary Award for Non-fiction.
the-tech-crisis-john-ralston-saul.subtitle: Humanity's response to tech and globalisation

consciousness-pre-dates-life-stuart-hame.speaker_desc: Stuart Hameroff is an American anesthesiologist and professor at the University of Arizona known for his studies of consciousness and his controversial claim, alongside Sir Roger Penrose, that consciousness originates from quantum states in neural microtubules.
consciousness-pre-dates-life-stuart-hame.subtitle: New evidence for a radical theory

land-ownership-and-hypocrisy.speaker_desc: Peter Singer is one of the most prominent figures in contemporary ethics. He has been recognized with numerous accolades, including the Berggruen Prize and, most recently, the BBVA Foundation Frontiers of Knowledge Awards. Dale Turner is an Associate Professor in the Department of Political Science and Centre for Indigenous Studies at the University of Toronto. He is working on his first hotly-anticipated novel, Vision, which draws from postcolonial and indigenous thought. Tommy J. Curry holds a Personal Chair in Africana philosophy and Black Male studies at the University of Edinburgh. In 2018, he won an American Book Award for the The Man-Not: Race, Class, Genre, and the Dilemmas of Black Manhood. Janne Teller is a critically-acclaimed writer of novels, essays, and short stories. Teller has received many literary awards including the Drassow’s Prize for literary works towards peace and human understanding. Hosted by Barry C. Smith.
land-ownership-and-hypocrisy.subtitle: How to deal with native land

in-defence-of-privacy.speaker_desc: Hugh Tomlinson KC is an English barrister and translator of the philosopher Gilles Deleuze. He is a noted specialist in media and information law including defamation, confidence, privacy and data protection. Tomlinson is famed for the central role he played in the litigation that sought the full disclosure of UK MP’s parliamentary expenses and was also a key figure in the News of The World phone-hacking case.
in-defence-of-privacy.subtitle: A worthy trade for freedom

the-future-of-particle-physics-harry-cli.speaker_desc: Harry Cliff is a particle physicist at the University of Cambridge and carries out research with the LHCb experiment at CERN’s Large Hadron Collider. He was a curator at the Science Museum, London for seven years and regularly gives public lectures and makes TV and radio appearances.
the-future-of-particle-physics-harry-cli.subtitle: The final science

the-real-me.speaker_desc: Steve Taylor is a senior lecturer in psychology at Leeds Beckett University and author of several best-selling books in the fields of psychology and spirituality. Jack Symes is a public philosopher, writer, and researcher at Durham University. Anneli Jefferson is a philosopher of psychology and moral philosophy, and lecturer at Cardiff University. And Frank Tallis is a clinical psychologist who specialises in obsessive compulsive disorder. Hosted by novelist Joanna Kavenna.
the-real-me.subtitle: Understanding our inner voices

nightmare-in-suburbia.speaker_desc: Mary Ann Sieghart hosts a debate on whether we need to abandon the nuclear family for a more communal model of living, or the family structures we're used to have withstood the test of time for a reason. Joining her are Nadia Idle, a communications lecturer and co-host of the left-wing podcast ACFM, Des Fitzgerald, a professor of Medical Humanities and Social Sciences at UCC, and Hannah Rich, a Senior Researcher at Theos. This event was sponsored by Theos.
nightmare-in-suburbia.subtitle: The myth of the nuclear family

the-trouble-with-language.speaker_desc: Hilary Lawson is a post-postmodern philosopher and a renowned critic of philosophical realism. He is best known for his work on reflexivity and his theory of Closure, which puts forward a non-realist metaphysics arguing that we close the openness of the world with our thought and language. Tim Maudlin is Professor of Philosophy at NYU and Founder and Director of the John Bell Institute for the Foundations of Physics. In his ground-breaking book The Metaphysics Within Physics, Truth and Paradox: Solving the Riddles and Quantum Non-Locality and Relativity, Maudlin challenges Einstein's criticisms of Quantum Mechanics as 'spooky action at a distance'. Maudlin is one of the world’s leading philosophical realists.
the-trouble-with-language.subtitle: Does language describe reality?

scott-aaronson-on-consciousness-and-ai-s.speaker_desc: Scott Aaronson is one of the top quantum complexity theorists in the world, renowned for both his research in quantum computing and computational complexity theory. Aaronson is famous for his popular blog Shtetl Optimized, which has kept the scientific community up to date on quantum hype for nearly the past two decades.
scott-aaronson-on-consciousness-and-ai-s.subtitle: The future of artificial intelligence

neoliberalism-a-soviet-nightmare.speaker_desc: Dr Abby Innes weaves political analysis with the scientific method to expose the ironic similarities between our current politics and the Soviet Union. She is an Associate Professor of Political Economy at the European Institute at the LSE. Her work focuses on party-state development, the transition from the Soviet system in Eastern Europe and the modern neoliberal state.
neoliberalism-a-soviet-nightmare.subtitle: Soviet and neoliberal false utopianism

exposing-the-windrush-scandal-amelia-gen.speaker_desc: Amelia Gentleman is an acclaimed British journalist, Guardian reporter and author of 'The Windrush Betrayal: Exposing the hostile Environment', which was a New Statesman and Spectator book of the year, shortlisted for the Orwell Prize for Political Writing and longlisted for Bailee Gifford prize.
exposing-the-windrush-scandal-amelia-gen.subtitle: Journalism’s impact on political scandals

navigating-the-new-world-order.speaker_desc: Christina Lamb OBE is the Chief Foreign Correspondent for the Times and Sunday Times, bestselling author and honorary fellow of University College Oxford. Armen Sarkissian is the former President of Armenia, a physicist, investor, businessman and computer scientist. And Bronwen Maddox is the Director and Chief Executive of Chatham House. Before joining Chatham House, Bronwen was Director of the Institute for Government, and she served as the chief foreign commentator, foreign editor and US editor at The Times. Hosted by the BBC's Roger Hearing.
navigating-the-new-world-order.subtitle: The new world disorder

belief-value-and-superstition.speaker_desc: Winston Marshall is a podcaster and political/cultural commentator, writing for publications such as The Spectator. He was previously member and is co-founder of the famous folk rock band Mumford & Sons. Paul Bloom is a psychologist and professor at Yale University and the University of Toronto. He has written about empathy, pleasure and suffering, for example in his book Against Empathy: The Case for Rational Compassion. Janne Teller is a novellist whose works have sold millions of copies. Her 2010 novel Nothing received numerous awards. Fellipe do Vale is the assistant professor of biblical and systematic theology at Trinity Evangelical Divinity School in Illinois. His research focuses on the connection between moral theology and theological anthropology. Rana Mitter hosts.
belief-value-and-superstition.subtitle: Are we entering a new age of belief?

barry-smith-on-consciousness-and-the-sen.subtitle: How our senses affect our reality

genes-are-not-the-blueprint-for-life.speaker_desc: Denis Noble is Professor Emeritus and co-Director of Computational Physiology at Oxford University. Noble was one of the pioneers of Systems Biology and developed the first viable mathematical model of the working heart. His books include the first popular science book on the subject, The Music of Life, which has been translated into 12 languages.
genes-are-not-the-blueprint-for-life.subtitle: Going beyond the selfish gene

telling-the-story-of-war.speaker_desc: Sophie Scott-Brown is joined by Myriam François, an author, broadcaster and academic on issues related to Islam, France and the Middle East, and Uriel Abulof, Professor of Political Science at Tel Aviv University and author of The Mortality and Morality of Nations, to examine whether we can overcome the limitations of truth in times of war.
telling-the-story-of-war.subtitle: Telling the story of war

ai-and-the-creativity-crisis.speaker_desc: Judith Donath is a social media expert and fellow at Harvard's Berkman Center, as well as the founder of the Social Media Group at the MIT Media Lab. Martha Fiennes is an award-winning film director, writer and producer, best known for her films Onegin and Chromophobia. John Ralston Saul is an award-winning essayist, novelist and a long-time champion of freedom of expression. He has written numerous best-selling books on culture, politics and philosophy. Hosted by Niki Seth Smith and sponsored by The New Humanist.
ai-and-the-creativity-crisis.subtitle: Are we seeing the end of human made art?

mystery-in-the-making.speaker_desc: Theoretical physicists Claudia de Rham and Avshalom Elitzur debate the mysteries of the universe with experimental CERN physicist Harry Cliff.
mystery-in-the-making.subtitle: Does science provide a complete explanation?

stoicism-reimagined-nancy-sherman.speaker_desc: Nancy Sherman is a Professor of Philosophy at Georgetown University who has conducted research in general ethics, moral psychology and the history of philosophy with a focus on the stoic tradition. She is a New York Times Notable Author and, from 1997-1999, served as the inaugural Distinguished Chair in Ethics at the U.S. Naval Academy.
stoicism-reimagined-nancy-sherman.subtitle: Nancy Sherman on ancient wisdom for a modern world

the-future-of-politics-john-bercow.speaker_desc: John Bercow is one of the most recognisable and iconoclastic figures in British politics. As Speaker of the House of Commons from 2009 to 2019, his distinctive bellow for order spanned the tenure of four Prime Ministers and a decade of political turmoil.
the-future-of-politics-john-bercow.subtitle: Finding order amongst the chaos

jessica-defino-on-the-politics-of-beauty.speaker_desc: Jessica De Fino is an award-winning beauty reporter and critic (New York Times, Sunday Times, Vice). She writes the beauty advice column Ask Ugly and publishes a weekly newsletter The Review of Beauty which “basically gives the middle finger to the entire beauty industry” (HuffPost).
jessica-defino-on-the-politics-of-beauty.subtitle: Why the beauty industry needs a revamp

singles-sex-and-society.speaker_desc: Güneş Taylor hosts a debate on the changing face of relationships, the increasing number of singles in our society and whether marriage has become obsolete. She is joined by Yasmin Benoit, an asexual activist, model and writer, Edward Davies, the Policy Director of the Centre of Social Justice, and Aline Laurent-Mayard, a journalist, author and podcast host.
singles-sex-and-society.subtitle: Is marriage finally obsolete?

tasneem-husain-on-creativity-in-physics.speaker_desc: Tasneem Zehra Husain is a theoretical physicist, writer, and educator. She is one of few Pakistani women to obtain a doctorate in physics, and the first Pakistani woman string theorist. Only the Longest Threads is her debut novel.
tasneem-husain-on-creativity-in-physics.subtitle: Why we need more creative minds in science

reality-after-realism.speaker_desc: Michael Della Rocca is a leading authority on Spinoza and expert in early modern philosophy. He is Sterling Professor of Philosophy at Yale University. Hilary Lawson is a philosopher and editorial director of the Institute of Art and Ideas. His main work, Closure: a story of Everything, has been described as ‘the first non-realist metaphysics’. Renowned intellectual historian Sophie Scott-Brown hosts.
reality-after-realism.subtitle: Embracing the death of language

why-we-fail-to-predict-market-crashes.speaker_desc: Economist and former BBC Chief Business correspondent Professor Linda Yueh holds positions as Fellow of Economics at St Edmunds College, Oxford, as well as Adjunct Professor of Economics at London Business School.
why-we-fail-to-predict-market-crashes.subtitle: Learning lessons from the history of finance

the-life-and-philosophy-of-paterson-jose.speaker_desc: Paterson Joseph is a cultural icon, best known for his roles in TV and film, from 'Peep Show' to 'Wonka', and his career in theatre with the Royal Shakespeare Company. He is also the current Chancellor of Oxford Brookes University. Jenny Kleeman hosts.
the-life-and-philosophy-of-paterson-jose.subtitle: Acting, performance, and identity

violence-vengeance-and-virtue.speaker_desc: Peter Singer is one of the most prominent figures in contemporary ethics. He is an Australian moral philosopher and the Emeritus Ira W. DeCamp Professor of Bioethics at Princeton University and the author of Animal Liberation. Ghada Karmi is a Palestinian-born academic, physician and author. She held a number of research appointments on Middle Eastern politics and culture at the School of Oriental and African Studies, and in the Universities of Durham and Leeds. Uriel Abulof is an associate professor at Tel-Aviv University’s School of Political Science, Government and International Affairs. Mary Ann Seighart hosts.
violence-vengeance-and-virtue.subtitle: The relationship between violence and ethics

general-david-petraeus-on-ukraine-israel.speaker_desc: General (U.S. Army, Ret.) David H. Petraeus is the Kissinger Fellow at Yale’s Jackson School of Global Affairs, and a former director of the CIA. Petraeus served over 37 years in the U.S. military, culminating his career with six consecutive commands as a general officer, five of which were in combat, including command of the Surge in Iraq, command of U.S. Central Command, and command of coalition forces in Afghanistan. This interview was recorded on Sunday 26th May 2024, at HowTheLightGetsIn, Hay-on-Wye.
general-david-petraeus-on-ukraine-israel.subtitle: What the world can learn from US foreign policy

ai-and-the-end-of-humanity.speaker_desc: Eliezer Yudkowsky is a leading AI safety researcher, renowned for popularizing the concept of friendly AI. Scott Aaronson is one of the top quantum complexity theorists in the world, renowned for both his research in quantum computing and computational complexity theory. A self-confessed nerd with a first-class degree in astrophysics, Liv Boeree combined her science background and passion for games to become one of the most recognizable faces in professional poker. Joscha Bach is a cognitive scientist who is pushing the limits of what we can achieve with Artificial Intelligence. Güneş Taylor hosts.
ai-and-the-end-of-humanity.subtitle: Does AI change what it means to be human?

the-indian-century.speaker_desc: S.Y. Quraishi is an Indian civil servant who rose to be the 17th Chief Election Commissioner of India. Kate Sullivan de Estrada is the Director of the Contemporary South Asian Studies Programme and Associate Professor in the International Relations of South Asia. Alpa Shah is a Professor of Anthropology at the London School of Economics, specialising in Indian and Nepalese minority and indigenous groups. Hosted by Rana Mitter, Harvard University ST Lee Chair in US-Asia Relations.
the-indian-century.subtitle: Does India need the West?

ruby-wax-on-meaning-and-mental-health.speaker_desc: Mental health, depression, comedy. Ruby Wax OBE is a seminal British-American talent, excelling as an actress, writer, TV personality, and mental health advocate. Her latest book is I Am Not As Well As I Thought I Was.
ruby-wax-on-meaning-and-mental-health.subtitle: Finding meaning in the madness

nihilism-and-the-meaning-of-life-nolen-g.speaker_desc: Nolen Gertz is Associate Professor of Applied Philosophy at the University of Twente, the Coordinator of the Human Condition Research Line of ESDIT, and a Senior Researcher of the 4TU.Centre for Ethics and Technology. His research focuses primarily on the intersection of political philosophy, existential phenomenology, and philosophy of technology.
nihilism-and-the-meaning-of-life-nolen-g.subtitle: Losing hope in the information age

how-oceans-shaped-the-world-helen-czersk.speaker_desc: Dr Helen Czerski is a a physicist, oceanographer, presenter and author, currently working as an Associate Professor at University College London in the Department of Mechanical Engineering.
how-oceans-shaped-the-world-helen-czersk.subtitle: Saving the heart of our planet

life-death-and-specialisation.speaker_desc: David Healy is a psychiatrist, scientist, author and professor of psychiatry at Bangor University in the United Kingdom. Caitjan Gainty is a historian of science and expert on twentieth century health and healthcare. She is a Senior Lecturer in the History of Science, Technology & Medicine at King’s College London. Nick Lane is a British biochemist and outstanding science communicator, asking the difficult question: what is the origin of life? He is a Professor of Evolutionary Biochemistry at University College London and a bestselling author. Hosted by Mark Salter.
life-death-and-specialisation.subtitle: Life, death, and specialisation

john-vervaeke-the-purpose-of-consciousne.speaker_desc: John Vervaeke is an award-winning professor of psychology, cognitive science, and Buddhist psychology at the University of Toronto.
john-vervaeke-the-purpose-of-consciousne.subtitle: Towards a naturalistic account of consciousness

how-to-heal-a-divided-nation-grafton-tan.speaker_desc: Grafton Tanner is the author of The Hours Have Lost Their Clock: The Politics of Nostalgia with Repeater Books. He also hosts Delusioneering, an audio series about the myths of capitalism, and writes and performs music with his band Superpuppet.
how-to-heal-a-divided-nation-grafton-tan.subtitle: We're not as polarised as we think

a-radical-step-to-gender-equality.speaker_desc: Join author and ethnographer Kristen Ghodsee, writer and editor Mary Harrington, and transhumanist and researcher Anders Sandberg as they debate the potentials of artificial wombs. Hosted by Güneş Taylor.
a-radical-step-to-gender-equality.subtitle: Making childbirth a technical phenomenon

sleeping-with-the-enemy-paul-dolan.speaker_desc: Paul Dolan is a Professor in the Department of Social Policy at the London School of Economics and Political Science where he holds a Chair in Behavioural Science.
sleeping-with-the-enemy-paul-dolan.subtitle: Why we should date those we disagree with

smashing-particles-at-the-energy-frontie.speaker_desc: Sarah Demers is an American physicist and the Horace D Taft associate professor of physics at Yale University.
smashing-particles-at-the-energy-frontie.subtitle: Discover the building blocks of the universe

myths-modernity-and-meaning-betty-sue-fl.speaker_desc: Betty Sue Flowers is a writer, editor and international business consultant. She is the former director of the Lyndon Baines Johnson Library and Museum and an Emerita Professor of English at the University of Texas at Austin. She pioneered the modern, psychological appreciation of ancient myths alongside the esteemed Joseph Campbell - whose work was famously the inspiration for the Star Wars franchise.
myths-modernity-and-meaning-betty-sue-fl.subtitle: The power of legend

the-reality-of-living-forever.speaker_desc: David Gems is a Professor of Biogerontology at University College London. Sunetra Gupta is a Professor of Theoretical Epidemiology at the University of Oxford, as well as an acclaimed novelist and essayist. Nolen Gertz is an Assistant Professor of Applied Philosophy at the University of Twente known for his work on nihilism. Güneş Taylor hosts.
the-reality-of-living-forever.subtitle: Should we stop resisting death?

protest-democracy-and-power.speaker_desc: Peter Tatchell is a human rights campaigner best known for his work with LGBTQ+ movements, a member of the gay rights group Outrage! and director of the Peter Tatchell Foundation, a human rights organization. Peter began campaigning in London, organizing sit-ins at pubs that refused to serve gay people and protests against the classification of homosexuality as an illness.
protest-democracy-and-power.subtitle: A worthy trade for freedom

mind-matter-and-everything.speaker_desc: Sean Carroll is the Homewood Professor of Natural Philosophy at John Hopkins University, and Fractal Faculty at the Santa Fe Institute. He also hosts the weekly podcast Mindscape, which explores interesting ideas in science, philosophy, culture, and the arts. Ellen Langer is Professor of Psychology at Harvard University and the author of The Mindful Body. Among other honours, she is the recipient of three distinguished scientist awards, a Guggenheim Fellowship, and the Liberty Science Genius Award. She is widely known as the mother of mindfulness. Tamar Gendler is Yale University's Dean of the Faculty of Arts and Sciences, the Vincent J. Scully Professor of Philosophy, and Professor of Psychology and Cognitive Science. A philosophical powerhouse bringing together the techniques of traditional Anglo-American philosophy with empirical work from psychology and other social sciences. Jack Symes hosts.
mind-matter-and-everything.subtitle: Can consciousness be solved by science?

astonishment-fear-and-quantum-physics-ti.speaker_desc: One of the world's foremost philosophers of physics, Tim Maudlin is Professor of Philosophy at NYU and Founder and Director of the John Bell Institute for the Foundations of Physics.
astonishment-fear-and-quantum-physics-ti.subtitle: Accepting Bell's theorem

a-universe-of-possibility.speaker_desc: George Ellis is a distinguished professor at the University of Cape Town in South Africa. He co-authored 'The Large Scale Structure of Space-Time' with physicist Stephen Hawking, and is considered one of the world's leading theorists in cosmology.
a-universe-of-possibility.subtitle: How reality emerges from chance

bill-browder-on-surviving-putin.speaker_desc: Bill Browder is an American-born British financier and political activist. He is the CEO and co-founder of Hermitage Capital Management, the investment advisor to the Hermitage Fund, which at a time was the largest foreign portfolio investor in Russia.
bill-browder-on-surviving-putin.subtitle: Life as an enemy of the state

crack-up-capitalism-quinn-slobodian.speaker_desc: Quinn Slobodian is an author and historian, specialising in modern Germany and international history. He is currently professor of international history at Boston University. He is also contributing writer to New Statesman, co-editor of Contemporary European History and co-director of the History and Political Economy Project. His most recent book is Crack-up Capitalism: Market Radicals and the Dream of a World Without Democracy.
crack-up-capitalism-quinn-slobodian.subtitle: Can we free ourselves from democracy?

danger-safety-and-the-future.speaker_desc: Frank Furedi is an emeritus professor of sociology at the University of Kent, Carol Gilligan is a pioneering feminist and ethicist best known for her revolutionary "ethics of care" theory and Paul Dolan is a leading behavioural scientist and bestselling author, with works like "Happy Ever After" influencing public policy. They join host Isabel Hilton for a debate on our changing relationship with risk.
danger-safety-and-the-future.subtitle: Is risk aversion damaging the next generation?

the-challenge-to-optimism.speaker_desc: Sir Angus Deaton is the Senior Scholar and Professor of Economics at the Princeton School of Public Affair and a Nobel prize-winner. Gillian Tett is an award-winning author, journalist, Provost of King's College Cambridge, and U.S. editor at large at the Financial Times.
the-challenge-to-optimism.subtitle: Economics needs philosophy

inside-anarchy-sophie-scott-brown.speaker_desc: Sophie Scott-Brown is the former Director of Gresham College and fellow at the University of St Andrews. An inspiring intellectual historian with research interests in modern European political thought, Anarchism, and the history of education, Sophie is also a fellow of the Higher Education Academy and of the Royal History Society. She is an author excited by historical biography as a means of understanding ideas. Her work includes The Histories of Raphael Samuel: A Portrait of a People’s Historian and Colin Ward and the Art of Everyday Anarchy.
inside-anarchy-sophie-scott-brown.subtitle: Inside anarchy

physics-particles-and-fairytales.speaker_desc: Sabine Hossenfelder is a theoretical physicist, author, musician, and science communicator who researches quantum gravity. Gavin Salam is an Oxford-based theoretical physicist celebrated for his groundbreaking work in quantum chromodynamics, the theory describing the strong nuclear force. He was formerly a Senior Research Scientist at CERN and the European Organization for Nuclear Research. Bjørn Ekeberg is a philosopher of science whose main interests lie in the limits of scientific knowledge. He argues that our current understanding of the universe, the Big Bang, and nearly all of Big Bang cosmology is based on faith rather than experimental evidence.
physics-particles-and-fairytales.subtitle: Towards the end of the standard model

electricity-creates-consciousness-nick-l.speaker_desc: Nick Lane is an multi-award-winning biochemist and an outstanding science communicator in the origins of life field. He is a Professor of Evolutionary Biochemistry at University College London and a bestselling author of five critically-acclaimed books on evolutionary biochemistry, selling over 150,000 copies worldwide. Transformer: The Deep Chemistry of Life and Death (2022) explores the elusive chemical logic of life, from genetic information to consciousness.
electricity-creates-consciousness-nick-l.subtitle: Why our idea of consciousness may be wrong

the-dream-of-democracy.speaker_desc: Mary Ann Seighart hosts an excellent panel on the future of democracy. Joining her are Nadhim Zahawi, former Chairman of the Conservative Party, Susan Neiman, a daring American philosopher and director of the Einstein Forum in Potsdam, and Philip Collins, Writer-in-Chief at The Draft and former speech writer for Tony Blair.
the-dream-of-democracy.subtitle: Does money poison politics?

how-to-use-adventure-for-wellbeing.speaker_desc: Belinda Kirk is an explorer, entrepreneur and author of best-selling book Adventure Revolution. She is a veteran of fifteen major expeditions and over forty remote filming trips. In 2010, Kirk skippered the first all-female boat to row around Britain.
how-to-use-adventure-for-wellbeing.subtitle: Why it's crucial to leave your comfort zone

the-matrix-myths-and-metaphysics.speaker_desc: Eric Weinstein is the host of the premiere podcast The Portal. A doctor of mathematical physics, Eric has proposed that the scientific consensus in physics is broken and radical change in the community is needed. Becky Parker is a renowned physicist who won the first RAS Patrick Moore Medal for outstanding work as a teacher of astronomy. She has received an Honorary Fellowship at the Institute of Physics. Hilary Lawson is a philosopher and an outspoken critic of philosophical realism. He is best known for his theory of Closure, which puts forward a non-realist metaphysics. He is the founder and editorial director of the IAI.
the-matrix-myths-and-metaphysics.subtitle: Is metaphysics still relevant?

the-ai-enigma.speaker_desc: Cognitive scientist Joscha Bach, and AI sceptic and philosopher Mazviita Chirimuuta grapple with the future of intelligence. Hosted by author Cory Doctorow.
the-ai-enigma.subtitle: Is artificial intelligence a threat?

biology-beyond-genes-denis-noble.speaker_desc: One of the pioneers of systems biology, Denis Noble is a Professor Emeritus at the University of Oxford. Renowned for challenging convention, Noble explores the interplay between an organism and its genes.
biology-beyond-genes-denis-noble.subtitle: Rethinking evolution

frank-furedi-interview-rethinking-identi.speaker_desc: Frank Furedi is a emeritus professor of sociology at the University of Kent. Since the late 1990s, he has been widely cited about his views on why Western societies find it so difficult to engage with risk and uncertainty. His book Invitation to Terror: expanding the empire of the unknown explores the way in which the threat of terrorism has become amplified through the ascendancy of precautionary thinking.
frank-furedi-interview-rethinking-identi.subtitle: On rethinking identity

naming-and-shaming.speaker_desc: Joanna Kavenna is an award-winning novelist. Sophie Scott-Brown is a prestigious intellectual historian, a lecturer at the University of Oxford, and a Director of the Europaeum Institute of European History. Peter Tatchell is an inspiring human rights campaigner, a member of the gay rights group Outrage!, and director of the Peter Tatchell Foundation, a human rights organization. Florence Read hosts.
naming-and-shaming.subtitle: Do we need shame for social progress?

scientists-and-their-demons-jimena-canal.speaker_desc: Jimena Canales is a pioneering historian of science and an expert in 19th and 20th century history of the physical sciences. She is currently Vice-President of the Board of the American Council of Learned Societies (ACLS).
scientists-and-their-demons-jimena-canal.subtitle: On scientists and their demons

the-centre-of-the-universe.speaker_desc: Lisa Randall is an Honorary Fellow of the Institute of Physics and Frank B. Baird, Jr. Professor of Science on the physics faculty of Harvard University. She has been named one of the most promising theoretical physicists of her generation. Neil Turok is a preeminent mathematical physicist. He is the inaugural Higgs Chair of Theoretical Physics at the University of Edinburgh and director emeritus of the Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics. Martin Cohen is a multitalented philosopher, author and journalist who has become a household name in popular philosophy. His books include the bestseller ‘101 Philosophy Problems’, now published in a dozen languages.
the-centre-of-the-universe.subtitle: Does science carry a human bias?

mental-health-reimagined-mark-salter.speaker_desc: Mark Salter is a consultant psychiatrist based in London’s East End, specialising in risk, untowardness and media portrayals of mental distress.
mental-health-reimagined-mark-salter.subtitle: Why we should value the awful

the-life-and-philosophy-of-alastair-camp.speaker_desc: Formerly Director of Communications for Tony Blair's New Labour government, Alastair Campbell is now an editor-at-large at The New European, has launched with Rory Stewart the most successful political podcast in the UK, 'The Rest Is Politics', and authored the acclaimed book, 'But What Can I Do?'
the-life-and-philosophy-of-alastair-camp.subtitle: Brexit, Labour and the problem with politics

fragments-and-reality.speaker_desc: Jack Symes is the producer of The Panpsycast Philosophy Podcast and editor of the Bloomsbury series Talking about Philosophy. He is currently Teacher and Researcher at Durham University, UK. Michael Della Rocca is Sterling Professor of Philosophy at Yale University and author of The Parmenidean Ascent. Tim Maudlin is Professor of Philosophy at New York University and the Founder and Director of the John Bell Institute for the Foundations of Physics. Kathleen Higgins is Professor of Philosophy at the University of Texas at Austin and the author of Comic Relief: Nietzsche's “Gay Science”.
fragments-and-reality.subtitle: Is the world really made of separate parts?

fascist-passions-judith-butler.speaker_desc: Judith Butler is Distinguished Professor in the Graduate School and formerly the Maxine Elliot Chair in the Department of Comparative Literature and the Program of Critical Theory at the University of California, Berkeley. They are most well-known for their ground-breaking book Gender Trouble (1990) and their theory of performativity.
fascist-passions-judith-butler.subtitle: Judith Butler on the animosity toward gender

democratic-capitalism-in-crisis.speaker_desc: Martin Wolf is Associate Editor and Chief Economics Commentator at the Financial Times, London. He was awarded the CBE (Commander of the British Empire) in 2000 for services to financial journalism. Sergei Guriev is a Russian economist, who is provost and a professor of economics at the Institut d'études politiques in Paris. From 2016 to 2019, he was the chief economist at the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development.
democratic-capitalism-in-crisis.subtitle: Has the snake eaten its own tail?

in-conversation-sabine-hossenfelder-and-.speaker_desc: Sabine Hossenfelder is a theoretical physicist, author, musician, and science communicator who researches quantum gravity. Hilary is a non-realist philosopher known for his theory of closure.
in-conversation-sabine-hossenfelder-and-.subtitle: On physics' need for philosophy

consciousness-and-the-material-reality-a.speaker_desc: Avshalom C. Elitzur is a Professor in the Centre for Quantum Studies at Chapman University in the United States. He is best known for his work on the Elitzur–Vaidman bomb-testing problem in quantum mechanics.
consciousness-and-the-material-reality-a.subtitle: Thinking outside the laws of physics

peter-woit-the-fall-and-resurrection-of-.speaker_desc: Peter Woit is an American theoretical physicist. He is a senior lecturer in the Mathematics department at Columbia University. Woit is the author of Not Even Wrong: The Failure of String Theory and the Continuing Challenge to Unify the Laws of Physics, and writes a blog by the same name. He recently appeared on The Lex Fridman Podcast.
peter-woit-the-fall-and-resurrection-of-.subtitle: The elusive world of quaternions

creativity-and-freedom.speaker_desc: Joanna Kavenna is an award-winning novelist, essayist, and travel writer. Her latest book, Zed, is a brilliant tale of big-tech dystopia and life under a global media tech corporation. Jolyon Maugham is an activist barrister. As founder of the Good Law Project, Jolyon has challenged the UK government's approach to Brexit, Covid, and transgender rights. Myriam François is a trailblazing filmmaker and writer. As founder and CEO of her own production company, Myriam specialises in documentary films which centre marginalised voices. Jack Symes hosts.
creativity-and-freedom.subtitle: Should there be limits on creative freedom?

the-ai-apocalypse.speaker_desc: Stephanie Hare is a researcher, broadcaster and author with expertise in politics, technology and history. Michael Wooldridge, head of the Computer Science department at the University of Oxford, is a leading figure in AI. Liv Boeree is a science communicator, host of the “Win-Win” podcast and one of the most successful female poker players of all time. Timothy Nguyen, a top AI researcher at Google DeepMind, he also hosts the podcast "Cartesian Café".
the-ai-apocalypse.subtitle: Is AI as dangerous as we think?

conspiracy-and-belief.speaker_desc: Michael Shermer is an American science writer, historian of science, executive director of The Skeptics Society, and founding publisher of Skeptic magazine, a publication focused on investigating pseudoscientific and supernatural claims. The author of over a dozen books, Shermer is known for engaging in debates on pseudoscience and religion in which he emphasizes scientific scepticism.
conspiracy-and-belief.subtitle: An interview with Michael Shermer

the-life-and-philosophy-of-rory-stewart.speaker_desc: An award winning writer, foremost politician and chart-topping broadcaster, Rory Stewart is one of the leading political figures of his generation. His career kicked off as the deputy governor of the Maysan province in Iraq during the 2003 invasion. He later authored an award-winning memoir of his time in Central Asia. He was then elected to be an MP where he was Secretary of State for International Development. Following his withdrawal from frontline politics, Rory has launched The Rest is Politics podcast with Alastair Campbell which is regularly the top political podcast in the UK. He is interviewed by Isabel Hilton, the founder of China Dialogue and a regular political commentator.
the-life-and-philosophy-of-rory-stewart.subtitle: Rethinking the future of conservatism

climate-culture-and-creativity-lola-youn.speaker_desc: Lola Young is an actress, author, and crossbench peer. She is also Chancellor of the University of Nottingham.
climate-culture-and-creativity-lola-youn.subtitle: Art and culture against climate change

the-tears-of-the-west.speaker_desc: Columnist at the Spectator and Marketing Executive at Ogilvy & Mather Rory Sutherland joins Nobel Prize winning economist Angus Deaton and Professor Emeritus of Sociology at the University of California Berkeley Arlie Hochschild. Roger Hearing, former news presenter for the BBC World Service, hosts.
the-tears-of-the-west.subtitle: Can we rekindle faith in civilisation?

loving-oneself-and-loving-others.speaker_desc: Carol Gilligan is a Professor of Humanities and Applied Psychology at New York University. A feminist icon, she is best known for the classic In a Different Voice (1982). Katarzyna de Lazari-Radek is a Professor of Philosophy at the University of Lodz. She is best known for her work on utilitarianism in collaboration with Peter Singer, most famously, The Point of View of the Universe (2014). Richard Wrangham is a Research Professor of Biological Anthropology at Harvard University. He is best known for his seminal work on primate social behaviour and the evolution of violence. Robert Lawrence Kuhn is the creator, writer, host and executive producer of Closer To Truth. Kuhn has written or edited over 30 books, including 'The Mystery of Existence: Why is there Anything At All?' and 'Closer to Truth: Challenging Current Belief'.
loving-oneself-and-loving-others.subtitle: How much should we really value altruism?

the-fatal-flaw-in-human-judgement-cass-s.speaker_desc: Cass Sunstein is a Harvard Law Professor, best-selling author of Nudge, The World According to Star Wars, and Noise: A Flaw in Human Judgement, which was co-authored with Daniel Kahnemann and Olivier Sibony. He is also a former advisor to President Barack Obama.
the-fatal-flaw-in-human-judgement-cass-s.subtitle: Why our systems are riddled with bias

searching-for-sanity-in-a-chaotic-world-.speaker_desc: Ruby Wax is a famed actor and author of the Sunday Times Bestseller, 'I'm Not As Well As I Thought I Was'.
searching-for-sanity-in-a-chaotic-world-.subtitle: Finding peace in the modern day

the-future-of-physics.speaker_desc: Join quantum physicist Suchitra Sebastian and YouTube sensation Dominic Walliman, as they explore the future of cutting edge physics.
the-future-of-physics.subtitle: Physics and beyond

homes-and-hierarchy.speaker_desc: Kristen Ghodsee is an award-winning author and firebrand ethnographer. Tom Copley is Sadiq Khan’s right-hand man the Deputy Mayor of London for Housing. Dr Anna Minton is an investigative journalist, policy researcher and author specialising in the London housing crisis. Liam Halligan is an award-winning economist, journalist, broadcaster and author. The host, Mary Ann Sieghart, is an English author, journalist, radio presenter and former assistant editor of The Times.
homes-and-hierarchy.subtitle: Ending the fantasy of homeownership

yanis-varoufakis-interview.speaker_desc: Yanis Varoufakis is a bestselling author, economist, professor, and former Finance Minister of Greece. His latest book Technofeudalism charts the end of Capitalism and the rise of new cloud feudal lords. Eshe Nelson is a reporter for the New York Times based in London. Her work focuses on central bank policy and the British macroeconomy.
yanis-varoufakis-interview.subtitle: On the prelude to feudalism

sophie-grace-chappell-epiphanies-ethics-.speaker_desc: Sophie-Grace Chappell is a Professor of Philosophy who writes about ethics, politics, feminism and epistemology. She argues that we should allow our epiphanies to guide us.
sophie-grace-chappell-epiphanies-ethics-.subtitle: On the phenomenology of being

bodies-brains-and-mental-health-david-he.speaker_desc: David Healy is a renowned professor of psychiatry at Bangor University. He is a psychiatrist, psychopharmacologist, scientist and author known for criticising a lack of neutrality regarding psychotropic drugs.
bodies-brains-and-mental-health-david-he.subtitle: Physiology's challenge to medicine

roger-penrose-interview-quantum-consciou.speaker_desc: Sir Roger Penrose is a world-renowned physicist, best known for his work on general relativity and sharing the Wolf Prize for Physics with Stephen Hawking for their work on black holes.
roger-penrose-interview-quantum-consciou.subtitle: On quantum mechanics and consciousness

the-perception-bias.speaker_desc: Sophie Scott-Brown is joined by Daniel Kahneman, a Nobel prize-winning economist, Ellen Langer, a Harvard psychologist known as the mother of mindfulness, and Hilary Lawson, a post-postmodernist philosopher and editorial director of the Institute of Art and Ideas, to debate whether perceptual biases influence or alter the way we see the world.
the-perception-bias.subtitle: Is bias at the heart of how we see the world?

the-truth-of-fiction-jesse-norman.speaker_desc: Conservative Party politician, Jesse Norman, explores the use of fiction to uncover the truth in contemporary issues.
the-truth-of-fiction-jesse-norman.subtitle: Harnessing the power of story

utopian-living.speaker_desc: Kristen Ghodsee is an anthropologist and Professor of Russian and East European Studies at the University of Pennsylvania. Her latest work is Everyday Utopia, which explores pioneering experiments in communal living.
utopian-living.subtitle: How community can save us

perception-as-a-fantasy-donald-hoffman.speaker_desc: Donald Hoffman is an American cognitive psychologist working at the University of California, Irvine. Hoffman's Interface Theory of Perception suggests that, instead of presenting reality as it "really is", our perception is like a desktop interface that has evolved to ensure survival. To advance his theory of consciousness, Hoffman explores cutting edge physics that suggests spacetime is non-fundamental. For Hoffman we must explain consciousness in fundamental terms, beyond spacetime.
perception-as-a-fantasy-donald-hoffman.subtitle: Reality as illusion

beauty-and-the-meaning-of-life.speaker_desc: Join Dominic Walliman as he hosts a panel discussion on the nature of beauty. Debating the topic are Denis Noble, Emeritus Rrofessor of Cardiovascular Physiology at the University of Oxford, Suchitra Sebastian, condensed matter physicist and recent winner of the New Horizons in Physics Prize, and George Ellis, mathematician at the University of Cape Town and Stephen Hawking collaborator.
beauty-and-the-meaning-of-life.subtitle: Will beauty lead science astray?

capitalism-big-tech-and-the-nation-state.speaker_desc: Join Stephanie Hare as she hosts a panel on the future of Big Tech, and its political and economic influence. Taking part in this debate are Aaron Bastani, the visionary co-founder of Novara Media, Kenneth Cukier, the host of the hugely popular podcast Babbage as well as the co-author of the best-selling book Big Data, and lastly Anu Bradford, a Professor of Law and International Organization at Columbia University.
capitalism-big-tech-and-the-nation-state.subtitle: How should we handle the rise of Big Tech?

confronting-lies-in-modern-politics-than.speaker_desc: Thangam Debbonaire is a British Labour Party politician, serving as the Shadow Secretary of State for Culture, Media and Sport since 2023 and the Labour MP for Bristol West since 2015.
confronting-lies-in-modern-politics-than.subtitle: An interview with Thangam Debbonaire

the-origin-of-life.speaker_desc: Join molecular biologist Güneş Taylor as she hosts a discussion on biology’s most central question: how did life begin? Joining her on the panel are cell biologist at the University of Minnesota Kate Adamala, Emeritus Professor of Chemistry at Ben Guiron University Addy Pross, and research scientist at Google DeepMind Chrisantha Fernando.
the-origin-of-life.subtitle: The mystery of life's beginning

china-and-india-the-future-of-the-next-c.speaker_desc: Bhavna Dave is a senior lecturer in Central Asian Politics at the Department of Politics and International Studies at the School of Oriental and African Studies, University of London. She specializes in issues of ethnic relations, identity politics and political transition in Central Asia.
china-and-india-the-future-of-the-next-c.subtitle: The fight for the future of Asia

the-morality-of-sex-work.speaker_desc: Maya Oppenheim is Women’s Correspondent - the only such job title at a UK news outlet - at The Independent. She also writes a popular weekly free newsletter titled Independent Women. Her most recent work is The Pocket Guide to the Patriarchy (2023).
the-morality-of-sex-work.subtitle: Why we still see sex work as taboo

discovering-the-world-beyond-science-rup.speaker_desc: Rupert Sheldrake is an English scientist whose research into parapsychology and evolution led to the theory of morphic resonance. Other topics he has written and spoken on include precognition, the relationships between spirituality and science and the psychic staring effect. Sheldrake's most recent book is Science and Spiritual Practices (2017).
discovering-the-world-beyond-science-rup.subtitle: Revisiting the supernatural

rob-boddice-the-happiness-crisis.speaker_desc: Rob Boddice is a writer and historian who unravels the complexities of the human condition; he is the author/editor of 14 books, most recently Knowing Pain: A History of Sensation, Emotion, and Experience (Polity Press). His 2018 and 2019 books, The History of Emotions and A History of Feelings, are defining works in the field. He is currently Senior Research Fellow at the Academy of Finland Centre of Excellence in the History of Experiences at Tampere University, Finland, and a Fellow of the Royal Historical Society.
rob-boddice-the-happiness-crisis.subtitle: Have we been measuring happiness in the wrong way?

redrawing-the-global-order.speaker_desc: Will the BRICS be the new superpower? Join Bill Browder, the famed thorn in Putin's side and CEO of Hermitage Capital, Yuan Yang the Financial Times' Europe China Correspondent, and Sergei Guriev, the provost and professor of economics and Science Po and former chief economist for the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development. Hosted by Sasha Polakow-Suransky and this event was sponsored by Foreign Policy.
redrawing-the-global-order.subtitle: Will the BRICS surpass the west?

the-quantum-age-michio-kaku.speaker_desc: Famed futurist and co-founder of String Field Theory, Michio Kaku has spent his career inspired by the search for a grand unifying theory of everything – carrying on Einstein’s quest to unite the four fundamental forces of nature. His latest book is Quantum Supremacy: How the Quantum Computer Revolution Will Change Everything.
the-quantum-age-michio-kaku.subtitle: Curt Jaimungal interviews Michio Kaku

the-psychedelic-revolution3.subtitle: A solution to the mental health crisis

a-rule-to-live-by.speaker_desc: Join Myriam François as she hosts this panel of distinguished guests as they discuss the idea of universal moral principles. Taking part in this debate are Daniel Markovits is an American legal scholar and Professor of Law at the Yale Law School; Carol Gilligan, a celebrated feminist, ethicist and psychologist; and finally, Peter Singer, one of the world's foremost public philosophers and a prominent figure in contemporary ethics.
a-rule-to-live-by.subtitle: Is it time to abandon the Golden Rule?

dreaming-beyond-time-gary-lachman.speaker_desc: Gary Lachman is the former Blondie bassist turned philosopher. He is the author of many books on consciousness, precognition, psychology and the occult.
dreaming-beyond-time-gary-lachman.subtitle: Studying the timeless tapestry

the-secrets-of-irrationality-dan-ariely.speaker_desc: Dan Ariely is James B. Duke Professor of psychology and behavioural economics at Duke University. He explores the secrets of irrationality, explains why rational people believe irrational things and what we can do about it. His latest book is Misbelief: What Makes Rational People Believe Irrational Things.
the-secrets-of-irrationality-dan-ariely.subtitle: Why we believe conspiracies

how-to-think-like-a-spy.speaker_desc: David Omand is a former British spy who served as Director of GCHQ. He was responsible to the Prime Minister for the professional health of the intelligence community, national counter-terrorism strategy and “homeland security”.
how-to-think-like-a-spy.subtitle: Espionage for dummies

the-quantum-hoax.speaker_desc: Quantum photonic expert Ruth Oulton, leading AI researcher Joscha Bach and science writer and YouTube sensation Dominic Walliman debate the potential of quantum computing. Neil Turok hosts.
the-quantum-hoax.subtitle: The science vs. the hype

solving-the-meaning-crisis-john-vervaeke.speaker_desc: John Vervaeke is an award winning professor at the University of Toronto in the departments of psychology, cognitive science, and Buddhist psychology. He is the creator of the widely viewed, 50-part lecture series on Youtube, Awakening from the Meaning Crisis.
solving-the-meaning-crisis-john-vervaeke.subtitle: How to live in a world without purpose

the-spectre-of-the-enlightenment.speaker_desc: Aviva Chomsky is a leading historian and activist and the Coordinator of Latin American, Latino and Caribbean Studies at Salem State University in Massachussets. She is the author of 10 books, including most recently Is Science Enough?: Forty Critical Questions About Climate Justice.
the-spectre-of-the-enlightenment.subtitle: Face to face with a destructive legacy

embracing-solidarity-in-a-secular-age-ro.speaker_desc: Rowan Williams, the 104th Archbishop of Canterbury, is a highly acclaimed theologian, writer, and pastor. In addition to his ten-year post as Archbishop, Lord Williams has also enjoyed an esteemed academic career, having been a lecturer at the University of Cambridge as well as having held the Lady Margaret Chair of Divinity at the University of Oxford.
embracing-solidarity-in-a-secular-age-ro.subtitle: An interview with Rowan Williams

the-mystery-of-emergence.speaker_desc: Suchitra Sebastian is a renowned scientist and a condensed matter physicist. She is based at the Cavendish Laboratory at the University of Cambridge where she is a Professor of Physics. Philip Goff is a leading philosopher of Consciousness in his field and a defender of panpsychism, the controversial proposal that everything contains consciousness, as the solution to the hard problem of consciousness. Hilary Lawson is a philosopher and long-standing critic of realism, best known for his theory of closure. Jack Symes hosts.
the-mystery-of-emergence.subtitle: Is complexity a cop-out?

the-life-and-philosophy-of-billy-bragg.speaker_desc: Billy Bragg is an English singer-songwriter and activist known for his blend of folk, punk rock, and protest music. Bragg's outspoken views and commitment to activism have cemented his place as one of the UK's most influential musical figures.
the-life-and-philosophy-of-billy-bragg.subtitle: Billy Bragg on the power of music and protest

mearshimer-and-the-death-of-ideology.speaker_desc: John Mearsheimer is the R. Wendell Harrison Distinguished Service Professor of Political Science at the University of Chicago and is considered to be one of the most influential international relations theorists of his generation.
mearshimer-and-the-death-of-ideology.subtitle: Realism on Ukraine, Israel, and China

truth-beauty-and-other-scientific-miscon.speaker_desc: One of the most daring theoretical physicists alive today, Lisa Randall is the Frank B. Baird, Jr. Professor of Science at Harvard University. Randall's books Warped Passages and Knocking on Heaven's Door have both been on the New York Times 100 notable books lists.
truth-beauty-and-other-scientific-miscon.subtitle: When beautiful theories are killed by ugly facts

the-dark-side-of-feminism-tommy-curry.speaker_desc: Tommy Curry is a philosophy professor at Edinburgh University where he holds a Personal Chair in Africana Philosophy and Black Male studies. His research focuses on Africana Philosophy, Critical Race Theory, Anti-Colonialism, Black Male Studies, and Public Health.
the-dark-side-of-feminism-tommy-curry.subtitle: Decolonising feminism

the-politics-of-desire.speaker_desc: Zoe Strimpel is an outspoken commentator, historian, and columnist at The Sunday Telegraph who specialises in all things gender and relationships. Maya Oppenheim is a writer and tireless advocate for women’s rights. Her role as Women’s Correspondent at The Independent is the only one of its kind in the UK. Kimberly McIntosh is a writer, Labour councillor and former love and dating columnist for ‘gal-dem’; her first book, black girl, no magic, is a searing collection of personal essays reflecting on living whilst black. Barry Smith hosts.
the-politics-of-desire.subtitle: Should we police sexual preference?

the-transgender-mind-body-problem-sophie.speaker_desc: Sophie Grace Chappell is a Professor of Philosophy at the Open University where she specialises in ethics, politics, feminism and epistemology. Her recent books include Ethics Beyond the Limits and Knowing What to Do.
the-transgender-mind-body-problem-sophie.subtitle: An interview with Sophie Grace Chappell

economic-fact-and-economic-fantasy.speaker_desc: Join Yanis Varoufakis, former finance minister of Greece, John Redwood Conservative MP, and Vicky Pryce, chief economics adviser to the Centre of Economics and Business Research. Hosted by the BBC's Roger Hearing.
economic-fact-and-economic-fantasy.subtitle: Is prediction a economic mirage?

the-dream-and-danger-of-ai.speaker_desc: Liv Boeree is one of the most successful female poker players of all time. A self-confessed nerd with a first-class degree in astrophysics, Liv combined her science background and passion for games to become one of the most recognizable faces in professional poker. Dominic Walliman is a science writer, physicist, and YouTube sensation. His popular YouTube channel, Domain of Science, and award-winning Professor Astro Cat science books for children have captivated audiences worldwide.
the-dream-and-danger-of-ai.subtitle: Balancing a future of innovation and regulation

gravity-and-the-universe.speaker_desc: Join celebrated theoretical physicist, Erik Verlinde, leading astrophysicist, Priya Natarajan, and famous physicist-YouTuber, Sabine Hossenfelder, as they take on the problems surrounding our conceptions of gravity today. Hosted by Bjørn Ekeberg.
gravity-and-the-universe.subtitle: The mysteries of gravity

the-tiktok-uprising.speaker_desc: Cindy Yu is a China reporter and broadcast editor at the Spectator. She has written extensively about Chinese society – from marriage to education – and politics for the Spectator. She is a frequent commentator on China issues for RTE and BBC World Service and World TV.
the-tiktok-uprising.subtitle: The global politics of a social media platform

dostoevsky-vs-nietzsche.speaker_desc: Kathleen Higgins is a leading continental philosopher at the University of Texas, Austin. Her research interests are broad and include the philosophy of aesthetics, emotions and music. Oliver Ready is a celebrated translator and literary scholar. His translation of Dostoevsky's Crime and Punishment has received critical acclaim. Janne Teller is a critically acclaimed writer whose novels include Odin's Island, and Come, an existential novel about ethics in art and modern life. Niki Seth-Smith hosts.
dostoevsky-vs-nietzsche.subtitle: The fundamental threat to humanity

how-we-let-russia-invade-ukraine-fiona-h.speaker_desc: Fiona Hill worked at the US National Intelligence Council as an intelligence analyst under Bush and Obama, and in 2017 was appointed by Donald Trump as Deputy Assistant to the President and Senior Director for European and Russian affairs on his National Security Council staff. She is now the Chancellor of Durham University.
how-we-let-russia-invade-ukraine-fiona-h.subtitle: An interview with Fiona Hill

we-need-a-scientific-revolution-eric-wei.speaker_desc: Eric Weinstein is a mathematical physicist and the host of the podcast The Portal. He is the former Managing Director of Thiel Capital in San Francisco and was formerly a Co-Founder and Principal of the Natron Group in Manhattan as well as a Visiting Research Fellow at Oxford University for the Mathematical Institute.
we-need-a-scientific-revolution-eric-wei.subtitle: An interview with Eric Weinstein

the-god-desire.speaker_desc: David Baddiel is an acclaimed comedian, screenwriter and actor. He is best known for creating and starring in The Mary Whitehouse Experience, as well as for his numerous collaborations with Frank Skinner. His most recent book, The God Desire, provides a fresh, exciting spin on the most ancient of debates.
the-god-desire.subtitle: How to confront oblivion

the-impartiality-illusion.speaker_desc: Join Florence Read as she hosts a debate between Matthew Goodwin, Professor of Politics at the University of Kent and bestselling author, Philip Collins, writer-in-chief at The Draft and contributing editor at the New Statesman, and Sophie Scott-Brown, fellow at the European Institute at the University of Oxford, on whether or not media can ever claim to be impartial.
the-impartiality-illusion.subtitle: Can the media ever be impartial?

uncovering-the-secrets-of-the-universe-p.speaker_desc: Priyamvada Natarajan is a Yale Professor of Astronomy and Physics and a science communicator. She was also the first woman in astrophysics to be elected as a Fellow of Trinity College, Cambridge. Her pionieering work includes Mapping the Heavens: The Radical Scientific Ideas that Reveal the Cosmos.
uncovering-the-secrets-of-the-universe-p.subtitle: How black holes change our sense of the cosmos

speaking-for-the-future.speaker_desc: Hilary Greaves is a professor of philosophy at the University of Oxford and a a founding director of the Global Priorities Institute. Lord Jonathan Sumption is an author, political commentator and one of the most decorated lawyers of his generation; he sat as a judge on the Supreme Court between 2012 and 2018, and appeared as a barrister for the Hutton Inquiry. Sophie Howe is a sustainable futures and wellbeing adviser who was the first to hold the role of Future Generations Commissioner in Wales. Philip Collins hosts.
speaking-for-the-future.subtitle: Can we legislate in the interests of the future?

challenging-the-caricature-doon-mackicha.speaker_desc: Emmy-award winning actress and writer for screen and stage best known for her role as one third of the anarchic Smack the Pony ensemble.
challenging-the-caricature-doon-mackicha.subtitle: A life fighting stereotypes

when-myth-becomes-reality-janne-teller.speaker_desc: Janne Teller is a critically acclaimed and best-selling novelist, known for her works Odin's Island and Nothing. Her books deal with the existential and ethical questions around life and civilisation.
when-myth-becomes-reality-janne-teller.subtitle: The power of misinformation

the-enlightenment-and-its-alternatives-s.speaker_desc: Sophie Scott-Brown, Director at Gresham College, hosts a debate between two of the most influential thinkers of our time. Join John Mearsheimer, Professor of Political Science at the University of Chicago, and Steven Pinker, Professor of Psychology at Harvard University, as they discuss the Enlightenment and its alternatives.
the-enlightenment-and-its-alternatives-s.subtitle: Which ideals are best to guide human betterment?

power-politics-and-mental-health.speaker_desc: Professor of population health Praveetha Patalay, Regius Professor of Psychiatry Sir Simon Wessley and co-founder of Novara Media and bestselling author Aaron Bastani debate the connection between science, politics, and mental health. Hosted by Joanna Kavenna.
power-politics-and-mental-health.subtitle: Rewriting mental health

the-quest-for-the-common-good.speaker_desc: Mike Herd is Investigations editor of The Conversation UK. Julia Davies is an angel investor, lawyer, philanthropist and environmental campaigner. Gerry Mitchell is a social researcher and writer who is also experienced in political campaigning, community engagement and teaching. Louise Ashley is Senior Lecturer in the School of Business and Management at Queen Mary University of London.
the-quest-for-the-common-good.subtitle: Moving beyond individualism

leaving-metaphysics-behind.speaker_desc: Michael Della Rocca is one of the world's leading authorities on Spinoza and the author of numerous field-defining articles and books, including most recently the Parmenidean Ascent. He is Sterling Professor of Philosophy at Yale University, which is awarded to a tenured faculty member considered one of the best in his or her field and is Yale University’s highest faculty honour.
leaving-metaphysics-behind.subtitle: An interview with Michael Della Rocca

the-morality-of-sex.speaker_desc: Famed twitch streamer Steven Bonnell (aka Destiny), Acclaimed filmmaker, journalist and writer Myriam Francois, Philosopher and Psychoanalytic theorist Isabel Millar, and Womens Correspondent at the The Independent Maya Oppenheim debate whether monogamy is still morally justified in our modern world. Sophie Scott-Brown hosts.
the-morality-of-sex.subtitle: Should monogamy fall from its moral highground?

quantum-computing-and-the-future-of-scie.speaker_desc: Dominic Walliman is a science writer, physicist, and YouTube sensation. His popular YouTube channel, Domain of Science, and award-winning Professor Astro Cat science books for kids have captivated audiences around the world
quantum-computing-and-the-future-of-scie.subtitle: An interview with Dominic Walliman

the-life-and-philosophy-of-slavoj-zizek.speaker_desc: Slavoj Žižek is a Slovenian-born political philosopher currently serving as International Director of the Birkbeck Institute for the Humanities. He has become world-renowned for his fearless overturning of the liberal left’s founding assumptions.
the-life-and-philosophy-of-slavoj-zizek.subtitle: Celebrity philosopher reflects on his life's work

the-economics-of-almost-everything.speaker_desc: Chief Economics Commentator for the FT Martin Wolf, Yale Law professor Daniel Markovits and Head of Research at Theos, Madeleine Pennington debate whether the 21st century will prove to be unique.
the-economics-of-almost-everything.subtitle: Rethinking economics

the-shadow-of-spirituality.speaker_desc: Award-winning professor at the University of Toronto John Vervaeke, Professor at the Open University Sophie-Grace Chappell and founder of the Skeptics Society Michael Shermer join their host, Professor Barry C. Smith to discuss new-age spirituality.
the-shadow-of-spirituality.subtitle: Is New Age spirituality leading us astray?

the-secrets-of-quantum-emergence-suchitr.speaker_desc: Recent winner of the New Horizons in Physics Prize and the Schmidt Science Polymaths Award, Suchitra Sebastian is an up and coming condensed matter physicist. She is based at the Cavendish Laboratory at the University of Cambridge where she is a Professor of Physics. Professor Sebastian is known for her discoveries of exotic quantum phenomena that emerge in complex materials. She was named as one of thirty Exceptional Young Scientists by the World Economic Forum in 2013, one of The Next Big Names in Physics by the Financial Times in 2013.
the-secrets-of-quantum-emergence-suchitr.subtitle: Exploring the greatest mystery in physics

science-fiction-for-a-dystopian-present-.speaker_desc: Cory Doctorow (craphound.com) is a prolific science fiction author, activist and journalist. He is the author of many books, most recently The Lost Cause, a solarpunk science fiction novel of hope amidst the climate emergency. His most recent nonfiction book is The Internet Con: How to Seize The Means of Computation, a Big Tech disassembly manual. Other recent books include Red Team Blues, a science fiction crime thriller. Interviewed by Darcy Bounsall.
science-fiction-for-a-dystopian-present-.subtitle: An interview with Cory Doctorow

dangerous-media-for-dangerous-times.speaker_desc: Alan Rusbridger is a world-renowned journalist, former principal of Lady Margaret Hall and former editor-in-chief of The Guardian. Matt Kelly is a career journalist and the owner of The New European, a paper that has taken the UK by storm since its humble beginnings in the wake of the Brexit vote.
dangerous-media-for-dangerous-times.subtitle: News in a post-trust world

confronting-the-enlightenments-mistakes-.speaker_desc: Kehinde Andrews is the first black studies professor in the UK, currently working at Birmingham City University. He is the director of the Centre for Critical Social Research, founder of the Harambee Organisation of Black Unity, and co-chair of the UK Black Studies Association.
confronting-the-enlightenments-mistakes-.subtitle: An interview with Kehinde Andrews

the-trouble-with-time.speaker_desc: Quantum theorist Avshalom Elitzur, theoretical physicist Michio Kaku, philosopher of physics Tim Maudlin, and historian of science Jimena Canales delve into the fascinating conundrum of time. Güneş Taylor hosts.
the-trouble-with-time.subtitle: Reality's challenge to physics

the-psychology-of-ai-isabel-millar.speaker_desc: Dr Isabel Millar is a groundbreaking philosopher and psychoanalytic theorist, currently working at Newcastle University and the Global Centre for Advanced Study.
the-psychology-of-ai-isabel-millar.subtitle: Lacan, ChatGPT and the future

marxism-vs-capitalism.speaker_desc: Aaron Bastani is co-founder of Novara Media, one of the most influential independent, radical left-wing media organizations in the UK. He is also author of Fully Automated Luxury Communism, a manifesto for his vision of 21st century communism. Matthew Lesh is the Director of Public Policy and Communications at the Institute of Economic Affairs. He is also a Fellow of the Adam Smith Institute and Institute of Public Affairs, and writes regularly for The Times, The Telegraph and The Spectator.
marxism-vs-capitalism.subtitle: Head to Head: Bastani vs Lesh

imagining-the-universe.speaker_desc: World-renowned mathematician and Nobel Laureate in Physics Roger Penrose, award-winning writer Esther Freud and ground-breaking polymath and former Oxford scholar Iain McGilchrist join Eliane Glaser to debate creativity, imagination and whether or not they can help us reframe our understanding of reality.
imagining-the-universe.subtitle: Is creativity an illusion?

unlocking-science-helen-czerski.speaker_desc: Dr Helen Czerski is a a physicist, oceanographer, presenter and author, currently working as an Associate Professor at University College London in the Department of Mechanical Engineering.
unlocking-science-helen-czerski.subtitle: An interview with Helen Czerski

narcissism-and-self-love.speaker_desc: Author of Think and Truth: A guide for the perplexed, Simon Blackburn has worked to bring philosophy to a wider audience. He was Professor of Philosophy at Cambridge and Vice President of the British Humanist Association.
narcissism-and-self-love.subtitle: Simon Blackburn on the dangers of self-love

destiny-and-the-new-world-of-internet-po.speaker_desc: Steven Bonnell (also known as Destiny) is an internet personality, live streamer and political commentator. He started out as a gaming livestreamer but became more politically engaged in the run up to Trump’s election in 2016. He is now known for debating far-right, white supremacist and antifeminist internet commentators in YouTube videos.
destiny-and-the-new-world-of-internet-po.subtitle: An interview with Steven Bonnell

in-pursuit-of-peace.speaker_desc: Renowned economist, Richard D. Wolff, award-winning journalist, Svitlana Morenets, and former intelligence chief, Sir David Omand, join Hilary Lawson to discuss escalating conflict worldwide and the possibility of peace.
in-pursuit-of-peace.subtitle: How can we secure peace in times of war?

the-life-and-philosophy-of-denis-noble.speaker_desc: Denis Noble is one of the pioneers of modern biology. He is a British physiologist and biologist who has worked at the University of Oxford.
