He developed the first viable mathematical model of the working heart, and is the author of several best-selling books.
the-life-and-philosophy-of-denis-noble.subtitle: Esteemed biologist reflects on life and career

the-broken-economics-of-the-sea.speaker_desc: Guy Standing is a Professorial Research Associate at SOAS, University of London, and a founder and co-president of the Basic Income Earth Network (BIEN). His most recent work is The Blue Commons (2022).
the-broken-economics-of-the-sea.subtitle: Rescuing the blue commons

the-end-of-good-and-evil.speaker_desc: Anthropologist and Harvard University Professor Richard Wrangham, renowened philosopher and cultural critic Slavoj Žižek, University of Hertfordshire professor Maria Balaska and the 104th Archbishop of Canterbury Rowan Williams join Myriam François to discuss the nature of good and evil.
the-end-of-good-and-evil.subtitle: Can humans ever be inherently good or evil?

the-awakened-brain.speaker_desc: Dr. Lisa Miller is an American professor, researcher and clinical psychologist, best known as a research scholar on spirituality in psychology. Miller is Founder of the Spirituality Mind Body Institute at Columbia University. Miller's published work on spirituality in renewal from addiction and depression has been featured in the New York Times and the Wall Street Journal, as well as in television interviews and podcasts. Tom Hodgkinson and Mark Vernon from The Idler host. This event was produced in partnership with The Idler.
the-awakened-brain.subtitle: Where science meets spirituality

the-ethics-of-industry.speaker_desc: Baroness Lola Young is a former actor and lecturer, and currently sits as an independent member of the House of Lords. As a peer, her work has focussed on ethics in industry and trade, founding and chairing key cross-party parliamentary groups on sustainability and modern slavery.
the-ethics-of-industry.subtitle: An interview with Baroness Lola Young

on-the-edges-of-knowledge-michael-sherme.subtitle: How do we assess claims to scientific knowledge?

down-the-wormhole.speaker_desc: Distinguished cosmologist, George Ellis, famous mathematician and polymath, Eric Weinstein, and celebrated astrophysicist, Matt O'Dowd, join Katie Robertson to discuss wormholes.
down-the-wormhole.subtitle: The myth of wormholes

justice-in-jeopardy.speaker_desc: Director of The Centre for Women's Justice Harriet Wistrich, leading philosopher of psychology and morality David Livingstone Smith and journalist and film-maker Myriam François debate justice, judgement and punishment. Isabel Hilton hosts.
justice-in-jeopardy.subtitle: Innocence and guilt in the modern world

based-on-a-true-story.speaker_desc: Leading academic and author, Remi Adekoya, director of the Institute of Philosophy at UCL, Barry Smith, and award-winning writer, Esther Freud, join Eliane Glaser to discuss the problem of subjectivity in historical narratives.
based-on-a-true-story.subtitle: Is an objective story of the past possible?

explaining-away-truth-paul-horwich.speaker_desc: Paul Gordon Horwich is a British analytic philosopher at New York University, noted for his contributions to philosophy of science, philosophy of physics, the philosophy of language and the interpretation of Wittgenstein's later philosophy.
explaining-away-truth-paul-horwich.subtitle: An interview with Paul Horwich

dopamine-nation-anna-lembke.speaker_desc: Anna Lembke is a groundbreaking psychiatrist and addiction medicine expert. Alongside her important clinical practice, Lembke has featured on the hit Netflix documentary, The Social Dilemma, and testified before various committees in the United States House of Representatives and Senate.
dopamine-nation-anna-lembke.subtitle: Causes and consequences of a "drugified" society

necessity-and-lies.speaker_desc: Senior Lecturer in Philosophy at Royal Holloway, Rebecca Roache, Professor of Psychology and Psychiatry at Cambridge University, Simon Baron-Cohen, and non-realist philosopher, Hilary Lawson join Samira Shackle to scrutinize honesty and deception.
necessity-and-lies.subtitle: Is it ever right to lie? Is honesty ever wrong?

waking-from-darkness-steve-taylor.speaker_desc: Steve Taylor is a senior lecturer in psychology at Leeds Beckett University, and has authored over fourteen books on psychology and spirituality.
waking-from-darkness-steve-taylor.subtitle: The psychology underpinning spirituality

the-pleasure-paradox.speaker_desc: Neurophilosopher Patricia Churchland, Ayn Rand Institute chairman Yaron Brook, and Stanford addiction expert Anna Lembke join host Robert Lawrence Kuhn to question why living standards do not seem to correlate with happiness. Produced in partnership with Closer To Truth.
the-pleasure-paradox.subtitle: Does pleasure lead to misery?

data-needs-theory-lisa-randall.speaker_desc: Lisa Randall is the Frank B. Baird, Jr. Professor of Science at Harvard University. Newsweek has called Randall "one of the most promising theoretical physicists of her generation." Randall's books Warped Passages and Knocking on Heaven's Door have both been on New York Times 100 notable books lists.
data-needs-theory-lisa-randall.subtitle: Exploring the mysteries of the universe

fantasy-faith-and-physics.speaker_desc: Sabine Hossenfelder is a theoretical physicist and science communicator who researches quantum gravity. She is the author of Lost in Math: How Beauty Leads Physics Astray. Michio Kaku has spent his career inspired by the search for a grand unifying theory of everything – carrying on Einstein’s quest to unite the four fundamental forces of nature. His latest book is Quantum Supremacy. Juan Maldacena is the Carl P. Feinberg Professor in the School of Natural Sciences at the Institute for Advanced Study. Due to his field-defining contributions to the foundations of string theory and quantum gravity, Leonard Susskind has called him “the greatest theoretical physicist of his generation.” Max Tegmark is a pioneering physicist, cosmologist, computer scientist, philosopher, and public intellectual based at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. Tegmark is the author of Our Mathematical Universe, which argues that reality is fundamentally a mathematical structure. Hosted by Mary-Jane Rubenstein, Professor of Religion and Science in Society at Wesleyan University.
fantasy-faith-and-physics.subtitle: The hidden motivations of physicists

reality-models-and-mayhem.speaker_desc: Pioneering philosopher of science Bjørn Ekeberg, pre-eminent sceptic Michael Shermer, and Professor of Theoretical Epidemiology at the University of Oxford Sunetra Gupta debate whether science can ever achieve an objective model of ultimate reality.
reality-models-and-mayhem.subtitle: Can science provide a complete account of reality?

the-goodness-paradox-richard-wrangham.speaker_desc: Richard Wrangham is Ruth B. Moore Research Professor of Biological Anthropology at Harvard University and one of the most influential anthropologists in the world.
the-goodness-paradox-richard-wrangham.subtitle: Humans are neither good or bad

the-life-and-philosophy-of-fiona-hill.speaker_desc: Fiona Hill is one of the most highly distinguished foreign affairs specialists and authors in the world today. Senior advisor to Presidents George W Bush, Barack Obama and briefly Donald Trump, she is a former official at the U.S. National Security Council specializing in Russian and European affairs.
the-life-and-philosophy-of-fiona-hill.subtitle: The thorn in Trump's side

the-blame-game.speaker_desc: Is blame a useful concept in the modern world? Join Baroness Young, development economicst Guy Standing, moral philosopher David Livingstone Smith and Claire Ogley, head of campaigns, policy and research at the Vegan society. Hosted by Isabel Hilton.
the-blame-game.subtitle: Inspiring change without pointing fingers

your-true-self.speaker_desc: Award-winning writer Joanna Kavena, Emerita Professor of English at the University of Texas Betty Sue Flowers and philosopher and jazz-musician James Tartaglia debate the notion of the authentic self. Bahar Gholipour hosts.
your-true-self.subtitle: Is the idea of an authentic self a mistake?

on-the-nature-of-reality-rowan-williams-.speaker_desc: Iain McGilchrist is a former Fellow of All Souls College, Oxford. He is committed to the idea that the mind and brain can be understood only by seeing them in the broadest possible context, that of the whole of our physical and spiritual existence. Rowan Williams is the 104th Archbishop of Canterbury, and is a highly acclaimed theologian, writer, and pastor.
on-the-nature-of-reality-rowan-williams-.subtitle: The limits of materialism

overcoming-opposition-paul-dolan.speaker_desc: Paul Dolan is a Professor in the Department of Social Policy at the London School of Economics and Political Science, where he holds a Chair in Behavioural Science.
overcoming-opposition-paul-dolan.subtitle: How to argue when you disagree

beyond-the-boundary.speaker_desc: Join Lisa Miller, New York Times Bestseller and professor of Clinical Psychology, Paul Bickley, head of research at Theos and Nick Lane, professor of Evolutionary Biochemistry at University College London. Hosted by Güneş Taylor.
beyond-the-boundary.subtitle: What comes after the afterlife?

rhetoric-and-reality.speaker_desc: Nolen Gertz is an Assistant Professor of applied philosophy at the University of Twente. He is the author of a number of books including Nihilism and Technology. Betty Sue Flowers is Emerita Professor of English at the University of Texas at Austin. She pioneered the modern, psychological appreciation of ancient myths alongside Joseph Campbell. Joscha Bach is an AI researcher for MIT Media Lab and the Harvard Program for Evolutionary Dynamics, where he explores new frontiers in cognitive architectures and mental representation. Katie Robertson hosts.
rhetoric-and-reality.subtitle: Why is language no guide to reality?

the-future-of-psychedelic-research-and-t.speaker_desc: David Nutt is the director of the Neuropsychopharmacology Unit in the Division of Brain Sciences at Imperial College, London and the author of six books, including most recently Psychedelics: The revolutionary drugs that could change your life.
the-future-of-psychedelic-research-and-t.subtitle: The fight for the right to research

the-contraception-delusion-gunes-taylor.speaker_desc: Güneş Taylor is an award-winning geneticist and pioneer of public engagement in her field. She is a training fellow at the Francis Crick Institute where her research predominantly focuses on the genetic formation of ovaries and testes.
the-contraception-delusion-gunes-taylor.subtitle: Fertility, sex, and the future

are-there-other-dimensions-michio-kaku.subtitle: An interview with a string theorist

is-mathematics-invented-or-discovered.subtitle: An interview with a mathematical physicist

guesses-errors-and-economics.speaker_desc: Join Gillian Tett, US editor of the Financial Times, Guy Standing, professor of development at SOAS and UBI advocate, and Richard Werner, economist renowned for coining 'quantitative easing'. Hosted by Linda Yueh.
guesses-errors-and-economics.subtitle: Are predictions a fool's errand?

what-are-breakthroughs-in-science.subtitle: An interview with a theoretical physicist

manners-maketh-man.subtitle: Civility and cohesion in the modern era

free-will-is-not-an-illusion.speaker_desc: Denis Noble is a renowned physiologist and one of the pioneers of Systems Biology. He is Emeritus Professor of Cardiovascular Physiology at Oxford University. Noble is known in his field for developing the first viable mathematical model of the working heart in 1960.
free-will-is-not-an-illusion.subtitle: Biology against determinism

the-quest-for-freedom.speaker_desc: As the leader of the Rights Lab's Law and Policy Programme at the University of Nottingham, Dr. Katarina Schwarz is dedicated to advancing our understanding of the legal and policy frameworks that govern anti-slavery efforts worldwide.
the-quest-for-freedom.subtitle: Slavery in the present day

ancient-traits-in-the-modern-world.speaker_desc: Professor of Theoretical Epidemiology at the University of Oxford Sunetra Gupta, research fellow at the Future of Humanity Institute at Oxford Anders Sandberg and philosopher of biology Subrena Smith debate whether or not our neurobiology inadequate to deal with the challenges of the 21st century. Güneş Taylor hosts.
ancient-traits-in-the-modern-world.subtitle: Is our neurobiology at odds with the life today?

matt-hancock-unveiled-regrets-and-reflec.speaker_desc: Matt Hancock is a British politician who served as Secretary of State for Health and Social Care from 2018 to 2021, and as Secretary of State for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport in 2018 for six months. A member of the Conservative Party, he has been Member of Parliament for West Suffolk since 2010. He served as Health Secretary during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom and oversaw the subsequent rollout of the UK's vaccination programme.
matt-hancock-unveiled-regrets-and-reflec.subtitle: The career of Parliament’s most notorious Tory

after-knowledge.speaker_desc: Philosopher of race Tommy Curry, theoretical physicist Suchitra Sebastian and outspoken scientist Rupert Sheldrake debate the limits of what we can know. Hosted by Joanna Kavenna.
after-knowledge.subtitle: The limits of knowledge

me-my-world-and-i.speaker_desc: Renowned musician and author on mysticism and the occult Gary Lachman, internationally aclaimed neuroscientist Hannah Critchlow, philosophy professor and expert of the senses Barry Smith debate collective experience versus subjectivity. Matt O'Dowd hosts.
me-my-world-and-i.subtitle: The myth and reality of collective experience

surplus-happiness.speaker_desc: Slavoj Žižek is a world-renowned philosopher, cultural critic and public intellectual. He is international director of the Birkbeck Institute for the Humanities and a senior researcher at the University of Ljubljana's Department of Philosophy.
surplus-happiness.subtitle: The false joy of excess

diplomacy-deception-and-disaster.speaker_desc: Former Foreign Secretary Malcom Rifkind, GCHQ director David Omand, Ambassador Laurie Bristow and Novellist Janne Teller debate the future of diplomacy and conflict. Hosted by Sasha Polakow-Suransky.
diplomacy-deception-and-disaster.subtitle: Can diplomacy end the Ukraine war?

iain-mcgilchrist-exclusive-interview.speaker_desc: Iain McGilchrist is an Oxford scholar and polymath whose 'clarity, lucidity and almost hypnotically compelling style' has seen him rise to prominence as a world-wide lecturer and public intellectual.

technology-is-not-neutral-stephanie-hare.speaker_desc: Dr Stephanie Hare is a researcher, broadcaster and speaker on technology, politics, and history.Stephanie has worked as a Principal Director at Accenture Research and a senior analyst for Western Europe at Oxford Analytica.
technology-is-not-neutral-stephanie-hare.subtitle: Technology cannot exist without ethics

emma-sulkowicz-performance-as-art.speaker_desc: Emma Sulkowicz is a sexual assault activist, artist and political commentator.
emma-sulkowicz-performance-as-art.subtitle: An interview with Emma Sulkowicz

philosophy-at-war.speaker_desc: Theoretical physicist Lisa Randall, post-postmodern philosopher Hilary Lawson and philosopher of science Paul Horwich debate the connection between science, philosophy and truth. Hosted by Maria Balaska.
philosophy-at-war.subtitle: A battle at the heart of philosophy

cities-of-the-future-lucelia-rodriguez.speaker_desc: Lucelia Rodrigues is one of the world’s foremost experts on sustainability. She is Chair of Sustainable and Resilient Cities in the Faculty of Engineering at the University of Nottingham.
cities-of-the-future-lucelia-rodriguez.subtitle: What is the architecture of a sustainable world?

the-game-of-life.speaker_desc: World-leading philosopher Slavoj Žižek, radical internet personality Steven Bonnell, and bestselling author and psychologist Lisa Miller grapple with the gamification of life. Hosted by pioneering journalist Myriam François.
the-game-of-life.subtitle: Should we stop the gamification of life?

the-reality-beyond-spacetime.speaker_desc: Donald Hoffman is an American cognitive psychologist working at the University of California, Irvine. He is making waves with a new theory suggesting that, instead of presenting reality as it "really is", our perception is like a desktop interface enabling us to use reality effectively.
the-reality-beyond-spacetime.subtitle: Is spacetime doomed?

beyond-reasonable-doubt.speaker_desc: LGBT rights activist Peter Tatchell, lawyer Harriet Wistricht and advocate for justice reform Emma Bryson explore the burden of proof. Hosted by Mary Ann Sieghart.
beyond-reasonable-doubt.subtitle: Should we lower the burden of proof for sex crimes

the-best-and-worst-of-all-possible-world.speaker_desc: Philosopher of physics Paul Horwich, philosopher and author Ben Burgis and theoretical physicist Tasneem Zehra Husain debate the continued attraction of many worlds theory. Hosted by Niki Seth-Smith.
the-best-and-worst-of-all-possible-world.subtitle: Are there alternate realities to ours?

capitalism-and-the-climate.speaker_desc: Join Rebecca Henderson, Harvard MBA's socialist, Troy Vettese, economic historian and author and Helen Czerski, pioneering physicist of the natural world as they debate the connection between capitalism and the climate. Hosted by Linda Yueh, Oxford professor of economics.
capitalism-and-the-climate.subtitle: Our planet and the economy

searching-for-justice-jesse-norman.speaker_desc: Jesse Norman is a Conservative Party politician who has served as MP since 2010. He served as Financial Secretary to the Treasury from 2019 to 2021. His book Compassionate Conservatism has been described as the "handbook to Cameronism".
searching-for-justice-jesse-norman.subtitle: The Conservative case for Justice

why-the-rational-believe-the-irrational.speaker_desc: Michael Shermer is the founder of The Skeptics Society, the editor-in-chief of its magazine Skeptic, and a Presidential Fellow at Chapman University, where he teaches Skepticism 101.
why-the-rational-believe-the-irrational.subtitle: Who believes conspiracies and why?

the-fantasy-of-fame.speaker_desc: Al Jazeera's royal correspondant Stefan Simanowitz, Grazia columnist Polly Vernon and award-winning author Will Storr take celebrity to trial. Hosted by Mary Ann Sieghart.
the-fantasy-of-fame.subtitle: Is our focus on fame destroying culture?

consciousness-and-chat-gpt-james-tartagl.speaker_desc: James Tartaglia is a trailblazing philosopher and the author of Philosophy in a Meaningless Life and Philosophy in a Technological World: GODS AND TITANS. His main interest is in understanding and enhancing our awareness of the nature of philosophical inquiry, which for him centres on the question of the meaning of life.
consciousness-and-chat-gpt-james-tartagl.subtitle: Is ChatGPT conscious?

democracy-in-the-dock.speaker_desc: Political philosopher Ruth Kinna, leading Conservative Party politician Jesse Norman and leading Labour MP Thangam Debbonaire debate the dire state of liberal democracy. Hilary Lawson hosts.
democracy-in-the-dock.subtitle: Remedying the dire state of liberal democracy

virtue-ethics-and-the-mob.speaker_desc: Prolific moral philosopher Simon Blackburn, intellectual historian Sophie Scott Brown and renowned human rights campaigner Peter Tatchell debate the value of appearing ethical in modern society. Hosted by Rana Mitter
virtue-ethics-and-the-mob.subtitle: Can morality matter and be private?

the-danger-and-desire-of-the-frontier.speaker_desc: Assistant Professor of Applied Philosophy at the University of Twente Nolan Geertz, renowned science fiction author, activist, journalist and blogger Cory Doctorow and leading New York-based journalist and neuroscientist Bahar Gholipour discuss the real goal is a technological journey into the unknown. Güneş Taylor hosts.
the-danger-and-desire-of-the-frontier.subtitle: Should we explore mars while the earth burns?

how-to-philosophize-behind-bars.speaker_desc: Andy West is senior specialist with the Philosophy Foundation and philosopher in residence at HMP Pentonville, London. He is the author of The Life Inside: A Memoir of Prison, Family and Philosophy (2022).
how-to-philosophize-behind-bars.subtitle: The case for prison abolition

an-unprecedented-experiment-with-money.speaker_desc: Entrepreneur Peter Schiff, World Bank Economist Carmen Reinhart and Economic Historian Brad de Long debate how our response to the financial crisis has impacted our current economy. Hosted by Gillian Tett.
an-unprecedented-experiment-with-money.subtitle: What caused the inflation crisis

psychoanalysis-and-revolution-ian-parker.speaker_desc: Ian Parker is a psychoanalyst and Emeritus Professor of Management in the School of Business at the University of Leicester.
psychoanalysis-and-revolution-ian-parker.subtitle: The intersection of personal and social liberation

the-end-of-everything.speaker_desc: World-leading string theorist Brian Greene, famed historian of science Michael Shermer, groundbreaking particle physicist Sabine Hossenfelder and radical mathematical physicist and podcast host Eric Weinstein lock horns over whether it's possible to find a theory of everything. Astronomer Royal for Scotland, Catherine Heymans, hosts.
the-end-of-everything.subtitle: Is a theory of everything just around the corner?

desiring-and-being-desired.speaker_desc: Catherine Hakim is a pioneering British social scientist and author. She is perhaps best known for her groundbreaking book ‘Erotic Capital’, and she is currently Professorial Research Fellow at Civitas, the London think tank. Peter Tatchell is a human rights campaigner best known for his work with LGBT movements, a member of the gay rights group Outrage! and director of the Peter Tatchell Foundation, a human rights organization. Katherine Angel is an academic and writer. She is the author of numerous works, most recently ‘Tomorrow Sex Will Be Good Again’, published in 2021, which received much critical acclaim and widespread international coverage.
desiring-and-being-desired.subtitle: Navigating power in #MeToo

politics-is-broken.speaker_desc: Thangam Debbonaire is the Labour MP for Bristol West and current Shadow Leader of the House of Commons, previously working as the Shadow Secretary of State for Housing. Describing herself as a "northern European socialist", Thangam supports "fettered capitalism".
politics-is-broken.subtitle: How to fix a broken system

anarchy-and-democracy-sophie-scott-brown.speaker_desc: Sophie Scott-Brown is an intellectual historian based at the University of East Anglia with research interests in modern European political thought and the history of education. She is the author of The Histories of Raphael Samuel: A Portrait of a People’s Historian and Colin Ward and the Art of Everyday Anarchy.
anarchy-and-democracy-sophie-scott-brown.subtitle: Is there room for leadership in anarchy?

taking-leave-of-reason.speaker_desc: Award-winning English novelist Joanna Kavenna, renowned public intellectual Rory Sutherland, philosopher and senior Lecturer Rebecca Roache debate whether we need reason as much as we think we do in an increasingly chaotic modern age. Bahar Gholipour hosts.
taking-leave-of-reason.subtitle: Is rationality as vital as we thought?

the-trouble-with-string-theory.speaker_desc: Nobel prize-winning physicist Roger Penrose, renowned string theorist and best selling author Brian Greene, groundbreaking scientist Tasneem Zehra Husain, and polymath mathematician Eric Weinstein debate the cosmological theory. Hosted by philosopher of physics Katie Robertson.
the-trouble-with-string-theory.subtitle: Is string theory doomed?

demystifying-psychedelics-matthew-johnso.speaker_desc: Matthew Johnson is one of the world’s most published scientists in the field of psychedelics with prior appearances on the Lex Friedman Podcast, 60 Minutes and National Geographic.
demystifying-psychedelics-matthew-johnso.subtitle: The science behind the trip

beyond-the-big-bang-bjorn-ekeberg.speaker_desc: Bjørn Ekeberg is a celebrated philosopher of science whose interests lie in the limits of scientific knowledge. He is the author of erudite, Metaphysical Experiments.
beyond-the-big-bang-bjorn-ekeberg.subtitle: How to reimagine our cosmological model

the-weapon-that-failed.speaker_desc: Commentator, journalist and historian Simon Jenkins, director and CEO of think tank Chatham House, Bronwen Maddox and Chief security and defence analyst for Sky News Michael Clarke debate the geopolitical soundness of sanctions.
the-weapon-that-failed.subtitle: Do sanctions ever work?

the-dark-matter-myth-pavel-kroupa.speaker_desc: Pavel Kroupa is professor of astrophysics at University of Bonn, in Germany, where he heads the Stellar Populations and Dynamics research group.
the-dark-matter-myth-pavel-kroupa.subtitle: An interview with astrophysicist Pavel Kroupa

revolutionising-our-idea-of-the-brain.speaker_desc: Simon Baron-Cohen is a pioneering psychologist whose work on autism has revolutionised the field of developmental psychopathology. As part of his empathizing-systemizing theory, Simon famously claimed that autism is an extreme of the male brain.
revolutionising-our-idea-of-the-brain.subtitle: How neurodiversity will change everything

anonymity-the-dream-and-the-nightmare.speaker_desc: Stephen Kinsella is founder of Clean Up the Internet. He is a competition lawyer with a longstanding interest in human rights, digital technology, and democracy. Victoria Baines is part of the organisation Demos. Her interests cover content moderation, digital labour, datafication and blockchain technologies. Hugh Tomlinson is a barrister, famed for his role in the UK MP’s parliamentary expenses scandal and in the News of The World phone-hacking case.
anonymity-the-dream-and-the-nightmare.subtitle: End internet anonymity to avoid social breakdown

the-rise-and-rise-of-populism.speaker_desc: Michael Howard is the former Leader of the Conservative Party. Prior to his leadership in the early 200s, he earned the trust of Conservative leaders Margaret Thatcher and John Major, holding prestigious cabinet positions in their governments including Secretary of State for Employment, Secretary of State for the Environment and Home Secretary.
the-rise-and-rise-of-populism.subtitle: Has politics changed forever?

how-i-changed-my-mind-about-truth-simon-.speaker_desc: Simon Blackburn is a philosopher at Cambridge University known for his work on meta-ethics. He has published over a dozen books on various philosophical issues and has appeared on shows such as Radio 4's The Moral Maze and PBS's Closer to Truth.
how-i-changed-my-mind-about-truth-simon-.subtitle: An interview with philosopher Simon Blackburn

the-good-the-bad-and-the-ignored.speaker_desc: Legendary moral philosopher Peter Singer (joining us live from Australia), eminent philosopher Julian Baggini and provocative biographer Sophie Scott-Brown clash over morality. Hosted by author Robert Rowland Smith.
the-good-the-bad-and-the-ignored.subtitle: The fantasy of agency

ai-consciousness-cannot-exist-markus-gab.speaker_desc: Markus is an internationally acclaimed philosopher and holds the Chair in Epistemology, Modern and Contemporary Philosophy at the University of Bonn. He is the Director of the Center for Science and Thought as well as Chairman of the International Centre for Philosophy NRW.
ai-consciousness-cannot-exist-markus-gab.subtitle: Why a mind will never exist in a machine

the-obscure-the-banal-and-the-magical.speaker_desc: T. S. Eliot prize-winning poet Hannah Sullivan, professor of philosophy and film critic Bence Nanay and novelist Janne Teller debate whether poetry has lost its way.
the-obscure-the-banal-and-the-magical.subtitle: Has poetry lost its vision?

life-and-death-on-the-front-line-anna-ke.speaker_desc: Anna Kent is a humanitarian aid worker, NHS nurse and midwife. After receiving a Nursing Master's Degree from the University of Nottingham, she completed a Diploma in Tropical Nursing in London and joined Medecins Sans Frontieres (Doctors Without Borders) in 2007. She gained her First Degree in Midwifery in 2010 and has worked as a midwife across the world, including in South Sudan, Haiti, Bangladesh and the UK.
life-and-death-on-the-front-line-anna-ke.subtitle: Delivering the future of childbirth

the-secrets-of-the-universe.speaker_desc: Harry Cliff is a particle physicist at the University of Cambridge working on the LHCb experiment at CERN. He is the author of How To Make An Apple Pie From Scratch: In Search of the Recipe for Our Universe.
the-secrets-of-the-universe.subtitle: The Higgs boson, dark matter and other mysteries

how-to-find-and-make-sense-of-happiness-.speaker_desc: Paul Dolan is Professor of Behavioural Science at the London School of Economics and Political Science. Professor Dolan's research focusses on the measurement of happiness, its causes and consequences, and the implications for public policy. He is the author of books: Happiness by Design and Happy Ever After.
how-to-find-and-make-sense-of-happiness-.subtitle: Reimagining our understanding of wellbeing

the-psychology-of-bad-habits-susan-michi.speaker_desc: Susan Michie is Professor of Health Psychology at University College, London.
the-psychology-of-bad-habits-susan-michi.subtitle: We have complete freedom of will

a-world-by-any-other-name.speaker_desc: Philosopher Arif Ahmed, radical linguist Ruth Kempson, and philosopher and author of Closure, Hilary Lawson put language to the test. Joanna Kavenna hosts.
a-world-by-any-other-name.subtitle: Can we crack our relationship to language?

getting-everything-losing-everything.speaker_desc: Maria Balaska is currently a research fellow at the University of Hertfordshire and at Åbo Akademi University. Anders Sandberg is a researcher, popular science debater, trans-humanist and author of Superhuman: Exploring Human Enhancement from 600 BCE to 2050. Massimo Pigliucci is a philosophy professor at the City College of New York and former co-host of the Rationally Speaking Podcast. His research interests include the Philosophy of Science and the Philosophy of Biology. Mazviita Chirimuuta is a Senior Lecturer in Philosophy at the University of Edinburgh. She is a self-described techno-pessimist and anti-transhumanist.
getting-everything-losing-everything.subtitle: The dawn of a new reality?

the-demons-of-thermodynamics.speaker_desc: Katie Robertson is a research fellow and cutting edge philosopher of physics at the University of Birmingham. Her research focuses on the role that entropy plays in black holes.
the-demons-of-thermodynamics.subtitle: Seeing the world through the geometry of chaos

democracy-is-dead-calvin-robinson.speaker_desc: Calvin Robinson is a political commentator, journalist, policy advisor and campaigner who is a senior fellow at the research institute Policy Exchange. Robinson worked as a secondary school teacher and became a video games journalist. He is a regular contributor to The Daily Telegraph and the Daily Mail.
democracy-is-dead-calvin-robinson.subtitle: Does the future hold a new authoritarianism?

a-better-tomorrow.speaker_desc: Isabel Hilton is the founder and and editor of chinadialogue.net, and is a former editor-in-chief of opendemocracy.net. As CEO, she oversees China Dialogue's efforts to stoke discussion about the environment between Chinese and non-Chinese sources Shaun Bailey AM is a distinguished politician and former journalist who famously led the 2021 Conservative campaign in London as the party's candidate for Mayor of London. Thangam Debbonaire is the Labour MP for Bristol West and current Shadow Leader of the House of Commons, previously working as the Shadow Secretary of State for Housing. Michael Bocirkiw is an acclaimed writer, global affairs analyst whose been on the frontline teams at many international humanitarian organizations. He is the esteemed author of Digital Pandemic- Covid-19: How Tech Went From Bad to Good.
a-better-tomorrow.subtitle: Is the world getting better or worse?

the-strangeness-of-the-universe.speaker_desc: Influential scientist Rupert Sheldrake, prominent physicist Sabine Hossenfelder and esteemed philosopher Bjørn Ekeberg get to grips with whether the universe is stranger than we can imagine. Johnjoe McFadden hosts.
the-strangeness-of-the-universe.subtitle: A weird and wonderful world

the-seduction-of-thought.speaker_desc: Bestselling author Miranda Keeling, psychologist Steve Taylor and prison philosopher Andy West decide: to think, or not to think? Janne Teller hosts.
the-seduction-of-thought.subtitle: Is thought a distraction from reality?

the-evolution-of-war.speaker_desc: Known for his trailbrazing research on cooperation, aggression, altruism, and war, Bonaventura Majolo is Professor of Social Evolution at the University of Lincoln.
the-evolution-of-war.subtitle: Are we made to go to war?

logic-for-the-left.speaker_desc: Ben Burgis is a philosophy professor at Morehouse University Perimeter College, a columnist for Jacobin Magazine and Arc Digital Media, and the co-host of the Dead Pundits Society. He also used to have a regular segment on The Michael Brooks Show called "the Debunk." Burgis is the author of several books including' Give Them an Argument: Logic for the Left' and 'Christopher Hitchens: What He Got Right, How He Went Wrong, and Why He Still Matters'.
logic-for-the-left.subtitle: Why rationality is important for the left

forbidden-fruit.speaker_desc: Journalist Zoe Strimpel, radical social theorist Myriam François and writer Louise Perry fight over forbidden fruit. Hosted by Rana Mitter.
forbidden-fruit.subtitle: Sex and taboo in the modern age

fact-checking-the-fact-checkers.speaker_desc: Renowned journalist Paul Mason, author of Technology is Not Neutral Stephanie Hare and UnHerd editor Freddie Sayers debate the facts behind the facts. Hilary Lawson hosts.
fact-checking-the-fact-checkers.subtitle: Is it possible for fact checking to be impartial?

how-philosophy-got-lost.speaker_desc: Slavoj Žižek is a globally renowned philosopher and cultural critic. He is international director of the Birkbeck Institute for the Humanities at the University of London, visiting professor at New York University and a senior researcher at the University of Ljubljana's Department of Philosophy. He is the author of several books, including The Sublime Object of Ideology, The Parallax View, Living in the End Times and Heaven in Disorder.
how-philosophy-got-lost.subtitle: An interview with philosopher Slavoj Žižek

material-girls-kathleen-stock.speaker_desc: Kathleen Mary Linn Stock OBE is a British philosopher and writer. She was a professor of philosophy at the University of Sussex until 2021. She has published academic work on aesthetics, fiction, imagination, sexual objectification, and sexual orientation.
material-girls-kathleen-stock.subtitle: Kathleen Stock’s perspective on sex and gender

beyond-the-darkness.speaker_desc: Trailblazing philosopher Bjørn Ekeberg, theoretical physicist Francesca Chadha-Day and influential astrophysicist Pavel Kroupa explore the many mysteries of dark matter. John-Joe McFadden hosts.
beyond-the-darkness.subtitle: Dark Matter: A Baseless Hypothesis?

truth-delusion-and-psychedelic-reality.speaker_desc: KCL psychiatrist James Rucker, philosopher Julian Baggini, and creative director and artist Eileen Hall debate psychedelics and science. Hosted by leading psychiatrist Mark Salter.
truth-delusion-and-psychedelic-reality.subtitle: Are psychedelics a window into reality?

the-science-of-uncertainty-with-tim-palm.subtitle: Uncertainty as the essence of understanding

there-is-no-planet-b.speaker_desc: Mike Berners-Lee is a pre-eminent expert in carbon footprinting and Professor and Fellow of the Institute for Social Futures at Lancaster University. He is also the director and principal consultant at Small World Consulting and the author of three books, including There Is No Planet B: A Handbook for the Make or Break Years.
there-is-no-planet-b.subtitle: An interview with Mike Berners-Lee

society-2-0.speaker_desc: Member of the Shadow Cabinet House Thangam Debbonaire, Radio 6 DJ and psychotherapist Nemone Metaxas and Marxist philosopher Ben Burgis explore the undervalued people in our society. Hosted by Mary-Ann Sieghart.
society-2-0.subtitle: Do we unfairly privilege the unelected?

being-ourselves-and-being-with-others.speaker_desc: Critically-acclaimed writer Janne Teller, world leading psychologist and psychiatrist Stefan Priebe, and actress-writer and Booker Prize nominee Sophie Ward debate the lures of loneliness. Hosted by renowned journalist Elaine Glaser.
being-ourselves-and-being-with-others.subtitle: Has independence undermined community?

why-dawkins-is-wrong-denis-noble.speaker_desc: Oxford Professor and one of the pioneers of Systems Biology, Noble developed the first viable mathematical model of the working heart in 1960.
why-dawkins-is-wrong-denis-noble.subtitle: An interview with the renowned biologist

the-accurate-the-perfect-and-the-dangero.speaker_desc: Futurist Anders Sandberg, Oxford bioethicist Michael Parker and author of Technology is Not Neutral Stephanie Hare fight for the future of tech, data and AI. Hosted by pioneering economist Linda Yueh.
the-accurate-the-perfect-and-the-dangero.subtitle: The potential and the threat of data

the-ignorance-of-experts.speaker_desc: Author of How The World Thinks Julian Baggini, philosopher of biology Ellen Clarke, and radical philosopher Ben Burgis tackle our diminishing trust in experts and what to do about it. Hosted by Güneş Taylor.
the-ignorance-of-experts.subtitle: Can we rely on science for the answers?

are-we-facing-a-new-world-order-nigel-in.speaker_desc: Nigel Inkster is the distinguished former director of intelligence for the British Intelligence Service, and now Director of Intelligence Analysis at Enodo Economics.
are-we-facing-a-new-world-order-nigel-in.subtitle: Interview with Nigel Inkster

how-to-see-the-world-through-kafkas-eyes.speaker_desc: Steven Berkoff is an actor, author, playwright, theatre practitioner and theatre director. He is noted for his roles in the James Bond film, ‘Octopussy’, A Clockwork Orange, and The Girl With The Dragon Tattoo. On the stage, he has performed the title roles in Shakespeare’s Hamlet, Richard II and Macbeth. He is recognised for his brand of “Berkovian theatre", which combines elements of physical theatre, total theatre and expressionism.
how-to-see-the-world-through-kafkas-eyes.subtitle: Unmasking the human condition

the-equality-myth.speaker_desc: Journalist and writer Laurie Penny, Shadow Leader of the Commons, Thangam Debbonaire and campaigner-author Louise Perry try to tip the scales. Hosted by Oxford historian Rana Mitter.
the-equality-myth.subtitle: Is the pursuit of absolute equality a mistake?

head-to-head-philosophy-vs-science-marik.speaker_desc: Marika Taylor is a Professor of Theoretical Physics and the Head of School within Mathematical Sciences at University of Southampton. Taylor's research is focussed on string theory, quantum field theory and gravitational physics. Julian Baggini is a philosopher, journalist, author and the co-founder of The Philosopher's Magazine. He is the acclaimed author of over 20 works of popular philosophy. Güneş Taylor hosts.
head-to-head-philosophy-vs-science-marik.subtitle: Does science need philosophy?

the-democracy-illusion.speaker_desc: Trailblazing journalist Calvin Robinson, social activist Shabnam Nasimi, and radical journalist Aaron Bastani debate the changing face of democracy in the 21st century. Hosted by Manveen Rana.
the-democracy-illusion.subtitle: Do elected politicians make a difference?

deconstructing-the-art-of-storytelling.speaker_desc: Danny Robins is an award-winning British writer, broadcaster and journalist. His most recent play, 2:22 A Ghost Story, has received much critical acclaim.
deconstructing-the-art-of-storytelling.subtitle: How to keep your audience hooked

the-key-to-consciousness.speaker_desc: Revolutionary cognitive psychologist Donald Hoffman (joining us live from across the pond), neuroscientist Hannah Critchlow and philosopher Sam Coleman battle to unlock consciousness. Hosted by award-winning novelist Joanna Kavenna.
the-key-to-consciousness.subtitle: Is materialism a fundamental mistake?

rebellion-and-rebirth.speaker_desc: Emma Sulkowicz is a performance artist living and working in New York City, most famous for her year-long performance art project Mattress Performance: Carry That Weight where she dragged a mattress around Columbia University in protest at the school’s mishandling of her sexual assault complaint, and becoming one of the faces of the movement against rape culture on college campuses.
rebellion-and-rebirth.subtitle: What activism teaches us about the world

the-future-of-cosmology-with-roger-penro.subtitle: Is the universe reborn in cycles?

gravity-a-new-window-to-the-universe-pau.subtitle: Black holes, gravity and the future of cosmology

after-happily-ever-after.speaker_desc: Academy award nominee David Hare, critically acclaimed writer Janne Teller and director-producer Sophie Fiennes talk endings. Hosted by Barry Smith, Director of the Institute of Philosophy.
after-happily-ever-after.subtitle: Do our lives tell a story?

feminism-and-identity-politics.speaker_desc: Award-winning, Ugandan-born author and columnist Yasmin Alibhai-Brown currently writes for The Independent and The Evening Standard, and is the founder of British Muslims for Secular Democracy.
feminism-and-identity-politics.subtitle: Is identity politics holding feminism back?

beyond-experiment.speaker_desc: Harry Cliff is a particle physicist at the University of Cambridge working on the Large Hadron Collider at CERN. A prominent promoter for the public's understanding of physics, Harry is also the author of the popular science book, How To Make An Apple Pie From Scratch. Tim Maudlin is a world leading researcher in the foundations of physics, metaphysics, and logic. He is a Professor of Philosophy at NYU and Founder and Director of the John Bell Institute for the Foundations of Physics. Marika Taylor is one of the foremost researchers of string theory, quantum field theory and gravitational physics. Having completed her doctoral dissertation under Stephen Hawking, Taylor went onto be Professor of Theoretical Physics and head of Mathematical Physics at the University of Southampton. Barry C Smith is a professor of philosophy and directs the Institute of Philosophy at the University of London’s School of Advanced Study. He is the founding director of the Centre for the Study of Sensess.
beyond-experiment.subtitle: Are some scientific theories fictional speculation

the-enduring-trauma-of-the-caste-system-.speaker_desc: Ashwini Deshpande is an Indian economist best known for her papers concerning various topics such as poverty, inequality, regional disparities and gender discrimination. She is currently working as a professor at Ashoka University, and formerly taught at Delhi School of Economics.
the-enduring-trauma-of-the-caste-system-.subtitle: Overcoming prejudice and brutal discrimination

the-future-of-freedom.speaker_desc: Prolific British writer, philosopher and co-founder of The Philosophers’ Magazine, Julian Baggini, renowned Australian philosopher of science, Peter Godfrey-Smith, and leading British neuroscientist and UCL professor, Sarah Garfinkel, argue about empiricism and its role in determining the existence of free will. Alex O'Connor hosts.
the-future-of-freedom.subtitle: Can experiments settle the free will debate?

a-tale-of-truth-with-simon-blackburn.speaker_desc: Author of Think and Truth: A Guide for the Perplexed , Simon Blackburn has worked to bring philosophy to a wider audience. He was a Professor of Philosophy at Cambridge University and Vice President of the British Humanist Association.
a-tale-of-truth-with-simon-blackburn.subtitle: The case against relativism

the-happiness-delusion.speaker_desc: Aaron Bastani is co-founder of Novara Media, an independent, self-described radical left-wing alternative media organisation. He is also the author ‘Fully Automated Luxury Communism’. Paul Dolan is a behavioural scientist and author of the bestselling book ‘Happiness By Design: Finding Pleasure and Purpose in Everyday Life.’ Joanna Kavenna is a multi-award-winning writer. She was named as one of Granta’s Best Young British Novelists for her ground-breaking novels including A Field Guide to Reality and Zed. Regular presenter of Night Waves and writer for the Financial Times, History Today, and the London Review of Books, Rana Mitter is Professor of the History and Politics of Modern China at Oxford.
the-happiness-delusion.subtitle: In search of the aim of life

the-theory-to-end-all-theories.speaker_desc: Theoretical physicist Peter Woit, physicist and educator Becky Parker and critic of realism Hilary Lawson test their theories of everything. Hosted by award-winning science documentary filmmaker David Malone.
the-theory-to-end-all-theories.subtitle: Is a theory of everything possible?

the-making-of-reality-hilary-lawson.speaker_desc: Hilary Lawson is a philosopher and a renowned critic of philosophical realism. He is best known for his work on reflexivity and his theory of Closure, which puts forward a non-realist metaphysics arguing that we close the openness of the world with our thought and language.
the-making-of-reality-hilary-lawson.subtitle: An interview with Hilary Lawson

the-mystery-of-prehistory-mary-ann-ochot.speaker_desc: Known best for her work as a presenter, Mary-Ann Ochota specialises in anthropology, archaeology and social history. She co-presented Channel 4’s cult archaeology show ‘Time Team’, and recently fronted the hugely successful ‘Feral Children’ series.
the-mystery-of-prehistory-mary-ann-ochot.subtitle: What makes us who we are?

equality-on-the-frontline.speaker_desc: Mary Ann Sieghart is a journalist and radio presenter and a former assistant editor of The Times . Her latest book is The Authority Gap: Why Women Are Still Taken Less Seriously Than Men . Minna Salami is journalist, feminist and author. She has written on the experiences of Nigerian women, the African Diaspora and feminism through her award-winning blog, MsAfropolitan . Her latest book is Sensuous Knowledge . Maya Oppenheim is Women's Correspondent for the Independent and writes on issues of domestic violence, sexual assault, abortion and period poverty. Rana Mitter is a regular presenter of Night Waves and writer for the Financial Times , History Today , and the London Review of Books . He is also a Professor of the History and Politics of Modern China at the University of Oxford.
equality-on-the-frontline.subtitle: Do women still need 'protecting' from men?

the-passion-of-reason.speaker_desc: Philosopher and acclaimed author, Julian Baggini, leading molecular biologist, Güneş Taylor, and critical race theorist, Tommy Curry, put passion and reason to the test.
the-passion-of-reason.subtitle: Does emotion rule over reason?

fiction-social-construction-and-gender-k.speaker_desc: Kathleen Mary Linn Stock OBE is a British philosopher and writer. She was a professor of philosophy at the University of Sussex until 2021. She has published academic work on aesthetics, fiction, imagination, sexual objectification, and sexual orientation.
fiction-social-construction-and-gender-k.subtitle: Freedom, truth and trans rights

how-occams-razor-changed-the-world-johnj.speaker_desc: Johnjoe McFadden is a Professor of Modular Genetics at the University of Surrey and the author of Quantum Revolution. His work focuses on how quantum mechanics influences our biology and the use of quantum theory to uncover alternative evolutionary frameworks.
how-occams-razor-changed-the-world-johnj.subtitle: The value of simplicity in a complex world

love-and-other-drugs.speaker_desc: Anders Sandberg is a research fellow at the Future of Humanity Institute at Oxford, where his research focusses on the societal and ethical issues surrounding human enhancement and new technologies. He is also research associate at the Oxford Uehiro Centre for Practical Ethics and the Oxford Centre for Neuroethics. A regular commentator and participant of public debates concerning human enhancement, Anders comes to the festival in support of an exciting transhuman future. On Twitter he describes himself as an academic jack of all trades, and we are sure he is a master of some. Ella Whelan is a political commentator and freelance journalist. After graduating in 2014, Whelan joined online politics magazine spiked, and quickly rose to assistant editor. She is a producer of the annual Battle of Ideas Festival in central London and writes for the Sunday Times, the Irish Times, the Sun and The Economist. Whelan regularly appears in the media; her support for Brexit and criticism of no-platforming and 21st century feminism has caused her to clash with mainstream journalists on the BBC, Sky, and Channel 4. Her first book, What Women Want: Fun, Freedom and an End to Feminism, was described as "a leading voice of a rising generation of young warriors for free speech" by distinguished social critic Camille Paglia. Rupert Sheldrake is a biologist, author and parapsychology researcher, best known for his hypothesis of morphic resonance. He is a critic of New Atheism, and has also challenged the idea that the laws of nature are fixed and unchanging. From 2005 to 2010, Rupert was Director of the Perrott-Warrick project for research on unexplained human and animal abilities, funded by Trinity College, Cambridge. Rupert has sole authored 9 books, including A New Science of Life, The Science Delusion and his newest book Ways to Go Beyond and Why They Work. Rupert is also famous for the controversial, viral TED talk he gave which was banned by the organisation. Myriam Francois is an author, broadcaster and academic on issues related to Islam, France and the Middle East. She is host of the increasingly popular We Need to Talk about Whiteness Podcast.
love-and-other-drugs.subtitle: Are psychedelics the love potion of the future?

trading-with-the-enemy.speaker_desc: Andrew Adonis is a Labour Politian, leading journalist and academic. John Kay is a bestselling author and one of the UK's most renowned economists. Janne Teller is a novelist and former conflict advisor for the UNO and EU. Hosting this debate is journalist and columnist at the Irish Times, Finn McRedmond.
trading-with-the-enemy.subtitle: Trading with the enemy

the-union-of-science-and-philosophy.speaker_desc: Bjørn Ekeberg is a philosopher of science whose main interests lie in the limits of scientific knowledge. He is also author of Metaphysical Experiments: Physics and the Invention of the Universe.
the-union-of-science-and-philosophy.subtitle: An interview with Bjørn Ekeberg

consciousness-in-the-machine.speaker_desc: Legendary anti-reality theorist Donald Hoffman, fearless computer scientist and philosopher Bernardo Kastrup and distinguished AI ethicist and philosopher Susan Schneider lock horns over the possibility of AI consciousness. Theories of Everything's Curt Jaimungal hosts.
consciousness-in-the-machine.subtitle: Could AI ever be conscious?

how-to-uncover-the-truth-with-manveen-ra.speaker_desc: Manveen Rana is a senior broadcast journalist who has hosted the Times Radio podcast Stories of our times since March 2020. Formerly she worked for the BBC, as a reporter for the Today programme.
how-to-uncover-the-truth-with-manveen-ra.subtitle: Impartiality, bias, and the role of journalism

rationality-and-the-left-ben-burgis.speaker_desc: Philosophy professor at Morehouse University Perimeter College, Ben Burgis is a columnist for Jacobin Magazine and a prolific Youtube debater.
rationality-and-the-left-ben-burgis.subtitle: Ben Burgis on media, culture wars, and the left

beyond-mad-or-bad.speaker_desc: Mark Salter is a consultant psychiatrist based in London’s East End, specialising in risk, untowardness and media portrayals of mental distress. He is currently the media expert for the Royal College of Psychiatrists and has worked as a broadcaster for the BBC and ITV. Sara Evans-Lacko is an Associate Professorial Research Fellow at the Care Policy and Evaluation Centre at the London School of Economics. She has a particular interest in the role of health services and social support in the prevention and treatment of mental illness. At the global level, she has advised on national and state mental health plans and her work has been cited in key government reports in Brazil, Colombia, the Czech Republic, Germany, Mexico and the UK and by international organizations such as the World Health Organization. Sir Simon Wessely is Professor of Psychological Medicine at the Institute of Psychiatry, Psychology & Neuroscience at King’s College London. He is a Consultant Psychiatrist at King’s College Hospital and the Maudsley Hospital. Sir Simon is currently Chair of the government’s Independent Review of the Mental Health Act. Stefan Priebe is a leading psychologist and psychiatrist and Professor of Social and Community Psychiatry at Queen Mary, University of London, He is also Director of the WHO Collaborating Centre for Mental Health Service Development, Director of the NIHR Global Health Research Group for Developing Psycho-Social Interventions.
beyond-mad-or-bad.subtitle: Mental health, social constructs and community

how-to-be-a-sceptic-massimo-pigliucci.speaker_desc: Massimo Pigliucci is a philosophy professor at City College New York and one of the world's leading thinkers in the study of Ancient Stoicism. His most recent books include The Quest for Character and Think like a Stoic.
how-to-be-a-sceptic-massimo-pigliucci.subtitle: Using scepticism in the search for truth

world-history-and-the-baby-bust.speaker_desc: Thangam Debbonaire is a Labour MP for Bristol West and shadow leader of the House of Commons. She describes herself as a supporter of 'fettered capitalism' and has argued for drug reform. Dr Aveek Bhattacharya is the Research Director of the Social Market Foundation and a former policy analyst for the Institute of Alcohol Studies. He also contributes regularly to The Guardian, The Critic and the Financial Times. Tim Palmer is an internationally renowned meteorologist and Professor at the University of Oxford. He works on the tough, crucial problems of uncertainty in our weather and climate, drawing on his background in fundamental physics to do so. He was appointed as CBE in the 2015 New Year’s Honours list for services to science and has won numerous other awards in recognition of his world-leading work. Mike Berners-Lee is an English researcher and writer on carbon foot-printing. He is a professor and fellow of the Institute for Social Futures at Lancaster University and director and principal consultant of Small World Consulting, where he advises organisations on how best to respond to the current climate and ecological issues
world-history-and-the-baby-bust.subtitle: Is population decline a bad thing?

the-medicine-myth.speaker_desc: Denis Noble is a world renowned biologist, and Professor Emeritus of Cardiovascular Physiology at the University of Oxford. Famous for developing the first mathematical model of cardiac cells. Nessa Carey is a ground-breaking British biologist working in the field of molecular biology and biotechnology. She is International Director of the technology transfer organization PraxisUnico and a Visiting Professor at Imperial College London. Guy Brown heads a research group at the University of Cambridge working on cell death in the brain, the heart and in cancer. His previous book The Energy of Life won the Wellcome Trust Prize for popular science. David Malone is an independent filmmaker, Green Party politician, and author of The Debt Generation.
the-medicine-myth.subtitle: The failure of medicalising philosophy

finding-transcendence-in-a-secular-world.speaker_desc: Rupert Sheldrake is a preeminent biologist and author best known for his hypothesis of morphic resonance. His books include Science and Spiritual Practices, Ways to Go Beyond And Why They Work and The Science Delusion. Furthermore, he was ranked in the top 100 thought leaders for 2013 by the Duttweiler Institute, Switzerland's leading think tank, and has been recognised as one of the 'most spiritually influential living people' by Watkins' Mind Body Spirit Magazine.
finding-transcendence-in-a-secular-world.subtitle: Spirituality amid secularism

how-to-learn-from-history-matthew-green.speaker_desc: Matthew Green is an historian and broadcaster with a doctorate from the University of Oxford. He writes for national newspapers, has appeared in many television documentaries, and is the author of London: A Travel Guide Through Time. His latest book is Shadowlands: A Journey Through Lost Britain, which explores the lost causes and dead ends of history in a deeply evocative and dazzlingly original account of Britain's past.
how-to-learn-from-history-matthew-green.subtitle: Learning the lessons from our past

the-code-to-the-cosmos.speaker_desc: Arif Ahmed is a University of Cambridge philosopher and well-known advocate for the tolerance of diverse political views. Peter Woit is a renowned theoretical physicist, Columbia University professor and critic of string theory. Marika Taylor is a Southampton University theoretical physicist and award-winning string theorist. Our host is David Malone, is an independent filmmaker, Green Party politician, and author of The Debt Generation.
the-code-to-the-cosmos.subtitle: Is maths the language of the universe?

the-future-of-sex.speaker_desc: Güneş Taylor is a training fellow at the Francis Crick Institute, the London-based biomedical research centre. Her research predominantly focuses on the genetic formation of ovaries and testes. In 2018, Güneş was awarded the Crick Public Engagement Prize for her efforts in the public communication of science.
the-future-of-sex.subtitle: Exploring the next stage of humanity

the-dream-of-progress.speaker_desc: Kenneth Cukier is a renowned American journalist and coauthor of the NYT Bestselling book “Big Data”. Caitjan Gainty is an established historian of 20th century health and co-runs the Healthy Scepticism project, Nolan Gertz is a philosopher of applied ethics, and author of the cutting-edge book "Nihilism and Technology". Our host, Jess Wade, is a well-loved British physicist, researcher and advocate for women in STEM.
the-dream-of-progress.subtitle: Why do we need technological progress?

the-new-10-commandments.speaker_desc: Professor of Philosophy at the Open University Sophie-Grace Chappell, Professor of Philosophy at the City College of New York Massimo Pigliucci and Professor in the Departments of Psychology and Psychiatry at the University of Cambridge Simon Baron-Cohen discuss if life can be reduced to a rulebook. Myriam François hosts.
the-new-10-commandments.subtitle: Do we really need codes for living?

new-politics-and-old-threats.speaker_desc: Michael Bociurkiw is an acclaimed writer, global affairs analyst and two-time TEDx speaker. He is also the author of Digital Pandemic- Covid-19: How Tech Went From Bad to Good. Tommy Curry is a trail-blazing philosophy professor at the University of Edinburgh, and author of ‘The Man-Not: Race, Class, Genre and the Dilemmas of Black Manhood’. Zoe Strimpel is a British journalist, academic historian, author, and commentator on gender and relationships. She is a columnist for The Sunday Telegraph where she writes a weekly column, commenting on gender, feminism, dating, relationships and identity politics. Barry Smith hosts.
new-politics-and-old-threats.subtitle: Are social issues more important than economics?

dawkins-on-the-crisis-of-rationality.speaker_desc: David Freeman formerly presented Science in Action for the BBC World Service as well as The Bookshow for Sky TV. For many years he hosted a daily book programme in Oxford. He has also featured on Jazz FM for many years and is now the resident expert on blues music.
dawkins-on-the-crisis-of-rationality.subtitle: In conversation with Richard Dawkins

the-one-true-story.speaker_desc: Janne Teller is a critically-acclaimed writer, whose oeuvre consists mainly of novels, essays, and short stories, often focusing on grand-scale existential topics which spark controversial debate. Barry C Smith is a philosophy professor, and the director of the Institute of Philosophy at the University of London’s School of Advanced Study. He also co-directs the Centre for the Study of the Senses, a research centre trying to understand how our senses contribute to our perception of the world. Sophie Allen is a renowned philosopher, her work focuses on philosophical methodology, metaphilosophy and metaphysics. She is a lecturer at the University of Keele where she writes on the very understanding of philosophy itself. Myriam Francois hosts.
the-one-true-story.subtitle: Is philosophy the disinterested pursuit of truth?

phil-collins-how-to-write-a-compelling-s.speaker_desc: 'Writer-in-chief at The Draft, contributing editor at The New Statesman, columnist for the Evening Standard, and the former lead writer at The Times, Philip Collins has held positions at almost every major newspaper in the country. Having previously been a speech writer for Tony Blair, the Director of the Social Market Foundation think tank and an Equity Strategist at two investment banks, Philip's wealth of experience makes him a one of the most trusted voices in politics.
phil-collins-how-to-write-a-compelling-s.subtitle: Tips and tricks on how to grip your audience

the-worrying-rebirth-of-expertise-david-.speaker_desc: 'David Goodhart is a British journalist, commentator and author. Along with being a correspondent for the Financial Times for 12 years, he is the founder and a former editor of Prospect magazine. 'Goodhart offers the best and most complete explanation I've seen for why things seem to be coming apart in so many countries at the same time.' -- Jonathan Haidt
the-worrying-rebirth-of-expertise-david-.subtitle: Experts, the rise and the fall

sins-of-the-past-visions-of-the-future.speaker_desc: Myriam Francois is an award-winning Franco-Irish journalist and research associate at the Centre of Islamic Studies at SOAS University. She has also hosted several documentaries for the BBC and Al Jazeera among others. Calvin Robinson is a British political commentator and broadcaster who is also a deacon of the Free Church of England. He is a regular contributor to the Daily Telegraph, Daily Mail and Spiked. Kehinde Andrews is a British Academic and author specialising in Black Studies. He is a professor at Birmingham City University, director of the Centre for Critical Social Research and the first Black Studies Professor in the UK.
sins-of-the-past-visions-of-the-future.subtitle: How our construction of race impacts the future

living-forever2.speaker_desc: Anders Sandberg is a researcher at the Future of Humanity Institute which centres on management of low-probability high-impact risks, estimating the capabilities of future technologies, and very long-range futures. Henry Marsh is a world leading neurosurgeon, pioneer of neurological advances and bestselling author. His memoir, Do No Harm: Stories of Life, Death and Brain Surgery, received wide acclaim detailing his work in the UK, former Soviet Ukraine and Nepal. Anna Kent is a humanitarian, a NHS nurse and a midwife. In her profoundly moving book 'Frontline Midwife' (2022) she gives a no holds barred account of delivering babies in war zones, Isabel Hilton hosts.
living-forever2.subtitle: Should we want to live forever?

food-morality-and-logic.speaker_desc: Alex O’Connor, also known by his YouTube alias ‘CosmicSkeptic’, is a prolific philosopher, youtuber, public speaker and animal welfare activist. His YouTube channel has amassed over 450 000 subscribers and discusses issues relating to free speech, free will, animal rights and the philosophical arguments against religion.
food-morality-and-logic.subtitle: Veganism for Philosophers

the-wealth-paradox.speaker_desc: Radical economist Guy Standing, Senior Research Fellow at the Institute of Economic Affairs Kristian Niemietz and acclaimed writer and former macroeconomist Janne Teller lock horns. Phil Collins hosts.
the-wealth-paradox.subtitle: How do we create a prosperous society?

how-to-write-your-first-novel-sophie-war.speaker_desc: Sophie Ward is a captivating stage and screen actress, and a writer of non-fiction and fiction. Her feature film debut in Steven Spielberg's Young Sherlock Holmes. She has written for The Guardian, The Times, and The Spectator, won the 2018 Royal Academy Pin Drop Award for her short story "Sunbed", and had her first novel, Love and Other Thought Experiments was longlisted for both the Desmond Elliott Prize and the Booker Prize.
how-to-write-your-first-novel-sophie-war.subtitle: Exploring the creative process

cosmology-and-the-big-bust.speaker_desc: The Big Bang Never Happened author, Eric Lerner, distinguished astrophysicist Claudia Maraston, and renowned physicist and author of The End of Time Julian Barbour argue lock horns over the Big Bang. Jess Wade hosts.
cosmology-and-the-big-bust.subtitle: Should we abandon the Big Bang theory?

seeing-happy-with-mandy-seligman.speaker_desc: Mandy Seligman is an award-winning black and white photographer who began her career as a developmental social psychologist. She has spent the last thirty years traveling around the world with Martin Seligman spreading Positive Psychology.
seeing-happy-with-mandy-seligman.subtitle: Honing in on that which makes us happy

the-good-and-the-evil.speaker_desc: Fearless thinker, Tommy Curry, esteemed philosopher, Massimo Pigliucci, and author of Zed, Joanna Kavenna, explore whether 'good' and 'evil' are just categories used for coercion. Hosted by Myriam Francois.
the-good-and-the-evil.subtitle: Can we make ultimate moral judgements?

finding-an-ultimate-theory-of-everything.speaker_desc: Eric Weinstein is an American podcast host and managing director of Thiel Capital. He received his PhD in mathematical physics from Harvard University in 1992 and in 2013, he proposed a unified theory of physics called ‘Geometric Unity’. Additionally, Weinstein was the first to coin the phrase the ‘intellectual dark web’, to describe a collection of heterodox commentators who oppose identity politics, political correctness and cancel culture.
finding-an-ultimate-theory-of-everything.subtitle: Eric Weinstein and Michael Shermer in conversation

the-good-the-great-and-the-ghosts-of-the.speaker_desc: British artist Stuart Semple, English journalist and broadcaster Jenni Murray and author of 'The Hours Have Lost Their Clock: The Politics of Nostalgia' Grafton Tanner debate whether we should see our attachment to the Beatles, Blackadder and Bach as a deep conservativism that should be overcome. Myriam François hosts.
the-good-the-great-and-the-ghosts-of-the.subtitle: Nostalgia vs. the new

from-one-universe-to-the-next-roger-penr.speaker_desc: Roger Penrose is a world-renowned mathematician, mathematical physicist, philosopher of science and Nobel Laureate in Physics. He is best known for his work on general relativity and sharing the Wolf Prize for Physics with Stephen Hawking for his work on black holes.
from-one-universe-to-the-next-roger-penr.subtitle: An interview with Roger Penrose

the-world-in-jeopardy.speaker_desc: Labour MP and Shadow Economic Secretary to the Treasury, Tulip Siddiq, renowned cultural critic Theodore Dalrymple, and former director of operations and intelligence for the British Secret Intelligence Service, Nigel Inkster lock horns. Myriam François hosts.
the-world-in-jeopardy.subtitle: A new era is upon us

truth-and-lies-in-politics-thangam-debbo.speaker_desc: Thangam Debbonaire is the Labour MP for Bristol West and current Shadow Leader of the House of Commons, previously working as the Shadow Secretary of State for Housing. She describes herself as a "northern European socialist".
truth-and-lies-in-politics-thangam-debbo.subtitle: How to fix parliamentary democracy

moral-facts-and-moral-fantasy.speaker_desc: Firebrand philosopher Slavoj Žižek, bestselling author of Zed Joanna Kavenna, and philosopher and author of Truth Simon Blackburn debate objective morality in a postmodern age. Hosted by Professor and Chair of Jurisprudence at the University of Oxford, Ruth Chang.
moral-facts-and-moral-fantasy.subtitle: Is our search for an objective morality misguided?

towards-a-just-economy-angela-eagle.speaker_desc: Angela Eagle DBE was the Former Shadow Secretary of State for Business, Innovation and Skills, and has been the Labour MP for Wallasey since 1992. Her engaging book The New Serfdom: The Triumph of Conservative Ideas and How to Defeat Them addresses how we can build a successful economy with greater equality for all.
towards-a-just-economy-angela-eagle.subtitle: An interview with Angela Eagle

breaking-through-the-consciousness-stale.speaker_desc: Philip Goff is a renowned philosopher of consciousness at Durham University. His unique research focuses on integrating consciousness into our scientific worldview.
breaking-through-the-consciousness-stale.subtitle: An interview with Philip Goff

the-gene-machine.speaker_desc: World-famous scientist Richard Dawkins goes head-to-head with celebrated biologist Denis Noble as they lock horns over the role of genes over the eons. Güneş Taylor hosts.
the-gene-machine.subtitle: Dawkins' legacy

the-betrayal-of-beauty.speaker_desc: Award winning director Sophie Fiennes, philosopher of the senses Barry Smith and legendary critic Julian Spalding battle for beauty. Mark Salter hosts.
the-betrayal-of-beauty.subtitle: Can we separate art from beauty?

the-fantasies-of-the-west.speaker_desc: Paul Mason is a radical author, commentator, and political journalist. Previously the Newsnight Business Editor, Economics Editor at Channel 4 News, where he reported on Europe's troubled economic crises. He is now a freelance author and journalist. Bhavna Dave is a Senior Lecturer in Central Asian Politics at the Department of Politics and International Studies at SOAS, University of London. Peter Hitchens is an award-winning conservative author, broadcaster, journalist and political commentator. He has a weekly column in the Mail on Sunday and is a prolific contributor to a wide range of magazines. Mary Ann Sieghart hosts.
the-fantasies-of-the-west.subtitle: Does the rest of the world really think like us?

the-world-after-reality-hilary-lawson.speaker_desc: Hilary Lawson is a philosopher and an outspoken critic of philosophical realism. He is best known for his theory of Closure, which puts forward a non-realist metaphysics.
the-world-after-reality-hilary-lawson.subtitle: Reality is dead

tomorrow-sex-will-be-good-again.speaker_desc: Katherine Angel is the author of Tomorrow Sex Will Be Good Again, published in 2021 to critical acclaim and widespread international coverage. She is also the author of Daddy Issues, and Unmastered: A Book on Desire, Most Difficult to Tell.
tomorrow-sex-will-be-good-again.subtitle: Challenging our assumptions about women’s desire

the-edge-of-the-universe.speaker_desc: Oxford maverick physicist David Deutsch, leading cosmology theorist George Ellis and theoretical physicist and origin of life expert Sara Walker debate whether the notion of infinity is a key insight into the character of the universe, a mathematical artefact, or simply nonsense. Hosted by the renowned public intellectual, writer and producer Robert Lawrence Kuhn.
the-edge-of-the-universe.subtitle: Is the idea of infinity nonsense or a key insight?

lost-in-language.speaker_desc: Distinguished philosopher of language and the senses Barry Smith, Wittgensteinian expert Maria Balaska and maverick post-post modern philosopher Hilary Lawson lock horns over whether philosophy's fixation on language has held us back. Rufus Duits hosts.
lost-in-language.subtitle: Is analytic philosophy's fixation on language bad?

the-life-inside-with-andy-west.speaker_desc: Andy West has taught philosophy in prisons since 2015. His first book, 'The Life Inside' - which explores the conversations he has with people inside about their lives, discusses their ideas and feelings and listens as the men and women he works with explore new ways to think about their situation.
the-life-inside-with-andy-west.subtitle: Exploring the world behind bars

exploring-the-dark-side-of-physics-john-.speaker_desc: John Ellis is a Maxwell prize-winning theoretical physicist, and is considered one of the world's leading physicists. John is currently Clerk Maxwell Professor of Theoretical Physics at King's College London, and since 1978 has held an indefinite contract at CERN.
exploring-the-dark-side-of-physics-john-.subtitle: Exploring the dark side of physics

overcoming-tribal-division.speaker_desc: Myriam François host of the ‘We Need to Talk About Whiteness’ podcast, which aims to explore the meaning of 'whiteness' in conversations around race and racism, is a writer and broadcaster. Paul Dolan is a behavioural scientist and author of the bestselling book ‘Happiness By Design: Finding Pleasure and Purpose in Everyday Life.’ Ella Whelan is a freelance journalist, commentator and author of What Women Want: Fun, Freedom and an End to Feminism. Isabel Hilton hosts.
overcoming-tribal-division.subtitle: Is our society too divisive?

the-ai-hoax-mazviita-chirimuuta.speaker_desc: Mazviita Chirimuuta is a Senior Lecturer in philosophy at Edinburgh University, with interests in neuroscience and philosophy of mind, especially in colour perception.
the-ai-hoax-mazviita-chirimuuta.subtitle: Is AI just a fantasy?

why-you-cant-pay-attention-bence-nanay.speaker_desc: Bence Nanay is a Professor of Philosophy, whose research focuses on philosophy of mind, philosophy of biology and aesthetics. He is co-director of the Centre for Philosophical Psychology at the University of Antwerp and also Senior Research Associate at Peterhouse, Cambridge University.
why-you-cant-pay-attention-bence-nanay.subtitle: Living in the age of the attention economy

the-future-of-money-vince-cable.subtitle: Vince Cable in conversation with Linda Yueh

catching-sight-of-our-self.speaker_desc: Author of 'The Master and his Emmisary', Iain McGilchrist, Professor of Philosophy at University of Antwerp, Bence Nanay, Emerita Professor of English at the University of Texas, Betty Sue Flowers, and famed author and science journalist, Anil Ananthaswamy, lock horns over the notion of self knowledge. Hosted by philosopher, Mary-Jane Rubenstein.
catching-sight-of-our-self.subtitle: Is it possible to know ourselves?

beyond-the-self-and-non-self.speaker_desc: Quantum biologist JohnJoe McFadden, distinguished immunologist Ane Ogbe and Professor of Paediatric Immunology Petter Brodin debate the self and the non-self. Gunes Taylor hosts.
beyond-the-self-and-non-self.subtitle: Is the biological self a delusion?

how-to-use-philosophy-for-a-better-life-.speaker_desc: Rebecca Roache is Senior Lecturer in Philosophy at Royal Holloway, University of London. Her research interests range from ethics and metaphysics to philosophy of mind and philosophy of language. She is a pioneer in field of philosophy of swearing, and her work has been featured in The Times, The Guardian and the BBC.
how-to-use-philosophy-for-a-better-life-.subtitle: The path towards more enlightened societies

the-future-of-ukraine-and-the-world.speaker_desc: Michael Bociurkiw is an acclaimed writer, global affairs analyst and two-time TEDx speaker. He is also the author of ‘Digital Pandemic- Covid-19: How Tech Went From Bad to Good’. Having worked on the frontlines of humanitarian emergencies, he’s become a familiar voice on BBC World Television, CNN, CNN International, Al Jazeera, and Bloomberg Television.
the-future-of-ukraine-and-the-world.subtitle: Michael Bociurkiw interviewed by Jacob Furedi

the-status-of-things.speaker_desc: Behavioural scientist Paul Dolan, senior lecturer in psychology at Leeds Beckett University Steve Taylor and British broadcaster and anthropologist Mary-Ann Ochota debate the status of things. Eliane Glaser hosts.
the-status-of-things.subtitle: Should we free ourselves of objects and clutter?

reigning-men.speaker_desc: Journalist and author of 'The Authority Gap', Mary Ann Sieghart, lecturer and author of 'Becoming Beauvoir', Kate Kirkpatrick, and cultural critic and author of 'What Men Want', Nina Power, ask whether the sun is setting on the reign of men. Hosted by BBC News presenter and journalist, Joanna Gosling
reigning-men.subtitle: Where does the future of feminism lie?

where-sceptics-fail-alex-oconnor.speaker_desc: Alex O’Connor, also known by his YouTube alias ‘CosmicSkeptic’, is a prolific philosopher, youtuber, public speaker and animal welfare activist. His youtube channel has amassed over 450 000 subscribers and discusses issues relating to free speech, free will, animal rights and the philosophical arguments against religion.
where-sceptics-fail-alex-oconnor.subtitle: An interview with CosmicSkeptic

what-the-world-is-made-of.speaker_desc: Legendary physicist Paul Davies, trailblazing author of 'The Science Delusion Rupert Sheldrake and ground-breaking philosopher of physics Katie Robertson debate the fundamental nature of reality. Acclaimed science presenter Dallas Campbell hosts.
what-the-world-is-made-of.subtitle: What is the fundamental nature of reality?

silenced-for-following-the-science-david.speaker_desc: David Nutt is a neuropsychopharmacologist and the former chairman of the Advisory Council on the Misuse of Drugs in the UK, a position he was dismissed from in 2009. Now chair of the Independent Scientific Committee on Drugs, Nutt has been a fierce defender of science based policy around the legalisation and decrimilisation of canabis and psychedelics. "Any sensible person or scientist knows that the drug laws are not based on the science of drugs."
silenced-for-following-the-science-david.subtitle: An interview with David Nutt

infinity-in-the-palm-of-your-hand.speaker_desc: Critically acclaimed writer Janne Teller, musical comedian and writer Isy Suttie, British philosopher James Tartaglia and Pulitzer prize poet Paul Muldoon as they debate whether art can uncover the essence of the world. Hosted by acclaimed author, Joanna Kavenna.
infinity-in-the-palm-of-your-hand.subtitle: Can art uncover the essence of the world?

the-new-science-of-consciousness.speaker_desc: Legendary theoretical physicist Carlo Rovelli, ground breaking metaphysical idealist Bernardo Kastrup, godmother of neurophilosophy Patricia Churchland lock horns over the New Science of Consciousness. Robert Lawrence Kuhn Hosts.
the-new-science-of-consciousness.subtitle: Will science crack the mystery of consciousness?

kafka-vs-camus.speaker_desc: Emma Sulkowicz is a performance artist, well-known for her year-long performance art project Mattress Performance: Carry That Weight protesting having to go to school with her rapist. Andrea Elliott is a Pulitzer Prize winning journalist, who writes for the New York Times as an investigative reporter, and is author of ‘An Invisible Child’. Paul Muldoon is a Pulitzer Prize winning poet and has served as both Professor of Poetry at Oxford University and the poetry editor of The New Yorker. Janne Teller hosts.
kafka-vs-camus.subtitle: Can we change the world?
