the-lessons-of-failure.speaker_desc: Ezgi Basaran is a journalist and author. She was formerly the youngest ever editor of Radikal, the biggest centre-left news outlet in Turkey. Shabbir Lakha is a political activist. He is an officer at Stop the War, a People's Assembly activist and a member of the socialist organisation Counterfire. Shabnam Nasimi is a British-Afghan social activist and political commentator. She is the Executive Director of Conservative Friends of Afghanistan. Stefan Dercon is Professor of Economic Policy at Oxford University, as was formerly Chief Economist of the UK's Department of International Development. Rana Mitter hosts.
the-lessons-of-failure.subtitle: Did the failure in Afghanistan lead to Ukraine?

the-civilisation-trap.speaker_desc: Paleobiologist Mark Williams, Conservative former cabinet minister Peter Lilley and former leader of the Green Party Natalie Bennett weigh in on civilisation as we know it. Hosted by Güneş Taylor.
the-civilisation-trap.subtitle: Did hunter-gatherers have a better life?

science-and-the-prejudice-of-the-west-ch.speaker_desc: Chandrima Ganguly is Wolfson's Henslow Junior Research Fellow at the University of Cambridge. They are a cosmologist interested in testing early universe models, and using cosmology to constrain particle physics and theories of gravity.
science-and-the-prejudice-of-the-west-ch.subtitle: Why we need to decolonise science

the-mystery-of-the-multiverse.speaker_desc: Michio Kaku is the co-founder of string field theory and the author of several books including several New York Times best sellers such as ‘The God Equation: The Quest for a Theory of Everything became.’ He is also professor of theoretical physics in the City College of New York and CUNY Graduate Center. Sabine Hossenfelder is a theoretical physicist who specializes in the foundations of physics. She is a Research Fellow at the Frankfurt Institute for Advanced Studies where she leads the group on Superfluid Dark Matter. Roger Penrose is a world-renowned mathematician and Nobel Laureate in Physics. He is best known for his work on general relativity and sharing the Wolf Prize for Physics with Stephen Hawking for his work on black holes. Hilary Lawson hosts.
the-mystery-of-the-multiverse.subtitle: Should we abandon the multiverse theory?

economics-matters-david-friedman.speaker_desc: David D. Friedman is one of the most renowned anarcho-capitalist theorists in the world. Son of Nobel Prize winning economist and father of modern economics, Milton Friedman, David has set out his own unique economic theory. His book, The Machinery of Freedom, is the go-to text for those interested in anarcho-capitalism, and it makes up one of the most reputable defences of setting capitalism completely free.
economics-matters-david-friedman.subtitle: Why economics is critical to your life

virtue-hypocrisy-and-the-natural-world.speaker_desc: Former leader of the Green Party and member of the House of Lords Natalie Bennett, influential economist Ashwini Deshpande and controversial Spiked journalist Ella Whelan clash over the merits of environmental ideals. Hosted by acclaimed historian, Rana Mitter.
virtue-hypocrisy-and-the-natural-world.subtitle: Environmental ideals and every day lies

the-search-for-certainty.speaker_desc: Distinguished philosophy professor Simon Blackburn, maverick post post-modern philosopher Hilary Lawson and ground-breaking philosopher of value Ruth Chang question whether we can be certain about anything. Maria Balaska hosts.
the-search-for-certainty.subtitle: Should we give up the dream of certainty?

the-trauma-of-everyday.speaker_desc: Neuroscientist Sarah Garfinkel, bestselling author of Zed Joanna Kavenna and fearless psychoanalyst Ian Parker explore modern trauma and what we can do about it.
the-trauma-of-everyday.subtitle: Have mundane setbacks become catastrophic?

writing-the-self.speaker_desc: Meg Rosoff is an award-winning writer. She is perhaps best known for the novels 'How I Live Now' which won the Guardian Prize, and 'Just In Case, for which she was awarded the Carnegie medal. Her most recent novel, 'The Great Godden' is a coming-of-age novel which was nominated for the Costa Book Award in 2020.
writing-the-self.subtitle: An interview with Meg Rosoff

corporations-vs-the-people.speaker_desc: Elizabeth and James Killian Professor of Economics at MIT Daron Acemoglu, journalist and editor-at-large of libertarian publication Reason Nick Gillespie and Chief Economist at the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development Beata Javorcik debate whether the state should take more control of key sectors including big tech. Linda Yueh hosts.
corporations-vs-the-people.subtitle: Who rules the world?

truth-prejudice-and-the-university3.speaker_desc: Tommy Curry is a philosophy professor at Edinburgh University where he holds a Personal Chair in Africana Philosophy and Black Male studies. His research focusses on Africana Philosophy, Critical Race Theory, Anti-Colonialism, Black Male Studies and Public Health. Aaron Bastani is co-founder of Novara Media, an independent, self-described radical left-wing alternative media organization based in the United Kingdom, and author of Fully Automated Luxury Communism. In his book, Bastani argues that ‘Fully Automated Luxury Communism’ is the paradigm of the future – and the path to a world of luxury, liberty and happiness. Kathleen Stock is a British philosopher and writer. She was a professor of philosophy at the University of Sussex until 2021. She has published several articles and her most recent book 'Material Girls' which argues against the idea of gender as a social construct.
truth-prejudice-and-the-university3.subtitle: Does the modern university undermine free thought?

afghanistan-and-the-failures-of-the-west.speaker_desc: Shabnam Nasimi is a British-Afghan social activist and political commentator. She is the Executive Director of Conservative Friends of Afghanistan, a group that exists to promote understanding and support for Afghanistan in the United Kingdom.
afghanistan-and-the-failures-of-the-west.subtitle: Where do we go from here?

beyond-right-and-wrong.speaker_desc: Author of Freedom in Age of Alternative Facts Santiago Zabala, pragmatic epistemologist Corine Besson and expert of Indian thought Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad clash over whether it is ever possible to be definitely right about anything.
beyond-right-and-wrong.subtitle: Should we give up on the idea of certainty?

the-challenge-of-china-vince-cable.speaker_desc: Vince Cable is the former leader of the Liberal Democrats, an economist by trade, and now author of a number of bestselling non-fiction works including China: Engage! Money and Power and the The Chinese Conundrum.
the-challenge-of-china-vince-cable.subtitle: Vince Cable on the rise of China

in-search-of-a-cleaner-world.speaker_desc: Expert in greenhouse gas footprinting and author of There is No Planet B , Mike Berners-Lee, radical environmentalist and author of Bright Green Lies, Lierre Keith, and former Secretary of State for Energy and Climate Change, Chris Huhne, debate renewable energy as the solution the climate crisis. Isabel Hilton hosts.
in-search-of-a-cleaner-world.subtitle: Is green energy even possible?

big-tech-and-lost-promises.speaker_desc: Oxford fellow Anders Sandberg, chief executive of leading think-tank Demos, Polly Mackenzie, author of 'Media Freedom', Damian Tambini, and Labour MP Thangam Debbonaire lock horns over the nightmare and dreams coming true with Big Tech. Hosted by metahumanist philosopher, Luke Robert Mason.
big-tech-and-lost-promises.subtitle: Will regulation solve our problems with Big Tech?

science-religion-and-the-quest-for-reaso.speaker_desc: Alister McGrath is a theologian, intellectual historian, scientist, and public intellectual. He currently holds the Andreas Idreos Professorship in Science and Religion in the Faculty of Theology and Religion, at the University of Oxford, McGrath is noted for his work in historical theology, systematic theology and the relationship between science and religion.
science-religion-and-the-quest-for-reaso.subtitle: An interview with Alister McGrath

should-we-care-for-ants-peter-godfrey-sm.speaker_desc: Peter Godfrey-Smith is professor in the School of History and Philosophy of Science at the University of Sydney. His main research interests are in the philosophy of biology and the philosophy of mind. He is the author of numerous highly-acclaimed, including 'Other Minds: The Octopus, The Sea, and the Deep Origins of Consciousness.'
should-we-care-for-ants-peter-godfrey-sm.subtitle: Moral limits in the contemporary world

the-equality-puzzle.speaker_desc: Former Minister for Women and Equalities Nicky Morgan, author and commentator Ella Whelan, and award-winning social critic and writer Minna Salami disucss the best way forward.
the-equality-puzzle.subtitle: Do we need a new direction for feminism?

postmodernism-in-the-dock.speaker_desc: Co-founder and editor of The Philosophers’ Magazine Julian Baggini, award-winning journalist Minna Salami, radical philosopher Hilary Lawson and boundary pushing feminist Julie Bindel line up as prosecution and defence with postmodernism in the dock. Hosted by journalist and author David Aaronovitch.
postmodernism-in-the-dock.subtitle: Are we right to abandon objective truth?

reviving-feminism-yasmin-brown.speaker_desc: Yasmin Alibhai-Brown is a respected pundit who writes regularly for the I, International Business Times, and New European. Describing herself as a "leftie liberal, anti-racist, feminist, Muslim", she is known for her interventions in UK immigration and multiculturalism policy. Born in Kampala, Uganda into a Shia Muslim family, Yasmin moved to the UK to complete her studies at Oxford. She worked as a teacher before moving into journalism in the 1980s, and has since published a slew of acclaimed books about her unique experience as an insider/outsider in British culture. Her most recent book Ladies Who Punch tells the story of courageous women who have changed history and remoulded our culture.
reviving-feminism-yasmin-brown.subtitle: How to become a better feminist

forests-hypocrisy-and-the-west.speaker_desc: Former leader of the Liberal Democrats Vince Cable, historian and author Avivia Chomsky and Director General of the Amazonas Sustainable Foundation Virgilio Viana take on the topic of Brazil’s Amazon. Hosted by economist and author, Linda Yueh.
forests-hypocrisy-and-the-west.subtitle: How can we prevent rainforest destruction?

crisis-and-desire.speaker_desc: Award-winning authors Elise Valmorbida and Meg Rosoff and philosopher and an honorary professor at UCL Nick Zangwill discuss the call of the catastrophe and calamity. Mary Ann Sieghart hosts.
crisis-and-desire.subtitle: Are we predisposed to catastrophise?

looking-for-life-avi-loeb.speaker_desc: Avi Loeb is Professor of Science at Harvard University, working primarily in astrophysics and cosmology. A New-York Times bestselling author, he consistently makes headlines for advocating that the search for intelligent extra-terrestrial life should be mainstream science. The only reason it isn't, he maintains, is unscientific prejudice.
looking-for-life-avi-loeb.subtitle: Are we the sharpest cookie in the jar?

beyond-innocence-and-guilt.speaker_desc: Eminent philosopher and literary critic Galen Strawson, stoic philosopher Massimo Pigliucci, and neuroscientist Sarah Garfinkel debate the essence of innocence and guilt. Hosted by novelist Joanna Kavenna.
beyond-innocence-and-guilt.subtitle: Is moral responsibility a mere illusion?

a-material-world.speaker_desc: Founding editor and publisher of Jacobin and author of 'The Socialist Manifesto' Bhaskar Sunkara, Distinguished Professor Emerita of Economics and History Deirdre McCloskey and human rights campaigner Peter Tatchell discuss consumer culture. Rana Mitter hosts.
a-material-world.subtitle: Does consumption genuinely make us more satisfied?

richard-lang-how-to-lose-your-head.speaker_desc: Richard Lang is an 'enlightened mystic' and teacher of spirituality. He is also the author of "The Man with No Head: The Life and Ideas of Douglas Harding", where he gives us insight into who this great man was and what he discovered.
richard-lang-how-to-lose-your-head.subtitle: Exploring the headless way

this-is-my-land.speaker_desc: Minna Salami is a Finnish Nigerian journalist, feminist and author. She has written on the experiences of Nigerian women, the African Diaspora and feminism through her award winning blog, MsAfropolitan. Additionally, she authored 'Sensuous Knowledge: A Black Feminist Approach for Everyone' and co-authored 'The Power Book: What is It, Who Has it and Why?'. Eric Kaufmann is Professor of Politics at Birkbeck College, University of London. He specialises in nationalism, political demography, and demography of the religious and irreligious. His most recent book is ‘Whiteshift: Populism, Immigration and the Future of White Majorities’ about the upsurge of right-wing populism in the West. Rana Mitter is Professor of the history and politics of modern China at Oxford University. Rana was educated at King's College. He has been elected for several prestigious positions including president of the Cambridge Union, Kennedy Scholar at Harvard University and Fellow of the British Academy. In 2019 he was appointed an OBE for his services to education. Mary Ann Sieghart hosts.
this-is-my-land.subtitle: Should the colonial powers give back reparations?

life-death-and-money.speaker_desc: Chief Social Policy Advisor to the Scottish government Linda Bauld, author of Sedated James Davies and eminent psychologist Susan Michie debate the future of healthcare. Hosted by leading psychiatrist, Mark Salter.
life-death-and-money.subtitle: Where do the limits of medicine lie?

the-dawn-of-consciousness.speaker_desc: Famed cognitive psychologist Donald Hoffman, celebrated psychiatrist and former literary scholar Iain McGilchrist, trailblaizing evolutionary theorist and geneticist Eva Jablonka and pioneering philosopher of consciousness Michelle Montague lock horns over whether consciousness evolved. Robert Lawrence Kuhn hosts.
the-dawn-of-consciousness.subtitle: Did consciousness evolve?

the-web-corporation.speaker_desc: Labour front bencher Tulip Siddiq, serial entrepreneur and philanthropist Luke Johnson and author of Internet for the People Ben Tarnoff debate the dismantling of Big Tech. Hosted by senior broadcast journalist at the Times, Manveen Rana.
the-web-corporation.subtitle: Is it time to reign in big tech?

innovation-and-the-future-of-capitalism.speaker_desc: Pravin Krishna is the Chung Ju Yung Distinguished Professor of International Economics and Business at Johns Hopkins University. He has served as a consultant to the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund and is also a regular host on the podcast Transforming India. Michael Howard was Leader of the Conservative Party in the early 2000s. Prior to his leadership, he was a senior cabinet minister under Margaret Thatcher and John Major, holding prestigious positions including Secretary of State for Employment, Secretary of State for the Environment and Home Secretary. Prem Shankar Jha is an Indian economist, journalist and writer. He has served in the United Nations Development Programme, the World Bank and as the information advisor to the Prime Minister of India. Rajini Vaidyanathan hosts.
innovation-and-the-future-of-capitalism.subtitle: Do governments really support free trade?

truss-defends-vision-for-the-future-of-b.speaker_desc: Elizabeth Truss is a British politician who has been the Member of Parliament for South West Norfolk since 2010. She has served in numerous ministerial poisitions, and currently holds the position of Foreign Secretary.
truss-defends-vision-for-the-future-of-b.subtitle: Leadership frontrunner speaks her mind in 2019

language-and-power.speaker_desc: Professor of Black Studies at Birmingham City University Kehinde Andrews, linguist and Associate Professor of English and comparative literature at Columbia University John McWhorter, and Professor of philosophy and cognitive science at Yale University Laurie Ann Paul discuss whether or not language is capable of communicating lived experience. Mary-Jane Rubenstein hosts.
language-and-power.subtitle: Is language capable of communicating experience?

seeing-how-it-is.speaker_desc: Steve Fuller is an academic studying science and technology. Fuller has published prolifically on such topics as intelligent design, the sociology of academia, and transhumanism. Fuller believes that academics reserve the special right to express their views without fear of retaliation. Angela Saini is an award-winning science journalist, author and broadcaster.She regularly presents science programmes for the BBC, and her writing has appeared in publications ranging from New Scientist, Wired and the Guardian. She wrote Inferior: How Science Got Women Wrong in 2017. Her book Superior: The Return of Race Science addresses the racial biases present in current scientific practices. Rupert Sheldrake is a biologist and bestselling author. Best known for his 2012 book 'The Science Delusion' and the controversial, viral TED talk he gave which was banned by the organisation. He has taken issue with the New Atheists and has challenged the idea that the laws of nature are fixed and unchanging. Peter Atkins is a chemist and Fellow of Lincoln College. He’s a Distinguished Supporter of Humanists UK, Atkins is outspoken in his opposition to religion. He argues that religion involves a lack of confidence in human powers of comprehension, encouraging us to be satisfied with ignorance instead of striving to understand the universe. Danielle Sands hosts.
seeing-how-it-is.subtitle: Can empirical observation lead us to the truth?

predicting-the-future.speaker_desc: Founder and editor of the Blind Spot Izabella Kaminska, former Leader of the Liberal Democrats Vince Cable, and Professor of the history and politics of modern China at Oxford University Rana Mitter discuss how accurate economic forecasting can be. Stephanie Hegarty hosts.
predicting-the-future.subtitle: How accurate can economic forecasting really be?

gods-worlds-and-monsters-mary-jane-rubbe.speaker_desc: Mary-Jane Rubenstein is Professor of Religion at Wesleyan University in Connecticut, USA. Her book Worlds Without End: The Many Lives of the Universe examines cosmological models throughout history, from the world-views of the Ancient Greeks through to the well-respected multiverse theory in modern science. She links contemporary models of the universe to their forerunners and explores the reason for their recent resurgence.
gods-worlds-and-monsters-mary-jane-rubbe.subtitle: The threats of pantheism

bad-boys.speaker_desc: Political commentator and assistant editor at Spiked, Ella Whelan is the author of What Women Want: Fun, Freedom and an End to Feminism. Myriam François is a journalist and presenter, as well as a Research Associate at the SOAS Centre for Islamic Studies. Journalist and broadcaster, Rowan Pelling is former editor of The Erotic Review, founder of The Amorist and columnist at the Daily Telegraph. Sean Curran hosts.
bad-boys.subtitle: Is danger integral to desire?

a-matter-of-facts.speaker_desc: Professor of Philosophy at the Open University Sophie-Grace Chappell, Professor of Philosophy at Stockholm University Anandi Hattiangadi and Professor of Philosophy at the New College of the Humanities Simon Blackburn dicuss the changing value of truth in contemporary society. Julian Baggini hosts.
a-matter-of-facts.subtitle: The value of truth in contemporary society

freeing-nazanin-zaghari-ratcliffe-tulip-.speaker_desc: Tulip Siddiq is a British politician serving as the Member of Parliament for Hampstead and Kilburn since 2015. A member of the Labour Party, she previously was the Camden London Borough Councillor for Regent's Park from 2010 until 2014.

profits-value-and-fantasy.speaker_desc: Author of 'The New Prophets of Capital', Nicole Aschoff, Director of the Institute of Economic Affairs, Mark Littlewood and economist Anatole Kaletsky explore the current asymmetries between profits and value. Hosted by researcher and author, Stephanie Hare.
profits-value-and-fantasy.subtitle: Exploring the new age of capitalism

the-world-that-disappeared.speaker_desc: Chemist and Fellow of Lincoln College Peter Atkins, Philosopher of Science at the University of Bristol James Ladyman and author of A Field Guide to Reality Joanna Kavenna debate whether the everyday objects that surround us are an illusion. Julian Baggini hosts.
the-world-that-disappeared.subtitle: Can we be sure there is a physical reality?

russia-ukraine-and-the-future-of-economi.speaker_desc: Vince Cable is a former acting leader of the Liberal Democrats and was an MP for over twenty years. He is the author of Money and Power, and the Chinese Conundrum.
russia-ukraine-and-the-future-of-economi.subtitle: Vince Cable on economics post-Ukraine

tommy-curry-dilemmas-of-black-manhood.speaker_desc: Tommy Curry is a philosophy professor at Edinburgh University where he holds a Personal Chair in Africana Philosophy and Black Male studies. His research focusses on Africana Philosophy, Critical Race Theory, Anti-Colonialism, Black Male Studies and Public Health.
tommy-curry-dilemmas-of-black-manhood.subtitle: An interview with philosopher Tommy Curry

nature-friend-or-foe.speaker_desc: World-famous intellectual Yuval Noah Harari and firebrand philosopher Slavoj Žižek debate whether nature is friend or foe. Hosted by scientist Güneş Taylor.
nature-friend-or-foe.subtitle: Does nature always know best?

what-is-happiness-paul-dolan.speaker_desc: Paul Dolan is Professor of Behavioural Science at the LSE. His main research interests are human behaviour and happiness, and the relationships between them, particularly as they apply to policy. He is author of the bestselling books Happiness by Design and Happy Ever After. He is also host of the Duck / Rabbit podcast about the polarisation problem in our society.
what-is-happiness-paul-dolan.subtitle: An interview with Behavioural Scientist Paul Dolan

from-the-matrix-to-the-metaverse.speaker_desc: David Chalmers is an Australian philosopher and cognitive scientist who specialises in the philosophy of mind, language and more recently, virtual reality. He is a Professor of Philosophy and Neural Science at New York University, as well as co-director of NYU's Center for Mind, Brain and Consciousness.
from-the-matrix-to-the-metaverse.subtitle: Finding meaning in a virtual world

the-oldest-gods.speaker_desc: Psychedelic philosopher Peter Sjöstedt-Hughes, internationally-renowned climate scientist Tim Palmer, and author-broadcaster-podcaster Melanie Challenger test each other's beliefs about nature and god. Hosted by philosopher Hilary Lawson
the-oldest-gods.subtitle: Should we return to the gods of nature?

china-and-the-art-of-peace.speaker_desc: Author and strategic forecaster Chris Parry, former director of operations and intelligence for MI6 Nigel Inkster, China reporter and broadcast editor at the Spectator Cindy Yu. Hilary Lawson hosts.
china-and-the-art-of-peace.subtitle: Western strategy in the new global order

dreams-delusions-and-data.speaker_desc: Distinguished journalist Kenneth Cukier, celebrated professor of ethics Joanna Bryson and esteemed academic Noortje Marres debate the opportunities and limits of Big Data. Luke Robert Mason hosts.
dreams-delusions-and-data.subtitle: Is Big Data just marketing hype?

why-the-world-is-in-constant-flux-iain-m.speaker_desc: Iain McGilchrist is psychiatrist, writer, and former Oxford literary scholar. He is committed to the idea that the mind and brain can be understood only by seeing them in the broadest possible context, a notion which is fundamental to his two most famous works: The Master and his Emissary, and The Matter With Things
why-the-world-is-in-constant-flux-iain-m.subtitle: An interview with Iain McGilchrist

debt-crisis-or-opportunity.speaker_desc: Legendary economist Stephen King, distinguished British politician Vince Cable and trailblazing political commentator Grace Blakeley debate the limits of government debt. Linda Yueh hosts.
debt-crisis-or-opportunity.subtitle: Are there limits to government debt?

how-to-write-a-memoir-laura-coleman.speaker_desc: Laura Coleman is the author of the widely praised memoir 'The Puma Years', which tells of her liberating journey in the Amazon jungle.
how-to-write-a-memoir-laura-coleman.subtitle: Unlocking the key to ourselves

inheriting-inequality.speaker_desc: Award-winning journalist and broadcaster David Aaronovitch, British commentator and former economics editor at the BBC Paul Mason and Chief Executive of Demos Polly Mackenzie discuss how to tackle inherited wealth. Rana Mitter hosts.
inheriting-inequality.subtitle: How should we tackle embedded privilege?

if-it-doesnt-kill-you.speaker_desc: Britain’s most beloved psychotherapist and author of “Fat is a Feminist Issue” Susie Orbach, renowned transhumanist Anders Sandberg, and Professor of Philosophy at the University of Bristol Havi Carel explore the significance of suffering in modern society. Hosted by philosopher Julian Baggini.
if-it-doesnt-kill-you.subtitle: Do we need suffering to lead a meaningful life?

untangling-space-and-time-tim-maudlin.speaker_desc: Tim Maudlin is founder and Director of the John Bell Institute for the Foundations of Physics and he is also Professor of Philosophy at New York University. He has done influential work on the metaphysical foundations of physics and logic.
untangling-space-and-time-tim-maudlin.subtitle: Framing the fundamental laws with Tim Maudlin

the-truth-about-the-nuclear-threat-micha.speaker_desc: The author of Winning and Losing the Nuclear Peace: The Rise, Demise, and Revival of Arms Control Michael Krepon uncovers the truth about nuclear deterrence, and what it means for the future of conflict.
the-truth-about-the-nuclear-threat-micha.subtitle: How concerned should we be?

the-universe-fixity-and-flux.speaker_desc: Physics professor Lee Smolin, theoretical physicist and author Sabine Hossenfelder and cosmologist and author Paul Davies thrash out the big questions about the nature of the universe. Hosted by renowned science writer, Phillip Ball.
the-universe-fixity-and-flux.subtitle: Exploring the laws of the universe

the-eclipse-of-the-west.speaker_desc: Writer-in-chief at The Draft Phil Collins, eminent LGBT activist and human rights campaigner Peter Tatchell and China reporter and broadcast editor at the Spectator Cindy Yu debate whether the strengths of liberal democracy win through and survive the economic eclipse of the West. Linda Yueh hosts.
the-eclipse-of-the-west.subtitle: Are we on the brink of a new world order?

how-to-do-philosophy-with-moby-dick.speaker_desc: Dean Moyar is Professor of Philosophy and Director of Graduate Studies at Johns Hopkins University. He is the author of 'Hegel's Conscience' and 'Hegel's Value: Justice as the Living Good'. He is currently working on an edited volume on Moby-Dick for the Oxford Studies in Philosophy and Literature series.
how-to-do-philosophy-with-moby-dick.subtitle: Uncovering truth through fiction.

the-life-and-philosophy-of-matt-hancock.speaker_desc: Matt Hancock is a British politician who served as Secretary of State for Health and Social Care from 2018 to 2021. He is a member of the Conservative Party, and has been Member of Parliament for West Suffolk since 2010.
the-life-and-philosophy-of-matt-hancock.subtitle: Meet the UK's controversial pandemic policy maker

machine-intelligence-joannna-bryson.speaker_desc: Joanna Bryson is professor at Hertie School in Berlin. She works on Artificial Intelligence, ethics and collaborative cognition. She advises governments, corporations, and other agencies globally, particularly on AI policy.
machine-intelligence-joannna-bryson.subtitle: An interview with Professor Joanna Bryson

heaven-is-other-people.subtitle: Is mental wellbeing a purely social issue?

a-life-in-activism-peter-tatchell.speaker_desc: Peter Tatchell is a human rights campaigner best known for his work with LGBT movements, a member of the gay rights group Outrage! and director of the Peter Tatchell Foundation, a human rights organization. Peter also identifies as a humanist, believing that reason, science and ethics are the best way to promote human rights and welfare.
a-life-in-activism-peter-tatchell.subtitle: An interview with Peter Tatchell

fantasy-and-the-void.speaker_desc: Scientist, author, and parapsychology researcher Rupert Sheldrake, Hegelian psychoanalyst Slavoj Zizek and Professor of History at University of Madison-Wisconsin Jennifer Ratner-Rosenhagen discuss whether the persistence of religion is an extended but ultimately temporary phenomenon. Wes Alwan hosts.
fantasy-and-the-void.subtitle: Will science ever replace religion?

sex-relationships-and-the-future.speaker_desc: Writer and author of ‘Why Sex Doesn’t Matter' Olivia Fane, English Anglican theologian and Emeritus Professor at the University of Nottingham John Milbank and radical feminist writer, journalist and author Julie Bindel discuss the idea of separating sex and relationships. Barry Smith hosts.
sex-relationships-and-the-future.subtitle: Should we pursue love and sex separately?

from-feminism-to-politics-and-back-again.speaker_desc: Thangam Debbonaire is the Labour MP for Bristol West and current Shadow Leader of the House of Commons, previously working as the Shadow Secretary of State for Housing. Thangam has co-authored two books and published numerous papers on domestic violence.
from-feminism-to-politics-and-back-again.subtitle: Mixing activism with politics

the-quest-for-a-final-theory-michio-kaku.speaker_desc: Famed futurist and co-founder of String Field Theory Michio Kaku has spent his career inspired by the search for a grand unifying theory of everything – carrying on Einstein’s quest to unite the four fundamental forces of nature, penning numerous bestselling books along the way.
the-quest-for-a-final-theory-michio-kaku.subtitle: Can we find a theory of everything?

rethinking-reason.speaker_desc: Eminent philosopher of mind and psychology Sophie Archer, groundbreaking Oxford logician Timothy Williamson and trailblazing cultural critic Nina Power put reason and emotion to the test. Hosted by Mary Ann Sieghart.
rethinking-reason.subtitle: Is rationality a delusion?

atheism-revisited-julian-baggini.speaker_desc: Julian Baggini is a British philosopher, journalist and author of over 20 philosophical books. Since graduating with a PhD from University College London in 1997, he has co-founded The Philosopher's Magazine and been a regular contributor to both national and international newspapers.
atheism-revisited-julian-baggini.subtitle: Changing beliefs in the Western world

dangerous-desires.speaker_desc: Chair of the Independent Scientific Committee on Drugs, David Nutt, Medical Anthropology and Ethnobotany academic Anna Waldstein, and bestselling author Joanna Kavenna go head to head on desire and restraint. Hosted by Postdoctoral Training Fellow at the Francis Crick Institute Güneş Taylor.
dangerous-desires.subtitle: Must we adopt a new attitude to social drugs?

war-and-peace-in-afghanistan-tariq-ali.speaker_desc: Tariq Ali is a famed political activist, writer, journalist, historian, filmmaker, and public intellectual. His latest book 'The Forty-Year War in Afghanistan: A Chronicle Foretold' explores the history and present of the war in Afghanistan.
war-and-peace-in-afghanistan-tariq-ali.subtitle: What does the future hold for Afghanistan?

determinism-is-a-superstition-james-tart.speaker_desc: James Tartaglia is a British philosopher, and Professor of Metaphysical Philosophy at Keele University. He is the author of Philosophy in a Meaningless Life and Philosophy in a Technological World: Gods and Titans. His main interest is in understanding and enhancing awareness of the nature of philosophical inquiry. James also leads a Jazz-Philosophy fusion band called 'Continuum of Selves'.
determinism-is-a-superstition-james-tart.subtitle: An interview with James Tartaglia

reality-fantasy-and-metaphor.speaker_desc: Fellow at the Francis Crick Institute Güneş Taylor, scientist and author Rupert Sheldrake, chemist and author of popular works of science Peter Atkins and post-postmodern philosopher Hilary Lawson debate whether scientific metaphors can be considered real descriptions of an underlying universe. Joanna Kavenna hosts.
reality-fantasy-and-metaphor.subtitle: Are scientific metaphors a description of reality?

the-new-ruling-class-yanis-varoufakis.speaker_desc: Economist, politician and best-selling author Yanis Varoufakis argues that a radical reassessment of property rights over machines and data is the only way for us to confront this new ruling class.
the-new-ruling-class-yanis-varoufakis.subtitle: How can we confront technofeudalism?

popularity-and-prejudice.speaker_desc: Literary theorist Stanley Fish, author of How I Live Now, Meg Rosoff, journalist and editor of MsAfropolitan, Minna Salami and writer and essayist Janne Teller rethink what makes a great work of art. Hosted by BBC Parliamentary Correspondent, Sean Curran.
popularity-and-prejudice.subtitle: How do we measure artistic greatness?

in-conversation-with-rupert-sheldrake.speaker_desc: Author of The Science Delusion, Rupert Sheldrake is a biologist whose research led to the theory of morphic resonance and nature's memory. He has also written on altered states of consciousness in Ways To Go Beyond.
in-conversation-with-rupert-sheldrake.subtitle: An exploration of the mind

how-to-create-art-by-a-scientist-walter-.speaker_desc: Walter Gilbert is biochemist, physicist, businessman, Nobel laureate and artist. Since being awarded the 1980 Nobel Prize in Chemistry, he has launched a successful career in digital photography.
how-to-create-art-by-a-scientist-walter-.subtitle: Exploring creativity in its various forms

the-new-right.speaker_desc: Conservative MP for Hitchin and Harpenden, Bim Afolami, author and Professor of Economics at the University of Illinois, Deirdre McCloskey, and author and political commentator, Paul Mason discuss the past, present and future of conservatism. Hosted by distinguished historian, Rana Mitter.
the-new-right.subtitle: What does modern conservatism stand for?

science-needs-philosophy-sabine-hossenfe.speaker_desc: Sabine Hossenfelder is a theoretical physicist who specialises in the foundations of physics. She is a Research Fellow at the Frankfurt Institute for Advanced Studies where she leads the group on Superfluid Dark Matter. She is the author of Lost in Math: How Beauty Leads Physics Astray, and the forthcoming Existential Physics: A Scientist's Guide to Life's Biggest Questions. Hossenfelder also has a popular YouTube channel called "Science without the gobbledygook".
science-needs-philosophy-sabine-hossenfe.subtitle: An interview with Sabine Hossenfelder

cracking-girl-code.speaker_desc: Social theorist and philosopher Nina Power, journalist Maya Oppenheim and historian of political thought at Kings College London Hannah Dawson debate whether or not women should support other women independently of their qualities and their approach. Barry Smith hosts.
cracking-girl-code.subtitle: The future of the feminist struggle

confessions-of-a-sex-worker-liara-roux.speaker_desc: Liara Roux is an American author, sex worker, indie porn director and human rights activist. Roux has written for Vice Media and HuffPost and has gathered a strong online following throughout her career. She is also an activist and community organizer who predominantly champions fighting structural discrimination against sex workers.
confessions-of-a-sex-worker-liara-roux.subtitle: Lessons from the sex industry

the-trouble-with-sex.speaker_desc: Current chairman of the board at the Ayn Rand Institute, Yaron Brook, sex worker and activist Liara Roux, and feminist writer Suzannah Weiss discuss how our attitudes to sex are affected by an increasingly technological world. Hosted by writer and broadcaster, Myriam François.
the-trouble-with-sex.subtitle: Is technology spelling the end of true intimacy?

the-workforce-revolution-peter-lilley.speaker_desc: Lord Peter Lilley is a British Conservative politician. He is a member of the House of Lords and was an MP from 1983 to 2017. He was a Cabinet minister in the governments of Margaret Thatcher and John Major, and was Chairman of the Globalisation and Global Poverty Policy Review Group under David Cameron.
the-workforce-revolution-peter-lilley.subtitle: How we can revitalise UK industries

new-gods-and-lost-rituals.speaker_desc: Research associate at the Centre for Islamic Studies at SOAS Myriam François, Oxford scientist and humanist Peter Atkins and philosopher and Closure theorist Hilary Lawson debate spirituality and secularism. Hosted by leading psychiatrist, Mark Salter.
new-gods-and-lost-rituals.subtitle: Should religion play a role in modern life?

dangerous-data.speaker_desc: Pioneering American physicist Lisa Randall, renowned philosopher of science Tim Maudlin and legendary cognitive scientist Donald Hoffman argue over the fundamental nature of science. Biologist Güneş Taylor hosts.
dangerous-data.subtitle: Is unwavering trust in science a dangerous move?

the-power-of-the-present.speaker_desc: Lecturer in Law and Government at Queen's University Belfast, Peter Doran, Head of Movement Building at Action For Happiness, Alex Nunn, and award-winning author, Meg Rosoff, debate the value of mindfulness. Hosted by distinguished historian, Rana Mitter.
the-power-of-the-present.subtitle: Does mindfulness improve our lives?

models-metaphors-and-minds.speaker_desc: Senior Economist Editor and author Kenneth Cukier, world-leading ethics, technology and AI expert Joanna Bryson, and psychedelic philosopher Peter Sjöstedt-Hughes get to grips with the concept of a 'mind'.
models-metaphors-and-minds.subtitle: Is the brain really a computer?

how-philosophy-occupies-the-everyday-tim.speaker_desc: Timothy Williamson is the Wykeham Professor of Logic at the University of Oxford and a fellow of New College, Oxford. His main research areas are philosophy of logic, philosophy of language, epistemology and metaphysics. He is the author of the widely translated Knowledge and Its Limits and The Philosophy of Philosophy.
how-philosophy-occupies-the-everyday-tim.subtitle: An interview with Timothy Williamson

memes-all-the-way-down.speaker_desc: Post-postmodern philosopher Hilary Lawson, Professor of Ethics and Technology at Hertie School Joanna Bryson and Professor of Philosophy at City College of New York Massimo Pigliucci discuss whether or not it is useful to think about sharing mimetic information like genetic information. Gunes Taylor hosts.
memes-all-the-way-down.subtitle: Is Dawkins' concept useful?

hidden-virtues-of-commercialism-jesse-no.speaker_desc: Jesse Norman is a leading British Conservative Party politician currently serving as the Financial Secretary to the Treasury and has been an MP for Hereford and South Herefordshire since 2010. He was a director at Barclays before leaving to research and teach at University College London. Norman has been recognised by the political editor of the Spectator as a potential future Leader of the Conservative Party.
hidden-virtues-of-commercialism-jesse-no.subtitle: Can commercial societies produce virtuous morals?

the-trouble-with-modern-feminism-julie-b.speaker_desc: Julie Bindel is a radical feminist activist, author and columnist for The Guardian. She co-founded Justice for Women and has campaigned against male violence and sex-trafficking. Her most recent book is 'Feminism for Women'.
the-trouble-with-modern-feminism-julie-b.subtitle: An interview with feminist activist Julie Bindel

the-inflation-crisis.speaker_desc: Former Reagan advisor Steve Hanke, award winning author and journalist Polly Toynbee and Lead Editor of FT Alphaville Izabella Kaminska clash over the causes of inflation and the future of our economy. Rana Mitter hosts.
the-inflation-crisis.subtitle: Are we on the brink of economic disaster?

wave-goodbye-to-being-human-luke-robert-.speaker_desc: Futures theorist Luke Robert Mason is a researcher, filmmaker and digital media artist. He has been a frequent contributor to BBC Click Radio, The Guardian, Discovery Channel, VICE Motherboard, Wired Magazine and Futurism.com.
wave-goodbye-to-being-human-luke-robert-.subtitle: The transhumanist dream

trash-trends-and-the-transcendent.speaker_desc: Thought-provoking author Olivia Fane, journalist and social critic Minna Salami, radical biologist Rupert Sheldrake and award-winning novelist Joanna Kavenna interrogate our awe at what lies beyond, and how it does - and doesn't - manifest today. Mark Salter hosts.
trash-trends-and-the-transcendent.subtitle: Has culture lost sight of the sublime?

the-strong-the-weak-and-the-deceitful.speaker_desc: Political activist and historian Tariq Ali, professor Emeritus at Harvard’s Kennedy School of Government Joseph Nye, writer and political commentator Yasmin Alibhai-Brown and senior lecturer in Security and Development Domitilla Sagramoso debate whether the West become a deceitful and untrustworthy ally. Economist Linda Yueh hosts.
the-strong-the-weak-and-the-deceitful.subtitle: Has the West become an untrustworthy ally?

stargazing-with-an-astronomer-catherine-.speaker_desc: Astrophysicist and Astronomer Royal for Scotland Catherine Heymans takes us on a virtual tour of the visible night sky from the Royal Observatory, Edinburgh.
stargazing-with-an-astronomer-catherine-.subtitle: An exploration into the night sky

masters-of-the-universe.speaker_desc: Molecular biologist and founding director of Editing Nature at Yale University Natalie Kofler, author of Humanity 2.0 Professor Steve Fuller, and science journalist and author of Geek Nation Angela Saini explore the radical new possibilities of biotechnology. Hosted by filmmaker and politician David Malone.
masters-of-the-universe.subtitle: How gene editing technology will change humanity

the-many-voices-of-consciousness.speaker_desc: Philip Goff is a philosopher of consciousness at Durham University. His research focuses on integrating consciousness into our scientific worldview. His 2019 book Galileo's Error sets out his defence of panpsychism rooted in an analysis of the work of Arthur Eddington and Bertrand Russell.
the-many-voices-of-consciousness.subtitle: Is consciousness fundamental to reality?

the-african-dream.speaker_desc: Watch former leader of the Liberal Democrats Sir Vince Cable, researcher Eka Ikpe and economist Stefan Dercon as they discuss whether foreign investment a necessary and valuable part of economic growth, or if it is simply ceding power and wealth to others. Isabel Hilton hosts.
the-african-dream.subtitle: Is pan-Africanism the way forward?

tolerance-and-outrage.speaker_desc: Television producer Roger Bolton, broadcaster and academic Myriam Fran ç ois and journalist Toby Young debate why it appears we have become an increasingly intolerant society. Isabel Hilton hosts.
tolerance-and-outrage.subtitle: Have we become an increasingly intolerant society?

how-to-write-and-why-we-should-elise-val.speaker_desc: Elise Valmorbida grew up Italian in Australia, and lives in London. Her 2018-19 award-winning novel The Madonna of the Mountains has been published internationally in several languages and editions. Other books she has authored include Matilde Waltzing, The TV President, The Winding Stick and The Book of Happy Endings. Elise is also an award-winning indie film producer and wrote SAXON: The Making of a Guerrilla Film.
how-to-write-and-why-we-should-elise-val.subtitle: A guide to the creative process

form-and-ritual-power-and-prejudice.speaker_desc: Historian of ideas Hannah Dawson pulls no punches debating philosopher of religion Linda Woodhead and distinguished art critic Noel Carroll on the place of formality and ritual in the modern world. Writer and broadcaster Myriam Francois hosts.
form-and-ritual-power-and-prejudice.subtitle: Is it time to abandon tradition?

asking-ultimate-questions-robert-lawrenc.speaker_desc: Robert Lawrence Kuhn is the creator, writer, host and executive producer of Closer To Truth. He has written or edited over 30 books, including The Mystery of Existence: Why is there Anything At All? And Closer to Truth: Challenging Current Belief.
asking-ultimate-questions-robert-lawrenc.subtitle: Enquiring into the nature of reality

the-science-of-consciousness-with-anil-s.speaker_desc: Anil Seth is a Professor of Cognitive and Computational Neuroscience at the University of Sussex and author of Being You: A New Science of Consciousness. He is also Co-Director of the Sackler Centre for Consciousness Science and Editor-in-Chief of Neuroscience of Consciousness. He is also a regular contributor to the New Scientist, The Guardian, and BBC, and writes the blog NeuroBanter.
the-science-of-consciousness-with-anil-s.subtitle: Anil Seth discusses the mystery of consciousness

virtue-and-vice.speaker_desc: Chief Executive of The RSA and former head of the No. 10 Policy Unit Matthew Taylor, ethicist Rebecca Roache and philosopher and Closure theorist Hilary Lawson ask whether it's time to move beyond our fixation on morality is misguided. Author Danielle Sands hosts.
virtue-and-vice.subtitle: Is our belief in morality a dangerous fantasy?

technological-parenting.speaker_desc: Melanie Challenger is a researcher on the history of humanity and the natural world, and on environmental philosophy. Her latest book, How to Be Animal: A New History of What It Means to Be Human was published by Canongate in 2021.
technological-parenting.subtitle: The new age of parenthood

the-return-of-metaphysics.speaker_desc: Legendary Neurophilosophy pioneer Patricia Churchland, Closure theorist Hilary Lawson and analytic philosopher Galen Strawson lock horns over the future of metaphysics.
the-return-of-metaphysics.subtitle: Should we return to grand stories about reality?

what-makes-up-chinas-dna.speaker_desc: Regular presenter of Night Waves and writer for the Financial Times, History Today, and the London Review of Books, Rana Mitter is Professor of the History and Politics of Modern China at Oxford.
what-makes-up-chinas-dna.subtitle: Explaining China's growing influence

the-search-for-meaning.speaker_desc: Distinguished scientist and author Rupert Sheldrake, philosopher of Wittgenstein Maria Balaska and Professor of Metaphysics James Tartaglia ask whether philosophy can really give meaning to our lives. Danielle Sands hosts.
the-search-for-meaning.subtitle: Does philosophy give meaning to our life?

galen-strawson-free-will-is-a-necessary-.speaker_desc: Galen John Strawson is an acclaimed British analytic philosopher and literary critic who works primarily on philosophy of mind and metaphysics. His work covers free will, panpsychism, the mind-body problem, and the self. He has been a consultant editor at The Times Literary Supplement for many years, and a regular book reviewer for The Observer, The Sunday Times, The Independent, the Financial Times and The Guardian. He is the son of philosopher P. F. Strawson.
galen-strawson-free-will-is-a-necessary-.subtitle: An interview with the acclaimed Galen Strawson

making-sense-of-mental-health.speaker_desc: Mark Salter is a consultant psychiatrist based in London’s East End, specialising in risk, untowardness and media portrayals of mental distress. He served as the media expert for the Royal College of Psychiatrists and has worked as a broadcaster for the BBC and ITV.
making-sense-of-mental-health.subtitle: An Interview with Mark Salter

the-arc-of-life-peter-mandelson.speaker_desc: After navigating himself through a sizeable series of appointments and dismissals during his time in government, Peter Mandelson sheds light on his wealth of political experiences.
the-arc-of-life-peter-mandelson.subtitle: An interview with a key architect of Blairism

the-next-environmental-crisis.speaker_desc: Cosmologist, astrophysicist, and Astronomer Royal Martin Rees, award winning economist and Professor of Environmental Economics Thomas Sterner, and controversial climatologist Judith Curry join us to ask if we're heading towards a new environmental crisis.
the-next-environmental-crisis.subtitle: Are our current solutions just a short term fix?

the-unsayable.speaker_desc: Author of the bestselling Zed Joanna Kavenna, philosopher and neuroscientist Ray Tallis, and post-realist philosopher and author of Closure, Hilary Lawson lock horns over how we understand the world. Hosted by author and research fellow at the University of Hertfordshire, Maria Balaska.
the-unsayable.subtitle: Can language adequately capture reality?

deconstructing-development-eka-ikpe.speaker_desc: Eka Ikpe is an academic and a senior lecturer in Development Economics in Africa and the Director of the African Leadership Centre at King’s College London. Her research centres around a critical understanding of socio-economic transformation processes within an African context.
deconstructing-development-eka-ikpe.subtitle: An Interview with Eka Ikpe

ai-emotions-and-the-tech-evolution.speaker_desc: Fotini G. Markopoulou-Kalamara is a Greek theoretical physicist interested in quantum gravity, foundational mathematics and quantum mechanics and a design engineer working on embodied cognition technologies. Markopoulou is co-founder and CEO of Empathic Technologies.
ai-emotions-and-the-tech-evolution.subtitle: Building a better world around AI

knowledge-v-creativity.speaker_desc: Conservative MP and thinker Jesse Norman, psychologist and author of How Emotions Are Made Lisa Feldman Barrett, and director of the StoryLab Research Institute Shreepali Patel debate the value of creativity. Hosting this debate is economist and former BBC Chief Business correspondent, Linda Yueh.
knowledge-v-creativity.subtitle: Should we value one over the other?

a-voice-for-all.speaker_desc: Dutch Historian Rutger Bregman, journalist and author Kenneth Cukier and journalist and politician Claire Fox debate whether we live under a tyranny of the majority. British historian Rana Mitter hosts.
a-voice-for-all.subtitle: Do we live under the tyranny of the majority?

cancel-culture-vs-free-speech-peter-tatc.speaker_desc: Peter Tatchell is a human rights campaigner best known for his work with LGBT movements, a member of the gay rights group Outrage! and director of the Peter Tatchell Foundation, a human rights organization. Peter also identifies as a humanist, believing that reason, science and ethics are the best way to promote human rights and welfare.
cancel-culture-vs-free-speech-peter-tatc.subtitle: Which voices deserve to be heard?

the-making-of-us.speaker_desc: Author of Blueprint Robert Plomin, geneticist at The Francis Crick Institute Güneş Taylor, author of The Essential Difference Simon Baron Cohen and author of Superior Angela Saini lock horns. Hosted by philosopher Barry Smith.
the-making-of-us.subtitle: Are humans shaped by genetics or  environment?

the-end.speaker_desc: Big Bounce theorist Steffen Gielen, cosmologist Chandrima Ganguly, and philosopher of science Alexander Franklin debate the end of everything. Scientist and writer Jonjoe McFadden hosts.
the-end.subtitle: Can we predict the fate of the universe?

moral-truths-and-moral-tyrannies.speaker_desc: Infamous anarcho-capitalist David Friedman, leading analytic philosopher Timothy Williamson and morality specialist Maria Baghramian dig into the true nature of morality. Robert Rowland Smith hosts.
moral-truths-and-moral-tyrannies.subtitle: Can we claim there exists a universal moral code?

democracy-a-failed-strategy.speaker_desc: Award winning columnist Yasmin Alibhai-Brown, groundbreaking 'lottocracy' theorist Alexander Guerrero, Unlock Democracy director Tom Brake and expert on Chinese law Taisu Zhang get to grips with the myriad failures of democracy, and try to chart a way forward. Best-selling economics author Linda Yueh hosts.
democracy-a-failed-strategy.subtitle: Should we seek a radical alternative to democracy?

hilary-lawson-the-trouble-with-truth.speaker_desc: Hilary Lawson is a post-postmodern philosopher and is best known for his theory of 'Closure' which calls for a post-analytic return to metaphysics.
hilary-lawson-the-trouble-with-truth.subtitle: Embracing a radical alternative to reality

johnjoe-mcfadden-life-in-the-quantum-uni.speaker_desc: Johnjoe McFadden is a scientist, professor and writer at the University of Surrey. He has written many popular science books including Life on the Edge: The Coming of Age of Quantum Biology and Quantum Evolution.
johnjoe-mcfadden-life-in-the-quantum-uni.subtitle: Quantum mechanics in the natural world

mind-maps-and-reality.speaker_desc: Renowned professor Quassim Cassam, cutting-edge brain expert Lisa Feldman Barrett and post-postrealist philosopher and Closure theorist Hillary Lawson debate the very fabric of reality. Maria Balaska hosts.
mind-maps-and-reality.subtitle: Finding order in our universe

paul-mason-fighting-fascism.speaker_desc: Paul Mason is a political commentator, journalist and author of 'How To Stop Fascism: History, Ideology, Resistance.'
paul-mason-fighting-fascism.subtitle: A blueprint for ending the nightmare of fascism

technology-saviour-or-threat.speaker_desc: Celebrated science presenter Dallas Campbell, world-leading addiction expert Anna Lembke, empathic technology pioneer Fotini Markopoulou and existential risk philosopher Toby Ord grapple with the future of technology. CRISPR geneticist Güneş Taylor hosts.
technology-saviour-or-threat.subtitle: Will our progress be the end of us?

alien-thinking.speaker_desc: Philip Ball is a science writer and broadcaster. He is the former editor of the journal Nature and a prolific author of popular science books. Ball’s 2004 book Critical Mass won the Aventis Prize, and in the same year, he presented Small Worlds, a three-part series on nanotechnology for BBC Radio 4.
alien-thinking.subtitle: An exploration of possible alien minds

privilege-and-freedom.speaker_desc: Former Cabinet Minister Peter Lilley, radical feminist writer Julie Bindel and rapper-activist Lowkey lock horns over the current state of our education system. Journalist and broadcaster Isabel Hilton hosts.
privilege-and-freedom.subtitle: The limits of free speech in education

new-theories-of-the-universe.speaker_desc: CERN research scientist Sam Henry, renowned author and theoretical physicist Sabine Hossenfelder, and distinguished philosopher of science Bjørn Ekeberg discuss whether it is time to move past the standard model of particle physics. Acclaimed science writer Philip Ball hosts.
new-theories-of-the-universe.subtitle: Is it time to move past the standard model?

the-return-of-idealism-james-tartaglia.speaker_desc: James Tartaglia is a British philosopher and author of Philosophy in a Meaningless Life and Philosophy in a Technological World: Gods and Titans. His main interest is in understanding and enhancing awareness of the nature of philosophical inquiry.
the-return-of-idealism-james-tartaglia.subtitle: A re-examination of knowledge, reality and truth

the-artistic-revolution-paddy-johnson.speaker_desc: Paddy Johnson is the editor of the forthcoming book Impractical Spaces and the founding editor of the contemporary art blog ArtFCity. She is the recipient of the Arts Writers Grant for blogging and a two-time nominee for Best Critic at the Rob Pruitt Awards. She contributes to VICE, Observer and CNN and teaches new media art and writing in New York, where she lives with her partner.
the-artistic-revolution-paddy-johnson.subtitle: How the digital landscape has revolutionised art

dissent-division-and-democracy.speaker_desc: Legendary Labour politician and strategist Peter Mandelson, conservative former Cabinet Minister Peter Lilley, Spiked editor Ella Whelan and writer Paul Mason clash over the state of politics today. Rana Mitter hosts.
dissent-division-and-democracy.subtitle: The end of the left and right

paul-davies-cosmologys-biggest-questions.speaker_desc: Paul Davies is a world-renowned physicist and best-selling author. He works on on the “big questions” of existence, ranging from the origin of the universe to the origin of life, from the nature of time to foundational questions in quantum mechanics.
paul-davies-cosmologys-biggest-questions.subtitle: The questions keeping cosmologists up at night

the-not-so-classical-liberal-deirdre-mcc.speaker_desc: Deirdre Nansen McCloskey is Distinguished Professor Emerita of Economics and of History at the University of Illinois. She has written 24 books, and is well known for her 2019 Why Liberalism Works: How True Liberal Values Produce a Freer, More Equal, Prosperous World for All , and her massive economic, historical, and literary trilogy The Bourgeois Era.
the-not-so-classical-liberal-deirdre-mcc.subtitle: Abandoning 'capitalism' to embrace an alternative

language-animals-and-us.speaker_desc: Bestselling author of The Genius of Birds Jennifer Ackerman, philosopher and cultural critic Ray Tallis, and author of A Field Guide to Reality and Zed Joanna Kavenna debate the uniqueness of human language. Hilary Lawson hosts.
language-animals-and-us.subtitle: The uniqueness of human language

desire-relationships-and-sex.speaker_desc: Esteemed author and commentator, Olivia Fane, cultural commentator and founder of cult polysexual magazine - The Demented Goddess - Soma Ghosh, and journalist and assistant editor of spiked, Ella Whelan debate one of the most pressing issues of our age. BBC Journalist Sean Curran hosts.
desire-relationships-and-sex.subtitle: Should we be having more or less sex

whos-afraid-of-the-big-bad-data.speaker_desc: Kenneth Cukier is a journalist, writer and author of science and technology. He is most acclaimed for his contribution to the Economist Magazine and his book, Big Data: A Revolution that Will Transform How We Work, Live and Think. Big Data won the Financial Times and McKinsey Business Book of the Year Award and has been translated into 21 languages.
whos-afraid-of-the-big-bad-data.subtitle: Big data as a force for good

maria-balaska-psychoanalysis-philosophy-.speaker_desc: Maria Balaska is a philosopher at the University of Hertfordshire. Her book Wittgenstein and Lacan at the Limit: Meaning and Astonishment brings together philosophy and psychoanalysis on the significance and the challenges of experiences of astonishment.
maria-balaska-psychoanalysis-philosophy-.subtitle: An interview with Maria Balaska

tim-harford-how-to-use-data-to-start-a-r.speaker_desc: Tim Harford AKA The Undercover Economist AKA The Data Detective is a leading economist, journalist and broadcaster.
tim-harford-how-to-use-data-to-start-a-r.subtitle: The power of number visualisation.

understanding-consciousness-anil-seth.speaker_desc: Anil Seth is Professor of Cognitive and Computational Neuroscience at the University of Sussex. His TED Talk on the brain has had close to 12 million views and he is the author of multiple books alongside his blog, NeuroBanter.
understanding-consciousness-anil-seth.subtitle: Anil Seth's radical new theory of the self

playing-with-fire.speaker_desc: Head of Influenza Scientific Affairs at Seqirus Beverly Taylor, political commentator Ella Whelan and Emeritus Professor of Decision Sciences at LSE Lawrence Philiips debate playing with fire. Mary Ann Sieghart hosts.
playing-with-fire.subtitle: Is life without risk ever possible?

the-time-of-our-lives.speaker_desc: Acclaimed labour writer Sarah Jaffe, mindfulness critic Ron Purser and poet and philosopher John Paetsch question whether we worry too much about time. Güneş Taylor hosts.
the-time-of-our-lives.subtitle: Do we worry too much about time?

the-paradox-of-radical-change.speaker_desc: Political philosopher Ruth Kinna, political theorist and activist Alex Callinicos and cultural critic Theodore Dalrymple debate the paradox of radical change. Mary Ann Sieghart hosts. Political philosopher Ruth Kinna, political theorist and activist Alex Callinicos and cultural critic Theodore Dalrymple debate the paradox of radical change. Mary Ann Sieghart hosts.
the-paradox-of-radical-change.subtitle: Steps to revolution

how-to-revolutionise-the-academy-michael.speaker_desc: Michael Hrebeniak is a polymath: an academic, author, film-maker, ex-jazz musician, and journalist. He is Director of Studies in English at Wolfson College and Lecturer in English at Magdalene College, Cambridge. Isabelle McNeill is Philomathia Fellow in French at Trinity Hall, University of Cambridge, where she teaches French literature and cinema.
how-to-revolutionise-the-academy-michael.subtitle: Democratising the university

lost-in-the-matrix.speaker_desc: Groundbreaking consciousness researcher Anil Seth, stoic philosopher Massimo Pigliucci, maverick physicist and Youtube sensation Sabine Hossenfelder and Oxford transhumanist Anders Sandberg ask if we are stuck in the matrix. Güneş Taylor hosts.
lost-in-the-matrix.subtitle: Are we living in a computer simulation?

the-age-of-independence.speaker_desc: Distinguished Professor Emerita of Economics and of History Deirdre McCloskey, renowned Emeritus Professor of Theology John Milbank, and award-winning social activist Yassmin Abdel-Magied come together to consider the pitfalls of this age of independence. Barry C. Smith hosts.
the-age-of-independence.subtitle: The pitfalls of social freedom

how-to-excite-people-with-your-ideas-dal.speaker_desc: Dallas Campbell is a celebrated science educator, who presents some of television’s most popular factual shows, including Bang Goes the Theory and The Gadget Show. Dallas is also an author, speaker, and ambassador for STEM education. He has won many plaudits for his services to the public understanding of science, including an Honorary Fellowship from the British Science Association and an honorary life membership for his work at the Royal Institution.
how-to-excite-people-with-your-ideas-dal.subtitle: The secrets of effective communication

the-hypocrisy-of-the-good.speaker_desc: Professor of International Relations David Chandler, award-winning journalist Ece Temelkuran, and esteemed philosopher Julian Baggini debate the hypocrisy of the good. Myrian Francois hosts.
the-hypocrisy-of-the-good.subtitle: Do strict moral codes prevent immoral acts?

money-fame-and-value.speaker_desc: Journalist and art market expert Georgina Adam, art-critic Paddy Johnson, and critically-acclaimed writer Janne Teller debate money, fame and value in the art world. Myriam Francois hosts.
money-fame-and-value.subtitle: Are today's artists monuments to status?

planck-and-the-consciousness-puzzle.speaker_desc: Cosmologist, theoretical physicist Laura Mersini-Houghton, groundbreaking physicist Brian Greene, esteemed physics and philosophy writer Amanda Gefter and eliminative materialism pioneer Patricia Churchland debate Planck and the Consciousness Puzzle. Catherine Heymans hosts.
planck-and-the-consciousness-puzzle.subtitle: Can we see matter as derivative of consciousness?

framing-the-world-kenneth-cukier.speaker_desc: Kenneth Cukier is the Senior Editor for The Economist, co-authored the New York Times bestseller “Big Data” which has been translated into 20 languages, and is the editor and host of the hugely popular technology podcast Babbage. Now a director at Chatham House and an Associate Fellow at Oxford’s Said Business School, Kenneth was also a fellow at Harvard’s Kennedy School of Government.
framing-the-world-kenneth-cukier.subtitle: The optimistic future of AI and humanity

the-new-roaring-20s.speaker_desc: Ayn Rand Institute Chairman, Yaron Brook, Founding editor of The Demented Goddess, Soma Ghosh, and best-selling psychology writer Steve Taylor debate the new roaring 20s. Güneş Taylor hosts
the-new-roaring-20s.subtitle: Will this decade give in to hedonism?

whats-eating-the-universe-paul-davies.speaker_desc: Paul Davies is Regents’ Professor of Physics and Director of the Beyond Center for Fundamental Concepts in Science at Arizona State University. He works on the “big questions” of existence, ranging from the origin of the universe to the origin of life, from the nature of time to foundational questions in quantum mechanics.
whats-eating-the-universe-paul-davies.subtitle: An interview with renowned physicist Paul Davies

in-conversation-rutger-bregman-and-grace.speaker_desc: Rutger Bregman is a historian and author, known for his advocacy of universal basic income, a fifteen hour work week and open borders. His books Humankind (2020) and Utopia for Realists (2017) were both New York Times Bestsellers, and have been translated in more than 40 languages. Rutger made headlines when he appeared at the World Economic Forum in Davos, and use the opportunity to call out the super-rich audience for tax avoidance.
in-conversation-rutger-bregman-and-grace.subtitle: On the future of the left and the nature of humans

alive-in-the-universe.speaker_desc: Professor of Evolutionary Biochemistry Nick Lane, revolutionary astrophysicist and Pulsars discoverer Jocelyn Bell Burnell and Harvard Scientist and New York Times bestseller Avi Loeb debate Alive in the Universe. Catherine Heymans hosts.
alive-in-the-universe.subtitle: Why are we so determined to believe in alien life?

islands-and-the-end-of-modernity-david-c.speaker_desc: David Chandler is Professor of International Relations at the University of Westminster, and edits the journal Anthropocenes: Human, Inhuman, Posthuman and the book series Routledge Studies in Resilience. His most recent monograph is Ontopolitics in the Anthropocene: An Introduction to Mapping, Sensing and Hacking (2018). Chandler’s long-term research focus is on new forms of subjectivity, shaped by both a retreat from the human as subject and the world as object.
islands-and-the-end-of-modernity-david-c.subtitle: The importance of islands in the Anthropocene

navigating-economic-crises-linda-yueh4.speaker_desc: Linda Yueh is an economist, writer and broadcaster. An Economics fellow Oxford University, Yueh is also Adjunct Professor of Economics at London Business School. Yueh has written and edited many books. Her latest The Great Economists: How Their Ideas Can Help Us Today was one of the The Times's Best Business Books of the Year and one of U.S. Newsweek's Best Books of the Year.
navigating-economic-crises-linda-yueh4.subtitle: What can we learn from the great economists?

fantasy-and-reality2.speaker_desc: Director and producer of The Pervert's Guide to Cinema Sophie Fiennes, leading figure in contemporary philosophy of art Noël Carroll and myths expert Betty Sue Flowers explore whether narratives should reflect reality, or escape it. Mark Salter hosts.
fantasy-and-reality2.subtitle: Should narratives reflect or escape reality?

the-stories-that-make-us-betty-sue-flowe.speaker_desc: Betty Sue Flowers is a renowned author and academic. She is the current Emerita Professor of English at the University of Texas and former director of Lyndon Baines Johnson Library and Museum. She has written several books including Four Shields of Power; Presence: Exploring Profound Change in People, Organizations and Society; and Transformations of Myths Through Time. In addition, she edited and consulted on the 1988 documentary, The Power of Myth, a series of interviews between Joseph Campbell and Bill Moyers.
the-stories-that-make-us-betty-sue-flowe.subtitle: How stories shape our understanding of reality

china-morality-and-self-interest.speaker_desc: Former Under-Secretary General of the UN Shashi Tharoor, foreign leader writer for The Guardian Tania Branigan, and former president of the UN Security Council and author of The New Asian Hemisphere Kishore Mahbubani consider the future of trade with China. Rajini Vaidyanathan hosts. This debate was filmed at HowTheLightGetsIn Global Festival in 2020.
china-morality-and-self-interest.subtitle: The future of trade with China

being-seen-to-be-good.speaker_desc: World-leading cultural theorist Kwame Anthony Appiah, Professor of sociology and African Studies and international authority on race, Crystal Fleming, and founder of Prospect Magazine David Goodhart probe the moral maze of public morality. Mark Linsenmayer hosts.
being-seen-to-be-good.subtitle: Probing the moral maze of public morality

the-pattern-seekers-simon-baron-cohen.speaker_desc: Simon Baron-Cohen's lifelong work on autism has revolutionised the world of experimental psychology. As part of his empathizing-systemizing theory, Simon famously claimed that autism is an extreme of the male brain. His new book The Pattern Seekers: How autism drives human invention presents dramatic evidence that autistic people and hyper-systemizers – those who can effortlessly analyse the patterns in systems to invent – share some of the same genes.
the-pattern-seekers-simon-baron-cohen.subtitle: Why can humans alone invent?

how-to-be-an-animal-melanie-challenger.speaker_desc: Melanie Challenger is a writer, poet and podcaster who researches the relationship between humans and the natural world. Initially working in the creative arts, Melanie soon started gaining recognition for her poems, choral works and librettos. Melanie has been a Fellow at the AHRC Centre for the Evolution of Cultural Diversity at UCL, a visiting Fellow at Durham University's philosophy department, and is currently a member of the Nuffield Council on Bioethics.
how-to-be-an-animal-melanie-challenger.subtitle: Animal sentience and ethical decision-making

the-final-wave.speaker_desc: Outspoken journalist and commentator Sonia Poulton, legendary LGBTQ+ rights campaigner Peter Tatchell, host of the We Need to Talk about Whiteness podcast Myriam Francois, and investigative journalist Ruth Michaelson debate the current state of the liberal feminism, and if there is a problem with suppressed dissent within the movement. Rana Mitter hosts.
the-final-wave.subtitle: Free speech and feminism

how-to-leave-the-planet-dallas-campbell.speaker_desc: Dallas Campbell is a celebrated science educator, who presents some of television’s most popular factual shows, including Bang Goes the Theory and The Gadget Show. Dallas is also an author, speaker, and ambassador for STEM education. He has won many plaudits for his services to the public understanding of science, including an Honorary Fellowship from the British Science Association and an honorary life membership for his work at the Royal Institution.
how-to-leave-the-planet-dallas-campbell.subtitle: What’s out there?

trust-science-and-neutrality.speaker_desc: Libertarian biochemist and former advisor to Thatcher Terence Kealey, particle physicist Tara Shears and evolutionary biologist and professor in exile Bret Weinstein debate bias in science. Hilary Lawson hosts.
trust-science-and-neutrality.subtitle: Is science the gold standard of objective truth?

being-good-and-being-authentic.speaker_desc: Radical feminist activist Julie Bindel, philosopher Jonathan Wolff and Financial Secretary to the Treasury Jesse Norman debate being good and being authentic. Mary Ann Sieghart hosts.
being-good-and-being-authentic.subtitle: Being good and being authentic

beyond-time-and-space.speaker_desc: Renowned multiverse theoriest Laura Mersini-Houghton, legendary physicist, writer and broadcaster Paul Davies, post postmodern philosopher and Closure theorist Hilary Lawson and philosopher of science Craig Callender lock horns over the arrows of time. Sara Walker hosts.
beyond-time-and-space.subtitle: Locking horns over the arrows of time

knowledge-reimagined.speaker_desc: Minna Salami is a Finnish Nigerian journalist, feminist and author. Her recent books include 'Sensuous Knowledge: A Black Feminist Approach for Everyone' and 'The Power Book: What is It, Who Has it and Why?'. As a key public figure, she has spoken at over 200 universities, cultural events and conferences spanning over 5 continents.
knowledge-reimagined.subtitle: Exploring sensuous knowledge with Minna Salami.

why-do-we-laugh-shazia-mirza.speaker_desc: Shazia Mirza is a multi-award winning stand-up comedian, actress, and writer. She is best known for her show The Kardashians Made Me Do It. Shazia began performing stand up comedy whilst pursuing a career as a teacher and quickly garnered attention for her provocative style. In 2007, she presented F*** Off, I'm a Hairy Woman on BBC Three, a documentary about body image and contrasting stereotypes surrounding women's body hair.
why-do-we-laugh-shazia-mirza.subtitle: The role of comedy in our lives

liberty-and-the-left.speaker_desc: Firebrand philosopher Slavoj Žižek, influential rapper and social commentator Lowkey, and outspoken author and journalist Ella Whelan debate the hypocrisies facing the Left. Philip Collins hosts.
liberty-and-the-left.subtitle: Does the left need to re-engage with freedom?

humanity-beyond-nature-ray-tallis.speaker_desc: Physician, philosopher, poet and novelist Raymond Tallis is ‘one of the world’s greatest living polymaths’ (Intelligent Life). He is the author of such wide-ranging books as The Enduring Significance of Parmenides, The Kingdom of Infinite Space and Aping Mankind .
humanity-beyond-nature-ray-tallis.subtitle: An interview with Raymond Tallis

stepping-into-the-unknown.speaker_desc: World-renowned physicist Paul Davies, simulations manager for the Muon 2-g experiment Renee Fatemi and groundbreaking astronomer Chris Impey debate stepping into the unknown. Philip Ball hosts.
stepping-into-the-unknown.subtitle: Is it time to throw away the Standard Model?

the-precarious-case-for-being-good.speaker_desc: Turkish journalist, author and activist Ece Temelkuran, Anglican priest and scholar Alison Milbank and philosopher of mind Peter Sjöstedt-H debate the existence of a secular morality. Mark Salter hosts.
the-precarious-case-for-being-good.subtitle: Are we living in the long shadow of a dead God?

in-conversation-esther-duflo-and-jesse-n.speaker_desc: Esther Duflo is an economist and profesor of Poverty Alleviation and Development Economics at MIT. She is the co-director of J-PAL and shared the 2019 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences "for their experimental approach to alleviating global poverty" Jesse Norman is a British Conservative Party politician serving as Financial Secretary to the Treasury since 2019 and as the Member of Parliament for Hereford and South Herefordshire since 2010.
in-conversation-esther-duflo-and-jesse-n.subtitle: The Nobel Prize winner on ending global poverty

the-search-for-wellbeing-mental-health.speaker_desc: Mental health campaigner Jonny Benjamin, experimental psychologist Miguel Farias, clinical psychologist Lucy Johnstone and Top Boy actor and Mind UK Ambassador Nicholas Pinnock discuss the search for wellbeing. Güneş Taylor hosts.
the-search-for-wellbeing-mental-health.subtitle: Can we talk ourselves better?

scientific-freedom-craig-callender.speaker_desc: Craig Callender is a professor of Philosophy at the University of California, San Diego. His main areas of research are philosophy of science, philosophy of physics and metaphysics.
scientific-freedom-craig-callender.subtitle: An interview with Craig Callender

natures-memory-rupert-sheldrake.speaker_desc: Rupert Sheldrake is a scientist, author, and parapsychology researcher. Best known for his 2012 book The Science Delusion and the controversial, viral TED talk he gave which was banned by the organisation. He has taken issue with the New Atheism of many and has also challenged the idea that the laws of nature are fixed and unchanging.
natures-memory-rupert-sheldrake.subtitle: The theory of Morphic Resonance

addiction-health-and-technology.speaker_desc: Royal College of Psychiatrists Member Bernadka Dubicka, co-founder of Big Brother Watch Silkie Carlo and co-founder of Humanity+ David Pearce plug into the dangerous and addictive qualities of tech.
addiction-health-and-technology.subtitle: Tech giants and our obsessive behaviour

what-ive-learned-about-whiteness-myriam-.speaker_desc: Myriam François is an Anglo-French writer and broadcaster. Myriam converted to Islam at the age of 21, convinced that the Qur'an represented "the culmination of all of [her] philosophical cogitation." She has written extensively on the place of Islam in the modern world and on European politics
what-ive-learned-about-whiteness-myriam-.subtitle: Moving towards a fairer society

drugs-death-and-hypocrisy.speaker_desc: Neuropsychopharmacologist and former government advisor David Nutt, distinguished economist Deirdre McCloskey and philosopher of mind Peter Sjöstedt-Hughes debate drugs, death and hypocrisy. Mary Ann Sieghart hosts.
drugs-death-and-hypocrisy.subtitle: Can and should we amend our drug policy?

philosophy-for-cynical-times-slavoj-zize.speaker_desc: Slavoj Žižek is a globally renowned philosopher and cultural critic. He is the author of The Sublime Object of Ideology and is the International Director of Humanities at Birkbeck. Image credit: Žižek in 2013 via Flickr/Simon Plestenjak (please hyperlink to here: https://www.flickr.com/photos/sim-ples/8542474381)
philosophy-for-cynical-times-slavoj-zize.subtitle: An interview with Slavoj Žižek

electric-brains-anders-sandberg.speaker_desc: Anders Sandberg is a research fellow at the Future of Humanity Institute at Oxford, where his research concerns the societal and ethical issues surrounding human enhancement and new technologies. He is also research associate to the Oxford Uehiro Centre for Practical Ethics and the Oxford Centre for Neuroethics.
electric-brains-anders-sandberg.subtitle: A journey through 'wireheading'

how-to-view-suffering-martin-seligman-ma.speaker_desc: Martin Seligman is a hugely influential American psychologist and author. His groundbreaking theories of positive psychology and well-being - especially of ‘learned helplessness’ - have made him one of the most referenced psychologists of the 20th century. Mandy Seligman is an award-winning black and white photographer who began her career as a developmental social psychologist. She has spent the last thirty years traveling around the world with Martin Seligman spreading Positive Psychology.
how-to-view-suffering-martin-seligman-ma.subtitle: Dissecting what it means to build well-being

nothing-but-the-truth.speaker_desc: Founder of The Skeptics Society, Michael Shermer, author of Closure, Hilary Lawson, and Professor of History at the University of Wisconsin-Madison Jennifer Ratner-Rosenhagen lock horns over the existence of truth. Hosted by Mary-Jane Rubenstein.
nothing-but-the-truth.subtitle: Are all views essentially perspectival?

standing-up-to-sexism-helen-lederer.speaker_desc: Ab Fab Star, Helen Lederer is a comedian, actress, and writer. Her first book, Losing It, was nominated for the Edinburgh First Book Award, and the P. G. Wodehouse Comedy Literary Award. Only four women have won the Wodehouse prize in its 20-year history, one of the reasons that Lederer created a new literary prize, the CWIP Awards for Comedy Women In Print.
standing-up-to-sexism-helen-lederer.subtitle: An interview with comedian Helen Lederer

leadership-hypocrisy-and-power.speaker_desc: Pultizer prize winning historian Joseph J Ellis, Global CEO of Havas Creative and author of 'No Bullsh*t Leadership' Christ Hirst, and former leader of the Green Party Natalie Bennett debate leadership, hypocrisy and power. Myriam Francois hosts.
leadership-hypocrisy-and-power.subtitle: How much should we trust our leaders?
