status-and-wonder.speaker_desc: Veteran columnist and former BBC Social Affairs Editor Polly Toynbee, award winning writer and cultural theorist Minna Salami, and Oxford chemist and prolific science writer Peter Atkins ask if we undervalue artistic education or overvalue its cultural worth. Isabel Hilton hosts.
status-and-wonder.subtitle: How vital is art to our lives and culture?

decolonising-science-sundar-sarukkai.speaker_desc: Sundar Sarukkai was, till 2019, a professor of philosophy at the National Institute of Advanced Studies. He was also the Founder-Director of the Manipal Centre for Philosophy and Humanities. His work is primarily in the philosophy of natural and social sciences.
decolonising-science-sundar-sarukkai.subtitle: Why non-Western science is paramount

the-necessity-and-danger-of-belief.speaker_desc: Former Director of Human Rights NGO Liberty, Shami Chakrabarti, groundbreaking physicist Carlo Rovelli, Consciousness expert Philip Goff, and world leader in relativity and cosmology George Ellis discuss the necessity and danger of belief. Isabel Hilton hosts.
the-necessity-and-danger-of-belief.subtitle: Does faith undermine knowledge?

arc-of-life-ayaan-hirsi-ali.speaker_desc: Ayaan Hirsi Ali is a Somali-born classical liberal, free speech advocate and an activist for the rights of women and girls. Ayaan rejected the her Muslim faith and became an atheist, and has since been a vocal critic of both Islam and the woke left.
arc-of-life-ayaan-hirsi-ali.subtitle: Interviewing the unflinching human rights defender

the-matrix-of-the-miracle.speaker_desc: Philosopher and co-founder of the World Transhumanist Association David Pearce, social commentator Theodore Dalrymple, and biomedical researcher Güneş Taylor imagine the future of the family. Stephanie Hare hosts.
the-matrix-of-the-miracle.subtitle: The future of the family

how-to-think-about-sex-victoria-brooks.speaker_desc: Writer and researcher, Victoria Brooks teaches Criminal Law, Philosophy of Law and Environmental Law at the University of Westminster. Her research interests include sex and its relationship to identity, femininity, law and philosophy.
how-to-think-about-sex-victoria-brooks.subtitle: Applying philosophy to our sex lives

sexuality-power-and-pornography.speaker_desc: Comedienne and star of Bridget Jones and Miranda Sally Phillips, legendary human rights campaigner Peter Tatchell, author of Fucking Law: The Search for Her Sexual Ethics Victoria Brooks, and author of Turned On Kate Devlin go head to head over feminist pornography, hosted by HuffPost journalist Nancy Groves.
sexuality-power-and-pornography.subtitle: Are we liberating female desires?

understanding-ourselves-patricia-churchl.speaker_desc: Patricia Churchland is a the distinguished founder of neurophilosophy. A pioneer of eliminative materialism, Patricia heralds a radically different way to understand the brain, arguing that ideas like pure morality and reason will eventually be abandoned in favour of a purely scientific view of the human mind.
understanding-ourselves-patricia-churchl.subtitle: The nature and data of morality

designer-babies-eugenics-debate.speaker_desc: Founder of deCODE Genetics Kári Stefánsson, bioethicist Rebecca Bennett, controversial polymath Jacob Appel and world-leading autism expert Simon Baron-Cohen debate designer babies. Science author, Emily Grossman, hosts.
designer-babies-eugenics-debate.subtitle: Debating designer babies

belief-hypocrisy-and-reason.speaker_desc: Distinguished philosophy professor Graham Harman, author of Oughts and Thoughts Anandi Hattiangadi and post-post-realist Hilary Lawson explore the difference between opinion and truth. Hannah Dawson hosts.
belief-hypocrisy-and-reason.subtitle: The difference between opinion and truth

how-to-empower-with-wit-helen-lederer.speaker_desc: Helen Lederer is a comedian, writer and actress, best known for her role as Catriona in Absolutely Fabulous. She is also the author of the comedy novel Losing It.
how-to-empower-with-wit-helen-lederer.subtitle: The powerful influence of humour

the-authority-gap-mary-ann-sieghart.speaker_desc: Mary Ann Sieghart is a journalist and radio presenter. A former assistant editor of The Times, Mary Ann is chair of the Social Market Foundation - a think tank for fairer markets and open public services. Mary Ann has also written for The Independent, The Economist and the Financial Times and was the presenter of Start the Week, Beyond Westminster and many other one-off documentaries.
the-authority-gap-mary-ann-sieghart.subtitle: How to work towards gender equality

tomorrows-world-technology.speaker_desc: Outspoken Oxford transhumanist Anders Sandberg, inventor of groundbreaking green technology Priyadarshini Karve and Director of Big Brother Watch Silkie Carlo get to grips with the potential of technology. Hosted by Aman Sethi.
tomorrows-world-technology.subtitle: Getting to grips with the future of technology

saving-liberal-democracy-bim-afolami.speaker_desc: Son of a Nigerian immigrant, Bim Afolami is a Conservative MP. After studying at Eton and Oxford, Bim worked in the City for 10 years before going into politics. He is known for his centre-ground beliefs
saving-liberal-democracy-bim-afolami.subtitle: Securing hope for the future

ideas-identity-and-influence-kwame-antho.speaker_desc: Kwame Anthony Appiah is Professor of Philosophy and Law at New York University and author of The Lies That Bind: Rethinking Identity and Cosmopolitanism: Ethics in a World of Strangers.
ideas-identity-and-influence-kwame-antho.subtitle: An interview with Philosopher Kwame Anthony Appiah

getting-real-about-global-power.speaker_desc: Former UK Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind, China reporter and broadcast editor at The Spectator Cindy Yu, writer and historian Michael Pembroke, and Global Reporting Centre collaborator Melissa Chan get real about global power. Rana Mitter hosts.
getting-real-about-global-power.subtitle: Is the West irrelevant?

the-last-mystery-of-cosmology-lee-smolin.speaker_desc: Lee Smolin is a theoretical physicist who has been, since 2001, a founding and senior faculty member at Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics. His main contributions have been to the quantum theory of gravity. He has been a co-inventor and major contributor to the field in two major directions: loop quantum gravity and deformed special relativity.
the-last-mystery-of-cosmology-lee-smolin.subtitle: Moving towards a unified physics

the-pursuit-of-happiness-transhumanism-d.speaker_desc: David Pearce is an eminent figure within the transhumanist movement, and co-founder of Humanity+, an international organisation which advocates for the technological enhancement of the human species. He envisions a future completely free of suffering for both humans and non-human animals, a pain-free paradise in which all thought, feeling, and experience is sublimated into what he calls "gradients of bliss". The abolition of suffering is for David an ethical necessity, elaborated in his manifesto, The Hedonistic Imperative.
the-pursuit-of-happiness-transhumanism-d.subtitle: An Interview with David Pearce

the-survival-paradox.speaker_desc: Distinguished Professor of Philosophy Graham Harman, Associate Professor of History and Philosophy of Science Mazviita Chirimuuta, and cognitive psychologist Donald Hoffman debate the survival paradox. Hosted by documentary film-maker David Malone.
the-survival-paradox.subtitle: Have we evolved to see the truth about reality?

humans-and-other-animals.speaker_desc: Philosopher, cultural critic and author of Aping Mankind Ray Tallis, writer, poet and podcaster Melanie Challenger, farmer, author, politician Jamie Blackett and Professor of Sociology at Kingston University Kay Peggs debate the hypocrisy of the way we treat animals. Myriam Francois hosts. In association with Future Normal
humans-and-other-animals.subtitle: The hypocrisy of the way we treat animals

the-black-hole-paradox.speaker_desc: Nobel Prize-winning physicist and Hawking collaborator Sir Roger Penrose, theoretical physicist Sean Carroll, and UCL Professor of Astrophysics Amelie Saintonge tackle the paradox of black holes. David Malone hosts.
the-black-hole-paradox.subtitle: The universe's unsolved mysteries

the-malthusian-catastrophe.speaker_desc: Transhumanist Anders Sandberg, author of Human Tide Paul Morland and former leader of the Green Party Natalie Bennett debate the perils of population. This debate was filmed at our HowTheLightGetsIn London 2019 festival.
the-malthusian-catastrophe.subtitle: The perils of population

no-bad-women-cari-mitchell.speaker_desc: Cari Mitchell is a spokeswoman for the English Collective of Prostitutes, a network of women working in different areas of the sex industry – both on the streets and indoors, which campaigns for decriminalisation of sex work and for sex workers' safety.
no-bad-women-cari-mitchell.subtitle: The case for the decriminalisation of sex work

dreams-delusions-and-class-interests.speaker_desc: Conservative Cabinet Minister Jesse Norman, world-renowned political satirist PJ O'Rourke and Jeremy Corbyn ally Dawn Butler wrestle with the relevance of class. Paul Waugh hosts.
dreams-delusions-and-class-interests.subtitle: The relevance of class

the-new-age-space-race.speaker_desc: Mary-Jane Rubenstein is Professor of Religion at Wesleyan University in Connecticut, USA. Her book Worlds Without End: The Many Lives of the Universe examines cosmological models throughout history, from the world-views of the Ancient Greeks through to the well-respected multiverse theory in modern science. She links contemporary models of the universe to their forerunners and explores the reason for their recent resurgence.
the-new-age-space-race.subtitle: Why space and why now?

the-truth-about-lies.speaker_desc: The Times journalist David Aaronovitch, author of Freedom In the Age of Alternative Facts Santiago Zabala, and philosophy of the mind specialist Åsa Wikforss lock horns over whether telling the truth still matters at all.
the-truth-about-lies.subtitle: Does telling the truth still matter?

the-hunt-for-expertise-anandi-hattiangad.speaker_desc: Anandi Hattiangadi is a Professor of Philosophy at the University of Stockholm, with interests in the philosophy of mind and language, epistemology, and meta-ethics. She is a core part of the interdisciplinary program Knowledge Resistance: Causes, Consequences, and Cures.
the-hunt-for-expertise-anandi-hattiangad.subtitle: The logical labyrinth

in-conversation-armando-iannucci.speaker_desc: Armando Iannucci is a legendary satirist, writer and film-maker and Claire Armitstead is the Associate Culture Editor for the Guardian.
in-conversation-armando-iannucci.subtitle: An exclusive interview with the legendary satirist

life-is-what-sara-walker.speaker_desc: Sara Walker is an astro-biologist and theoretical physicist interested in the origin of life and how to find life on other worlds.
life-is-what-sara-walker.subtitle: Our explanation for life will be counterintuitive

new-pilgrims-rupert-sheldrake.speaker_desc: Rupert Sheldrake is a biologist, author and parapsychology researcher, best known for his hypothesis of morphic resonance. He is a critic of New Atheism, and has also challenged the idea that the laws of nature are fixed and unchanging.
new-pilgrims-rupert-sheldrake.subtitle: Why spiritual journeys draw non-religious people

mind-over-matter.speaker_desc: Author of The Science Delusion Rupert Sheldrake, chairman of Humanity+ Natasha Vita-More and philosopher of mind and AI specialist Susan Schneider debate the potential of mind-computer interface technology.
mind-over-matter.subtitle: The potential of mind-computer interface tech

beyond-us-bonus-review.speaker_desc: Series hosts Bernardo Kastrup and Fred Matser. In association with Essentia Foundation . Read Beyond Us . Watch Beyond Me .
beyond-us-bonus-review.subtitle: Episode 5: Bonus Review

how-to-live-forever-natasha-vita-more.speaker_desc: Dr. Natasha Vita More is an author, strategic designer, and scientist, working in the fields of human enhancement technology and life extension. Natasha is the Executive Director of Humanity+, the world's largest transhumanist organisation, which advocates the ethical use of technology to expand human capacities.
how-to-live-forever-natasha-vita-more.subtitle: Radical life extension' technology

why-we-need-free-speech-michael-shermer.speaker_desc: Michael Shermer is the founder of The Skeptics Society, the editor-in-chief of its magazine Skeptic, and a Presidential Fellow at Chapman University, where he teaches Skepticism 101.
why-we-need-free-speech-michael-shermer.subtitle: The dangers of silencing discussion

science-and-its-great-corrupter-peter-at.speaker_desc: Peter Atkins FRSC is an English chemist, outspoken atheist, and author of works of popular science such as Atkins' Molecules.
science-and-its-great-corrupter-peter-at.subtitle: An interview with Peter Atkins

land-of-the-free.speaker_desc: The BBC's North America correspondent, Jon Sopel, chair of Republicans Oversees, Sarah Elliott and author of Against Democracy Jason Brennan clash over the future of the Land of the Free. Hosted by Isabel Hilton.
land-of-the-free.subtitle: Post-Trump America

how-to-die-before-you-do-brian-muraresku.speaker_desc: Brian C. Muraresku is a classicist, lawyer and New York Times bestselling author. His debut book, The Immortality Key, combines Muraresku’s classical research interests to provide a groundbreaking dive into the role psychedelics have played in the origins of Western civilisation.
how-to-die-before-you-do-brian-muraresku.subtitle: Discovering psychedelics in the Ancient world

the-rational-animal.speaker_desc: Professor of Psychology and Behavioral Economics at Duke University Dan Ariely, Professor of Psychology and Cognitive Science at Yale Paul Bloom, and Patty Kostkova, Professor in Digital Health and the Director of UCL IRDR Centre for Digital Public Health in Emergencies debate if humans are truly rational animals. Güneş Taylor, training fellow at the Francis Crick Institute, hosts.
the-rational-animal.subtitle: Are we any good at making decisions?

an-intro-to-crispr-gunes-taylor.speaker_desc: Güneş Taylor is a training fellow at the Francis Crick Institute, the London-based biomedical research centre. Her research predominantly focuses on the the genetic formation of ovaries and testes.
an-intro-to-crispr-gunes-taylor.subtitle: The potential of CRISPR technology

the-anti-universe.speaker_desc: Founding member at Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics, Lee Smolin, professor of Physics at Liverpool University, Tara Shears and leader of the Superfluid Dark Matter group at the Frankfurt Institute, Sabine Hossenfelder battle over the very fabric of the universe. Hosted by Hilary Lawson.
the-anti-universe.subtitle: The biggest jump in physics?

where-is-racial-justice.speaker_desc: Now the Merton P. Stoltz Professor at Brown University, Glenn Loury became the first black tenured professor of economics in the history of Harvard University in 1982. Glenn's vehement criticism of affirmative action along with his argument that African-Americans' own behaviour is responsible for their plight, and not white racism, led to him becoming a hero of the Reagan intellectual Right. "A genuine maverick thinker and a shrewd political operator" The New York Times Magazine
where-is-racial-justice.subtitle: The dangers of victimhood

lessons-from-the-universe-ralph-cordey.speaker_desc: Head of Future Missions at Airbus, Ralph Cordey focuses on providing new engineering solutions for scientific missions. The space missions that Ralph works on can focus on anything from searching for life in our solar system and beyond, to gaining a greater understanding of our own planet's climate.
lessons-from-the-universe-ralph-cordey.subtitle: An interview with Airbus's Ralph Cordey

the-limits-of-sexuality.speaker_desc: Award-winning author Yasmin Alibhai-Brown, writer and feminist Mikki Kendall, spokesperson for the English Collective of Prostitutes Nikki Adams, and novelist Oliva Fane debate the limits of sexuality. Rana Mitter hosts.
the-limits-of-sexuality.subtitle: Should we eradicate sexuality from public life?

arc-of-life-daniel-dennett5.speaker_desc: Daniel Dennett is a world-renowned philosopher and cognitive scientist. He is a major contributor to the understanding of the conceptual foundations of evolutionary biology. Alongside Sam Harris, Christopher Hitchens and Richard Dawkins, Daniel is well known for being one of the “four horse-men of new atheism” who dedicated themselves to actively countering religion in every form. He is currently the Austin B. Fletcher Professor of Philosophy, and Co-Director of the Center for Cognitive Studies at Tufts University “Perhaps America’s most widely read and debated living philosopher” New York Times
arc-of-life-daniel-dennett5.subtitle: An interview with the world-renowned philosopher

deregulate-to-innovate-matt-ridley.speaker_desc: Matt Ridley is a British journalist and businessman. Matt worked for the Economist for nine years as science editor, Washington correspondent and American editor, before turning to writing and business.
deregulate-to-innovate-matt-ridley.subtitle: An interview with Matt Ridley

chicken-or-egg.speaker_desc: Legendary American philosopher Daniel Dennett, astrobiologist and famed science communicator, Sara Walker, and evolutionary (and revolutionary) biochemist Professor Nick Lane tackle the most fundamental question of all. Hosted by Güneş Taylor.
chicken-or-egg.subtitle: Are we looking at life wrong?

the-breakdown-of-cosmology-bjorn-ekeberg.speaker_desc: Bjørn Ekeberg is a philosopher of science, author of Metaphysical Experiments Physics and the Invention of the Universe. "Ekeberg provides a unique synthesis that will be of interest to philosophers of science and contemplative scientists alike." Graham Harman
the-breakdown-of-cosmology-bjorn-ekeberg.subtitle: Exploring its biggest problems

our-saviour-or-our-downfall.speaker_desc: Biologist and evolutionary theorist Bret Weinstein, inventor of voice assistant SIRI Luc Julia, genetic researcher Güneş Taylor and Flint water crisis whistle-blower Marc Edwards debate our saviour or our downfall. Mary Ann Sieghart hosts.

beyond-us-language.speaker_desc: Series hosts Bernardo Kastrup and Fred Matser discuss this fascinating topic with renowned British philosopher of language, Jennifer Hornsby. In association with Essentia Foundation . Read Beyond Us . Watch Beyond Me .
beyond-us-language.subtitle: Episode 3: the uses and limitations of language

evolution-in-politics-jesse-norman.speaker_desc: Jesse Norman is a leading British Conservative Party politician, currently serving as the Financial Secretary to the Treasury and tipped by some to be a future leader of the party. He has been an MP for Hereford and South Herefordshire since 2010. Before becoming an MP he led an educational charity in Eastern Europe and was a director at Barclays bank.
evolution-in-politics-jesse-norman.subtitle: An interview with Jesse Norman MP

arc-of-life-paul-krugman.speaker_desc: "The most celebrated economist of his generation" The Economist
arc-of-life-paul-krugman.subtitle: An interview with Nobel Prize-winning economist

east-meets-west-chris-impey.speaker_desc: Chris Impey is a Distinguished Professor at Arizona University, where he leads one of the largest astronomy departments in the USA. "Chris Impey manages to rejuvenate that 'Space Is Our Future' feeling that pervaded human culture a half century ago." Neil deGrasse Tyson
east-meets-west-chris-impey.subtitle: Can Buddhism inform science?

values-of-the-west.speaker_desc: Cultural critic and philosopher Raymond Tallis, founder of the first Black Studies university course Kehinde Andrews, and writer, broadcaster and academic Myriam Franҫois question our faith in Western values.
values-of-the-west.subtitle: Do we need a new set of ideals?

the-church-s-decline-linda-woodhead.speaker_desc: Linda Woodhead is a distinguished Professor of Religion and Society, director of the Religion and Society Programme and co-founder of the Westminster Faith Debates.
the-church-s-decline-linda-woodhead.subtitle: An Interview with Linda Woodhead

in-conversation-carlo-rovelli-jim-al-kha.speaker_desc: Carlo Rovelli is a theoretical physicist and founder of loop quantum gravity theory. Jim Al-Khalili is a theoretical physicist, author and broadcaster who regularly presents science programmes on BBC radio and television.
in-conversation-carlo-rovelli-jim-al-kha.subtitle: On fundamental physics and the nature of reality

the-economy-of-the-future-joseph-stiglit.speaker_desc: Neoliberalism is failing us. Tech companies steal our data, banks control financial regulation, and inequality continues to skyrocket. As the global economy slowly recovers from Covid-19, policy makers need to take this chance to forge a new, progressive form of capitalism. Nobel prize winning economist and author Joseph Stiglitz proposes how we might rebuild the economy in a way that works for everyone.
the-economy-of-the-future-joseph-stiglit.subtitle: With Nobel-prize winning economist Joseph Stiglitz

experimenting-with-the-truth.speaker_desc: Professor at the Stanford University School of Medicine, and author of the most downloaded paper in history John Ioannidis, theoretical physicist and winner of the 2020 Blavatnik Award for Young Scientists Claudia de Rham and sociologist of science and author of Are We All Scientific Experts Now Harry Collins discuss the importance of replicability and objectivity in science.
experimenting-with-the-truth.subtitle: The importance of objectivity in science

beyond-us-competition-episode-two.speaker_desc: Series hosts Bernardo Kastrup and Fred Matser discuss this fascinating topic with American evolutionary psychologist, Donald Hoffman. In association with Essentia Foundation . Read Beyond Us . Watch Beyond Me .
beyond-us-competition-episode-two.subtitle: Episode 2: Did we evolve to compete or cooperate?

are-you-an-illusion-the-self.speaker_desc: Author of Self and Other Dan Zahavi, Philosophy Professor and philosophy of the cognitive sciences researcher Lisa Bortolotti and Research Fellow at the Future of Humanity Institute Anders Sandberg debate whether the self is an illusion.
are-you-an-illusion-the-self.subtitle: Reshaping the self

trust-in-a-relative-world.speaker_desc: Maria Baghramian is the Professor of American Philosophy at University College Dublin and one of the world’s leading experts on moral and epistemological relativism."
trust-in-a-relative-world.subtitle: An interview with Maria Baghramian

power-to-the-people.speaker_desc: Former Brexit Party MEP Claire Fox, Academic Director of the Royal Institute of Philosophy Julian Baggini, and former political strategist Matthew Taylor clash over the future of democracy.
power-to-the-people.subtitle: The future of democracy

ai-and-the-future-of-the-mind-susan-schn.speaker_desc: Susan Schneider is an American academic and public philosopher, the William F. Dietrich Professor of Philosophy at Florida Atlantic University, and a recipient of the National Endowment for the Humanities Public Scholar Award. She is the author of Artificial You: AI and the Future of Your Mind.
ai-and-the-future-of-the-mind-susan-schn.subtitle: Is it possible that we'll merge with AI?

newton-s-space-emily-thomas.speaker_desc: Emily Thomas is an Associate Professor of Philosophy at Durham University, whose research interests are in space and time, early modern metaphysics and the philosophy of travel.
newton-s-space-emily-thomas.subtitle: And its enduring impact

race-identity-and-justice.speaker_desc: Award winning spoken-word artist George the Poet, economist and first black tenured professor of economics at Harvard Glenn Loury and First elected Black female government minister in the UK Dawn Butler debate the relevance of racial identity in the modern world.
race-identity-and-justice.subtitle: The relevance of race in the modern world

preparing-for-utopia-anders-sandberg.speaker_desc: Anders Sandberg is the James Martin Fellow at the Future of Humanity Insitute at Oxford University whose research centres on the ethical and social implications of future technologies and human enhancement.
preparing-for-utopia-anders-sandberg.subtitle: An interview with transhumanist Anders Sandberg

how-we-became-who-we-are.speaker_desc: Hugely influential geneticist Robert Plomin, libertarian journalist and author of The Evolution of Everything Matt Ridley, and award-winning journalist Yasmin Alibhai-Brown explore the relevance of politics in the nature/nurture debate. Mary Ann Sieghart hosts.
how-we-became-who-we-are.subtitle: Politics in the nature vs nurture debate

the-struggle-for-dignity-david-goodhthe-.speaker_desc: David Goodhart is a British journalist and cultural commentator, and the founder and former editor of Prospect magazine. "David Goodhart is among the most insightful analysts of Anglo-American society" - Jonathan Haidt
the-struggle-for-dignity-david-goodhthe-.subtitle: How do we allocate reward in our society?

beyond-us-knowledge-episode-one.speaker_desc: Series hosts Bernardo Kastrup and Fred Matser discuss this fascinating topic with Canadian philosopher and champion of the enlightenment project, Rebecca Goldstein. In association with Essentia Foundation . Read Beyond Us . Watch Beyond Me .
beyond-us-knowledge-episode-one.subtitle: Episode 1: What is knowledge and what is it for?

consciousness-and-the-world.speaker_desc: Post-postmodern philosopher and renowned critic of philosophical realism Hilary Lawson, author of the NYT Bestseller '‘Conscious: A Brief Guide to the Fundamental Mystery of the Mind’ Annaka Harris, Iranian philosopher and the author of 'Intelligence and Spirit' Reza Negarestani, and computer scientist, researcher, and proponent of "metaphysical idealism" Bernardo Kastrup debate Consciousness and the World. Mary-Jane Rubenstein hosts.
consciousness-and-the-world.subtitle: The relationship between experience and reality

cosmological-mysteries-chris-impey.speaker_desc: Chris Impey is a professor and deputy head of the department of astronomy at the University of Arizona. His astronomy research focuses on observational cosmology—using telescopes and other instruments to study the large-scale structure and evolution of the universe.
cosmological-mysteries-chris-impey.subtitle: An interview with Chris Impey

the-future-of-feminism-ella-whelan.speaker_desc: Ella Whelan is a freelance journalist, commentator and author of What Women Want: Fun, Freedom and an End to Feminism. She is the former assistant editor at spiked .
the-future-of-feminism-ella-whelan.subtitle: Where is women's politics going?

stories-to-believe-in.speaker_desc: Former Conservative MP Rory Stewart, economist and voice of the left Grace Blakeley, and leading public intellectual Michael Sandel battle it out over the case for ideological politics.
stories-to-believe-in.subtitle: Is idealism central to politics?

poetry-live-paul-muldoon.speaker_desc: Pulitzer Prize winner Paul Muldoon is one of the greatest poets alive today. Paul has served as both Professor of Poetry at Oxford University and the poetry editor of The New Yorker. He published his first book at the age of just 21, and is now the author of thirteen major collections of poetry, and has taught at Princeton University since 1987. "The most significant English-language poet born since the second World War". TLS
poetry-live-paul-muldoon.subtitle: With Pulitzer Prize-winning Paul Muldoon

behind-black-holes-amelie-saintonge.speaker_desc: Amélie Saintonge is a professor of Astrophysics at UCL whose research is currently funded by the Royal Society.
behind-black-holes-amelie-saintonge.subtitle: How to listen to the celestial giants

a-writers-voice-meg-rosoff.speaker_desc: Meg Rosoff is a writer best known for her award-winning novel How I Live Now. Her second novel, Just in Case, won the annual Carnegie Medal.
a-writers-voice-meg-rosoff.subtitle: Shedding light on the conscious and sub-conscious

the-different-places-of-the-self.speaker_desc: Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad, FBA is the Distinguished Professor of Comparative Religion and Philosophy at Lancaster University. His research focuses on Indian religions – Hinduism, Buddhism and Jainism – and comparative phenomenology, epistemology, metaphysics and philosophy of religion.
the-different-places-of-the-self.subtitle: The problem with individualism

human-blueprints-robert-plomin.speaker_desc: Robert J. Plomin, FBA is an American psychologist and geneticist best known for his work in twin studies and behavior genetics.
human-blueprints-robert-plomin.subtitle: An interview with Robert Plomin

our-story-of-the-universe.speaker_desc: Astronomer, cosmologist and author Chris Impey, theoretical physicist and creator of the influential Backreaction blog Sabine Hossenfelder and philosopher of science Bjørn Ekeberg explore the beginning of everything. James Ladyman hosts.
our-story-of-the-universe.subtitle: And how it really began

after-the-end-of-history-malcolm-rifkind.speaker_desc: Malcolm Rifkind is a politian who served in various roles as a Cabinet minister under Margaret Thatcher and John Major, including Defence Secretary and Foreign Secretary. "Malcolm Rifkind was in the top rank of twentieth-century politicians. Few saw events at closer quarters." John Major
after-the-end-of-history-malcolm-rifkind.subtitle: How we remain on the right track

promiscuity-and-power.speaker_desc: Multi-award winning comedian Shazia Mirza, founder of the sex-party company Killing Kittens Emma Sayle and writer, broadcaster and academic Myriam Fran ç ois clash over the role promiscuity plays in the fight for equality. Stephanie Hare hosts.
promiscuity-and-power.subtitle: A path to empowerment?

the-empathy-trap-dan-zahavi.speaker_desc: Dan Zahavi is a Professor of Philosophy at the University of Copenhagen and the University of Oxford. "One of the most prolific and insightful phenomenologists of his generation" Distinguished Professor Alessandro Duranti, University of California
the-empathy-trap-dan-zahavi.subtitle: Is empathy our best base for morality?

challenging-the-scientific-dogma-rupert-.speaker_desc: Rupert Sheldrake is a biologist and author best known for his hypothesis of morphic resonance. His book, The Science Delusion, was a bestseller.
challenging-the-scientific-dogma-rupert-.subtitle: An interview with Rupert Sheldrake

the-known-and-the-unknown.speaker_desc: Renowned philosopher and ethicist Simon Blackburn, psychoanalyst and sociologist Renata Salecl, and author of Galileo's Error: Foundations for a New Science of Consciousness Philip Goff try to find their way through the fog of uncertainty. Joanna Kavenna.
the-known-and-the-unknown.subtitle: Finding our way through the fog of uncertainty

how-to-right-wrongs-peter-tatchell.speaker_desc: Peter Tatchell is a human rights campaigner best known for his work with LGBT+ social movements. Since 2011 he has been the Director of the Peter Tatchell Foundation.
how-to-right-wrongs-peter-tatchell.subtitle: Moving forward without forgetting our past

eradicating-gender.speaker_desc: Legendary poet Eileen Myles, Founder, President and Chief Executive of the Bianca Jagger Human Rights Foundation Bianca Jagger and social theorist and cultural critic Nina Power unravel the path to equality. Rana Mitter hosts.
eradicating-gender.subtitle: Unraveling the path to equality

the-continuity-of-the-self-chakravarthi-.speaker_desc: Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad, FBA is the Distinguished Professor of Comparative Religion and Philosophy at Lancaster University. His research focuses on Indian religions – Hinduism, Buddhism and Jainism – and comparative phenomenology, epistemology, metaphysics and philosophy of religion.
the-continuity-of-the-self-chakravarthi-.subtitle: An interview with Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad

how-to-fathom-timelessness-via-psychedel.speaker_desc: Peter Sjöstedt-H is a philosopher of mind who specialises in the thought of Whitehead, Nietzsche, and Spinoza, and in fields pertaining to panpsychism and altered states of mind.
how-to-fathom-timelessness-via-psychedel.subtitle: What should time mean to us?

uncovering-the-universe2.speaker_desc: Theoretical physicist Claudia de Rham, Closure theorist Hilary Lawson and philosopher and author of Translating the World: Science and Language Sundar Sarukkai go head to head to investigate whether science can really uncover the secrets of the universe. Philosopher James Ladyman hosts.
uncovering-the-universe2.subtitle: Can science really reveal its secrets?

the-path-to-the-future-susan-schneider-a.speaker_desc: Susan Schneider is an academic and public philosopher, who writes about the philosophy of mind and artificial intelligence. She believes that individuals, not companies, need to consider and decide the philosophical issues that will affect them as a result of artificial intelligence.
the-path-to-the-future-susan-schneider-a.subtitle: Susan Schneider on AI

how-to-think-about-whiteness-myriam-fran.speaker_desc: Myrian Fran ç ois is an academic, documentary maker and currently a research associate at the School of Oriental and African Studies at the University of London (SOAS).
how-to-think-about-whiteness-myriam-fran.subtitle: Overcoming the taboo

passion-action-and-hypocrisy.speaker_desc: Anarchist and primitivist ecophilosopher John Zerzan, financial analyst turned Buddhist nun Emma Slade, Novara Media co-founder Aaron Bastani, and former UK Liberal Democrat party leader Vince Cable debate passion, action and hypocrisy. Find out more at sayyourpeace.org , and check them out on Instagram and Facebook.
passion-action-and-hypocrisy.subtitle: Do you have the capacity to make a change?

how-to-transform-your-life-with-curiosit.speaker_desc: Garrick Jones is a businessman, academic, musician and Founding Partner of The Ludic Group where his research into Cloud Based Transformation Consulting, Digital Learning Programmes and Engagement are put into practice. how-to-transform-your-life-with-curiosit.subtitle: And how to use it to your advantage

in-love-with-animals.speaker_desc: World-renowned moral philosopher Peter Singer, Honorary Associate in Philosophy at the Open University Christopher Belshaw, former assistant editor of The Times Mary-Ann Sieghart and British actor and longtime vegan Peter Egan debate our love for animals. Myriam Francois hosts. In association with Future Normal .
in-love-with-animals.subtitle: Can we care about animals if we eat them?

the-left-and-anti-semitism-david-aaronov.speaker_desc: David Aaronovitch is a journalist, television presenter and author. He is a regular columnist for The Times and the author of Paddling to Jerusalem: An Aquatic Tour of Our Small Country (2000).
the-left-and-anti-semitism-david-aaronov.subtitle: An interview with David Aaronovitch

confronting-crisis-santiago-zabala.speaker_desc: Santiago Zabala is a philosopher and ICREA Research Philosopher at the Pompeu Fabra University, where he currently teaches contemporary and political philosophy.
confronting-crisis-santiago-zabala.subtitle: Taking emergencies seriously

the-mystery-of-reality.speaker_desc: CERN physicist John Ellis, theoretical physicist and Research Fellow at the Frankfurt Institute for Advanced Studies Sabine Hossenfelder, and award-winning science writer and quantum expert Jim Baggott debate the crisis in physics. David Malone hosts.
the-mystery-of-reality.subtitle: The mystery of reality & physics' biggest problem

the-corona-crash-grace-blakeley.speaker_desc: Described by Owen Jones as "one of the most inspiring, thought provoking and insightful voices on the left", Grace Blakeley is an economics and politics commentator and Marxist economist. She is a staff writer for Tribune and was previously the economics commentator of the New Statesman.
the-corona-crash-grace-blakeley.subtitle: Why we should radically restructure society

dicing-with-death.speaker_desc: Epidemiologist Sunetra Gupta, anarcho-capitalist David D. Friedman and renowned human rights lawyer Indira Jaising debate whether human beings are capable of keeping themselves safe. Sean Curran hosts.
dicing-with-death.subtitle: Are we capable of keeping ourselves safe?

constructing-consciousness-colm-toibin.speaker_desc: Colm Tóibín is a novelist, short story writer, essayist, playwright and poet. Currently the Chancellor at the University of Liverpool, Tóibín's notable works include 'The Heather Blazing', 'Brooklyn' and 'The Master'.
constructing-consciousness-colm-toibin.subtitle: An interview with novelist Colm Tóibín

arc-of-life-peter-singer.speaker_desc: Described by The New Yorker as "the world's most influential living philosopher" and known for his book Animal Liberation, Peter Singer specialises in applied ethics. He approaches ethical issues from a secular, utilitarian perspective, arguing in favour of veganism and of donating to help the global poor. Interviewer Jenny Kleeman is a documentary film-maker and journalist who is best known for her work on Channel 4's foreign affairs series Unreported World and BBC One's Panorama. Her book Sex Robots & Vegan Meat was published in 2020.
arc-of-life-peter-singer.subtitle: The biography of a world leading moral philosopher

science-hypocrisy-and-lies-john-ioannidi.speaker_desc: John Ioannidis is a physician-scientist, writer and Stanford University professor who has made contributions to evidence-based medicine, epidemiology, and clinical research. Ioannidid studies scientific research itself, meta-research primarily in clinical medicine and the social sciences.
science-hypocrisy-and-lies-john-ioannidi.subtitle: The truth deficit

women-vs-feminism-joanna-williams.speaker_desc: Dr Joanna Williams is Head of Education and Culture at Policy Exchange. She is an author, commentator and the associate editor of Spiked, writing on matters such as feminism, academic freedom and education.
women-vs-feminism-joanna-williams.subtitle: Has feminism lost its edge?

the-freedom-paradox.speaker_desc: Groundbreaking philosopher and cognitive scientist Daniel Dennett, Cognitive Neuroscience specialist Patrick Haggard and author of A Metaphysics for Freedom Helen Steward deliberate over the existence of free will. Mark Linsenmayer hosts.
the-freedom-paradox.subtitle: Does free will exist?

anarchy-in-capitalism-david-friedman.speaker_desc: David D. Friedman is an economist, physicist, legal scholar and anarcho-capitalist theorist. He is known for his popular book The Machinery of Freedom.David Friedman advocates a consequentialist version of anarcho-capitalism, arguing for anarchism on a cost-benefit analysis of state versus no state.
anarchy-in-capitalism-david-friedman.subtitle: An interview with David Friedman

the-happiness-trap-john-milbank.speaker_desc: Described by Rowan Williams as "unquestionably among the most sophisticated voices in the whole world of modern theology", John Milbank is an Anglican theologian and Emeritus Professor in the Department of Theology and Religious Studies at Nottingham University, where he is the President of the Centre of Theology and Religion.
the-happiness-trap-john-milbank.subtitle: How to outgrow this self-centred ideology

in-conversation-michael-sandel.speaker_desc: Michael Sandel teaches political philosophy at Harvard University. His books What Money Can't Buy: The Moral Limits of Markets , and Justice: What's the Right Thing to Do? were international best sellers and have been translated into 27 languages. Sandel's legendary course 'Justice' was the first Harvard course to be made freely available online and on television and has been viewed by tens of millions of people. His BBC series 'The Global Philosopher' explores the philosophical ideas lying behind the headlines with participants from around the world.
in-conversation-michael-sandel.subtitle: The Tyranny of Merit

life-as-we-know-it-nick-lane.speaker_desc: Nick Lane is a biochemist, writer and professor in evolutionary biochemistry at University College London. He has published four books including The Vital Question: Why Is Life The Way It Is?
life-as-we-know-it-nick-lane.subtitle: What does it mean to be alive?

not-so-equal-global-inequality.speaker_desc: Nobel prize winning economist Joseph Stiglitz, rising economics commentator Grace Blakeley and Labour politician Lisa Nandy examine our commitments to global equality.
not-so-equal-global-inequality.subtitle: Commitments to global equality

the-arc-of-life-bianca-jagger.speaker_desc: Bianca Jagger is Founder, President and Chief Executive of the Bianca Jagger Human Rights Foundation (BJHRF), which she established in 2005 to be a force for change and a voice for the most vulnerable. She is the recipient of numerous prestigious awards, including The Right Livelihood Award (2004) also known as the ‘alternative Nobel prize. In association with HuffPost.
the-arc-of-life-bianca-jagger.subtitle: A biography of a leading human rights defender

for-your-own-good.speaker_desc: Transhumanist Natasha Vita-More, pioneering neuroscientist Henry Marsh and Chief Executive of Dignity in Dying Chief Sarah Wootton.
for-your-own-good.subtitle: Longevity vs. wellbeing

the-future-of-india-shashi-tharoor.subtitle: Will India hold on to secular liberalism?

the-ai-illusion.speaker_desc: Astronomer Royal and author of On the Future Martin Rees, theoretical physicist Laura Mersini-Houghton, Closure theorist Hilary Lawson and computer scientist Kate Devlin question the reality of artificial intelligence. Stephanie Hare hosts.
the-ai-illusion.subtitle: What does the future really have in store?

science-and-discovery-henry-gee.speaker_desc: Henry Gee is a paleontologist, evolutionary biologist and senior editor of the scientific journal Nature.
science-and-discovery-henry-gee.subtitle: The limits of knowledge

the-future-of-war-lawrence-freedman.speaker_desc: The "dean of British strategic studies" Sir Lawrence Freedman is Emeritus Professor of War Studies at King's College London and was a member of the Iraq Inquiry published in 2016.
the-future-of-war-lawrence-freedman.subtitle: Understanding conflict

metaphysics-morality-and-mayhem.speaker_desc: Cultural critic and polymath Raymond Tallis, award-winning novelist Joanna Kavenna and renowned philosopher and ethicist Simon Blackburn investigate the relationship between metaphysics and morality. Hilary Lawson hosts.
metaphysics-morality-and-mayhem.subtitle: Which theories should we prioritise?

the-anxiety-of-choice-renata-salecl.speaker_desc: Renata Salecl is a philosopher, sociologist and legal theorist currently working as a senior researcher at the Institute of Criminology at the University of Ljubljana.
the-anxiety-of-choice-renata-salecl.subtitle: Freedom and popular culture

getting-high-and-being-human.speaker_desc: Imperial College psychiatrist and former government drugs adviser David Nutt, philosopher of mind Peter Sjöstedt-H, and addiction advocist Annemarie Ward get to the bottom of getting high. Psychiatrist Mark Salter hosts.
getting-high-and-being-human.subtitle: Debating drug law reform

editing-the-future-gunes-taylor.speaker_desc: Güneş Taylor is a postdoctoral Training Fellow at the Crick Institute where she currently researches the mechanisms of sex determination and CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing.
editing-the-future-gunes-taylor.subtitle: The influence of CRISPR-Cas9

the-truth-about-free-will-raymond-tallis.speaker_desc: Professor Raymond Tallis is a philosopher, poet, novelist and cultural critic and was until recently a physician and clinical scientist. In the Economist's Intelligent Life Magazine (2009) he was listed as one of the top living polymaths in the world.
the-truth-about-free-will-raymond-tallis.subtitle: Is choice an illusion?

ideas-to-live-and-die-by-terry-eagleton.speaker_desc: Terry Eagleton is a Marxist literary critic and public intellectual, widely recognised as a mainstay of British academia. He has published over forty books on topics ranging from Samuel Richardson to the banality of evil.
ideas-to-live-and-die-by-terry-eagleton.subtitle: Which do we take seriously?

the-return-of-the-colosseum.speaker_desc: Award-winning author Meg Rosoff, cultural critic Soma Ghosh and Orange First Novel prize winning novelist Joanna Kavenna debate the return of the Colosseum. Roger Bolton hosts.
the-return-of-the-colosseum.subtitle: The morality of salacious entertainment

leading-from-the-left-chantal-mouffe.speaker_desc: Chantal Mouffe is a political theorist best known for her contribution to the development of the Essex School of discourse analysis, a post-Marxist political inquiry that redefines Leftist politics in terms of radical democracy.
leading-from-the-left-chantal-mouffe.subtitle: The case for left populism

physics-doesnt-have-to-be-pretty-sabine-.speaker_desc: Sabine Hossenfelder is an author and theoretical physicsist who researches quantum theory. She is a Research Fellow at the Frankfurt Institute for Advanced Studies where she leads the Analog Systems for Gravity Duals group.
physics-doesnt-have-to-be-pretty-sabine-.subtitle: Shedding light on theoretical physics

in-search-of-the-self-will-self.speaker_desc: William Self is an author, journalist, political commentator and television personality. His fiction is known for being satirical, grotesque, and fantastical, and often explores mental illness, drug abuse and psychiatry.
in-search-of-the-self-will-self.subtitle: The benefits of psychogeography

the-half-life-of-science-barry-barnes.speaker_desc: Barry Barnes is a former Professor of Sociology at Exeter University, known for his naturalistic approach to science. He worked at the 'Science Studies Unit' at the University of Edinburgh with David Bloor, where they developed the strong programme in the Sociology of Scientific Knowledge.
the-half-life-of-science-barry-barnes.subtitle: Do scientific facts exist?

the-rise-and-fall-of-globalisation.speaker_desc: Director general of the Institute of Economic Affairs Mark Littlewood, Tribune staff writer Grace Blakeley, and former Leader of the Liberal Democrats Vince Cable debate the rise and fall of globalisation. Editor of Chinadialogue Isabel Hilton hosts.
the-rise-and-fall-of-globalisation.subtitle: Do we need to pursue localism?

the-madness-of-quantum-jim-baggott.speaker_desc: Jim Baggott is an award-winning science writer who has been published in Aeon, Prospect, New Scientist and Nature. According to Popular Science, Jim is "one of the UK's best science writers and never disappoints".
the-madness-of-quantum-jim-baggott.subtitle: Difficulties in understanding the integral theory

extinction-and-renewal.speaker_desc: Prominent transhumanist David Pearce, former leader of the UK Green Party Natalie Bennett and paleontologist and senior editor of Nature Henry Gee debate extinction and renewal. Myriam Francois hosts.
extinction-and-renewal.subtitle: Are we facing the Sixth Great Mass Extinction?

stories-worth-telling-michael-morpurgo.speaker_desc: Michael Morpurgo OBE is a book author, poet, playwright and librettist who is best known for children's novels such as War Horse. His work is noted for its "magical storytelling".
stories-worth-telling-michael-morpurgo.subtitle: Politics in children's literature

the-end-of-the-whitewash.speaker_desc: The UK's first Professor of Black Studies Kehinde Andrews, award winning actress Adjoah Andoh and acclaimed journalist and novelist Will Self unravel the relationship between colourblind casting and historical accuracy. Joanna Kavenna hosts.
the-end-of-the-whitewash.subtitle: Colourblind casting and historical accuracy

left-right-and-covid.speaker_desc: Conservative MP Bim Afolami, director and founder of the Institute of Ideas Claire Fox, and former Culture and Digital Editor of Channel 4 News Paul Mason discuss the future of political lines. Editor of Chinadialogue Isabel Hilton hosts.
left-right-and-covid.subtitle: Are responses to crises divided along party lines?

church-state-and-nietzsche.speaker_desc: Giles Fraser is a journalist, broadcaster and Rector at St Mary's Church in Newington, South London. He is known for his resignation from St Paul's Cathedral after a disagreement over the removal of Occupy prostesters.
church-state-and-nietzsche.subtitle: Is the church inescapably political?

artists-crusade.speaker_desc: Director of the Tate Modern Frances Morris, conceptual artist and sculptor Anish Kapoor and legendary poet Eileen Myles consider the importance of politics in art. Mary-Ann Sieghart hosts.
artists-crusade.subtitle: The politics in art

the-consciousness-puzzle-panpsychism.speaker_desc: Philip Goff is a philosopher and consciousness researcher at Durham University, who is a leading defender of panpsychism. ‘Suddenly the universe appears in a new and much more revealing perspective." Phillip Pullman
the-consciousness-puzzle-panpsychism.subtitle: Is panpsychism the solution?

the-miracle-of-mind-consciousness.speaker_desc: Philosopher of mind Tim Crane, metaphysical idealist Bernardo Kastrup and consciousness specialist Susan Blackmore debate the miracle of mind. Closure theorist Hilary Lawson hosts
the-miracle-of-mind-consciousness.subtitle: Will there ever be consensus on consciousness?

calculating-reality-silvia-jonas.speaker_desc: Silvia Jonas is a philosopher at the Munich Center for Mathematical Philosophy working in metaphysics, philosophy of mathematics, and epistemology. She is the author of 'Metaphysics: The Unspeakable in Art, Religion, and Philosophy'.
calculating-reality-silvia-jonas.subtitle: How mathematics shapes our world

china-ally-or-threat-trade-wars.speaker_desc: Foreign secretary under John Major, Malcolm Rifkind, founder of China Dialogue Isabel Hilton and former Lib Dem leader Vince Cable debate the West's future relationship with China. Director of Oxford University's China Centre Rana Mitter hosts.
china-ally-or-threat-trade-wars.subtitle: Rising tensions on the world stage

writing-the-future-claire-van-kampen.speaker_desc: Claire Van Kampen is a highly respected director and composer, who has served as the Director of Theatre Music at the Shakespeare's Globe since 1997. She is now focusing her talents on playwriting. In this exclusive interview, Claire Van Kampen discusses how she made the transition from composer to playwright, the process of bringing life to the stage, the problems with theatre today and her hope for the future of the arts.
writing-the-future-claire-van-kampen.subtitle: Bringing life back to theatre

drugs-the-case-for-decriminalisation-dav.speaker_desc: David Nutt is a neuropsychopharmacologist and the former chairman of the Advisory Council on the Misuse of Drugs in the UK, a position he was dismissed from in 2009. "Any sensible person or scientist knows that the drug laws are not based on the science of drugs." David Nutt
drugs-the-case-for-decriminalisation-dav.subtitle: The best choice for drug law reform

science-to-the-rescue-covid-19.speaker_desc: Founder of loop quantum gravity theory Carlo Rovelli, philosopher of science at Michigan State University Heather Douglas, and esteemed analytic philosopher Patricia Churchland discuss how we should respond to disagreement in science during the Covid-19 pandemic. Award-winning science journalist Anil Ananthaswamy hosts.
science-to-the-rescue-covid-19.subtitle: How do we decide on the truth?

moments-of-discovery-sophie-grace-chappe.speaker_desc: Sophie Grace Chappell is the author of numerous books and articles on ethics, ancient philosophy, epistemology and philosophy of religion. TLS described her as "an inspiring expression of an ethical vision"
moments-of-discovery-sophie-grace-chappe.subtitle: How do we decide on a moral system?

the-dark-energy-phenomenon-subir-sarkar.speaker_desc: In this interview, Oxford Professor of Physics Subir Sarkar outlines the problems with Dark Energy, cosmological homogeneity and questions our entire understanding of the universe.
the-dark-energy-phenomenon-subir-sarkar.subtitle: Have we misunderstood the universe?

capitalism-and-covid-paul-krugman.speaker_desc: Nobel Prize winning economist Paul Krugman, UIC Distinguished Professor Deirdre McCloskey and Tribune staff writer Grace Blakeley debate on Capitalism and Covid. Matthew Taylor hosts.
capitalism-and-covid-paul-krugman.subtitle: A new solution to societal inequality?

the-smartphone-society.speaker_desc: Nicole Aschoff is the author of The Smartphone Society: Technology, Power, and Resistance in the New Gilded Age and The New Prophets of Capital and is on the editorial board of Jacobin. According to author Nicole Klein “Aschoff tackles slippery subjects with confidence and subtlety, providing readers with key intellectual tools to separate fact from fiction.”
the-smartphone-society.subtitle: Health, wealth and power in the digital age

risk-evidence-and-lockdown-covid-19.speaker_desc: Professor of Theoretical Epidemiology Sunetra Gupta, director of the UCL Institute for Human Health and Performance Hugh Montgomery and ISI highly cited statistician David Spiegelhalter weigh up risk, evidence and lockdown. Rana Mitter hosts.
risk-evidence-and-lockdown-covid-19.subtitle: The right response to Covid-19?

how-to-talk-to-climate-change.speaker_desc: Psychotherapist, Social Work Academic, and Climate Psychology Therapist and Researcher Caroline Hickman teaches us how to talk about climate change.
how-to-talk-to-climate-change.subtitle: Emotionally engaging in the crisis

evil-acts-good-people-the-problem-of-dir.speaker_desc: In this interview, philosopher Stephen de Wijze outlines the messy issue of the Problem of Dirty Hands, what evil really is and why it may make sense to call acts, but not people, evil.
evil-acts-good-people-the-problem-of-dir.subtitle: The problem of dirty hands

living-dangerously-covid-19.speaker_desc: Nobel Prize winning economist Daniel Kahneman, Harvard psychologist Steven Pinker and Labour MP, barrister and human rights activist Shami Chakrabarti explore risk, rationality and coronavirus. Anil Anathaswamy hosts.
living-dangerously-covid-19.subtitle: Risk, rationality and coronavirus

how-to-decolonise-your-mind-kehinde-andr.speaker_desc: Kehinde Andrews is a Professor of Black Studies, director of the Centre for Critical Social Research and co-chair of the UK Black Studies Association.
how-to-decolonise-your-mind-kehinde-andr.subtitle: Improving conversations surrounding race

locking-down-on-human-rights-covid-19.speaker_desc: Shami Chakrabarti is a Labour Party politician, barrister and human rights activist who served as the director of the advocacy group Liberty.
locking-down-on-human-rights-covid-19.subtitle: Lessons from lockdown

illusions-and-dreams-philosophy-of-perce.speaker_desc: In this interview philosopher Jan Westerhoff outlines the philosophy of illusions and dreams, and his theory of an external world whose fundamental constituents are bits of mind, not bits of matter.
illusions-and-dreams-philosophy-of-perce.subtitle: The philosophy of perception

media-responsibility-and-a-good-story.speaker_desc: Labour MP Jess Phillips, journalist and presenter on the BBC's Today programme Nick Robinson, and founder and former editor of Prospect magazine David Goodhart debate the ethics of coronavirus coverage. Mary Ann Sieghart hosts.
media-responsibility-and-a-good-story.subtitle: The ethics of coronavirus coverage

the-uncanny-valley-pandemic-model.speaker_desc: Professor of Theoretical Epidemiology at the University of Oxford, Sunetra Gupta addresses these tricky questions.
the-uncanny-valley-pandemic-model.subtitle: How to model a pandemic

the-morality-of-pandemic-covid-19.subtitle: What duty do we have to others during COVID-19?

a-physicists-approach-to-problem-solving.speaker_desc: Chiara Marletto is a quantum phsycisist based at the University of Oxford who co-developed constructor theory, a proposal for a new mode of explanation in fundamental physics.
a-physicists-approach-to-problem-solving.subtitle: The fun to be had in getting it wrong

crime-and-punishment.speaker_desc: Anthony Malcolm Daniels, also known by the pen name Theodore Dalrymple, is an English cultural critic, prison doctor and psychiatrist.
crime-and-punishment.subtitle: Criminal pscyhology's insights into human nature

the-right-way-to-think-reason.speaker_desc: Oxford Intellectual Historian Alister McGrath, philosopher and author of Fear of Knowledge Paul Boghossian, and Professor of Religion and author of Strange Wonder Mary-Jane Rubenstein rethink our faith in rationality and reason.
the-right-way-to-think-reason.subtitle: Can we trust our reason?

sex-brain-and-gender-binaries.speaker_desc: Daphna Joel is an Israeli neuroscientist. She is a senior member of the faculty of the School of Psychological Sciences and the School of Neuroscience at Tel Aviv University.
sex-brain-and-gender-binaries.subtitle: The binaries holding progress back

a-history-of-the-conscious-world-indian-.speaker_desc: Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad is the Distinguished Professor of Comparative Religion and Philosophy at Lancaster University. His research focuses on Indian religions and comparative phenomenology, epistemology, metaphysics and philosophy of religion.
a-history-of-the-conscious-world-indian-.subtitle: Panpsychism's roots in ancient Indian philosophy

the-cause-of-death-lockdown.speaker_desc: Nobel-prize winning biophysicist Michael Levitt debates with Professor of Infectious Disease Epidemiology Anne Johnson and Professor of Risk and Disaster Reduction David Alexander, both at University College London, and associate editor of The Spectator Toby Young, who recently launched the website Lockdown Sceptics. Philosopher and author of Closure Hilary Lawson hosts.
the-cause-of-death-lockdown.subtitle: Nobel laureate challenges lockdown

where-are-we-going.speaker_desc: CERN physicist John Ellis is a pioneer in the emerging field of particle astrophysics, who has also made important contributions to particle physics, astrophysics, cosmology and quantum gravity.
where-are-we-going.subtitle: Tackling science's biggest questions

brian-eno-philosophy-of-art.speaker_desc: Musical pioneer Brian Eno is co-founder of the art rock group Roxy Music and producer of recordings by the likes of David Byrne, U2, David Bowie, John Cale, and Robert Fripp.
brian-eno-philosophy-of-art.subtitle: Insights from a music legend

the-age-of-anxiety-covid-19-legacy-will-.speaker_desc: Psychotherapist and member of the Climate Psychology Alliance Caroline Hickman, neuropsychopharmacologist and author David Nutt, and consultant in adult psychiatry for the NHS Mark Salter debate the growing phenomenon of anxiety. Rana Mitter hosts.
the-age-of-anxiety-covid-19-legacy-will-.subtitle: COVID-19 legacy will be psychiatric

cybersecurity-and-huawei-nigel-inkster-i.speaker_desc: Security expert Nigel Inkster worked for 31 years in the British Secret Intelligence Service (MI6), retiring as Assistant Chief and Director of Operations and Intelligence. After leaving MI6, he became Director of Transnational Threats and Political Risk at the International Institute for Strategic Studies, where he is now Senior Advisor, and has also been engaged in a variety of para-diplomatic activities on behalf of the UK government. His research portfolio has included transnational terrorism, insurgency, transnational organised crime, cyber security, intelligence and security, and the evolving character of conflict.
cybersecurity-and-huawei-nigel-inkster-i.subtitle: China's rise as a digital superpower

against-psychiatry-richard-bentall-inter.speaker_desc: Richard Bentall is Professor of Clinical Psychology at the University of Sheffield, a Fellow of the British Academy and a leading researcher on schizophrenia, psychosis and public mental health. He is the author of Madness Explained and Doctoring the Mind.
against-psychiatry-richard-bentall-inter.subtitle: Prevention and treatment

is-capitalism-broken-democracy-reform.speaker_desc: Author of Plunder of The Commons, Guy Standing, politician and libertarian economist Jamie Whyte, FT Alphaville editor, Izabella Kaminska and senior economic adviser at HSBC Holdings, Stephen King ask whether we can save Capitalism - and whether we should.
is-capitalism-broken-democracy-reform.subtitle: Can, and should, it be saved?

after-the-god-particle-the-nightmare-sce.speaker_desc: Cambridge physicist Ben Allanach, Maxwell prize-winning CERN theoretical physicist John Ellis and Edinburgh Astrophysicist Catherine Heymans look at what's missing from our picture of particle theory. David Malone hosts.
after-the-god-particle-the-nightmare-sce.subtitle: The nightmare scenario

learning-to-love-uncertainty-alternative.speaker_desc: Åsa Wikforss is a professor of theoretical philosophy at Stockholm University. Wikforss is a member of Swedish Academy whose research focuses on the intersection of philosophy of mind, language and epistemology, ans in 2017 Wikfoss published Alternative facts. On knowledge and its enemies, a book that has had a great impact in Sweden.
learning-to-love-uncertainty-alternative.subtitle: The individual vs alternative facts

metropolis-untamed-tech-giants.speaker_desc: Author of The Age of Surveillance Capitalism Shoshana Zuboff, Conservative MP Bim Afolami, author of Zed Joanna Kavenna, and Labour MP Angela Eagle debate the power and peril of the tech giants.
metropolis-untamed-tech-giants.subtitle: Tech giants on collision course with democracy

science-trust-and-truth.speaker_desc: Philosopher of science and author of How The Laws of Physics Lie, Nancy Cartwright untangles the evidence and asks "science: why trust it?"
science-trust-and-truth.subtitle: When to interrogate the data

life-without-labels-mental-health.speaker_desc: Mark Salter is a consultant in adult general psychiatry. His special interests include risk, untowardness and media portrayals of mental distress. "It is not much to ask for mental health to be given the same degree of consideration as physical health." Mark Salter
life-without-labels-mental-health.subtitle: Problems with modern mental health

izabella-kaminska-in-depth-interview.speaker_desc: Izabella Kaminska is editor of FT Alphaville. Before that she worked as a producer at CNBC, a natural gas reporter at Platts and an associate editor of BP's internal magazine.
izabella-kaminska-in-depth-interview.subtitle: On the next economic crisis and phony regulators

in-search-of-freedom.speaker_desc: Historian of ideas and author of Life Lessons from Hobbes Hannah Dawson, post-realist philosopher Hilary Lawson, neuropsychologist and science writer Paul Broks and author of Freedom Regained Julian Baggini ask who's really in control. David Aaronovitch hosts.
in-search-of-freedom.subtitle: Do we choose to follow the rules?

the-tyranny-of-the-new.speaker_desc: Composer and former musical director at Shakespeare's Globe Claire van Kampen, film director Sophie Fiennes, Observer music journalist Ammar Kalia and art rock icon Brian Eno debate the value of the new. Joanna Kavenna hosts.
the-tyranny-of-the-new.subtitle: Is innovation unstoppable?

time-is-running-out-for-supersymmetry-an.speaker_desc: Royal Observatory astrophysicist Catherine Heymans, theoretical physicist at the University of Cambridge Ben Allanach, head of the Particle Theory Group at Oxford University Subir Sarkar, Cambridge string theorist David Tong, experimental physicist Tara Shears, and author of The End of Science John Horgan discuss whether it is time to do away with beautiful theories.
time-is-running-out-for-supersymmetry-an.subtitle: Are physicists giving up?

whats-wrong-with-us.speaker_desc: Psychiatrist David Healy, Oxford University futurist Anders Sandberg, and former leader of the Green Party Natalie Bennett debate the future of AI doctors. Emily Grossman hosts.
whats-wrong-with-us.subtitle: Is it time for AI to do more to help doctors?

digital-apes-nigel-shadbolt-technology.speaker_desc: Nigel Shadbolt is the author of The Digital Ape and co-founder of the Open Data Institute with Tim Berners-Lee and was identified as 'one of the most fascinating and important scientists alive today' by Jim Al-Khalili.
digital-apes-nigel-shadbolt-technology.subtitle: Technology as a force for good

emily-thomas-in-depth-interview-travel-t.speaker_desc: Emily Thomas is a historian of philosophy at Durham University. Her main research interests include space, time, and the relationship between philosophy and travel.
emily-thomas-in-depth-interview-travel-t.subtitle: On travel, time and women in philosophy

lies-damned-lies-and-post-truth.speaker_desc: Author of Post Truth Steve Fuller, theoretical philosopher Åsa Wikforss, continental philosopher Sacha Golob, and former Moscow journalist and author of This is Not Propaganda Peter Pomerantsev ask whether anybody has a monopoly on truth.
lies-damned-lies-and-post-truth.subtitle: Is there still space for alternative perspectives?

ben-allanach-in-depth-interview-supersym.speaker_desc: Ben Allanach is a professor of theoretical physics at the University of Cambridge. His research focuses on collider searches for new physics with the Cambridge Pheno Working Group and at CERN's Large Hadron Collider.
ben-allanach-in-depth-interview-supersym.subtitle: On supersymmetry, particle physics and beyond

bart-streumer-in-depth-interview-error-t.speaker_desc: Bart Streumer is professor of philosophy at the University of Groningen in the Netherlands. Streumer's main research interests are metaethics, ethics, and political philosophy.
bart-streumer-in-depth-interview-error-t.subtitle: On metaethics, error theory and beyond.

the-future-of-thought.speaker_desc: Author of How the World Thinks Julian Baggini, political philosopher Jamie Whyte, and Oxford Professor of China Studies Vivienne Shue consider China's influence on the future of ideas. Journalist and broadcaster Isabel Hilton hosts.
the-future-of-thought.subtitle: Is the sun setting on Western ideas?

work-and-play-are-we-searching-for-joy-i.speaker_desc: Ab Fab star Helen Lederer, Director of the Einstein Forum and author of Why We Grow Up? Susan Neiman, and novelist Janne Teller join Julian Baggini to seek new answers to life’s biggest question.
